author: axet
body: ### Motivation There is currently no way to keep a torrent's record and settings without keeping it loaded in the session. Users who want to "retire" a torrent have to either remove it (and lose its resume data) or leave it in the transfer list, where it still takes part in queueing and session management. This adds an archive concept: the torrent is unloaded from libtorrent, but its resume data is kept and it can be restored later with all of its settings intact. Related to #11878, which asks for a similar "archived" state. Also partially solving https://github.com/qbittorrent/qBittorrent/issues/21121. ### What it does - Adds an **Archive** action to the transfer list context menu. Archiving requests fresh resume data, marks it as archived, persists it, and then unloads the torrent from libtorrent. Downloaded content is kept on disk. - Adds a **History** tab that lists archived torrents with name, size, progress, category, tags, added/completed dates, ratio, transferred amounts and save path. Rows are shown in a muted color. - History actions: **Restore**, **Export .torrent...** and **Delete** (with the usual option to also delete the content). - Restoring adds the torrent back in stopped state with its original settings. Restore is rejected if the same info hash is already active. - Archived torrents survive restarts: they are skipped when resume data is loaded and are never passed to libtorrent. - Adding a new torrent whose info hash is already archived is rejected with a message asking to restore it from History instead. - `removeTorrent()` and `isKnownTorrent()` now also consider archived torrents. ### Persistence The state is stored as a single `archived` boolean in `LoadTorrentParams`: - bencode backend: `qBt-archived` - SQLite backend: `archived` column, schema bumped to version 11 with an automatic migration No additional archive metadata (timestamps, original paths, etc.) is stored; everything shown in History is derived from the existing resume data. ### WebAPI - `POST torrents/archive` - archive torrents by `hashes` - `POST torrents/unarchive` - restore archived torrents by `hashes` - `GET torrents/archived` - list archived torrents (supports `hashes`, `category`, `tag`) - `torrents/delete`, `torrents/export`, `torrents/count` (`filter=archived`) and `torrents/fetchMetadata` now handle archived torrents. `WebAPI_Changelog.md` is updated. ### Testing - Full build with `GUI=ON`, `WEBUI=ON`, `TESTING=ON` succeeds without warnings in the touched files. - `ctest` passes (25/25), including new unit tests for `ArchivedTorrent` derivation (with/without metadata, lost download stats, seed mode). ### Screenshots ### Notes - Archived torrents are a persisted record, not a `TorrentState`; they never reach libtorrent, so no state-specific code paths are affected. - Magnet links archived before metadata is available can be restored, but cannot be exported until metadata is fetched. ### Further impovements Right now implementation is based on separate tab for minimizing code base changes. Which makes UI a bit ugly. Moving History tab into left side panel is possible but requires a much more code refactoring. I would like to do it in a separate pull request after this one is merged.

author: ilien-dev
body:
Every change here answers a failure found in real use: 2,361 MCP calls across 159 sessions on v1.3.1, where 13.6% of the URLs asked for came back `cooldown`, 28% of searches returned nothing, and binary downloads arrived corrupted. This is the 1.4.0 release branch.

## What changes for a caller

- **An unknown parameter now refuses the call** and names the closest real one. Numbers and booleans sent as strings are accepted.
- **`web_fetch_many` has a total budget** (8,000 tokens by default, shared across the URLs), with a cursor per cut page and results in input order.
- **`web_status` is a summary by default**; the rest comes with `sections=`.
- **Search `attempts` are objects** with an `outcome`, not strings.
- **`request_cooldown_seconds` now means the maximum backoff**, not a fixed hold.

## What was fixed

**Visit limit and cooldowns.** One fetch is one visit however many tiers it climbs. A full window is a wait for the next slot, never a 900 s hold. `Retry-After` is honoured as given; without it the backoff starts at 30 s. `wait` lets a call wait out a hold, `clear_cooldown` clears every kind of hold, and a refusal says the budget is shared by every session on the machine. A ladder walk that just failed is remembered for ten minutes (`fresh` forces a new one).

**Files and APIs.** Bodies stay bytes: `out_file` writes exactly what was served, streamed, with resume and a sha256. JSON and plain text are no longer read as walls or judged as prose, `json_path` projects a JSON answer, and source files come back byte for byte. New `web_probe` answers whether URLs exist without reading them.

**GitHub.** github.com URLs for a repo, tree, file, issue, pull request, release or commit are answered from the API or the raw host, with rate limits reported as rate limits. The instructions, the skill, the README and the setup memory block now say to prefer the `searchGitHub` tool of the grep.app MCP server for finding code across repositories when the session has it; Svipall does all of it when that tool is absent.

**Search.** Each engine answer is classified, so a challenge page is no longer "0 results". Engine health is remembered, a failing engine rests, and a zero-result answer says which engines were blocked and what to try. Redirect-wrapped links are unwrapped, locale follows the query, and a `news` engine is added. The lite endpoint that returned nothing on 307 of 331 attempts was being sent a POST; it gets a GET now.

**Pages, browsers, CLI.** Walls are recognised in Spanish, Portuguese, French and German; a browser no longer turns a short refusal into a 200. Literal `query` terms such as `--effort` match, cursors survive a changed query, a small token budget is filled rather than returning one line, PDF glyph-width ranges no longer break words apart, and blank table rows are dropped. Browser errors carry their cause, `browser_do` keeps its per-action results, the managed browser updates itself, `web_map` and `web_site_search` look in more places, and every CLI subcommand has `--help` and rejects unknown flags.

## What did not improve

- The Cloudflare check on manualslib.com and lib.rs, and the mojeek captcha, are still not passed. Measured before and after, including one `solve_and_continue` attempt each.
- One search engine still answers multi-word queries with unrelated pages; those results are flagged `off_topic` and ranked last, not fixed.
- Not verified: streaming on the non-default HTTP engine and over HTTP/3, downloads of several gigabytes, a real GitHub 429.
- Own-IP masking does not cover files written with `out_file`/`out_dir`, `web_capture` bodies, `web_watch` or the request log.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1,597 passed, 0 failed, 42 ignored (network and browser tests, run by hand by the lanes that wrote them).
- Each item has an offline end-to-end test through the real handler or the built binary, seen failing before the change.
- Live runs of the built 1.4.0 binary against the cases that failed in use: 16 rapid requests to one API host, a font download checked by sha256 against curl, `web_probe`, three searches, a GitHub repo, file and API search, a blocked reddit JSON endpoint, the PDF that had broken spacing, and a six-page `web_fetch_many` over MCP stdio.
- `scripts/qc.sh` fails two steps this branch does not touch: the installer prompt test does not run under Git Bash on Windows, and `CLAUDE.md` is about 16 tokens over its size cap, as it is on `main`. The extraction floors were skipped because no corpus is configured on this machine.
- The tool list is 38,547 characters, smaller than on 1.3.1 despite the new tool.

Merging this bumps the workspace version to 1.4.0, which is what triggers a release.

author: yishai946
body:
Closes #75

## What
Field records the searcher's GPS route in the background and sends it to the API (UC-S01, decisions 43, 65).

- `LocationTracker` interface (TECH_STACK.md), with `expoLocationTracker` over `expo-location` + `expo-task-manager`. The rest of the app talks to the interface only.
- **Background task** `trace-location`, defined at module top level and imported first by the root layout, as expo-task-manager requires: the phone can start the app in the background to deliver fixes with no screen mounted. Each batch goes to `POST /missions/:id/track-points` (#146).
- **Marking**: `toTrackPoints` marks every fix by the searcher's task, `search` while Searching and `safety` otherwise.
- **When it runs**: a new session flag `tracking` turns on at the first Start Search and stays on across a move to another polygon and while paused, until the activity ends, the searcher leaves the mission or signs out (decision 20). The mission layout starts and stops the tracker from it.
- **Force-close**: the tracker stops with the app (`killServiceOnDestroy`), which UC-S01 allows ("המעקב עשוי להיפסק"); the commander then sees the last update. Nothing restores the mission after a restart yet (#40), so continuing in the background would only collect points it cannot send.
- **Settings**: the time and distance intervals are left to the phone, because the sampling rate is TBD in the spec. `Accuracy.High` is a provisional choice: on Android it also sets the default intervals, so it should be revisited with the sampling rate. Android gets the foreground-service notification "TRACE רושמת את המסלול שלך"; iOS shows the background location indicator.
- `app.json`: `isAndroidForegroundServiceEnabled` for the expo-location plugin (the foreground-service permissions Android 14 needs). **This needs a new native build (IPA/APK).**

## Not in this Pull Request
- Nothing sets the task to Searching yet: Start Search and its permission checks are #30, so the tracker does not start in practice until then.
- A batch that fails to upload is lost: keeping points without signal is #76 (outbox #97). Restoring the mission and the tracking state after a restart is #40.
- GPS unavailable: #77.

## Checks
- `pnpm format`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`: pass.
- Field tests in the touched folders: 122 pass (the expo modules are mocked).
- Not checked on a real device: the issue's "route recorded with the screen locked" test needs a build with Start Search (#30).

## Review
A separate reviewer agent read the diff against the issue, UC-S01, decisions 20, 43, 65, the installed expo-location and expo-task-manager types and the standards. The task options and the config plugin option are valid for SDK 58.

Fixed:
- After a force-close the store is empty, so background batches were dropped silently while the Android notification still said the location was being sent. The tracker now stops with the app. The fallback to the saved token, which could not happen in practice, is removed with its test.
- The tracking flag turned on only with Searching. It now follows any started task (searching, paused or finished), also when entering a mission, so a paused searcher who joins again is tracked.
- When the server answers 409 `PARTICIPATION_ENDED` (the activity ended while the socket was down), the phone marks it and stops tracking instead of sampling GPS for nothing.
- Tests for the background task's handler (upload, ignored error and empty delivery, stop on an ended activity) and for the derived flag.

Left:
- `Accuracy.High` is provisional until the sampling rate is decided (TBD).
- The foreground-service notification text is new copy, in no wireframe ("TRACE רושמת את המסלול שלך" / "המיקום נשלח למנהל המסע עד סיום הפעילות.").
- Not checked: whether Android evaluates the root layout (where the task is defined) on a headless relaunch. With `killServiceOnDestroy` there is no such relaunch.

author: t0msilver
body:
## What

When the reconnect attempts ran out during an Overlay Buffer dictation with polishing on (or the Mistral second pass), "Connection lost. Dictation stopped." and the red icon gave way to "Ready" and the idle icon as soon as the polish finished. `endDictationAfterLostConnection` set the status and the icon after `finishStoppedSession` returned (`Sources/localvoxtral/DictationSessionController+Reconnect.swift:319-326`), but with a polish the commit ends later in a task, and its cleanup sets Ready and idle because this path set neither `stoppedOnItsOwnStatus` nor `holdFailureIndicatorUntilStopCompletes`. The network-lost branches of `handleNetworkChange` had the same order.

These paths now set `stoppedOnItsOwnStatus` before the stop, and the lost connection also holds the failure icon until the stop completes, as the microphone-unavailable stop does. No new user-visible string.

Closes #2065

It relies on #2063 (merged), which keeps the red icon for its full window after the stop completes.

## Proof

Regression tests: `RealtimeReconnectTests.testAnExhaustedReconnectKeepsItsStatusAndRedIconThroughThePolish` and `testANetworkLossKeepsItsStatusThroughThePolish`.

Before the fix (`remote-build.sh test --filter RealtimeReconnectTests`):

```
RealtimeReconnectTests.swift:363: error: -[... testANetworkLossKeepsItsStatusThroughThePolish] : XCTAssertEqual failed: ("Ready") is not equal to ("Dictation stopped after the network disconnected.")
RealtimeReconnectTests.swift:340: error: -[... testAnExhaustedReconnectKeepsItsStatusAndRedIconThroughThePolish] : XCTAssertEqual failed: ("Ready") is not equal to ("Connection lost. Dictation stopped.")
RealtimeReconnectTests.swift:342: error: -[... testAnExhaustedReconnectKeepsItsStatusAndRedIconThroughThePolish] : XCTAssertEqual failed: ("idle") is not equal to ("recentFailure")
Executed 35 tests, with 3 failures (0 unexpected)
```

After (`--filter RealtimeReconnectTests --filter MicrophoneDisconnectedIndicatorTests`, then `--filter DictationPipelineTests`):

```
Test Case '-[localvoxtralTests.RealtimeReconnectTests testANetworkLossKeepsItsStatusThroughThePolish]' passed (0.011 seconds).
Test Case '-[localvoxtralTests.RealtimeReconnectTests testAnExhaustedReconnectKeepsItsStatusAndRedIconThroughThePolish]' passed (0.010 seconds).
Executed 40 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)
DictationPipelineTests: Executed 126 tests, with 0 failures (0 unexpected)
```

- [ ] Unit suite green: hosted run on this PR

**Blast radius:** without a polish the stop completes inside `finishStoppedSession`, which consumes both flags at once, so the status, the error line and the icon end as before; the network-restored branch still matches the same status and resets it to Ready.

Review: GLM 5.3, no findings.

Left before ready: mac-lanes, which starts when the PR is marked ready.

author: cobarx
body:
## What this is

A new skill, `error-reporting`: every error is reported with a unique code, its native cause and
the context to debug it, and every code has a runbook entry. The caller receives only the code and
a request ID; everything else goes in the server's log record.

## What to review

- `skills/error-reporting/SKILL.md`: rules 1 to 9 (45 counted lines, against the limit of 50).
- `skills/error-reporting/references/record.md`: the response, the log record and the registry
  entry, field by field.
- `skills/error-reporting/references/examples.md`: twelve failures of an API request, each with the
  HTTP response the caller receives and the log record the server writes. The payloads are plain
  HTTP and JSON, with no code in any language, formatted with Prettier.
- `skills/error-reporting/references/categories.md`: the failure types (the `TT` in a code) and the
  four reasons.
- `docs/decisions/0041` to `0045`: the name (this skill replaces the planned `error-taxonomy`), the
  code-only response, the code form, classification by the fix, and the standards adopted in part.

A script outside the repository checked the examples against the rules: every code is well formed
and unique, each response agrees with its log record, no response names a reason or a type, and the
status class matches the reason. It fails on a deliberately broken copy. Committing it is part of
#192.

## Choices to confirm

Recorded in the decision records. Two are the draft's own and unconfirmed: the counter has three
digits (the owner's example had two), and the failure-type numbering (01 request, 02 api, 03 net,
04 db, 05 sys, 06 int). The `Error-Code` header name is also the draft's.

## Examples

None yet from an agent. The owner decided that running the skill happens together with the
TypeScript reference implementation, so the before and after pairs (`writing-skills` rules 2 and 6)
and the `skill-review` runs come in that follow-up (#192), not here. The pairs owed, one per kind of
output the skill governs:

- code that catches and wraps an error
- adding a code to the registry with its runbook entry
- the response and the log record for a failure

The `skill-review` checks that need a run (its rules 2 to 6) are blocked until then.

## Not done in this PR

- The TypeScript reference, the agent runs and the committed example checker: #192.
- The runbook entry template and an entry for each example code: #193.
- OpenTelemetry field names for the log record: #194.
- Retargeting the `error-taxonomy` pointer in `platform-correctness`: #195. Until it merges, that
  pointer names a skill that does not exist.
- Programs with no HTTP response: #196.

## Version

`0.29.0` to `0.30.0`: a skill is added, which `skill-versioning` makes a minor bump. The other open
draft PRs that change `plugin.json` propose older numbers and will need rebasing anyway. This PR's
decision records use 0041 to 0045, the next free numbers on main.

body:
**Refactor stack: server.** Based on the body-phase Overpass timeout log fix, https://github.com/panevain/observation/pull/163; merge that first, with a merge commit.

## What and why

Part one of the bundle-service-seams step. The tests follow in
`claude/refactor-server-11b-bundle-service-tests`. The step was split because together the two parts come to
about 874 lines (+853/−21).

`BundleService` held `Arc<Cache>`, `Arc<OverpassClient>` and `Arc<Elevation>`. Its single-flight, refund and
stale-on-error rules could therefore only be reached through real upstreams over sockets. It now holds ports:

- `store: Arc<dyn BundleStore>`: the existing port; `Cache` in production.
- `overpass: Arc<dyn MapDataSource>`: new in `ports.rs`, with `fetch_since(&BBox, tokio::time::Instant)`.
  `OverpassClient` implements it by delegating to its inherent `fetch_since`.
- `elevation: Arc<dyn TerrainSource>`: new in `ports.rs`, with `terrain(&BBox)`. `Elevation` implements it by
  delegating to its inherent `terrain`.

The method bodies of `get`, `flight` and `produce` are unchanged, apart from `self.store.get/put` replacing
`BundleStore::get/put(&*self.cache, ..)`. That covers the spawn inside the `in_flight` lock, the cleanup inside
the task, `.instrument(Span::current())`, every refund point and every metric call site. The region agent stays a
concrete `Option<Arc<Regions>>` until the regions-api step gives it a port.

`testing` (cfg test or feature `testing`) gains `FakeMapData` and `FakeTerrain`, which are one generic
`FakeSource<T>`:
- Replies are taken in order. `gated(reply)` returns a `Gate` with `entered().await` and `open()`.
- `calls()` counts the calls, and `started()` lists the budget start each map data call was given.
- An unscripted call answers `ApiError::Internal` and is counted, because a panic inside a spawned build would be
  lost. `assert_drained()` reports it.

## Checks

- [ ] `mise run check` passes (or the equivalent commands in `mise.toml`)
- [ ] Docs and `CHANGELOG.md` updated if behaviour, configuration or the API changed
- [ ] New environment variables appear in `docs/design.md`

## Review notes

- **Size:** +250 / -21, of which `testing.rs` is +159, including a unit test of the fake.
- **Equivalence:**
  - `git diff` of `bundles.rs` shows only the field types, the constructor parameters and the two store calls.
  - `lib.rs` passes the same `Cache`, `OverpassClient` and `Elevation` instances, now coerced to trait objects.
  - The trait impls are one-line delegations; inherent methods take precedence, so there is no recursion.
  - The existing `tests/api` suite (147 tests, sockets) passes unchanged.
- **Behaviour differences:** none.
- **Cross-stack edits:** none.
- **Independent review:** APPROVE; it compared the production diff of `bundles.rs` line by line, checked the ports and fakes, and ran the server suite (159/159); it had no blocking or should-fix findings; optional notes not taken: moving `OsmData` out of the Overpass module (`ports.rs` imports it from there) and renaming the `overpass` field to `map_data`.

author: inzodious
body:
## What changed

Before: the night's jobs each had their own clock time, ran side by side inside cron's 640 MB, and nothing repeated the evening run after a late deploy. A restart in the middle lost whatever was running, and nobody can press anything on the box tonight.

After: every night the scheduler runs the night's work in order, one heavy job at a time, with no tap.

| Point | Rule |
|---|---|
| Window | Starts 23:30 Eastern, ends 06:30. A scheduler that comes up inside the window carries on where it was |
| One at a time | While it runs, heavy jobs take turns, whatever low-memory mode says |
| First: the evening run again | `mirror`, `engine-daily`, `engine-review`, `engine-discounts`, the Plan keeper, the debrief. Only when a new version went live after 16:00, and then only the jobs that haven't run well on the version that is live now. A quiet night repeats nothing |
| Then: the night jobs | Every job whose `jobs.py` entry has `"overnight": N`, lowest first. Tonight: `agents-run-research` (200, the holdings pass) and `opportunities-night` (210), from their owners' PRs. The job's own schedule line is the fallback and is skipped on a night when the run has done it or is about to |
| A restart mid-step | The step runs again (three times at most). Steps already done stay done |
| A new version | Before 03:00 the night starts again from the top, so a late fix is used. After 03:00 it only carries on |
| Room for a deploy | After each step the run waits for the host's next 5-minute check-in (10 minutes at most), so a waiting deploy takes the gap instead of stopping a job |
| 06:30 | Steps not started are closed as "The night ran out before its turn." A running one finishes |
| 06:45 | One alert on `desk-research`: what is ready, then what didn't finish. It opens the Bridge |
| Today's run | `stages` gains `overnight`; night jobs show under it |
| The app | `GET /api/overnight`: tonight's order before it starts, the steps while it runs, last night's result through the day |

## How

- `desk/overnight.py` (new): the chain, kept in `data/run/overnight/chain.json`, and `build.json` for when the live version came up. Same pattern as Start the desk: the scheduler starts each step's own job and reads its `last_run`.
- `desk/scheduler.py`: jobs carry `overnight`; `launch` and `drain` run heavy jobs one at a time in low-memory mode **or** while the night runs; a schedule line is skipped when tonight's run has the job; the loop advances the night after the Start chain. A job's last line may say `{"ready": "14 holdings analysed"}`, kept on its `last_run`.
- `desk/worker/jobs.py`: `worker-apply` is marked light. It copies a result file without parsing it (Statistics' `stage_file`), so Horizon's answers are applied during a long step instead of waiting behind it.
- `desk/notify/jobs.py`: `notify-morning` at 06:45, light.
- The alert reads counts where they are: each step's `ready` line, plus `ready(cfg)` in `desk.engine.lab.shelf` and `desk.opportunities` when those exist (Statistics' library is not a cron job). It names what did not finish. If nothing is ready it says the run didn't finish instead of saying the desk is ready.

Agreed with the owners (their words, in their threads): the holdings pass and the opportunities job skip what was already written tonight on any version, so a restart from the top repeats no paid model work; the engine steps rerun freely; the Plan keeper and debrief skip when nothing changed. Statistics need no slot: `engine-lab-export` at 00:55 queues the library and offers it in the same run, and they are marking it light.

Limits to know:

| Limit | Detail |
|---|---|
| Old box script | It checks for a running job once, before it builds, and restarts without checking again. A step that starts during a build is stopped by the restart and then run again. Nothing in the app can close that; the gap after each step makes it rare |
| A long step holds a deploy | A fix merged during the holdings pass deploys when the pass ends |
| Queue across a restart | Scheduled jobs that were waiting their turn are dropped by a restart, as in low-memory mode today. Night steps are not |
| Not run on the box | Tested with real subprocesses through the scheduler's own `launch`, `reap` and `drain`, and the real loop was started for a few seconds on an empty data folder. The first real night is tonight |

## Checks run locally

`scripts/check.sh` at 9f75f9e with main c13ab3a merged in:

```
ok    ruff check
ok    ruff format
ok    pytest
ok    shellcheck
ok    secrets scan
ok    compose config
ok    ui lint, test, build
skip  image builds: add --docker
```

- pytest: 1017 passed. New: `tests/infra/test_overnight.py` (16): the window; order after an evening deploy; a quiet night repeats nothing; an evening job already run on the live version is skipped; a failed step doesn't stop the night; a restart reruns the interrupted step and keeps the rest; a new version before 03:00 starts again and after 03:00 only carries on and adds a new job; the gap for the host's check-in; 06:30 closes what hasn't started and lets a running step finish; heavy jobs take turns and a fallback schedule line is skipped; one key joins a job; the `ready` line; the API; the alert's words.
- UI: unchanged. `ui/src/lib/todayRun.js` already titles a stage it doesn't know, so "Overnight" appears in Today's run without a UI change (checked by reading it, not by screenshot).

## Checklist

- [x] `Changelog:` line and delivered roadmap items in this body (Lead writes them into `CHANGELOG.md` and `ROADMAP.md`)
- [x] Only files this workstream owns are changed (see `CLAUDE.md`)
- [x] No personal figures, account numbers or statements

Changelog: The desk now runs its night's work by itself, in order and one heavy job at a time, from 23:30 to 06:30 Eastern; it carries on after a deploy, and one alert at 06:45 says what is ready.

Roadmap: the night's order, the Overnight stage in Today's run, the 06:45 alert (overnight brief, Infrastructure).

author: lakshya-2440
body:
## Problem

The generated C++ DDS service client and action `GetResult` client store in-flight `RmwRequestId` entries in an unbounded `Vec`. When a ROS 2 server drops or never replies, stale entries stay in memory forever, unlike the Zenoh client and service server paths which already enforce `MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS` and `SERVICE_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT`.

## Solution

- Added `PendingDdsRequests<T>` in `dora-ros2-bridge` (`transport::dds`) to cap tracked requests at `MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS` (evicting oldest) and prune expired entries on push/match when a timeout is configured.
- Switched the generated DDS service client to `PendingDdsRequests` with `MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS` (64) and `SERVICE_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT` (30s).
- Switched the generated DDS action `GetResult` client to `PendingDdsRequests` capped at `MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS` (64, with no short timeout so long-running goals still receive results).

## Validation

**Class**: B

- `cargo test -p dora-ros2-bridge-msg-gen`: 112 passed (added `dds_service_client_bounds_pending_requests` and `dds_action_client_bounds_pending_results`)
- `cargo test -p dora-ros2-bridge --lib`: 25 passed (added 3 unit tests in `transport::dds::pending_requests_tests`)
- `AMENT_PREFIX_PATH="$PWD/tests/ros2-cxx-zenoh/ament" cargo check -p dora-node-api-cxx --features ros2-bridge` and `--features ros2-bridge,rmw-zenoh`: passed
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed
- `cargo clippy -p dora-ros2-bridge-msg-gen -- -D warnings`: passed
- `cargo clippy -p dora-ros2-bridge -- -A deprecated -D warnings`: passed (`-A deprecated` for pre-existing `Atomic*::fetch_update` warnings in untouched files)

author: millzach
body:
## What changed

- **Watcher's question can be skipped (#2477).** The card Watcher puts up with `ask_user` now offers the same Skip a watched thread's card has: **Skip question** on the desktop, **Skip** on the iPhone. The card is marked `skippable`, so both clients draw their existing control. No new look and no Swift change.
- **A skip reaches Watcher as news with no answer.** The question becomes `skipped` with no choice. Watcher gets `user-answered` news: "The user skipped your question … on its card and gave no answer. Its card no longer waits on them." It's told not to ask again and to go on without the answer. The news is saved and goes first, the way an answer does.
- **On the desktop, the card gives way to one line:** **You skipped this question.** Needs you stops counting it.
- **A skipped settle question agrees no settle.** It works like Keep watching, and the news tells Watcher not to settle the thread on it.
- **Docs.** ADR-0073 gains a November 11 amendment. `CONTEXT.md` (Watcher's question), `docs/guide.md` and `docs/agent-control.md` say how skipping works. The verification note is [docs/verification/2026-11-11-watcher-question-skip.md](docs/verification/2026-11-11-watcher-question-skip.md).
- **After review** (two-axis, Sol at max reasoning):
  - Main takes only the card's own skip. The card is skippable but its one question is not, so a skip of that question alone is refused (ADR-0135).
  - Answering and skipping now share one step that ends a question.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`: clean. `npx eslint` on the changed files: clean. `npm run notices:verify`: clean. `npm run i18n:extract`: one new message, catalogs committed.
- Targeted vitest only: per Zach's rule, the full suite runs in CI, not here.
  - Changed: `watcherQuestions.test.ts`, `watcherAsks.test.tsx`, `watcherOwnQuestion.test.ts`, `watcherPhone.test.ts`.
  - Unchanged, near the change: `watcherTools`, `watcherOwnTools`, `watcherSettleJudgment`, `hiddenWakeUpInvariants`, `agentRequestCard`, `interfaceCatalogs`, `adrNumbers`, `codeSizeBudget`, `copySites`, `zodSchemaSites`.
  - All passed.
- The integration tests run over the real coordinator:
  - A skip marks the question `skipped` with no choice, and no provider hears it.
  - Watcher's next news says the user skipped and gave no answer.
  - A later choice is refused because the question no longer waits.
  - A skip of the card's one question on its own is refused.
  - On the phone, the card arrives `skippable`, and the skip the iPhone sends is taken as the user's, under the answers grant.
- Ran `npm run build && SOTTO_E2E_EVIDENCE=publish xvfb-run … npx playwright test tests/e2e/watcher.spec.ts -g "own question is a card"` on Linux: 1 passed, dark and light with reduced motion. It's the only journey over this card, and I extended it to check that **Skip question** shows and that the skipped line replaces the card.
  - Checked at 1600×1000, 1280×800 and 820×560: no clipping, and the lowest text contrast is 6.15:1.
  - The captures are in `artifacts/watcher-own-question/own-question-skip-card-*` and `own-question-skipped-*`. #2269's own captures are unchanged.
- No design baselines were regenerated; none cover Watcher's room.
- Hand tests left for Zach, which need his devices or a live Watcher:
  - [ ] On Owl (Windows or Mac), when Watcher asks a question, press **Skip question**. The card gives way to **You skipped this question.**, and Watcher's next reply goes on without asking it again.
  - [ ] On the iPhone, a question from Watcher under Needs you offers **Skip**. Skipping it takes it out of Needs you.

## Out of scope

- The iPhone shows no line after a Watcher question is answered or skipped; the card just leaves Needs you. #2269 left the answered half this way, and fixing it needs new iPhone UI: #2478.

## Known limitation

- The journey seeds Watcher's room, so it proves the card and the line in the built app but not the press through main. The integration tests prove the press.

Closes #2477

author: niteshbalusu11
body:
A customer's backend had no client for the server's REST API. Every integrator would have had to rediscover the hold-token flow, idempotency keys, draft etags, pagination cursors, the problem+json errors and session-token signing. `@cavea/server-sdk` packages those rules once. It is generated from the committed OpenAPI document, so new server routes reach it without hand work.

```ts
import { Cavea, isCaveaError } from "@cavea/server-sdk";

const cavea = new Cavea({ baseUrl: "https://seats.example.com", secretKey: process.env.CAVEA_SECRET_KEY, keyId: process.env.CAVEA_KEY_ID });
const token = await cavea.holdTokens.create({ event: "hamlet" });
await cavea.events.hold("hamlet", { hold_token: token.hold_token, objects: ["Orchestra-C-12"] });
await cavea.events.book("hamlet", { hold_token: token.hold_token, order_ref: "77120" }, { idempotencyKey: "order-77120" }); // retried safely, booked once
for await (const seat of cavea.events.listObjects("hamlet", { status: "booked" })) console.log(seat.label); // every page, every seat once
try { await cavea.events.hold("hamlet", { hold_token: token.hold_token, objects: ["Orchestra-C-12"] }); }
catch (e) { if (!isCaveaError(e, "object_not_free")) throw e; /* e.details.objects names the seats */ }
const session = await cavea.signSessionToken({ sub: "buyer-42", event: "hamlet" }); // for the picker's Cavea-Session (08 §11)
```

## What a backend can do now
Charts (create, draft with its etag, validate, publish, versions, thumbnails, the editing lock), events (create, change, archive, list with filters, counts), seats (hold, release, book, change status, objects by label or page), hold tokens, keys (create, revoke, origins), image uploads, and the operator's workspaces with the admin key. It also signs buyers' session tokens: HS256 with the secret key, which the server verifies against the key's stored SHA-256 (D-34). Node 20.3+ and bun, the platform's `fetch`, no runtime dependencies, an ES module with declarations, `sideEffects: false`. It refuses to run where `window` and `document` exist unless `dangerouslyAllowBrowser` is set. Docs: `docs/05-web-sdk.md` §15, decision D-77.

## How it is generated and checked
- `cargo xtask types` now also writes `packages/server-sdk/src/generated.ts` from `openapi.json`, using the console's generator in `xtask/src/api.rs`, not a code-generation package. It contains the types the SDK's operations reach, plus a table of every operation a secret key or the admin key may call: method, path, credential, whether it takes an `Idempotency-Key`, whether it is a page, and each success status with its media type. The console's generated file is byte-identical. `cargo xtask types --check` and `cargo test -p xtask` fail while the file is stale.
- `cavea.call(operationId, input)` reaches every operation in the table, typed. `src/wrappers.ts` maps each operation to its method and is typed against the table, so a new operation fails `bun run typecheck` until it gets a method or `null`. This worked as intended on rebase: #76's six new routes and its `chart_locked` code broke the type check until they were mapped.
- The build writes `dist/` and fails while `packages/server-sdk/api.md`, the public declarations as one file, is stale (as D-58 does for the renderer).

## Retry and idempotency rules
- Seat commands (hold, release, book, change status, extending and releasing a hold token) always send an `Idempotency-Key`: the caller's (1 to 255 printable ASCII, no space at either end), else a UUID made once per logical call and reused on every retry.
- Retries happen only where a repeat cannot act twice: `GET`, `DELETE` (idempotent by the API), a draft saved over `If-Match: *`, and calls carrying an idempotency key. They are triggered by network failures, timeouts, `429` and `5xx`. Creates, publishes, event changes, hold-token creation and drafts saved over an etag are never retried.
- `Retry-After` is honoured, or the call fails at once when it is longer than `maxRetryAfter`.
- Each attempt has a timeout; an `AbortSignal` covers the whole call, waits included.
- A `2xx` must be a status and media type the document lists. A proxy's login page or an empty `200` is `unexpected`, never a booking that looks done.
- Errors are one `CaveaError`: `code`, `reason`, `details`, `status`, `requestId`, `retryAfter`, `operation`. It never carries the key, the body, the URL (secret routes put hold tokens in paths) or the server's free text, which can quote body values.

## The HTTP fuzz target (TST-027): on `slice/server-sdk-http-fuzz-unreviewed`, not in this PR
Together the two tasks came to about 3,900 lines of my own code, so, as the brief said, this PR carries the SDK only. The fuzz target is pushed, unreviewed, to `slice/server-sdk-http-fuzz-unreviewed` (head `26852e3`, rebased on `main`):
- **Design.** A libFuzzer target `http_api` drives the real router in process, with no socket. Its database is the run's own, created and dropped by the run: the handlers query PostgreSQL directly, so an in-memory server would mean rewriting the HTTP layer (D-78 there). Each input gets two fresh workspaces with the same chart and event keys, then up to 12 requests generated from the document: mostly the right credential, values and bodies taken from the world, with a minority of wrong ones.
- **Property checked on every answer.** No panic and no `5xx`. The status and body agree with the document (the router tests' own check, exposed by a `fuzzing` feature, the server's only seam). No `2xx` without an accepted credential. Nothing of the other workspace appears in an answer.
- **Planted bugs.** Three were planted one at a time and removed. A handler `unwrap` was caught in 239 s. A status the document does not list was caught on the first input. Accepting revoked keys was caught in 30 s.
- **Runs.** 30 minutes clean: 26,657 executions, 14/s, coverage 16,844 → 22,177. 10 minutes clean after rebasing.
- **Release binary.** Unchanged by the seam: `.text` is the same size and both builds have the same symbols. The file is 272 B apart, from constant layout only.
- **Two real findings** (release blockers by 13 §5):
  - A path or query holding U+0000 answered `500`. Fixed on that branch in the server's `Path`/`Query` extractors (`404`, and `400 reason: "query"`), with the input as a regression seed. The server's owner should review this.
  - **Open:** the server accepts a JSON array where the document says a request body is an object, because serde reads struct fields by position: `PATCH /v1/events/{event}` with `[]` answers `200`, and `["e1"]` reads as `{"event":"e1"}`. It is recorded as a known failure with its input in `fuzz/known/`.

## What this work showed about the API description and the server
- `details.reason` values are not enumerated in the document, so the SDK types `reason` as a string.
- The server's problem `message` for a refused body can quote body values (axum's serde text), so the SDK leaves it out of its errors.
- A secret key cannot learn its own id from the API except by listing keys and matching the prefix. Signing session tokens needs the id, so `keyId` is a constructor option.
- Secret-key routes are not rate limited (08 §12), so no SDK call can get a real `429` from `cavea-server`. The end-to-end test makes one with a wrapping `fetch`.
- The two server findings above (fuzz branch).

## Review
`sol-loop` with GPT-6.1 Sol (codex, reasoning effort high): five rounds. The budget of four ran out with the round-4 fixes unreviewed, so I ran one more. Findings, all fixed:
- S1 (P1): an admin key with a newline was printed by the platform's `Headers` error; it is now checked against the server's rule at construction.
- S2 (P2): two fixture checks shared one database.
- S3 (P2): a session token could exceed the server's 1,024 bytes.
- S4 (P2): a non-JSON `2xx` passed as a reply.
- S5 (P2): `Headers` trimmed the spaces at the ends of idempotency keys, so two keys could collide.
- S6 (P2): binary or empty successes

## Summary

A corner radius is kept, set and drawn by one rule each, so the radius dots of step 3 and the panel cannot disagree.

```text
packages/schema/src/style.ts             where each layer type keeps its radius, and only here:
                                         cornerRadiiOf, withCorners (exported now), keepsEachCorner (new)
packages/editor/src/layers/radius.ts     (new, no state) the rule for a new radius: radiiOf, radiiPatch, radiusPatch;
                                         never below 0, to hundredths, null when the layer already has it
packages/editor/src/layer-edits.ts       setRadius(ids, to, corner?): one undo step named `edit`, built on setProps
packages/renderer/src/draw/corners.ts    (new, no CanvasKit) how far a radius draws: drawnRadii, shapePoints, cornerAt;
                                         paths.ts builds every outline from them
apps/web/.../edit-panel/                 the corner fields read radiiOf and set through setRadius;
                                         apps/web/lib/editor/corners.ts and its test are gone
```

```diff
 The polygon's and the star's radius knob
-  stopped at 200 and kept whole numbers
+  has no top and keeps hundredths, as a rectangle's field does; its fill, line and scrub are as they were
+  Home and End move the caret, where they set 0 and 200 (the outline's width field is the same)
```

Move commits, moved lines only: `a8aff2cf` (the corner rules and their three tests from the web app to `layers/radius.ts`), `89942ff5` (a polygon's and a star's corners from `paths.ts` to `draw/corners.ts`), `ad0a26be` (two outline tests to the new `paths.test.ts`), `1539b845` (a field's press-and-move from `number-field.spec.ts` to `tests/e2e/support/fields.ts`).

## Evidence

- **Before and after, the Polygon and Star cards** at 1280 × 760, light and dark, on `main`'s build and on the round's head: 8 of 8 pictures byte for byte the same ([`evidence/feat/619-radius-home`](https://github.com/imkeshav98/dazbee/tree/evidence/feat/619-radius-home/pictures)).
- **The knob in the built app:** typed 250 stores 250 (`main` stored 200); a 30 px scrub from 180 gives 234; typed 12.5 stores 12.5.
- **Every outline is the same,** but for a rectangle's own corners that are scaled down, which are within 0.001 px: in the round, 8,000 outlines (2,000 places, each as a box, a rectangle, a polygon and a star) against `main`'s numbers, 7,043 exact and 957 scaled rectangles within 0.00027 px. The code check's own sweep of 2,000 rectangles against Skia's scaling: at most 0.000244 px, no path different in its verbs. The pixel suites' references did not move (688 tests in the round; two of their fixtures draw such rectangles).
- **Tests that failed before their code:**

| Test | Before |
|---|---|
| `drawnRadii` for one radius, four and a lone corner; the limits of a triangle, a pentagon and a star | `drawnRadii is not a function` |
| `radiusPatch` for a box, a rectangle, a polygon and a star; one corner; four radii; unchanged | the functions missing |
| `setRadius` through the test editor: one step named `edit`, undo, a linked copy kept, an ellipse left alone, a style lock alone and among several | `core.setRadius is not a function` |
| `keepsEachCorner` | `keepsEachCorner is not a function` |
| Browser, rows 39 and 40: 250 typed into the polygon's and the star's radius is kept; a scrub past 200 | on `main`'s build: `cornerRadius` 200, not 250 |
| Four equal radii set as four stay each corner's own | fails with `withCorners` collapsing them (a mutant) |

- **The outlines' kept tests** (`paths.test.ts`, no fixture): 300 seeded rectangles with own corners, `shapePath`'s commands against Skia's own `addRRect` of the unscaled radii (the same verbs, each number within 0.001), and `boxPath`'s four conics against the same. Mutants, one at a time: the scale ×0.99999 fails both sweeps; `boxPath` or `shapePath` with width and height swapped, `boxPath` unscaled and `boxPath`'s corners out of order each fail their sweep; a corner's limit ×0.9999 fails the polygon's and the star's limit tests.
- **Checks on the head, on a PC:** lint and typecheck 16 of 16; renderer 76 tests, editor 1,396, web 346 (349 less the three moved), schema 97; the pixel suites that run on a PC, 60. In the round: all 16 test tasks, and the two panel specs in a browser, 26 of 26 before and after.

The independent code check found D1 to D5 and both invariants kept, and three things to change, all done: the round's 468 KB fixture of 8,000 outline digests is replaced by the tests against Skia above; the code layout's table names `layers/radius`; and the spec's scrub helper was a second copy. `setRadius` on a rectangle, a box, a polygon, a star, an ellipse and a text at once set the four with a radius in one step and left the other two and every linked copy alone.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** corners

A rectangle with its own corners now has them scaled before Skia builds the path, which reaches drawing, hit tests, booleans and every export, by at most 0.00027 px. A square with four equal own corners at or past half its side, at a fractional place, is built as a rounded rectangle with four lines of no length where Skia built an oval: the same points within 0.000122 px. The panel's corner fields write through `setRadius`.

Notes, for the cleanup: `paths.ts` still reads "own corners, else the one radius" itself where `cornerRadiiOf` could; the top bar picks the Corners pop-up by `ownShape === 'rect'` with no box among the selection, so a box and a rectangle together get none, as on `main`; the four radii have four type names across the packages; no kept browser test types 12.5 on a polygon.

author: rowingchenn
body:
Builds on #124, which is merged; the stack (#126) rebased this PR onto `main`, where it
merges without conflicts.

## Summary

`ale vm-image push`, `ale vm-image pull` and the QEMU Provider's resolution of a registry
`vm_image` or Windows `vm_base` move a qcow2 as fixed-size chunk layers of an OCI artifact,
through the OCI distribution API directly, without `docker buildx`, `docker pull` or
`docker cp`, and with no fallback to that path. A Host keeps one copy of a pulled disk:
the uncompressed qcow2, which is also the base of the layers #124 builds on it.

Three commits:

1. `refactor(qemu)`: delete the unused `GUEST_IMAGE` constant, which named a private image
   nothing reads.
2. `feat(images)`: the chunked format, the registry client, parallel and resumable
   transfers.
3. `feat(images)`: one copy per Host. A published disk is uncompressed, and the pulled
   disk is the base of the chain in place.

### Format and integrity

- **Manifest.** An OCI image manifest with `artifactType` `application/vnd.ale.vm-disk.v1`
  and the empty config.
  - Its layers are the qcow2 file in 512 MiB chunks, in order, each compressed alone with
    zstd level 3 as `application/vnd.ale.vm-disk.chunk.v1+zstd`.
  - Each layer's `ale.vm-disk.chunk.digest` annotation is the SHA-256 of its uncompressed
    chunk. The manifest annotations `ale.vm-disk.size` and `ale.vm-disk.chunk-size` give
    the file and chunk sizes.
  - A published disk is a standalone, uncompressed qcow2. `ale vm-image push` refuses a
    backing file (#124's refusal) and compressed clusters, which `qemu-img check` counts.
- **Identity.** A disk is identified by its manifest digest, which must match a
  digest-pinned reference, and its cache entry is named after it.
- **Checks.**
  - Every downloaded chunk is checked against its layer digest (the compressed bytes) and
    its annotation (the decompressed bytes).
  - The assembled file must pass `qemu-img check` and be standalone before it is renamed
    into place.
  - Decompressed output is bounded by the chunk's size; manifest and token responses are
    bounded too.

### One copy per Host

- Each chunk is decompressed straight to its offset in one `.partial` file, and aligned
  64 KiB runs of zeros stay holes. That file is the cache entry, or `<destination>.partial`
  for `ale vm-image pull`, which does not use the cache.
- The pulled disk is recorded as a chain base under its manifest digest (`disk.json`
  beside it). `images.base_layer` uses it as it is, so the framing overlay and Task layers
  back onto `vm-images/<digest>/disk.qcow2`.
- A local `vm_image` or `vm_base` is still copied uncompressed by `base_layer`, since it
  may be compressed and is not ALE's to keep.
- A cached registry disk is re-pulled only through #124's `remove_disk`, which refuses
  while a layer sits on it.
- A digest-pinned disk already in the cache, with its base record, needs no registry.
- `compact.sh` writes the Windows base uncompressed. The Windows README and the spec say
  why.

### Transfers and credentials

- **Pull.** Eight chunks at once. A read that breaks continues with `Range`, and rerunning
  a stopped pull keeps every chunk whose bytes already match its annotation.
- **Push.** Four chunks at once, from temporary files beside the source disk; each upload
  must finish within GHCR's ten minutes. A push uploads only the blobs the repository
  lacks, so a stopped push can be rerun, and it refuses a tag that already exists.
- **Credentials.**
  - Docker's for the registry host: a credential helper (`credHelpers`, `credsStore`) or
    `auths` in `$DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json`. Without them the request is anonymous.
  - A Bearer token is renewed on a 401 (one renewal shared by concurrent requests). It is
    never sent to a redirect target or another host.
  - Plain HTTP is used only for `localhost` and loopback addresses.
- **CLI.** `vm-image push` and `vm-image pull` now exit 3 on failure instead of 0.
- **Dependencies.** `zstandard` is new, and `yarl` is now declared.

## Choices, with data

All numbers are from superserver with Windows base 0.1.2.

**Chunk size.** Measured with ranged reads of the published 0.1.2 layer on GHCR
(read-only, anonymous). Each chunk was one token-authorized request plus its redirect.

| Chunk | Connections | Mbit/s |
|---|---|---|
| whole blob (first 3 GiB) | 1 | 396 |
| 512 MiB | 4 | 791 |
| 1 GiB | 4 | 822 |
| 256 MiB | 8 | 852 |
| 512 MiB | 8 | 862 |
| 1 GiB | 8 | 804 |

Chunk size does not change throughput; parallelism does. I chose 512 MiB (as Tart does)
for uploads: four parallel 512 MiB uploads fit GHCR's ten minutes on about 30 Mbit/s of
uplink, where 1 GiB chunks would need about 56 Mbit/s.

**zstd level.** Two 512 MiB chunks, one core, streaming:

| Level | Ratio | Compress MB/s | Decompress MB/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.9857 | 517 | 2924 |
| 3 | 0.9776 | 431 | 2928 |
| 6 | 0.9772 | 325 | 2904 |
| 9 | 0.9766 | 223 | 2475 |
| 19 | 0.9722 | 4 | 1698 |

Level 3 is in the fastest decompression tier. Level 19 saves 0.5% more but compresses
100× slower.

## Measurements

Every run used a local `registry:3` on NVMe.

**Uncompressed against compressed base**, pushed and pulled with this branch:

| 0.1.2 disk | File | Chunks | On the wire | Push | Pull (8 connections) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| qcow2-compressed, as published | 10.16 GB | 19 | 9.96 GB | 33 s | 24.5 s |
| uncompressed | 17.70 GB | 33 | **9.52 GB** | 52 s | 28.3 s |

Per-chunk zstd compresses better than qcow2's per-cluster zstd, so the uncompressed base is
4.4% smaller on the wire. Locally it pulls slower, since it hashes and writes more bytes.

**Node disk after a pull and two Windows Task builds** (empty: `build.ps1` installs
nothing; office: LibreOffice 26.8.2 MSI plus `numpy pandas matplotlib openpyxl`), through
`prepare_task_image_result`:

| ALE cache | Before: compressed base, copied | After: one copy |
|---|---|---|
| pulled disk (`vm-images`) | 9.46 GiB | 16.47 GiB |
| base copy (`vm-builds`) | 16.49 GiB | none |
| empty Task layer | 0.63 GiB | 0.62 GiB |
| office Task layer | 2.32 GiB | 2.32 GiB |
| **total** | **29.05 GiB** | **19.57 GiB** |
| pull | 24.9 s | 28.9 s |
| empty build | 101 s (includes the base copy) | 68 s |
| office build | 149 s | 150 s |

"Before" is commit 2 on its own; "after" adds commit 3.

**End to end on the stacked branch.**
- `ale run --agent oracle` on a Windows Task whose `vm_base` is
  `localhost:5077/win/base:uncompressed`, from an empty ALE cache, ran pull → Task layer →
  boot → oracle → verify. It got reward 1.0 in 2 min 12 s.
- The RunLock's base material is the manifest digest `sha256:70838f49…`.
- The Task layer's record names that digest as its parent and backs onto the pulled disk.
  `vm-builds` held only the 0.6 GiB layer.

**Against today's path** (compressed 0.1.2):

| | BuildKit gzip layer; `docker pull` + `docker cp` | Chunks |
|---|---|---|
| Publish | 444 s | 33 s |
| Pull, verify, ready disk | 246 s | 22 s (8 connections), 27 s (4), 79 s (1) |
| Disk after the pull | 18.7 GB in Docker + 10.2 GB disk | 10.2 GB |
| Largest layer | 9.97 GB | 0.53 GB |
| Interrupted pull | starts over | killed at 15 s; the rerun kept 9 of 19 chunks |

- Today's pull ran in a fresh Docker 29.9 daemon, because the shared daemon already holds
  the 0.1.2 layer.
- A single-connection pull here is CPU-bound: two SHA-256 passes per byte at 400 MB/s, on a
  CPU without SHA instructions.

**GHCR, read-only.**
- Anonymous token, manifest GET and HEAD (200 and 404), and a blob redirect followed to
  `pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com` without the registry token, with `Range` → 206.
- `ale vm-image pull …vm-windows10-base:0.1.2` reports that it is not an ALE VM disk.
- GHCR documents a 10 GB per-layer limit, but it accepted 0.1.1's 14.7 GB single layer.

## Published: Windows base 0.1.3

`ghcr.io/agentslastexam/vm-windows10-base:0.1.3@sha256:70838f4927a8606c4b3a9d45a809e41b4efad9963b2fa5b7802777af4d71e0af`

- **Content.** The 0.1

Jellyflix 1.8.1: the first round of what the audit of 1.8.0 left for later. One commit; the details are in `CHANGELOG.md` and the plan and status in `docs/PLAN-1.9.md`.

## Tested

- Web: 980 unit tests, lint, type check, build within the size budget (239.2 of 250 kB). Container: 135 tests and the contract check. TV: unit tests and lint.
- Browser tests (Playwright): two full runs had a few failures that did not repeat when run alone; a final run was still going when this was opened.

author: bossee95
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Bossee95"} -->
_Requested by **Bossee** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01C5BK1eJM6NRfRfiXc9zAzKKvKxRZhvid3pjzvGQ29YXY)_

## Summary
Implements GDD §10–13. This PR is stacked on the core framework (#4) and targets its branch, so the diff only shows this work. Retarget it to `main` once #4 merges. The design is in `docs/design/gathering-crafting-territory.md`.

**Gathering (§10)**: `Services/Production/`
- Resource nodes have finite capacity and refill per PD, on a timer during a PD, or never.
- Gathering is a server-timed channel that cancels on range, combat or the PD ending. Yields go into the carried inventory.

**Crafting (§11)**
- Recipes are crafted at stations. A craft checks materials, faction, minimum rank (read only), role permission flag and staff recipe locks.
- Inputs and outputs are applied all or nothing.
- **Crafting grants items only, never kits.** It has no path to ranks, Trials, kits or G abilities.

**Facilities (§12)**: `Services/Territory/`
- One facility type per GDD bullet for each faction, with neutral display names in config.
- Facilities are built on `BuildZone` slots. Members deposit materials and do build work together.
- Facilities take combat damage via `CombatService:RegisterStructure`, and drop to Damaged below 50% health.
- They can be repaired, destroyed, rebuilt on the ruin, or captured. Capture means holding the radius uncontested, with contesting and decay.
- Operational facilities provide crafting stations.

**Territory (§13.1)**
- Owning a territory's anchor facility controls it. By default the change is immediate, and a config flag switches to Loreteam ratification.
- Loreteam rulings can set control and lock a territory against capture.
- Control gates gathering and building, and nothing else.

**Entitlements and challenges (§13.2–13.3)**
- These are staff-only records (`ManageEntitlements`). Players can only view them and file challenges, with limits.
- Confirmed PD death vacates the holder's entitlements and flags them. A capture flags the affected entitlements for review.
- **Nothing is reassigned automatically.** Resolving a challenge as "Transferred" moves the entitlement in the same logged step.

**Staff commands** are registered with `StaffCommandService:RegisterCommand`: `/nodes`, `/node`, `/recipe`, `/facility`, `/territory`, `/ent`, `/challenge`. Every write is permission-checked and written to `AuditLogService`.

**World state** (nodes, recipe locks, facilities, territory, entitlements) persists in its own DataStore, `ProductionWorld_v1`.

**Dependencies** are resolved lazily, and gates fail closed without them: CharacterService and PermadeathService (#4), PDEventService, StaffService, StaffCommandService and AuditLogService (#5, which now has the needed permissions), InventoryService, and CombatService (#2, `RegisterStructure`).

**Also edits** `WorldConfig.Places`, adding the display names for three placeholder territories.

## Not done yet
These are listed in the design doc, §12:
- Facility item storage, which needs faction-owned containers from inventory.
- Spawn points, heal zones and comms are config markers only.
- A real UI. The clients use proximity prompts only.
- Running more than one server at once.

## Test plan
- [x] `lua5.4 tools/run-world-specs.lua`: 41 passed, 0 failed (NodeEngine, CraftingEngine, FacilityEngine, TerritoryEngine, EntitlementEngine)
- [x] Every new `.luau` file parses
- [ ] Studio playtest once #2, #4, #5 and inventory merge:
  - Add parts tagged `ResourceNode` (`NodeType=ScrapPile`), `CraftingStation` (`StationType=Forge`) and `BuildZone` (`ZoneId`, `Territory=NorthRidge`).
  - Start a PD, then gather, craft, and build a facility.
  - Damage the facility and capture it with the other faction.
  - Check `/territory list` and `/ent list review`.

author: blackwolfjm
body:
## VIS-18 — Lección de Riemann interactiva en una sola escena

**Base comprobada:** `main` = `fd50c40be101aa20baf22910f8fc48e85279c74a`, idéntico al commit de auditoría.

### Implementación
- Sustituye los dos bloques `plot2d` del ejemplo de Riemann por **un bloque portable** `calculusviz` con `id: riemann-interactive`, `f: a*x`, `g: x^2`, `samples: 160`. El ID en el Markdown hace que funcione también después de guardar, renombrar y reabrir el archivo.
- `computeRiemannLesson` usa directamente `computeRiemannPartition("a*x","x^2",[0,a],n,"midpoint",{a})`. Reutiliza sus rectángulos y suma para producir la escena y el panel, con referencia matemática **a³/6** y error absoluto separado.
- El SVG reutiliza las capas existentes de polígonos y curvas de `calculusviz`, con los polígonos debajo de ambas curvas en sus colores originales, más dos marcadores de intersección con coordenadas. La escala abarca (2,4).
- Los sliders globales `a` y `n` actualizan simultáneamente la misma escena y los resultados de la lección, incluidos los rectángulos al cambiar `n` aunque la dependencia algebraica no cambie. El muestreo de curvas se controla mediante `samples`, independientemente de `n`; otras gráficas siguen el comportamiento existente.
- La explicación define los cruces (0,0) y (a,a²), el área a³/6, y limita 1/6 explícitamente al caso a=1.

### Pasos de reproducción
1. Abrir la lección Riemann desde Studio; comprobar **una** escena, dos curvas y dos intersecciones.
2. Manteniendo a=1, mover `n=2`: 2 rectángulos, (0,0) y (1,1), referencia 1/6, suma **0,1875**.
3. Cambiar `n=10`: 10 rectángulos, suma **0,1675**, mismo área analítica, error menor.
4. Mantener n=10, fijar `a=2`: 10 rectángulos cubren [0,2], cruce (2,4) dentro de SVG, referencia **4/3** y suma **1,34**.
5. Comprobar que los rectángulos están detrás de las curvas y las intersecciones encima. Confirmar que mover sliders no modifica Markdown.
6. Renombrar a `riemann-guardada.bwjm`, guardar con Ctrl+S, reabrir el archivo descargado y repetir cambios de `a` y `n`.

### Regresiones
- Unitaria: `apps/playground/__tests__/vis18RiemannLesson.test.ts`, verifica datos geométricos, valores, errores y muestreo independiente.
- Navegador: `scripts/vis18-browser.mjs` usa Chromium para comprobar los controles reales, la geometría del SVG, los resultados, la escala, el orden de las capas y la portabilidad del archivo.

### Resultados reales
**Resultados reales del commit `5f20b5a943a9f4884cc3582ba17a4393b44aa6fa`:**
- ✅ `pnpm lint`: aprobado.
- ✅ `pnpm typecheck`: aprobado.
- ✅ `pnpm test`: aprobado, incluidas las pruebas unitarias `vis18RiemannLesson.test.ts` (n=2, n=10, a=1, a=2, valores, errores, cruces y muestras separadas).
- ✅ `pnpm build`: aprobado. [GitHub Actions CI #43136543985](https://github.com/BlackWolfJM/BWJM-WEB-/actions/runs/43136543985).
- ✅ `node scripts/vis18-browser.mjs`: aprobado en Chromium. [GitHub Actions VIS-18 #43136543972](https://github.com/BlackWolfJM/BWJM-WEB-/actions/runs/43136543972). Se validan controles reales `a` y `n`, número de polígonos, cruces matemáticos, suma/área/error, capa SVG con curvas sobre rectángulos, cruce (2,4) dentro del viewport y guardar/reabrir con otro nombre.

**Incidencias durante la validación:** dos primeras ejecuciones de navegador fallaron por selectores auxiliares incorrectos del test (una búsqueda de tarjeta como descendiente de sí misma y un selector SVG que incluía el icono de la cabecera). Se corrigieron sin cambiar el código matemático. Los enlaces anteriores corresponden a la ejecución final exitosa.

author: luosky-bot-pusher
body:
## agent 撞到用量上限时：这个 agent 停派到解除，被打断的那一条留言后转 `pending/human`

Refs #341

开了 `ENABLE_USAGE_LIMIT_PAUSE` 的项目里，worker 撞到包月用量上限后不再悄悄占着名额、也不再让新派出去的会话接着撞。不开这一项时行为和合并前一样（轮询的 GitHub 调用、tmux 调用、`state.json` 与合并基点对拍一致）。

| | 合并前 | 合并后（开关开着） |
|---|---|---|
| 看得出撞上限吗 | 看不出，`poll.log` 只有「active workers 1」 | `poll.log`：「⏸ 用量上限：claude 撞到用量上限（issue #7），暂停派工到 …」；条目上有一条 daemon 留言 |
| 解除前排给这个 agent 的条目 | 名额有空就照派，新会话一开口又撞 | 不派，标签不动、不计派工失败；到点自动恢复。别的 agent 照常 |
| 被打断的那一条 | 一直挂 `doing/agent` 占名额 | 留言（哪个 agent、几点解除、标签改回哪个）→ `pending/human`，名额空出；会话不动 |
| 解除后 | 靠人进会话敲字，或 CLI 自己继续 | 人把标签改回留言里写的触发标签，照常派工、续接登记的原会话 |

⚠️ 合并后本仓库自己不会自动开启：本机配置里没有这一行，daemon 会按现有的「配置缺新功能」机制开一条提示 issue；要开就在本机配置里加 `ENABLE_USAGE_LIMIT_PAUSE="true"`。

⚠️ 已知限制（方案里已列，实现照做）：
- 上限提示只出现在窗格里，会话记录里没有对应标记，所以来源核对是「记录里看不到这句话是模型或工具打出来的」，不是证明。认错的代价：一条条目被留言并转给人（把标签改回即可），这个 agent 暂停到屏上读出的时间（最长 8 天；可按文档命令手动解除）。
- 转人工不停会话：现有的完工回收会在它闲置满宽限后关掉它（后台命令随之结束）；带「到点自动继续」的 claude 可能到点自己接着干。
- 三次写入之间条目被人改了就停手、不撤回，所以条目可能同时挂着 `pending/human` 和 `doing/agent`，继续占一个名额，直到人摘掉 `doing/agent`。文档「要知道的限制」里写了。
- 周上限撞满的屏、CLI 启动就退出时的屏没有真实样本：前者按同一结构匹配但没有实测，后者不处理（照原流程）。真实的 claude / codex 上没有实跑过整条流程：测试用的是放着真实截屏的窗格。

<!-- autopilot-summary:begin -->
<details><summary>背景</summary>

两个 agent 都跑在包月订阅上，有时段用量上限。worker 撞上之后，CLI 停在一条提示上：会话活着、条目还挂 `doing/agent`、名额占着；daemon 认不出这种情况，名额有空时还会继续往这个 agent 上派，新会话一开口又撞一次。本机窗格日志里实际出现过 13 个 claude 会话、11 个 codex 会话撞上限。

</details>
<details><summary>采用的方案</summary>

daemon 每轮看一眼本机派出去、仍挂 `doing/agent` 的会话。窗格最后一块是 CLI 的上限提示、agent 空闲、这条会话的记录里看不到这句话是模型或工具打出来的、连续两轮都没变——四样齐了才认定。认定后做两件事：这个 agent 在提示写的解除时间之前不再派工（整台机器、按 agent 和账号目录记，读不出时间就固定等 1 小时）；被打断的那一条留言后从 `doing/agent` 转 `pending/human`，由人在解除后把标签改回。

关键取舍：
- 维护者在方案阶段定的：被打断的条目交给人，daemon 不往会话里送字、不停进程、不自己续接。
- 转人工的三次写入（留言、加标签、摘标签）每次之前都重读条目、PR、标签事件和本机会话，和认定时整份比对；只允许多出 daemon 自己上一步写的。确认变了就停手且不撤回；读不到就等下一轮；写成功但没收到回应、或写完没记账就退出，下一轮按标签事件的操作人和事先记下的步骤认出来接着做。
- 暂停只按时刻结束或由人删记录解除，不因为「别的会话在忙」提前结束。
- 暂停记录读不出一律当没有暂停，避免整个项目悄悄不派工。

</details>
<details><summary>排除的方案和原因</summary>

- 会话原地等、到点由 daemon 往里送「接着做」：占着并发名额，并发上限为 1 时别的 agent 也接不到活；维护者最后选了交给人。
- daemon 停掉干等的进程、把条目退回触发标签（自己翻或交给现有自愈）：链路长，方案复审连续三轮在「前一步的证据到后一步失效」上找出问题，后台还有任务在跑时也不能停。
- 看到这个 agent 有会话在忙就提前结束暂停：忙是按终端文字判的，证明不了额度恢复，还会被另一个账号的会话误清。
- 转人工中途停手时把 daemon 自己加的 `pending/human` 摘回去：人这时如果已经摘了 `doing/agent`，条目会一个流程标签都不剩。
- 认 CLI 启动就退出时的上限提示：本机没有以这种方式出现的真实样本，不凭印象写匹配。

</details>
<!-- autopilot-summary:end -->

### ⚠️ 和其他进行中条目的重叠

- #339（PR #354）：`scripts/_lib.sh`、`scripts/agent-poll.sh`、`scripts/drivers/_common.sh`、`cavil-loop.config.example`、`scripts/config-notices.txt`、`docs/operations{,.zh}.md`、`docs/architecture{,.zh}.md`、`AGENTS{,.zh}.md`、`tests/ci-weights.txt`、`tests/config-notice.test.sh`。逻辑上：撞上限的条目转 `pending/human` 后不再挂 `doing/agent`，不会进入 #339 的催促阶梯；但认定之前的那一两轮、以及转人工停手后仍挂 `doing/agent` 的条目，#339 的卡住检测仍可能去催。后合并的一方需要让卡住检测跳过「本功能已认出上限」的会话（本 PR 合并时 #339 还没进主干，这里没有可接的代码）。
- #343（PR #384）：`scripts/_lib.sh`、`scripts/_names.sh`、`scripts/agent-poll.sh`、`cavil-loop.config.example`、`scripts/config-notices.txt`、`docs/operations{,.zh}.md`、`AGENTS{,.zh}.md`、`tests/ci-weights.txt`。

<details><summary>改了什么</summary>

- `scripts/usage_limit.py`（新）：屏幕规则（claude / codex 各一段，按结构认）、解除时间解析、会话记录来源核对

author: tejachavali
body:
## Why

`prefixwise.wrap(client)` dropped every streamed call, so an agent that streams (most do) recorded nothing. The README had no picture of what Prefixwise does, and on PyPI an image would have pointed nowhere. The repo root carried a build log and a working note.

No release: these wait for the batched 0.12.0.

## What

- **Streamed calls are recorded** (`src/prefixwise/sdk.py`):
  - **What's covered:** `create(..., stream=True)`, sync and async, on Anthropic `messages` and `beta.messages`, OpenAI Chat Completions and OpenAI Responses. Also the `.stream()` helpers on all of them, recorded once each:
    - OpenAI's helpers call `create`, so their stream is recorded there.
    - Anthropic's are recorded from the final message.
  - **The caller's stream is unchanged.** The caller still gets the SDK's own stream: `isinstance`, `.response`, context managers and `close()` all behave as before. Usage is read from the events as they pass, and the call is recorded once, when the stream ends.
  - **Streams that don't finish:**
    - A stream closed, cancelled, or left inside a `.stream()` block before its end is a failure row (`client_disconnected`), as the proxy records a client that hangs up.
    - One the server or the network breaks, such as an `error` event mid-stream, is `upstream_dropped`.
    - A stream dropped without being closed or read to its end is not recorded: recording from the garbage collector could block on the ledger.
  - **Chat Completions `include_usage`:** when the caller hasn't set it (in `stream_options` or `extra_body`), `wrap` asks for it on a copy and keeps the extra usage-only chunk out of the caller's stream. A server that rejects `stream_options` gets the call as the caller made it, and is not asked again.
  - **Raw responses:** `with_raw_response` and `with_streaming_response` streams are left untouched and unrecorded.
  - **Session:** the session and task are the ones current when the call was made, wherever and whenever the stream is consumed.
- **Streamed responses record the model that answered**, in the proxy too: they used to be priced by the model asked for.
- **README:**
  - CI, PyPI and MIT badges; the architecture diagram, light and dark, in a `<picture>`.
  - The PyPI build rewrites image paths to raw GitHub files, and the `LICENSE` link.
  - Checked by building the wheel and rendering it with `readme_renderer[md]`: no relative links are left.
- **Repo root:**
  - `build.log` untracked and `*.log` ignored.
  - `WORKLOG.md` moved to `docs/WORKLOG.md`, with its links and the pyproject regex updated.
  - Excluded from the sdist.

## Review

Three rounds of independent review. Fixed:
- raw-response calls got the extra usage chunk;
- `stream_options` set through `extra_body` was ignored;
- the OpenAI helpers recorded nothing when left early;
- cancellation was labelled an upstream failure;
- the first fix for the helpers, a hook on the HTTP response's `close`, could deadlock from the garbage collector and kept responses alive. It was replaced by wrapping the helper context managers.

## Tests

- `tests/test_sdk.py` has 26 tests. The new ones fail on the old code. Covered:
  - sync and async, with all three APIs, through `create(stream=True)` and `.stream()`;
  - early close, cancellation, error events;
  - raw responses and `extra_body`;
  - a server that rejects `stream_options`;
  - dropped streams and memory;
  - the session across asyncio tasks and async-generator yields.
- Full suite after merging `main` (#127, #128): 2,555 passed.

author: evan-rawson-software
body:
Docs only. Resolves the two items still marked `OPEN — owner to confirm` after #127: owner decisions 18 and 19 on #124. No `OPEN` marker of this change is left in `docs/`.

## CB-15c / PP-11 (decision 18)

> **A unit attacks whatever enemy is in range, including enemy Cores that are not its target.** Where a unit walks does not change: it heads for its target Core (CB-15b).

It reuses the existing engagement rules: an enemy unit in reach first (rules a, a2); otherwise an enemy Core within reach (rule b), where a non-target Core stands exactly where the target Core stands today; reach is measured edge to edge as before. Rule b now reads "any living enemy Core within reach", not only the target Core. A non-target Core is still not a goal (no field leads to it), still blocks movement, and still costs the breach price in the breach field. The unit's `target` does not change when it attacks one. After the Core falls, rule b stops firing and the unit resumes walking to its own target.

Changed in `docs/specs/03-combat.md` (CB-15, CB-15c), `docs/specs/07-open-questions.md`, and `docs/rules-reference.md` (PP-11 "Other Cores" and "Uses", the "Goals and movement fields" status row and intro, the goal building bullet, the target-selection summary, the status table at the top).

## CB-24a / PP-8 (decision 19)

> **Economy buildings help only their owner.** A player's Overclocker, unit-strength building and similar affect only that player's collectors and units, and the cap applies per player.

The draft already said this; the OPEN markers, the "conservative reading" wording and the "if the owner decides side-wide" alternative are removed, in both specs and in every PP-8 status row of the rules reference.

## Readings I had to choose (not stated by the owner)

1. A unit with an enemy Core in reach stops and attacks it, and does not walk on until it falls (it "holds", as it does for any building it attacks). A unit can therefore stay at a non-target Core indefinitely. A unit does not walk towards a Core it has not yet reached (no aggro for buildings).
2. An enemy unit in contact still takes precedence over a Core in reach (rule a before rule b, unchanged).
3. With several Cores in reach, rule b takes the unit's target Core if it is one of them; otherwise the nearest by `buildingDist2`, ties by the existing target key `(|q - opposite(owner)|, -q)`. This tie-break is the only addition and reuses the existing order.
4. Non-target Cores keep their breach-field cost, so a sealed unit can also breach through one.

## Issues updated

- #133 (units, target Core, fields): scope and acceptance criteria now include rule b for any Core in reach, plus vectors for it. Comment added.
- #137 (economy buildings): "blocked on owner decision" removed, title and dependencies updated. Comment added.
- #132 (several Cores in battle) is not changed: its single-goal stop-gap is removed by #133, which carries the new rule.

author: francescok
body:
Probed at master `8bc7af5e3d`, macOS, Apple clang 21. Follows up #11606 and its review thread https://github.com/matz/spinel/pull/11606#discussion_r4536148503: since #11606, a program's Object method of a name String has (`bytesize`, `length`) breaks the C build of a boxed receiver's call when a program class defines the name too:

```ruby
class Object
  def bytesize = $nb
end
class Foo
  def bytesize = $nf
end
$nb = nil
$nf = nil
xs = ["abc", Foo.new, 5]
xs.each { |x| p x.bytesize }
$nb = 4
$nf = 9
xs.each { |x| p x.bytesize }
```

| | CRuby 4.0 | Spinel before #11606 | Spinel master | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the program above | `3`, `nil`, `nil`, `3`, `9`, `4` | as CRuby | C error: `assigning to 'sp_oint' from incompatible type 'sp_int'` | as CRuby |
| with a Float and nil beside, `r.nil? ? :none : r + 1` | `3`, `nil`, `nil`, `nil`, `nil`, `4`, `10`, `5`, `5`, `5` | as CRuby | C error | as CRuby |
| `module Kernel; def length = $nk; end` over `["abc", Foo.new, 5]` | `3`, `nil`, `nil`, `3`, `7`, `7` | as CRuby | C error | as CRuby |

- The boxed dispatch's String pre-arm (`emit_poly_str_prearm`) re-enters the call as String's and lifts String's plain sp_int into the dispatch's nil-able slot when `node_is_oint` says the arm's answer is plain.
- #11606 made `node_is_oint_asked` (`repr.c`) answer "oint" in every builtin arm whose call name a program's Object method with an oint return has: right for the default arm, whose re-entered call lands on that method (`emit_root_reopen_call`), wrong for the String arm, which runs String's own method. The arm wrote String's sp_int bare into the sp_oint slot.

**Layer: the call plan answers which method a builtin arm's call reaches; the arm context carries the arm's class, and Repr follows the plan.** `cplan_arm_object_target(c, call, cls)` (`call_plan.c`) answers the program's Object method a builtin arm's call reaches: for an arm whose values are instances of builtin class `cls`, the one `cplan_root_reopen` binds, the rule the plan already uses for a call on a builtin value (none where `cls` answers the name ahead of Object, as String does `bytesize`); for an arm of any builtin's value (`cls` NULL), Object's method of the name, exactly the lookup master makes. The arm context gets the class (`ArmCtx.arm_cls`, reset by `view_push_arm`, set to String by the String pre-arm), and `node_is_oint_asked` asks the plan with it in place of its own Object lookup. For every arm but the String pre-arm the question and its answer are master's.

**C diff.** Compiling 723 programs in both load models against master (the 217 of `test/` and `packages/*/test/` that reopen Object, BasicObject or Kernel, the 74 benchmarks, and 432 others near the change): only the new test's C changes (master's does not build). One other program, `packages/openssl/test/openssl_secure_compare.rb`, differs only in the worktree path its package's source path embeds. A builtin arm other than the String pre-arm asks exactly what master asks, and a String pre-arm's answer changes only where a program's Object or Kernel method of the name answers an oint, which no other corpus program has. optcarrot's and the benchmarks' C is unchanged.

**Tests.** `test/boxed_string_arm_object_method_oint.rb` (new): the String arm beside an Object and a program class's `bytesize`, with a Float and nil in the same dispatch and the answers used as numbers, and a Kernel `length`. It fails to build on master and passes here, plain, under `--int-overflow=promote` and under `SPINEL_GC_STRESS=1`, in both load models; `--plan-check`: 0 conflicts. `make infer-test` passes.

Not covered, also on master (and before #11606):
- Under `--int-overflow=promote`, a boxed String or Integer's call of a program Object method raises NoMethodError (`class Object; def foo(x) = x; end; class Foo; end; ["abc", Foo.new, 5, 2.5, nil].each { |x| p x.foo(4) }` prints `4` five times in CRuby and plain Spinel).
- With a program's `String#bytesize` beside the Object and class methods of the name, the String's answer stays nil after the String method's global changes (`3`, `nil`, `nil`, then `3`, `nil`, `nil` where CRuby prints `nil`, `nil`, `nil`, `1`, `nil`, `nil`).
- An Object `ord` or `to_i` beside a program class's: every boxed value answers the Object method's nil (`"a".ord`, `5.ord`, where CRuby gives `97` and `5`); an Object `size`: a boxed Integer answers nil where CRuby gives `8`.

## `make gate` (on this branch merged with current master)

The local `make gate` (this branch merged with the cache base) is running; its `Tests:`, `scale-test` and `gate:` lines will be added here when it finishes.

- [x] New tests have `.expected` files that match CRuby 4.0 run with `--enable-frozen-string-literal`
- [x] Values past 2^31 are marked `# spinel: int64` (the new test has none)
- [x] If optcarrot's generated C changed: callgrind numbers, checksum 59662 (optcarrot's generated C is unchanged: none needed)
- [x] Depends on: none

## Purpose

Purpose: register the sealed Qwen3.8-27B version 4 dev approval in the production registry, with its pins, so that version 4 can be promoted.

## What and why

- `runtimes/templates/APPROVALS.json`: adds `approvals["qwen3.8/qwen3.8-27b/v4"]` with `approval_sha256` `d17dda427fbf9ba6e2b9b03706b4f8a366c627a894cefdbdb8efa664b629167f`, `runtime_id` `qwen38-27b-dflash2-exl3-4.00`, `source_commit` `75031112ba1279b6da97d5604be5160648cc9f2c`, `source_tree` `519678470f283dd5d39281d7d90df8bbc31999e8`, read from the sealed `approval.json` of dev release `approve-qwen38-27b-dflash2-exl3-4.00-4` (published, `approved_by` `am423`). The entry also carries its carried-gate pins (CONTRIBUTING section 2): `binary_sha256` `4fc2cb440b9e668ba07618faabd23c213feb2a28968370950fa98f0b0d165fe5` (the `rexl3-serve` of engine release `engine-v0.1.1-75031112`) and `profiles/qwen38-single-262k/receipt/sha256` `85d85e8f5b84240928b1e938c299e8b62acf99228023e154eb3ba42d16ed1de8`. Every other entry, including `qwen3.8/qwen3.8-27b/v3`, is byte-identical; the file is written in the registry's canonical form (`json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys=True)` plus a newline, which round-trips main's file byte for byte).

## Summary

Go 1.27.4 fixes [GO-2026-6859](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6859) in `net/http`. In Go 1.27.3, a header race in `MaxBytesReader` can crash an HTTP/1 server.
