author: luisgustavolucaslima
body:
## O que muda

Catálogo por unidade (pedido do dono em 12/11/2026). Antes, serviços e produtos eram da conta inteira (só o preço do serviço mudava por unidade), então uma unidade nova já nascia com todos os serviços. Agora cada serviço e produto tem "Disponível em".

- **Banco:**
  - `servico.unidade_ids` e `produto.unidade_ids` (uuid[], com índice GIN).
  - A migração preenche com as unidades de cada conta, então nada muda para quem já usa. O FORCE da RLS sai só durante o preenchimento e volta na mesma transação, como em migrações anteriores.
- **Cadastro:**
  - "Disponível em" nos formulários de Serviços e Produtos (aparece com mais de uma unidade). O item nasce na unidade escolhida no topo, ou em todas, com "Todas as unidades".
  - Na API, sem a lista, vale para as unidades que existem no momento.
- **Telas filtradas pela unidade:** catálogo de serviços, produtos, tabela de preços, nova comanda, itens da comanda, agenda, lista de espera e planos do clube. Em "Todas as unidades", cada item mostra em quais unidades está.
- **Travas na API:**
  - comanda, agenda (o que passa pelo bot e pelo site também) e planos do clube recusam o que não está na unidade (`fora_da_unidade`);
  - o bot, o link de agendamento, os planos sugeridos e a conferência de "falta preço" listam só a unidade.
- **Preço e unidade:** gravar o preço de um serviço numa unidade inclui o serviço nela.
- **Unidade nova:** começa vazia, com "Copiar catálogo de outra unidade" (`POST /unidades/:id/copiar-catalogo`). A cópia traz os serviços com os preços de hoje e os produtos.
- **Outros caminhos de cadastro:** configuração inicial, importação, modelos e seed passam a gravar as unidades.

## Como foi testado

- `apps/api/test/catalogo-unidade.e2e-spec.ts`:
  - serviço e produto só da B recusados na comanda da A;
  - plano da A com serviço da B recusado;
  - preço gravado na A inclui o serviço na A;
  - unidade nova vazia;
  - cópia com serviços, preço e produto, e cópia da própria unidade recusada.
- `apps/web/e2e/cadastros.spec.ts`: serviço criado no Centro já vem marcado só no Centro e não aparece no Jardins.
- Os testes de banco que criam serviço direto passaram a informar a unidade.
- Bateria completa em sequência: lint, typecheck, `test --concurrency=1`, `test:db`, `test:e2e`, build e Playwright (portas 3100 e 3101).

author: trillx
body:
## Problem

With several programming PCs on one shared Library, a job, library part or stock change saved on one PC didn't show on the others until someone pressed Refresh or reopened the window. A job open on PC 2 that PC 1 saved stayed as PC 2 opened it, so PC 2 kept working on an old copy until the save check stopped them.

## What changed

- **The auto-refresh setting** (Settings → Folders, under the Library folder): the original's option, off on a new install, the full reload's period in whole minutes from 1 to 1440, kept on each PC (JX8, JX9). Ticking it starts at 1 minute. Importing a Lantek install takes its period.
- **Lists update by themselves (LB14).** While it's on, the window looks every 5 seconds, and at once when it comes back to the front, at the date and size of the Library's list, its folder trees and its stock. It reads them only when one changed. Whatever changed is read again: the Job Explorer's saved jobs, the Library window, Add product's library parts (only the parts that changed) and the Sheet stock. Once per period everything is read again. The dates are taken before reading, so a save landing during a look shows at the next look. Refreshing only reads: no write lock, no writes, and it never creates a Library.
- **Open jobs someone else saved (LB15).** If the job has no unsaved changes here, it reloads by itself as saved now. The stock isn't touched, and the job holds what their save holds. A note shows "Sam on PROG-2 saved this job at 09:20". If it has unsaved changes, the window asks: **Reload theirs**, **Keep mine** (its next save still asks first) or **Save mine as a copy** (filed next to theirs, takes its own sheets, as LB9).
- **When the job or the Library goes (LB16, gaps under JOB-62).** A job deleted on another PC stays open here with its changes, the window says so once, and Save to library saves it again. A job moved on another PC shows in its new folder; the open job isn't reloaded and its save leaves it there. A Library that can't be reached is reported once in LB11's words. Until it's back, the window looks for it in the background, so a share that's down never freezes the window. When it's back, the lists come back by themselves.
- With the option off, nothing reloads by itself, and Refresh works as before. Agents' `library` and `stock` already read the Library fresh on every call; a test now covers this.
- Rules LB14–LB16 in `app/MECHANICS.md` and `app/mechanics.json`. `FEATURES.md`: JOB-51 moved to Done, and a new JOB-62 row lists what was estimated.

## Merged from spec/44

Nothing new: `spec/44` was still at f7e0f86 (the #49 merge) when checked. #52 (PR #91) hadn't landed. When it does, the list reload in `refreshui.rs` also needs to read the library parts' folder tree, which #52 adds.

Part of #54

## Review

Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with gpt-6.1-sol (xhigh), on the branch merged with spec/44 at b50f2e0.

| ID | Severity | Finding | Done |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | should | A job in front that reloaded by itself went back to the sheet it was on, but its program and overlaps were still worked out for sheet 1, so the program panel showed the first sheet's cuts. | Fixed: the sheet is restored through `select_sheet`, which works them out again. Test `a_job_reloaded_in_front_shows_the_program_of_the_sheet_it_was_on`. |
| S2 | should | A job with no unsaved changes could reload by itself while a "save this part to the library" question about one of its parts (LB9) was still up, so Overwrite or Save mine under a new name then acted on the reloaded part. | Fixed: no open job reloads by itself while a save question about a job or a part waits (LB15); the first look after the answer does it. Test `nothing_reloads_while_a_save_question_waits`. |
| S3 | should → nit | A stock or folder-tree file missing for a moment would read as empty stock or a rebuilt tree. | Declined. Writes replace files by rename, so a file never goes missing while the Library can be reached. A missing tree file checks that the Library can be reached first. What's left is the share dropping between a look's first check and the stock read. That is listed under FEATURES JOB-62. |

Both fixes are small, so no second round.

**Repo:** hotel_social_posts · **Stack:** a follow-up to #182 (deploy messages in Slack), docs only · **Waits on:** nothing.

This rewrites the RUNBOOK's "Deploy messages in Slack" setup steps (`apps/aipostit/docs/RUNBOOK.md`) to match how the webhook was actually set up on 2026-11-11:

- The Slack app is **aipostit-deploys**. It is separate from the alerts' app (aipostitalerts, whose webhooks the platform holds) and from deploybot's: messages show the app's name, and each app can be reinstalled or removed without affecting the others.
- Its only scope is `incoming-webhook`, which Slack adds when the webhook is created.
- The secret is set with `pbpaste | gh secret set …`. `gh secret set`'s own hidden prompt didn't take a paste and kept waiting, so the RUNBOOK says to stop it with Ctrl+C and pipe instead.
- A check step: `gh secret list`, and a `curl` test post that answers `ok`.

ARCHITECTURE needs no change: it already describes the webhook and deploybot.

## What

Adds `MathlibExt/Analysis/Convex/OnlineGradientDescent.lean` (roadmap package **ML-13**):

- `ogdIter`: projected online gradient descent iterates (projected gradient step per round, with an abstract subgradient oracle).

author: charlescnorton
body:
## Change

- `examples/joint_mhd_stable.py`: `MHDStableProblem` poses ConStellaration's `MHDStableQIStellarator` for `vmecpp.joint` at one aspect ratio per run. It adds the two stability limits of that problem to `SimpleToBuildProblem` as constraints: the magnetic well above 0 and the flux compression in regions of bad curvature below 0.9.
- `field_line_geometry` is the part of SIMSOPT's `vmec_fieldlines` that the flux compression takes, in JAX, and `flux_compression` the benchmark's measure. The constraint counts the part of each cell on which the curvature drift is unfavourable, which is continuous where the benchmark's count of whole cells jumps, and `whole_cells` gives the benchmark's value.
- `examples/joint_mercier.py`: `MercierStableProblem` holds `DMerc` of VMEC above a bound on the surfaces between two radii, for the rotating ellipse at a pressure.
- `converged_wout` of `examples/joint_quasi_isodynamic.py` takes the number of surfaces of its cold run.

It contains #1076.

## Evidence

Each run alone on 10 threads of an i9-12900H with exact products, from the near-axis boundary of the benchmark's baseline. The last six columns are those of ConStellaration 0.4.0's forward model at high fidelity, with the score `(1 + L) (20 - A)` of the one boundary.

| Run | Method | Wall | Force evaluations | Gradient scale length | `qi` | Flux compression | Magnetic well | Largest violation | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `joint_mhd_stable.py` | joint | 189 s | 30,129 | 11.64 | 2.9e-4 | 0.891 | +0.0001 | 0 | 126.4 |
| `--nested` | nested | 194 s | 76,984 | 11.61 | 3.9e-4 | 0.888 | +0.0001 | 0.025 | 0 |
| `--mpol 6 --modes 4` | joint | 406 s | 38,555 | 11.50 | 9.9e-5 | 0.891 | +0.0002 | 0 | 125.0 |
| `--mpol 6 --modes 4 --nested` | nested | 286 s | 72,560 | 11.56 | 1.5e-4 | 0.890 | +0.0002 | 0 | 125.6 |
| the result of the third row, `--mpol 6 --modes 4 --length 13` | joint | 245 s | 11,253 | 12.66 | 3.4e-4 | 0.890 | +0.0006 | 0.0097 | 136.6 |
| the result of the third row, `--mpol 8 --modes 4 --length 13` | joint | 500 s | 22,812 | 12.62 | 2.8e-4 | 0.895 | +0.00001 | 0 | 136.2 |

The quasi-isodynamic boundaries that these runs start from have a magnetic well of -0.02 and a flux compression of 0.97.

A front from the boundary of the last row, aspect ratio 8 from it and each higher one from the boundary of the one before, with `--start`, `--mpol 8 --modes 4`, `--aspect` and `--length`, on 8 to 10 threads:

| Aspect ratio | `--length` | Force evaluations | Gradient scale length | `qi` | Largest violation | Longest of the leaderboard up to that aspect ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8, with `--elongation 7.5` | 8.44, then 8.78 | 30,743 | 8.51 | 1.1e-4 | 0 | 7.22 |
| 10, the last row | 13 | 22,812 | 12.62 | 2.8e-4 | 0 | 10.45 |
| 12 | 16.51 | 19,654 | 16.28 | 3.0e-4 | 0 | 14.11 |
| 14 | 20.07 | 14,650 | 19.74 | 3.0e-4 | 0 | 18.48 |
| 16 | 23.61 | 24,535 | 23.24 | 3.3e-4 | 0.0037 | 22.20 |

Together the five score 219.3 in the benchmark's `MHDStableQIStellarator`.

The paper's baseline, ALM-NGOpt, scores 130.0 with boundaries at aspect ratios up to 6, 8, 10 and 12, each from a run of 15 to 24 hours on 96 vCPUs (arXiv:2506.19583, Table 5). The best of the public leaderboard on 2026-11-11 is 237.4, from 1010 boundaries at aspect ratios 6.7 to 20.

`joint_mercier.py`, with the quasisymmetry error by SIMSOPT and `DMerc` on the 41 surfaces between the radii of a cold run on 51 surfaces:

| Pressure on axis | Run | Wall | Force evaluations | Quasisymmetry | Lowest `DMerc` | Surfaces below 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6000 Pa | joint, no constraints | 19.8 s | 15,534 | 6.4e-6 | -24.9 | 41 |
| | nested, `DMerc` above 0 | 26.0 s | 38,911 | 2.7e-5 | +0.031 | 0 |
| | joint, `DMerc` above 0 | 30.3 s | 23,222 | 2.7e-5 | +0.015 | 0 |
| 20000 Pa | joint, no constraints | 18.0 s | 13,305 | 1.8e-5 | -87.3 | 41 |
| | nested, `DMerc` above 0 | 181 s | 578,722 | no step | | |
| | joint, `DMerc` above 0 | 31.1 s | 33,736 | 4.2e-5 | -0.016 | 2 |
| | joint, `DMerc` above 0.05 | 37.6 s | 55,361 | 4.2e-5 | +0.033 | 0 |

On four processors with one OpenMP thread, as the examples job of the CI runs them, `joint_mhd_stable.py` takes 12 minutes and `joint_mercier.py` 4. The two test files take 4.5 minutes, with exact products and with differenced ones.

## Tests

`tests/test_joint_mhd_stable.py`:

- `field_line_geometry` against SIMSOPT's `vmec_fieldlines` on the benchmark's grid, to 1e-10.
- `magnetic_well` and `flux_compression` with whole cells against ConStellaration's values for the same wout, to 1e-5, and against SIMSOPT's `vacuum_well` and the benchmark's formula on SIMSOPT's field lines, to 1e-10.
- The derivative of `flux_compression` against differences, and the parts of the cells of a line against the length on which a linear drift is unfavourable.
- The two constraints of a state against a cold run of its boundary, and their derivatives against central differences of re-converged equilibria.
- A run that raises the magnetic well by 0.01 and lowers the flux compression by 3% within the other limits, checked by a cold run on more modes and surfaces.

`tests/test_joint_mercier.py`: `DMerc` of a state against a cold run and its derivatives against differences; the run without the constraint ends with `DMerc` below 0 on every surface, and the runs of both methods with it end with none.

## Run

```
python examples/joint_mhd_stable.py
python examples/joint_mhd_stable.py --mpol 6 --modes 4 --save a10.npy
python examples/joint_mhd_stable.py --start a10.npy --mpol 6 --modes 4 --length 13
python examples/joint_mhd_stable.py --start a10.npy --mpol 8 --modes 4 --length 13 --save b10.npy
python examples/joint_mhd_stable.py --start b10.npy --mpol 8 --modes 4 --aspect 12 --length 16.51 --save b12.npy
python examples/joint_mhd_stable.py --start b10.npy --mpol 8 --modes 4 --aspect 8 --length 8.44 --elongation 7.5
python examples/joint_mercier.py
python examples/joint_mercier.py --pressure 20000 --mercier 0.05
```

author: plainprogrammer
body:
Closes #257

## What this does

A collector swaps a proxy for real copies from the proxy row's "…" menu on the deck page, which now lists **Use my copy**, **Add a new copy**, **Change proxy count**, then **Remove proxy** (spec 070, on spec 068's proxies).

- **Use my copy** (`/decks/:deck_id/proxies/:proxy_id/replacement`): the free copies of the card (any printing, retired ones included), the proxy's own printing and finish first under "This printing", then "Other printings", each lot a row with its own number field, nothing preselected. The chosen copies move into the zone through `Lot::Move` and the proxy is lowered by the copies used, removed at zero, in one transaction.
- **Add a new copy** (`/decks/:deck_id/proxies/:proxy_id/copy`): the existing Add a copy form with the proxy's printing, finish and zone filled in (the zone read-only); the copy lands in the zone and the proxy is lowered by the same quantity.
- **Free** means in no deck zone, Considering included (`Lot.free`). All or nothing at the 9,999 merge cap. A form posts what it showed (`shown[<lot id>]`, `shown_quantity`), so a second submit of one form (two tabs, a double click) is refused instead of moving twice; a refused page is drawn from a fresh read, so correcting and submitting again works.
- No migration, no export/import/backup change, no ADR: a replacement writes lots and one proxy row, which format version 4 already carries.

## Shared with spec 071 (#255)

`Lot.free` (a chainable scope) and `Lot::MoveIntoZone` (an all-or-nothing move of chosen `[lot, count]` pairs into a zone, through `Lot::Move`, judged under the lock; joins an outer transaction; raises `Refused` with per-lot reasons `:not_free :count :not_saveable :cap`) are the first two commits (`6fc4b8c9`, `22ed55b3`); spec 071 cherry-picks them.

## How it was checked

- Spec approved at Gate A, plan at Gate B, each after two Opus review rounds; implementation review (Mode B) **SPEC-ALIGNED**, ten minor findings all taken (see `verification.md`, which maps every acceptance criterion to its example).
- Suite: 4289 examples, 0 failures: the pre-push full `bin/ci` passed at `eda53399` (RuboCop, YARD, comment ratchet, Brakeman, bundler-audit, importmap audit, RSpec) and GitHub CI is green on the same commit (checks, RSpec 1/4 to 4/4, both images).
- New examples: model specs for `Lot.free`, `Lot::MoveIntoZone`, `Deck::Proxy::UseCopies` and `AddCopy`; request specs for both pages, every 404 and tenancy case; system specs in Firefox and under `rack_test` (no script) at 360, 640 and 1280px in both themes, the refused pages, the touch-floor rules and the focus ring; an export-and-restore round trip. Examples that passed on arrival were mutation-checked and say so in `verification.md`.
- One new CSS rule (the wrap and margins of Add a new copy's read-only Location line); the design-system documents and previews (`UseMyCopy`, `AddProxy`, `DeckPage`, a new `AddNewCopy` pair) and the area docs are updated.

## Screenshots (factory data, placeholder card images)

All shots are in `docs/specs/070-replace-proxy-with-copy/screenshots/` (wide = 1280px, phone = 360px frame, light and dark).

## Notes for the maintainer

- My calls beyond the issue, all accepted at Gate A: the lot row's label adds the price paid when a lot has one; Add a new copy's Quantity starts at 1 with the finish editable and the zone fixed; the new sentences ("Those copies changed…", "This proxy changed…", "Edit this copy first…"); a lot id in the form that isn't the account's free lot counts as "no longer free" (422), a deliberate departure from spec 006's "ignored" for bulk ids.
- `main` moved four times during the work (#319, #321, #322 the deck shape panel, and the merge conflict that came with it, resolved keeping both sides and summing the deck core guard's counts); all merged without a rebase. Spec 070 is patched to 0.4.1 for one sentence (AC-6.2 now names spec 072's app-wide `.c-field select` rule, which replaced spec 068's `.c-decks` rule).
- Seen while capturing, not this PR's: the deck page's `DeckPage.html` previews still draw "Move copies" on rows with no proxy (spec 068 made that cell empty), at 360px the last items of a row menu near the bottom sit behind the tab bar until scrolled, and a short card name can break mid-word in the narrow Card column.
- Not done here (by design): the Distillation log rows say "spec 070's pull request" until the number exists, and the plan's retirement follows the merge (`distill-feature`, state 1).

**Pure move (larger than the usual size by design): nothing but moved code, imports and visibility.**

## What and why

`bundle.rs` (752 lines) held six concerns: the wire format and its codec, address queries on a loaded area, the OSM input types, the tag policy, the build pipeline and the OSM fingerprint. This pure move puts each in its own file. No code changes:

| New file | Contents | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bundle/format.rs` | `BUNDLE_MAGIC`, `BUNDLE_VERSION`, `BUNDLE_CONTENT_TYPE`, `Building`, `AreaBundle`, `BundleError`, `encode`/`decode`/`projection`/`footprints` | bundle.rs |
| `bundle/query.rs` | `address_at`, `building_near`, `owner_of`, `building_address`, `address_pointed_at`, `buildings_at` | bundle.rs |
| `osm/features.rs` | `OsmBuilding`, `OsmRoad`, `OsmAddressPoint` | bundle.rs |
| `osm/tags.rs` | `FOOT_WAYS`, `names_addresses`, `road_width_m` | bundle.rs |
| | `STOREY_M`, `parse_length_m`, `default_height_for`, `infer_heights` | building.rs |
| `osm/build.rs` | `build_bundle` (still eight arguments) | bundle.rs |
| `osm/fingerprint.rs` | `osm_fingerprint`, its road margin and `segment_near` | bundle.rs |
| `road.rs` | `Road` | bundle.rs |

The `AreaBundle` impl block is split in two: the codec half stays in `format.rs` and the queries move to `query.rs`. Each test moves with the code it tests. There are 282 workspace tests before and after.

**Paths.** Every existing public path listed below stays as a plain `pub use`:
- `bundle::{OsmBuilding, OsmRoad, OsmAddressPoint, road_width_m, build_bundle, osm_fingerprint, FOOT_WAYS, Road}`
- `building::{infer_heights, parse_length_m, default_height_for}`
- `building::STOREY_M`

author: maniator
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"maniator"} -->
_Requested by **Naftali** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVeca2nMyie8SiSsA47Ydd?thread=cmsg_01BVeca2nMyie8SiSsA47YddHjUp7LyFn7pvQyZ3y1ZGUX)_

## What & why

Each open pull request that changes the engine docs gets a preview at `docs.verticopolis.com/pr-preview/pr-<number>/`, a comment linking it, and loses it when it closes. The owner asked for previews whenever the generated docs would change, so the trigger covers the docs pages and the site and also the engine's sources (the Rust API reference comes from their doc comments) and `engine-rs/Cargo.toml` (the crate version it shows).

**Stacked on #1958**, which reworks the same workflow and the site config. Retarget to `main` once it merges.

**How it works**

- GitHub Pages takes the whole site in one deploy and has no per-folder deploys, so the live docs and the previews are kept together, built, on a new `docs-pages` branch: the live docs at its root, each preview under `pr-preview/pr-<number>/`. The branch holds one commit, force-pushed with a lease on each change, so builds do not pile up in history. The Pages source stays "GitHub Actions"; no settings change.
- `docs-pages-publish.yml` (reusable) stores one part on that branch, drops previews of pull requests that are no longer open, and deploys the branch tip. Stores retry when another run moved the tip; deploys queue one at a time.
- `engine-docs.yml` builds a pull request under its preview path (`DOCS_BASE` sets Astro's `base`), runs `preview-base.mjs` to move the links written from the site root (hero links, Markdown links, the Rust API reference's header and menu) and mark the pages noindex, and uploads the build. A push to `main` stores the live docs through the same reusable workflow.
- `docs-preview.yml` runs from `main` (`workflow_run`) once the pull request's build passes, takes only the built files, publishes them under that pull request's own path, and keeps one comment per pull request, edited in place. The pull request's code never runs with a write token. Fork pull requests get no preview, since their pages would go out on the project's domain. `pull_request_target: closed` removes the preview.
- The `github-pages` environment deploys from `main` only, so a pull request stacked on another branch that closes still removes its preview from the branch, and the next deploy carries the removal.

Previews start after this lands: the merge push redeploys the live docs, which creates `docs-pages`. Until then a preview run stops with a clear error instead of deploying a site without its root.

## Type of change

- [x] Docs / tooling

## Quality gates

- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [ ] `npm test`: 6,514 of 6,515 pass locally. The one failure is `src/wasmhost/packageHash.test.ts` (the local engine package is older than #1958's Rust sources); this PR changes no Rust or app code.
- [ ] `npm run build`: left to CI; no app source changed

Also checked: a local build at `/pr-preview/pr-12/` with the real `cargo doc` output (463 pages, 17 MB) served from that path in Chromium. Every page loads with no 4xx, and every same-site link on the overview, crate, API and Rust reference pages stays inside the preview. The store script was run against a local bare repository: first-run refusal, live docs first, preview add, idempotent rebuild, closed-PR prune, live docs replaced with previews kept, and removal.

## Versioning

- [x] This PR changes no deployed path (workflows, the docs site's build config and a test); `npm run version:check` passes.

## Complexity

n/a: CI workflows and the docs site build only.

Hot-path record (section 6): no hot-path surface.

## Notes for reviewers

- `/bmad-code-review` ran one lean pass (Blind Hunter and Edge Case Hunter in one pass; no spec, so no Acceptance Auditor). One patch fixed: a per-PR concurrency group on `docs-preview.yml`, so an older build that finishes storing late cannot replace a newer one. One noted: `preview-base.mjs` matches attribute text, so a code example showing `href="/..."` is moved too; that only changes the preview.
- `upload-artifact` skips hidden files, so rustdoc's `.lock` file no longer ships. Nothing reads it.
- `src/dualrun/engine.d.ts` is not on the docs site today, so it is not a trigger.

author: pschleger
body:
Implements #704 (callback scopes), which fixes #702 (a failed joined write must make the owner's transaction rollback-only). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-704-callback-scopes-design.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-08-704-callback-scopes.md`.

## Summary

- **Every joined request runs in a scope.** A callback scope is all-or-nothing: its writes are kept only when it is answered `2xx`. A retryable failure leaves the transaction usable; a non-retryable failure of a joined write makes the enclosing scope rollback-only, and the owner fails with `409 TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK_ONLY` naming the failed code. An `ASYNC_NEW_TX` processor scope absorbs its callbacks' marks.
- **Transaction coordination behind one interface** (`internal/txcoord`): the scope tree, the per-transaction gate with selective admission (siblings of a paused callback get `503 TRANSACTION_BUSY`), the callout fence, the waits, marks, broken transactions and `Seal`. Every owner commit and rollback seals first; the owner's gate is gone. An exit check keeps the gate, the fence and savepoints inside `txcoord`.
- **Both doors** (HTTP middleware, gRPC routing interceptor) classify routes (write / read / outside the transaction), record the answered outcome, and send only the rewritten error when a scope's end rewrites the answer.
- **`TRANSACTION_NODE_UNAVAILABLE` is retryable only with proof that nothing was sent** (HTTP: dial failed and no connection was opened; gRPC: no header reached a transport).
- **Optional SPI capability** (`TransactionCoordinationCapable`, cyoda-go-spi #77/#78/#79): a backend that supplies durable coordination gets location-independent transactions (selection at start-up, owner-less passes and hand-overs). No in-tree backend implements it; it is tested against a test double running the SPI's conformance suite.
- **Backends agree**: savepoints nest as in SQL on memory, SQLite and PostgreSQL; PostgreSQL messages are written outside the transaction; a reclaimed PostgreSQL session reads as not found.

## Breaking

See `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` → `### Breaking`: callback answers that changed (spec section 9 table), a failed joined write dooms the owner, an in-progress callback is discarded and answered `410` when its callout moves on, `TRANSACTION_ROLLBACK_ONLY` and `TRANSACTION_BUSY`, `TRANSACTION_NODE_UNAVAILABLE` retryability. SPI pinned to `main` (pseudo-version; tag at the release cut) — `COMPATIBILITY.md` updated.

## Coverage waivers

Recorded in the plan's "Coverage waivers":
- Later joined read/write on a rollback-only transaction → `409` (both doors): unit-tested on live coordination; end to end the mark cancels the callout first, so the answer is `410`/`404` (pinned by an e2e).
- Superseded scope with a marked descendant: unit-tested; on the in-tree backends nothing holds the scope open between the mark and its end.
- Messages/async search under a supersession; completion failure on PostgreSQL; `TRANSACTION_NODE_UNAVAILABLE` multinode (no node-stop helper) — carried by unit tests.

## Test plan

- [x] `make test` (unit + cross-backend parity) green; full `internal/e2e` green locally
- [x] RED proofs: every new callback-scope e2e fails on the commit before Task 11; the sibling-acknowledged-write race fails on the commit before Task 9
- [x] SPI conformance (savepoint nesting; coordination suite on the test double)
- [ ] CI green on the exact head
- [ ] Whole-branch code review and security audit on the exact head

Cloud parity: `docs/cloud-parity/callback-scopes.md`.

author: sundamunda289-art
body:
## Observed root cause
On Android devices with 2–3 GB RAM, AarisMobileRuntime modifies the **shared** URP pipeline renderScale and QualitySettings.streamingMipmapsMemoryBudget. On scene unload the component unsubscribed events but never restored these global quality settings. Restarting or reloading a level therefore starts from a degraded prior baseline and may progressively lower the recoverable visual ceiling.

## Saved source fix
- Capture the initial mipmap budget and the most recent render scale actually written by this runtime.
- Restore the original render scale and mipmap budget on teardown only when the values still match what this instance last applied; do not clobber later changes from another graphics controller.
- Continue adapting 2–3 GB Android devices exactly as before during the scene. Leave unknown-RAM/high-RAM devices, source TerrainData, meshes, URP asset serialized files and map streaming untouched.
- Extend mobile hotpath regression with ownership and repeated scene lifetime assertions, including an independent controller takeover.

## Safety and validation
- Changes only `AarisMobileRuntime.cs` and `check_mobile_hotpaths.py`. No LFS binary, scene, prefab, asset, token or Codespace worktree edits. Does not overlap open gameplay PR #307 or scene draft PR #334.
- Request existing GitHub Actions `Aaris Mobile Gameplay and Hotpath Regression` on PR; includes C# syntax parsing and Python contracts.
- Static tests are not a native Unity Editor compile or actual Android-device FPS benchmark.

author: wilnergraph92
body:
**Phase 1 du suivi universel**, conçue selon le dossier de conception validé par le CEO le 12/11/2026. **Ne pas fusionner sans son accord écrit.** Fusionner publie le site, mais la base n'est modifiée que lorsque la migration est exécutée à la main dans Supabase, elle aussi sur accord écrit.

## Ce que fait la migration (`outils/supabase-suivi-externe.sql`, 30e de la chaîne)
- **Quatre tables fermées et vides** (RLS sans aucune règle pour les comptes) :
  - `suivis_externes` : un numéro de vendeur, son transporteur et son dernier statut, sans aucune donnée client ;
  - `suivis_externes_evenements` et `suivis_externes_journal` : immuables, sans doublon d'événement ;
  - `fournisseurs_suivi` : 17TRACK et AfterShip, livrés « DISABLED ». Une contrainte refuse d'activer un fournisseur qui n'est pas « VERIFIED ».
- **La colonne vide `prealertes.suivi_externe_id`.**
- **La correspondance des statuts de 17TRACK** vers les 12 statuts du cahier des charges (`statut_suivi_normalise`). Un statut inconnu reste vide, jamais « DELIVERED ».
- **Deux lectures** : `suivi_externe` et `etat_fournisseurs_suivi`, sous `tracking.view`.
- **Deux permissions** : `tracking.view` (employé, gérant, administrateur) et `tracking.manage` (administrateur). Elles sont écrites dans `supabase.sql`, qui fait foi, et recopiées mot pour mot dans `supabase-naissance.sql`, dans la nouvelle migration et dans la copie démo d'`api.js`.

## Ce qui ne change pas
- Aucun appel extérieur, aucune tâche planifiée, aucune page modifiée, aucun coût.
- **Aucun lien avec `colis.statut` ni `colis_historique`** : un « livré » du transporteur ne devient jamais un statut GoShip.
- **Application mobile** : la réponse de `creer_prealerte` a la même forme qu'avant, l'insert direct des anciennes versions fonctionne toujours, et un client ne peut pas remplir la nouvelle colonne.

author: rawnaldclark
body:
Phase 4, app part 2 (plan `addons-phase4.md` §7 steps A4, A6 and A7). Stacked on #882 (`feat/addons-phase4`). Room stays at 80. Draft: do not merge. The builder used no phone; what the lead checked on the Pixel 5, and what is still owed, is at the end.

## What changes for people

- **Settings has an Add-ons page.** It lists where songs come from, in the order Stash asks: your Qobuz account (when one is connected), Tidal, and each add-on. Every add-on says **Official** or **Not made by Stash** with the address it runs on, and has a switch. Tidal has a switch too.
- **You choose the order, once, for playing and for downloading.** Drag a row (or use Move up / Move down). Until you drag, the order is what it is today: your Qobuz, then Tidal. (In #881, which is not released, a download asked add-ons last while a play asked your own add-on first.)
- **A new add-on is asked after Stash's own lossless sources**, so a server Stash doesn't run only sees the songs those don't have. The preview says so; one drag changes it.
- **Add from a link works three ways:** paste it, share it to Stash from another app, or scan a code. Stash reads the add-on and shows its name, the address it runs on, what Stash will use from it and where it lands in the order. Nothing is added before you tap Add.
- **An add-on Stash doesn't run asks first.** A sheet says where it runs, what its server will see and what it never gets. What it will see is what Stash sends: the name, artist, album, length and recording code of each song you play and of the next song in your queue, of each song you save when Stash would take downloads from it, and your internet address. Nothing you type in Search goes to an add-on, and the sheet does not say it does. The add-on's page says the same sentence. It shows once per add-on, and again only if the add-on later wants to see more; until you agree to that, it isn't used.
- **Each add-on has a page:** how it is doing in plain words (Working, Paused for now, Needs a new link, Needs a newer Stash, Wants to see more, Not reachable right now), what Stash uses from it, what it can see, where it is asked, its allowance, Replace link and Remove. Remove always asks first and says that downloaded songs stay.
- **Stash can turn a harmful add-on off on every phone without an app update.** Its row then says so in one fixed sentence, with Remove. A link to it is refused.
- **The Custom Tidal server row is gone.** If you set one, nothing changes: the Tidal row reads "Tidal · your own server" with its address, and its page has "Use Stash's Tidal instead".
- **A refusal is one plain sentence**, such as "That link isn't an add-on." or "Add-ons can't use addresses on your own network." After one, Read link is still there to try again; a refusal that comes from Add is said on the preview, which stays.
- **Switched off means not asked at all.** Tidal switched off is out of both chains (and out of the line each lookup logs), its allowance is not asked for at a start, and the next song is still found ahead from the sources behind it.

## How it works

**A4, one play order** (`PlayOrder`, stored as `play_order` in `lossless_source_preferences`; nothing saved means automatic).
- `StreamSourceRegistry` builds its lossless rungs by walking the order; `LosslessSourceRegistry` sorts its sources by it; `LosslessAvailability.routingRows` lists Lossless sources in it.
- The own-Tidal-server-first rule applies only while the order is automatic. Tidal dragged ahead of Qobuz is asked for FLAC first and for its AAC only after Qobuz misses. A look-ahead still stops at Stash's shared Tidal and at a metered add-on.
- The switches of rows that aren't a user's add-on (Tidal, default add-ons) are stored beside the order. Tidal switched off has no route at all: it never falls through to Stash's relay.
- `priority_order`, which no screen ever wrote, is removed and purged.

**A6, the signed index** (`AddonIndexFetcher`, `AddonIndex`, `SignedIndexAddonCatalog`).
- Fetched from the address the signed config names (`addon_index`), verified with the key that verifies `lossless.json`, checked to be an index (`type` first, so a signed `lossless.json` can never pass as one), capped at 64 KiB, held to a rollback floor, kept across restarts, at most one fetch in 6 hours with `If-None-Match`. It is asked for after every applied config and when Settings › Add-ons opens.
- The reader is the publisher's (#884), rule for rule, and passes its fixtures exactly as they are at `ffd822f6` (32 files, the folder copied byte for byte: the new key, the new signatures and the `valid-unknown-platform` case).
- A platform word this app doesn't know drops out of its entry and never refuses the index, so a later list that says "ios" still delivers its blocks to an older app. An entry left with no platform this app knows is not offered here and not Official here; Official by the index also needs the entry's `min_build`.
- A block whose reason this app doesn't know still blocks, with a sentence that gives no reason.
- Trust is decided only by the signed config and the signed index: first-party, official, not made by Stash, turned off by Stash. A blocked add-on is never published and never asked, not even for its manifest; lifting the block reads it again.
- Found in the audit and fixed here:
  - A cold start has two collectors that can run the first pass, and only one waited for the kept index. In the other order a blocked add-on was published from its kept manifest, and asked, until the index arrived. Every pass waits now, and that wait is a file read (reading the kept index no longer queues behind a fetch in flight). `d8445774`
  - A link shared to Stash can be read within the app's first second: the preview and Add wait for the kept blocklist too. `754e9ba7`

**A7, the screens** (`feature/settings/.../addons/`, `AddonOverview`, `AddonLinks`).
- `AddonOverview` builds the page's rows from the same pieces the chains read (the registry, the play order, the switches, the index), with a pure `build()` the tests call. The screens only pick words, all from string resources.
- `AddonLinks` answers with reasons (`Refusal`), never text. The id, name, what was agreed and when are sealed in the stored entry at Add.
- The registry (`InTreeAddonRegistry`): every pass publishes the kept manifests before it asks anything, reads the add-ons side by side, stamps only the ones that answered, retries the others by itself (15 s, 30 s, 1, 2, 5, 10 minutes), and one entry's failure of any kind costs that entry only. It holds, with the reason on the row: switched off, turned off by Stash, wants to see more, now serves another add-on than the one approved, replaced by one of Stash's own, serves only BitChord.
- Found on the phone and fixed here:
  - At a cold start every add-on's manifest was read twice within a second: the user's list, the config's defaults and the first applied config each start a pass, and the pass for a changed list read everything again. It reads what is due now, like every other pass (an add-on that has not answered in 10 minutes, which a new or re-linked one never has). `cccc558e`
  - "Downloads", the sheet's "and save" and the page's come from one condition (below). `cf2d8068`
  - The list, the page and Add from a link end with space under their last card. `84ff41a3`
- **After Remove** (the lead's question). Remove forgets the add-on's refs, its place in the play order and its pause. Two things named the add-on afterwards. The quality line of a song that is in the queue ("FLAC · addon:…") is the queue item's own text, in memory, and goes when the item does; nothing of it is stored. A stream link the add-on had handed out stayed in the player's cache for up to an hour, and playing the song again fetched it from a host the add-on chose: the cache now serves an add-on's link only while that add-on is on, for Remove, the switch and a block alike. A song already playing plays to its end.

author: cagataykavas
body:
## Engineering value

The paired experiment reports three hypothesis tests (human accuracy, harmful agreement, and beneficial override). Reading the smallest raw p-value as confirmatory evidence inflates the chance of a false positive across that family.

This change:

- applies deterministic Holm-Bonferroni step-down adjustment to the three prespecified randomization tests;
- reports each raw p-value, adjusted p-value, and reject/retain decision;
- exposes a bounded `familywise_alpha` through the existing API;
- validates hypothesis names, p-values, and alpha before producing evidence;
- preserves the original effect estimates and metric-wise bootstrap intervals.

Holm controls family-wise error without requiring independent endpoints and is less conservative than a single Bonferroni threshold.

## Test evidence

- `ruff check .`
- focused `ruff format --check`
- `pytest -q` — **18 passed**
- `python -m compileall -q experiment.py evaluation.py app tests`
- `pip check`
- existing `python experiment.py` demo
- wheel build and isolated installed-wheel import/smoke
- credential-pattern scan and `git diff --check`
- published Git tree exactly matches the reviewed local tree
- [GitHub Actions run 22](https://github.com/cagataykavas/responsible-ai-interaction-lab/actions/runs/43136315715) — quality and container jobs passed

## Limitations

This controls multiplicity only for the three declared endpoints. The bootstrap intervals remain metric-wise rather than simultaneous, randomization p-values are Monte Carlo estimates, and synthetic reviewer responses are not evidence about real human behavior.

## Next step

Pre-register a primary endpoint and minimum detectable effect, then add power diagnostics or simultaneous intervals for experiments that require confirmatory claims.

author: dotcoocoo
body:
## What and why

When VectorCraft has to forget a plug-in's grant (a module that lists no permissions replaced a granted one) but can't remove it from `grants.json`, it stops counting that grant. The set of grants it stopped counting was kept on each `Session`, so a second `Session` attached to the same `Plug-ins` folder in the same process still counted the grant: `plugin.inspect` reported `needsApproval: false`, an install without `grant` was accepted, and loading the folder admitted the formerly approved bytes.

The set is now kept for the process, keyed by the folder and the plug-in id (`crates/engine/src/store.rs`):
- The folder key is the folder's canonical path once the folder exists. For a folder that does not exist yet, the key is the absolute path with `.` and `..` removed by name, with its nearest existing parent replaced by that parent's canonical path. Every path to an existing folder (relative, `..`, a link) gets one key. Before the folder exists, a path whose `..` follows a link, or on Windows a path in other letter case, can get a different key. The key is worked out on each lookup, so those paths get one key once the folder is made, and a link pointed at another folder is matched with where it now leads.
- A successful write of `grants.json` for the id, in any session, makes the grant count again for all of them. A failed removal does not override a write another session made for the id in the meantime; for that check the process keeps the latest write of each of at most 256 folder and id pairs, and a write whose pair has been dropped is not seen, so the grant stays uncounted.
- Attaching another folder no longer clears the set; that folder's grants count as they are, and the first folder's entry still applies when a session comes back to it.
- Another process on the same folder, for example `vectorcraft-cli` beside the app, still reads `grants.json` as it is written. Nothing is signaled to it.

The grant itself still has to match the module's id, SHA-256 and permissions (`grant_covers`). This is VectorCraft's own rule; no public source covers it. It changes existing behavior in one way: attaching a different `Plug-ins` folder to a session no longer forgets the grants that session had stopped counting for the first folder.

`docs/plugins.md` states the process-wide rule, the other-process behavior and the other-folder case, and `docs/target-app-parity.md` gets a progress line.

## How it was tested

New tests in `crates/engine/src/tests/plugins.rs`, each shown failing when the part of the change it covers is undone:
- `an_ignored_stored_grant_is_shared_by_sessions_on_the_same_folder`: session A fails to remove a grant; session B, attached by another spelling of the folder, reports `needsApproval: true`, refuses the install without `grant` and does not load the old module. A session attached later reports `needsApproval: true`. B's grant in another folder counts, and back on the first folder it does not. A successful `store_grant` makes it count again in all three sessions.
- `a_plugin_folder_has_one_key_for_every_path_to_it`: a missing folder spelled with `sub/..` and `./` has the same key before and after it is made.
- `sessions_attached_before_the_folder_exists_share_its_ignored_grants`: two sessions attached by different paths before the folder exists share the ignore after it is made; a write by one session between the other's failed removal and its ignore keeps the grant counting.
- `the_process_keeps_a_bounded_number_of_grant_writes`: 300 no-op writes of unknown ids leave at most 256 kept.
- `a_linked_plugin_folder_uses_the_ignored_grants_of_where_the_link_leads` (Unix): a link redirected to an ignored folder uses that folder's entry.

`a_grant_the_load_cannot_remove_stops_counting_for_the_session` is renamed `..._in_the_process`, and a successful load between its sections makes the unreadable-file section cause its own ignore.

The `#[cfg(windows)]` parts of `a_plugin_folder_has_one_key_for_every_path_to_it` (a `\\?\` path) and `sessions_attached_before_the_folder_exists_share_its_ignored_grants` (other letter case) were not run; the checks below ran on Linux.

Focused checks on the final tree, on `main` at `7f3a046b18`:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p vectorcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check --workspace --tests`
- `cargo test -p vectorcraft-engine --lib` filtered to the new and changed tests and the other grant tests in `tests::plugins`: 13 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo check -p vectorcraft-engine --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- `cargo xtask brands`, `layers` and `assets`
- `cargo xtask ci` runs in this pull request's CI.

The branch merges cleanly with `main` at `7f3a046b18`.

`cargo xtask ci` passed in this pull request's CI run on `45987bc948`: https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/actions/runs/43136317578/job/130925941202

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, brands, layers, wasm).
- [x] No panics in shipped code: no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!` or
      `unimplemented!` outside tests, and no unchecked indexing on data from files, parameters or
      messages. Errors are returned as `Result` and shown to the user
      ([why and how](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/docs/development.md#robustness-vectorcraft-never-crashes)).
- [x] Clean-room: nothing copied from Adobe products or GPL/AGPL code ([AGENTS.md](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/AGENTS.md)).
- [x] Every new asset has a row in `ASSETS.md`.

author: diegopereiran
body:
## Thinking Path

> - OpenAstro Ara is the observatory control app: a .NET daemon on the telescope computer and a Flutter client
> - Every pull request that a user would notice adds a line under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`
> - Parallel pull requests edit the same lines, so the second one to merge gets a conflict. 174 commits touched the file in one month, and the section grew to about 1,140 lines with no shape check
> - AlpacaBridge had the same problem and fixed it in its PR #760 with changelog fragments
> - This pull request adopts that scheme: a pull request adds `changelog.d/<branch-slug>.md`, CI checks it, and only the release step writes `CHANGELOG.md`
> - The benefit is that pull requests merge in any order without changelog conflicts, and the first release (#1119) is one command

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

- Closes #1812: the spec
- Refs #1119: the first release, which will run `--release 0.0.1-ara.1`
- Related: #1810 adds a line under `[Unreleased]`. Whichever merges second moves that line into a fragment

## What Changed

- `scripts/changelog-fragments.py`: new. `--check` validates every fragment and refuses an `## [Unreleased]` section in `CHANGELOG.md`. `--preview` prints the next section. `--release X.Y.Z-ara.N --date D` writes the dated section above the latest release (above the pre-release history for the first one), collapses the previous release into `<details>`, and deletes the fragments. It is a port of AlpacaBridge's script without `--bump`, the `VERSION` file, betas and the Debian changelog
- `changelog.d/unreleased-001…041-*.md`: the old `[Unreleased]` section, split in its original order, word for word
- `CHANGELOG.md`: the `How to update this file` section and `[Unreleased]` are replaced by a pointer to `changelog.d/README.md`. The pre-release history is unchanged
- `changelog.d/README.md`: new. File name rule, body grammar, categories, "Breaking or not", correction rule, commands
- `changelog.d/changelog-fragments.md`: this pull request's own fragment
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a "Changelog fragments" step in the Sanity job
- `scripts/classify-changed-paths.py`: `changelog.d/` is an inert directory and `scripts/changelog-fragments.py` skips the .NET and client jobs, so a fragment-only change classifies like a `CHANGELOG.md`-only change today
- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`: `changelog.d/**` in `paths-ignore`, which mirrors the inert directories (a test checks this)
- Docs: `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` step 6, the pull request template checklist, `claude-review.yml` (fragments have no test surface), `.claude/commands/pr-checker.md`, `.claude/skills/port-driver/SKILL.md`, and `design/PORT_PLAYBOOK.md` (the release steps and §33.7) now name the fragment

## Decision records

- None

## Verification

- Migration: every line of the old `[Unreleased]` section appears in `--preview` of the new fragments the same number of times. Result: `old lines 962 new lines 962 identical multiset: True`. The pre-release history is byte-identical (`diff` of the two tails is empty)
- `python3 scripts/changelog-fragments.py --check`: `changelog fragments OK (42 file(s)).`
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests` (with PyYAML in a virtualenv): `Ran 392 tests`, `OK (skipped=11)`
- `python3 .github/scripts/check-unicode.py`: `Unicode scan OK -- no forbidden characters.`
- RED runs: the classifier case failed before `changelog.d/` was inert (`docs_only: True` against `False`). The first script case failed before the script existed. `test_the_previous_release_is_collapsed` failed on the first port: the collapsed release swallowed the pre-release history below it, which is fixed. The paragraph and dotfile cases failed before their fixes
- Each case below was run with its one-line mutation applied, and each one failed
- Not tested on hardware. No product code changed. Pull request CI covers the .NET and client jobs

Falsified by:
- "CheckTest.test_a_valid_fragment_passes": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:180 check returns 3 on success
- "CheckTest.test_a_bad_file_name_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:127 skip the file name rule
- "CheckTest.test_an_uppercase_branch_slug_gets_the_lowercase_hint": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:130 drop the lowercase hint
- "CheckTest.test_a_version_heading_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:136 skip the heading rule
- "CheckTest.test_an_unknown_category_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:143 skip the category rule
- "CheckTest.test_a_category_with_no_bullet_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:148 skip the empty category rule
- "CheckTest.test_text_before_the_first_category_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:96 drop the stray text problem
- "CheckTest.test_text_before_the_first_bullet_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:110 drop the text before bullet problem
- "CheckTest.test_a_wrapped_bullet_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:104 drop the wrapped bullet problem
- "CheckTest.test_an_unclosed_fence_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:119 skip the unclosed fence rule
- "CheckTest.test_nested_bullets_paragraphs_and_fences_are_accepted": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:103 treat a fence as wrapping
- "CheckTest.test_the_readme_is_not_a_fragment": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:156 count the README as fragment
- "CheckTest.test_an_unreleased_section_in_the_changelog_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:165 skip the undated section rule
- "PreviewTest.test_categories_follow_the_release_order_and_entries_the_file_names": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:213 keep categories in insertion order

- "ReleaseTest.test_the_first_release_goes_above_the_pre_release_history": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:263 insert at end of file
- "ReleaseTest.test_the_previous_release_is_collapsed": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:259 collapse up to end of file
- "ReleaseTest.test_a_version_outside_the_ara_convention_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:238 skip the version rule
- "ReleaseTest.test_a_malformed_date_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:240 skip the date shape rule
- "ReleaseTest.test_an_impossible_date_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:243 skip the real date check
- "ReleaseTest.test_a_version_already_released_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:249 skip the already released check
- "ReleaseTest.test_an_invalid_fragment_stops_the_release": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:286 release despite fragment problems
- "ReleaseTest.test_nothing_to_release_is_refused": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:252 release an empty section
- "CheckTest.test_a_dotfile_is_not_a_fragment": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:156 count a dotfile as fragment
- "PreviewTest.test_a_paragraph_after_a_blank_line_keeps_the_blank_line": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:106 drop a blank before paragraphs
- "ReleaseTest.test_the_third_release_collapses_only_the_second": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:193 skip collapsed release blocks
- "ReleaseTest.test_a_collapsed_release_counts_as_released": scripts/changelog-fragments.py:248 ignore collapsed release headings
- "ClassifyTest.test_a_changelog_fragment_is_prose_like_the_changelog": scripts/classify-changed-paths.py:73 drop changelog.d from INERT_DIRS

## Risks

- Low risk. No product code changes.
- An open pull request that adds a line under `[Unreleased]` conflicts once with this change. The fix is to move the line into its own fragment. If the line merges back without a conflict, `--check` fails in the Sanity job.
- `--release` collapses older releases into `<details>` blocks. The daemon's `/release-notes` endpoint is a placeholder today. When the §33.7 parser is written, it must read sections inside `<details>` and the `] - date` heading form.
- `design/COMMIT-PR-RULES.md:324` still says `[Unreleased]`. It is a dated progress log line, so it is not changed here.

## Purpose

Purpose: register the sealed Qwen3.8-Flash-Next version 3 dev approval in the production registry, with its pins, so that version 3 can be promoted.

## What and why

- `runtimes/templates/APPROVALS.json`: adds `approvals["qwen3.8/qwen3.8-flash-next/v3"]` with `approval_sha256` `bc2371eb5b2e8021b281b6082f89986ea25285b3750ea375b5a3012cd981a8b7`, `runtime_id` `qwen38-flash-next-exl3-3.05`, `source_commit` `75031112ba1279b6da97d5604be5160648cc9f2c`, `source_tree` `519678470f283dd5d39281d7d90df8bbc31999e8`, read from the sealed `approval.json` of dev release `approve-qwen38-flash-next-exl3-3.05-3` (published, `approved_by` `am423`). The entry also carries its carried-gate pins (CONTRIBUTING section 2): `binary_sha256` `4fc2cb440b9e668ba07618faabd23c213feb2a28968370950fa98f0b0d165fe5` (the `rexl3-serve` of engine release `engine-v0.1.1-75031112`) and one receipt digest per profile choice:

  Every other entry, including `qwen3.8/qwen3.8-flash-next/v2`, is byte-identical; the file is written in the registry's canonical form (`json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys=True)` plus a newline, which round-trips main's file byte for byte).

- The folder key follows the dev repository's `MODEL.json` at the source commit (`runtimes/qwen3.8/qwen3.8-flash-next/MODEL.json`, the same runtime id and metadata as production's v2), version 3 from the release tag.

body:
- When more than one attack target is declarable, the line protocol now refuses a declaration of attackers, with a reason, if no CR 508.1b announcement could make it legal. Before, the engine rewound it with no `Request.problem`, and repeating it fell back to the forced declaration. New `Combat.attackCreaturesAllowed` does the judging, and the same path now covers the single-target case. Closes #6291
- CR 508.1b, 508.1c, 508.1d.
- Design: `attackCreaturesAllowed` uses `couldAttack`'s boost. It puts a heavier-than-everything requirement on each chosen creature's announcements and confines `ceilingUnder` to the chosen creatures. Then it checks that the witness holds exactly those creatures and passes `attackProposalAllowed`. The boost appeared three times (`couldAttack`, `declarableBlockers`, and now this), so it is one function, `Requirement.boosted`. Rejected: carrying the engine's refusal into the re-asked `Prompt.DeclareAttackers`. That changes `Prompt`, and a repeat would still be forced. Rejected: brute force over every announcement, which is |targets|^n.
- Verified: suite 29213 -> 29214, all green. Proving test is `ProtocolSpec`'s "CR 508.1b-c with several attack targets, an attack no announcement makes legal is refused…": Bonded Construct and Grizzly Bears into a player who controls Jace Beleren. The lone Construct is refused twice; the pair is asked where each attacks and attacks as announced. It answers by prompt kind, so a mutant run still ends in a declaration. Mutations:
  - guard to `False &&`: reddened its `problems` assertion.
  - `heavier` to `0 *` in `attackCreaturesAllowed`: reddened its `problems` assertion (the pair refused too).
- `ClientSpec`'s "each reader's answer…" attackers case and "all and a range pick options…" attack cases used made-up ids on a board with no defending player. The old guard skipped that board and the line now refuses it, so both run on a real Hill Giant combat with the same assertions.
- Sites read: every caller of `attackProposalAllowed` (now only `attackCreaturesAllowed` and specs); both `heavier` sites `Requirement.boosted` replaced. Behaviour is unchanged for both: `insertWith` of one pair equals `unionWith` of a singleton map.
- Does the rules core case on an effect's identity? No.
- Deferred: refusing CR 508.1b announcements that make legal attackers illegal (Alluring Siren's requirement with Jace Beleren), filed as #6996, related to #6291. GraphQL is unavailable here, so the two are not formally linked.

author: tyler-r-kendrick
body:
## Summary

Stacked on hobo-labs/hobo#1913; until #1913 merges, this diff includes it.

This adds "The Cloudflare experiment" to the ADR-0179 amendment. It shows HoBo can get a valid Cloudflare claim link through Cloudflare's documented REST flow for temporary accounts:

1. The owner types `accept` to agree to Cloudflare's terms.
2. HoBo solves Cloudflare's proof-of-work challenge off the main thread.
3. HoBo creates the temporary account.
4. The claim link is sealed so only `hobo claim open` can show it, once.
5. The temporary API token is destroyed.

With `--experiment-worker`, HoBo also uploads its config-service Worker into that account before handing it over:

- values live in a SQLite-backed Durable Object, so there is no root secret;
- reads use the relay's Vercel OIDC token and writes use GitHub Actions OIDC;
- the first seed uses a single-use bootstrap credential;
- after the claim, the owner writes through Cloudflare Access.

**This is not the relay's store.** The relay keeps deploying to its Vercel project `hobo-ci` and reading from Infisical. The routing gate stays shut by default, and the offer runs only with `--offer cloudflare-temporary` in an interactive terminal. No binding file is written, and the relay's loader, Yard and workflow are unchanged.

## Documentation

- [x] Updated:
  - the ADR-0179 amendment ("The Cloudflare experiment");
  - the design doc;
  - the package READMEs, `CONFIG-SERVICE.md` and `CI.md`;
  - the `hobo-deploy` skill, in both mirrors.
- [x] `docs:freshness` and the docs lint pass.

## Testing

| Package | Result |
|---|---|
| `@hobo/config-service-worker` | 21 tests (the Worker, its module, and a workerd run through Miniflare) and 2 pact tests |
| `@hobo/secret-store-claim` | 32 |
| `@hobo/provider-cloudflare` | 4 new; the existing temporary-account suite passes |
| `@hobo/hobo` | `ci-secret-store` 8 (4 new); 215 tests across the relevant files |

- [x] Two pacts:
  - The relay, the provisioning step and the deploy workflow against the Worker: consumer tests plus provider verification against the real handler.
  - HoBo against Cloudflare's provisioning API: consumer only.
- [x] Pre-commit passed all 20 checks: architecture guard, konsistent, standards, anti-slop, docs, schema and typecheck.

## Changes

- **`@hobo/config-service-worker` (new):**
  - The Worker.
  - Records as protobuf and CUE with fixtures.
  - A client and an in-memory stand-in.
  - A pact verified against the real handler.
  - A workerd suite run through Miniflare.
- **`@hobo/provider-cloudflare`:**
  - `uploadTemporaryAccountWorker`, which uploads with the Durable Object binding and a `new_sqlite_classes` migration.
  - Custody lending, so the upload can borrow the temporary token.
  - `solvePreviewChallengeOffThread`.
- **`@hobo/secret-store-claim`:**
  - The experiment end to end, with routing by name.
  - `finalize` for this kind: Cloudflare documents no claim-status endpoint, so it checks that the Worker still answers after the claim deadline.
  - A consumer pact for the Cloudflare requests.
- **`hobo`:**
  - `hobo ci secret-store --offer <kind> [--experiment-worker]`.
  - The typed `accept` prompt.
  - `finalize` for Cloudflare items.

## Notes / limitations

- **No live calls:** nothing was sent to Cloudflare, Vercel or GitHub.
- **Live checks still needed:**
  - that the temporary token accepts the Durable Object migration on upload;
  - the shape of the workers.dev route response, and how long a new Worker takes to answer;
  - how soon after the deadline an unclaimed account is actually deleted;
  - that a claimed account keeps its workers.dev subdomain.

author: potenlab
body:
## What

QA TC-310 (Ubuntu 24.04): after `nft flush ruleset` as root (a ufw, firewalld or Docker reload can do the same), the AI engine's turns could reach the LAN, the cloud metadata address and the internet until `run/firewall.json` was 10 minutes old, and the person then read "The answer stopped partway" (`internal/crash`). `mycel-ctl status` still said `firewallOk: true`, and Admin › System › Health showed the firewall as passed. The launcher, `mycel-ctl status` and the diagnostics read only the status file. None of them looked at the rules the kernel actually holds.

## How

- **The launcher checks the live rules before every turn** (`native/internal/fwprobe`). It runs as the engine account with no capabilities, so it can't list nftables (and the root unit takes no input from it). Instead it tests what the rules do. Three TCP connections must be refused at once by the table's `reject with tcp reset`: to its own listener on 127.0.0.1 (never the model proxy's port), to 169.254.169.254:80 and to 192.0.2.1:443 (TEST-NET-1). If any of them goes through or hangs, the turn is refused with `firewall_off: …`. A pass is kept for 3 s; a failure is never kept.
- **Faster repair**: the firewall timer (and `supervise`) now re-applies every 30 s instead of 2 min.
- **Plain words**: the server maps `firewall_off` / `firewall_not_loaded` to a new chat error `network_protection_off` in five languages, and never retries it as a crash. Members see: "The server's network protection is off, so the AI can't answer right now. Try again in a minute; if it keeps happening, ask your admin to check Trina's server." The owner is pointed to Admin › System › Health.
- **`mycel-ctl status`** lists `table inet <id>` and runs the same `checkTable` as `firewall apply`. If the table is missing or changed, it reports `firewallOk: false` and `firewallLive: false`, and records the failure in `run/firewall.json`. A good table writes nothing.
- **Admin › System › Health**: the launcher's status report now has `firewall.live` and `firewall.liveProblem`. When `live` is false, the firewall line fails with plain words: the self-hosted wording names the commands to run, the hosted wording says to contact support. A launcher from before this change leaves the fields out, and the file decides as before.
- Not in this PR: a turn that is already running when the table disappears keeps running; the next turn is refused.

Plan: `docs/AGENTS/plan/20261112-0211-firewall-live-check.md`. Decision: `docs/DECISIONS.md` (last section). Changelog: `changes/firewall-live-check.md`.

Version impact: **patch**. Security fix in the Linux launcher, its status and its diagnostics; no API shape, data or migration change.

## Tests

- `go test` for `native/cmd/mycel-ctl` (new `TestStatusChecksTheLiveTable`, fake nft) and `native/internal/...` (new `fwprobe` tests); the Linux-only launcher test `TestFirewallLiveKeepsOnlyAPass` and the `fwprobe` tests also ran as linux/arm64 binaries in the test image.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run check:i18n` (0 issues), `bun run check:docs`.
- Unit tests: `g-linux-diag` (new live-off case, self-hosted and hosted wording), `l18-forget-limits` (new: both engines, no retry, plain words), `web/test/unit/chat-error-words`, `chat-errors-plain`, `i18n-languages`, `g-scripts`, `g-menubar`, `korean-register`, `b-full-disk`.
- Docker Linux attack suite (`tests/linux`, real bwrap + nftables + cgroups): new case where root flushes the ruleset while the status file is still fresh. The next turn is refused with `firewall_off`, the launcher reports `live: false`, and after re-applying, turns run and `live` is true. 47/48 checks pass. The one failure is the bundled unit-test check: `proxy-credentials.test.ts` S-4/S-6, which also fail when that file runs on its own in the image. They pass when run alone with `-t S-6` and pass on macOS. That file uses a simulated launcher and touches nothing changed here.

author: jatmn
body:
Fixes #554.

## Problem

On **Known spam**, a bot owner who adds a sample or URL pattern with **Applies to: Global** gets a successful save, but the page stays dirty. After that, every in-app navigation asks "Discard unsaved changes?" and every reload or close triggers `beforeunload`, even though nothing is left to save. A failed add was reported only through a toast that disappears after 5 seconds. That fits the reported symptom: "save never happens", plus a leave prompt.

## Root cause

The **Add sample** and **Add URL pattern** buttons pass explicit `savedFields` so that adding one entry keeps the other unsaved entry. That list left out `known-spam:scope`. `captureDrafts` therefore kept the scope draft, and after `reloadAfter` → `renderTab`, `handleEvent` → `retainDrafts` restored `{ "known-spam:scope": "global" }` and set `edits: "dirty"`. "This server" is the select's default, so it creates no draft, which is why only the Global case reproduces. The template and Badwords scope selects are not affected: their buttons pass no `savedFields`, so their whole draft group is captured out.

## Change

- `frontend/app.js`: add `known-spam:scope` to both Known spam buttons' `savedFields`. The other unsaved entry (sample vs URL) is still kept as a draft.
- `frontend/app.js`: once the server acknowledges an add, the scope just used becomes the "Applies to" select's baseline. It's stored in `ui.draftBaselines`, which `useDraftControl` reads before `defaultValue`. It's set right after the POST resolves, so it holds even if the config refresh then fails. It's cleared everywhere drafts are cleared (navigate, server switch, membership change). As on `main`, Global stays selected for consecutive adds during one visit to the page, but now without an unsaved draft, and leaving the page resets it to "This server". No other control sets a baseline, so other pages are unchanged.
- `frontend/app.js`: when an add isn't confirmed, show the reason inline beside the button that failed (`role="alert"`), in addition to the existing toast. The reason is stored on the failed draft, so it stays with that unsaved entry through remounts and the other entry's add, and goes away when the entry is edited, saved or cleared. The text is "<Sample|URL pattern> not confirmed as added: <reason>". The browser can't tell a rejection from a `save_unknown`, pending or timed-out save that may have committed, so the text doesn't claim either outcome. If the click was a lookup-only retry (`x-jmodguard-save-lookup: 1`), the message adds: "Retrying the same entry, note and scope only looks up the earlier request; no new save was sent." `submitSave` only tags the thrown error in lookup mode; its save and lookup behavior is unchanged.
- `scripts/frontend-state-test.mjs`: three regressions.
  - A Global sample add, then a URL add without reselecting Global. The first add keeps only the unsaved URL draft and leaves Global selected. The second add posts `global`, and `isDirty()` is false afterwards. Leaving the page and coming back resets the scope to "This server".
  - An acknowledged Global add whose `/config` refresh fails: after Retry, Global is still selected, there's no inline alert, and the page is clean.
  - A failed add: a 400 rejection, then a lookup retry answered with `save_unknown` (confirm declined), then a lookup retry where `fetch` rejects. Each shows the exact inline text, and none says "checked" or "did not complete". A successful URL add afterwards keeps the sample warning and draft. Editing the sample clears the warning.

Not included: fix direction 2 from the issue (a `config_patch` from `add_known_spam`). The full `/config` reload already shows the new row.

## Validation

Head `27d3865` (second review follow-up, on top of `84beecf` and `0d3347d`):

- Each review round's regressions failed at their intended assertions on the previous head. On `main`: a stale scope draft, and no inline alert. On `0d3347d`: the scope reset and the old wording. On `84beecf`: Global outliving the page, the scope lost when the refresh fails, and the sample warning wiped by the URL add. They pass now: `node --test --test-name-pattern='known spam' scripts/frontend-state-test.mjs` is 6/6.
- On the final tree, `bash scripts/ci-preflight.sh --only frontend --only contracts` exited 0:
  - frontend-state 297/297, contrast 3/3, warmup 13/13, package-webui 3/3, administration 40/40
  - ESLint web selftest and `npm audit --audit-level=high` passed
  - contracts scripts passed
- `git diff --check` is clean.

Limitations:

- The `api` and `supply-chain` groups that `select-checks` picks were not run locally. No Rust code or manifests changed, and CI runs them.
- The tests use the existing jsdom/Node VM harness with mocked `fetch`. They don't prove behavior in a real browser or against a live API and bot.
- Hypotheses H2 and H3 in the issue (production diagnosis) were not confirmed against prod.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Keep Known spam additions clean after Global saves and make unconfirmed add failures visible beside the affected entry.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent Known spam pages from retaining a dirty Global scope after successful adds, including when the configuration refresh fails.
- Keep Global selected for consecutive Known spam additions while resetting it when leaving the page.
- Show persistent inline explanations when Known spam additions are not confirmed, including lookup-only retry context.

Enhancements:
- Retain add failure messages with their corresponding drafts and clear them when the draft is edited, saved, or removed.

Tests:
- Add regression coverage for Global-scope draft handling, refresh failures, persistent add errors, and lookup retries.

body:
## Why

- `PUT /collections/:id {"auth":{"mode":"Inherit"}}` (also `Bearer`, ` inherit`, a non-string mode) answered 200 and stored the row. The composer treated it as a concrete credential that stops the inherit walk, and `parse_auth` then sent the request with no credential.

Closes #3464

## What changed and why this way

- **Plan.** Root cause: modes match by exact lowercase string and no write path checked membership. Fix: a new `reject_unknown_auth_mode` (beside `reject_blank_name`) answers 400 naming `auth.mode`, called from the collection and request create/update cores. The shared appliers are untouched, so `/import/apply` and `/specs/sync` do not fail atomically. Rejected: validating inside `apply_*` fields, which would break imports.
- The closed set moves to `auth_resolver.hpp` (`AUTH_MODES`, `is_known_auth_mode`) and `vayu_extensions.cpp` reads it instead of its private identical copy, so the write routes and the extension reader cannot drift. It is the app's `AuthMode`, including the stored-but-unexecuted modes (digest, ntlm, ...) so editing imported requests still works.
- No app change: the only outside consumer of the list is the app's `AuthMode` type, which already matches.

## Review guide

**Look closely at:**
- `routes.hpp` `reject_unknown_auth_mode`: it also refuses an `auth` object with no `mode` (`{}`, `{"token":"t"}`), which the issue does not name literally; the credential fields would otherwise go nowhere. No app or engine caller sends a mode-less block.
- Collections keep refusing `inherit` (#3445, runs after this check); `inherit` stays valid for requests.

**Safe to skim:**
- Docs (`api-reference.md` "Auth modes" section, `engine/CLAUDE.md` note).
- `request_body_depth_test.cpp`: its at-bound fixture gained `"mode":"none"`; the depth under test is unchanged.

## How it was verified

- `ctest --preset linux-dev`: 7141 of 7141 passed. 12 new tests: POST and PUT per resource over nine bad blocks (`Inherit`, `Bearer`, ` inherit`, `""`, numeric, null, array, missing mode, `{}`) asserting 400 naming `auth.mode` and nothing stored; valid modes and `null` still store; three `AuthModes` tests pin the set.
- Mutation checks, each reverted: check body made a no-op (4 fail), call removed from the request cores only (2 fail, collection tests stay green).
- clang-format clean; pre-push clang-tidy ran on the push.
- Review: I read the full diff myself; I did not run the separate acceptance-criteria and conventions reviewer agents this run.

## Docs and follow-ups

- Updated: `docs/engine/api-reference.md`, `engine/CLAUDE.md`.
- None filed.

## Visual changes

No user-visible change.

## Objetivo

Closes #10

Criar o pipeline de integracao continua e o primeiro deploy automatizado da aplicacao web no GitHub Pages.

## Implementacao

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (push em `main` e pull requests)

- `setup-dotnet` lendo `global.json`.
- Cache de NuGet com chave por `packages.lock.json`.
- `restore --locked-mode`, `build -c Release`, `test` com logger TRX e `format --verify-no-changes`.
- Resultados de teste como artefato, mesmo em falha.
- `concurrency` cancelando execucoes antigas do mesmo ref; permissao apenas `contents: read`.

`.github/workflows/deploy-web.yml` (push em `main` que afete `src/**` ou build)

- `publish` com `BaseHref=/GISORA/` para o caminho do Pages.
- `404.html` copiado de `index.html` (fallback SPA).
- `actions/configure-pages`, `upload-pages-artifact` e `deploy-pages`.
- Permissoes minimas (`pages: write`, `id-token: write`), ambiente `github-pages` e URL no resumo do job.

Lock de dependencias

- `RestorePackagesWithLockFile` habilitado; 17 `packages.lock.json` versionados.

## Decisoes

- `--locked-mode` no CI: alteracao de dependencia exige atualizar lock e revisar no PR.
- Deploy condicionado a caminhos de build: mudanca apenas em `docs/` nao republica a aplicacao.
- Pages habilitado via API com `build_type=workflow`, sem branch `gh-pages` (artefato direto).
- Sem segredo em texto claro: apenas `GITHUB_TOKEN` com escopo minimo.

## Testes executados

- [x] `dotnet restore --locked-mode` — sucesso.
- [x] `dotnet build -c Release` — 0 avisos, 0 erros.
- [x] `dotnet test -c Release` — **170 aprovados**, 0 falhas.
- [x] `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` — exit 0.
- [x] GitHub Pages habilitado (`build_type: workflow`, html_url `https://celinhodaltro.github.io/GISORA/`).

## Criterios de aceite atendidos

- [x] CI roda build, testes (unitarios + arquiteturais) e formatacao.
- [x] Falha de teste quebra o job.
- [x] Testes publicados como artefato.
- [x] Deploy publica a SPA com `base href` e fallback corretos.
- [x] Deploy nao executa em pull request.
- [x] Lock files versionados e restore em `--locked-mode`.

## Limitacoes conhecidas

- A primeira execucao real dos workflows ocorre no merge deste PR; correcoes de ambiente, se necessarias, entram como novo commit/PR.
- Sem assinatura de artefatos Android/iOS nesta fase (Fase 5), por ausencia de certificados.

body:
Why
===
Duo Lab's Arrangement screen gave each Options submenu two names, its opener's and its choices' (`-content-scroll` and `-scroll`, `-title-display` and `-title`, `-bar-minimization` and `-minimize`). Its root restated the `display` and `flex-direction` that `column` sets, and its pane container the `display`. Nothing in the route hook said why More's bar keeps UIKit's large-title setting. The diary placed the platform insets' gutter inside the padding box, led the nil entry with one option where any option change showed it, said the hook leaves More's bar alone where it cannot reach it, and kept its Checkpoints as a test log, where `docs/diary.md` asks for one line per step. The diary and a QUEUE line also blamed the `arrangement-pane` hatch for a `contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior` change the development log no longer reports.

How
===
Each submenu has one name, which its opener's and its choices' testIds share, and the two `column`s say only what differs from `column`. The hook's comment says that under More `route.navigation` is nil, since More's stack is UIKit's. The diary places the gutter below the padding box, says any option change showed the nil, adds the overflow menu the agent cannot open from the second screen on, moves More's bar from Checkpoints to Rough, says what would have helped where something would, and lists its checkpoints as steps that point at their Rough entries. The QUEUE line and the diary keep the gesture recognizers the development log still blames on the hatch.

Test Plan
===
On an open iPhone Duo simulator (iOS 27.1) with `bun scripts/agent.mjs ios --chrome platform --touch platform --timing platform`, the Options menus answer to their one name each: Content Scroll View Secondary hands the bar to the secondary pane (a secondary drag minimizes it, a primary drag does not), Bar Minimization Never keeps the bar, Title Display Large shows a large title, and Overlay and Split Automatic lay the panes out. Opened at `/arrangement/3` from the first screen, Next pushes Arrangement 4 and two Backs return through 3 to the first screen, with Exact drawing the header. The development log of the Options drive blames the `arrangement-pane` hatch for eight gesture recognizers and reports no `contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior` change. `git grep` finds no other use of the renamed testIds. The six checks pass: `cargo build --all-targets --keep-going`, `cargo test --tests --no-fail-fast`, which compiles and runs Duo Lab's Contract, `cargo clippy --all-targets --keep-going -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `bun scripts/caps.mjs`, `bun scripts/boot.mjs` and `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --keep-going`.
