## Summary

Before: 16 table components on the chat screen (`/app/chat`) failed design-system certification on states, tests and a11y: UnifiedTable and its skeleton, the virtualized, grouped and loading bodies, rows, cells, group headers, the empty state, the context menu, the action bar and page toolbar, and the column-priority and snap-motion helpers.

## DEV-only next step after merged PR #109

This PR corrects three isolated-prototype engineering mismatches identified by the previous integration-readiness audit, **without** changing the live applicant questionnaire.

### Fixes
- **Canonical answer state:** answered multi-choice and compound candidates now use `values` and `fields` without `answerState`; explicit legacy `yes/no` state is rejected on those types. Planned-only climbing/diving branches open from state-free selections, including nested detail branches.
- **Unknown/declined:** do not turn uncertain/declined into No. Stale field, detail or option content alongside those states is rejected in the synthetic validator. Missing content stays incomplete; no applicant values are emitted in reports.
- **Field limits:** import the server's shared 500-character compound-field and 4000-character answer/detail limits. Assert exact boundary acceptance/rejection in synthetic tests.
- **Fail-closed integration audit:** remove only the three now-resolved *DEV engineering* blocker labels; enforce corrected parity dynamically while retaining nine unresolved **release blockers** and unchanged human approval gates.
- Update the offline CI check and add a current DEV parity decision document.

### Safety
Changed files are confined to `scripts/`, `docs/`, and the isolated GitHub DEV workflow. **No** `src/`, `supabase/`, questionnaire version, active 92-row bank, Production, Vercel, Upstash Free, Tiger, external carrier API, database credentials, or real applicant data.

author: patch-ops-llc
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
Plan piece V0. It changes no rule and adds no order: it makes room for the on-screen pieces (the research grid, resources and supply, attack orders with health bars, and later structures and the fog) so that each can be its own pull request.

It needed [pull request 20](https://github.com/patch-ops-llc/empire-earth-4/pull/20) on `main`, and is based on `main` alone. It touches `game/` outside `game/data/`, plus `README.md` and `docs/testers.md`.

[A match alone: the top bar, the selection and the order mark](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-a159082a-c383-56f0-8063-a99f0c48cb0d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fsolo-match.png)

[solo-match.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-a159082a-c383-56f0-8063-a99f0c48cb0d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fsolo-match.mp4)

## Playing alone

The menu's first button, Play alone, starts a match on this machine with no network in it: no port is opened, nothing is sent, and no second copy is needed, so the system has no firewall question to ask. It was in #20 already; this pull request checks it (the game process holds no UDP or TCP socket during a match alone), says so in `docs/testers.md`, and adds `--alone` after `--` to start one from the command line.

## What is new

| What | Where | What a later piece adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The frame of the interface: a top bar, a bottom panel for the selection and its commands, a place for one full-screen panel, a message line | `game/ui/InterfaceFrame.cs`, `InterfacePart.cs`, `FramePanel.cs`, `SelectionCommand.cs` | An `InterfacePart` of its own |
| Layers in the world. `WorldView` keeps drawing units and calls every layer after every tick and in every frame | `game/scripts/WorldLayer.cs` | A `WorldLayer` of its own |
| One answer to "what is under the pointer": a unit of the player's, an enemy unit, a deposit, a structure, or the ground | `game/ui/UnderPointer.cs` | A `PointerPicker` for its kind of thing |
| One table that turns the selection, that answer and a modifier into a command | `game/ui/OrderTable.cs` | An `OrderRow` |
| The smoke test's script as parts that run one after another, each counting its own ticks | `game/scripts/SmokePart.cs`, the list in `SmokeTest.cs` | A `SmokePart` |
| The match as every part of the view gets it | `game/scripts/MatchView.cs` | Nothing |
| The pieces, a folder each, and the list that names them | `game/pieces/` | A folder and one line |

What was there is now built on this: the rings under the selection and the order mark are layers, the move order is a row of the table, the unit under the pointer comes from a picker, the line about the match and its Leave button is a part in the top bar, and the smoke test's four move orders are a part of the script. `UnitControl` only takes the clicks.

The order mark now stays at the point the player ordered. It used to jump to the destination of the first selected unit that walked, which is one unit's destination and from M12 not the group's.

## How three pieces stay out of each other's way

A piece adds files in a folder of its own and one line in each of three shared files: `game/pieces/ViewPieces.cs`, the list in `game/scripts/SmokeTest.cs`, and the input map in `game/project.godot` when it reads a key. In each of the three, every piece of the plan (11v, 13v, 14v, 15v, 17v) has a comment line of its own, and a piece adds directly under its line. Two pieces therefore never add at the same place.

Tried with three stand-in pieces on throwaway branches, not in this pull request: a resource readout with a deposit, its picker and a work order; a full-screen grid of six tracks by nine tiers with a key and a message; health bars, an attack row for enemy units, an attack-move row on a held modifier and a Stop command with a key. The three branches merged in four different orders without a conflict and to the same tree, built with warnings as errors, passed the smoke test with their three parts added, and worked in a window.

Not covered: `README.md` and `docs/testers.md`. Two pieces that both add a row at the end of the controls table will still conflict there.

## Two gaps the research grid found, fixed in two commits

The research grid (`cursor/m14-research-grid-810a`, built on this branch) found both. The three shared files' comment lines are untouched, and that branch still merges onto this one without a conflict.

**The smoke test printed its OK line when a piece of the view threw.** Godot catches an exception that leaves a method it called, logs it and goes on, so the match ran to its end with a part of the view missing. With a throwaway piece, the old code printed `SMOKE_TEST_OK` in 8 of 10 ways to fail; in the other two, an exception in `AddTo` or in a part's `Attach`, it printed no line but idled to the frame limit first.

- `game/scripts/SmokeLog.cs` is a Godot `Logger` that counts the errors the engine logs from the start of the smoke test. `Main` ends the test with exit code 1 and without the line on the first of them. Warnings are not counted.
- `MatchView.Open` catches a piece that throws in `AddTo`, logs it as an error and adds the pieces after it. In the smoke test that error fails the test. In play the match is shown without that piece; before, the view was built again in every frame.

**The message line was drawn over an open full-screen panel and over the F3 readout.** A third overlap of the same kind turned up while looking: the bottom panel was drawn over the lower edge of an open full-screen panel.

- The message line and the full-screen panel now stand in one column under the top bar, the messages first. While a panel is open, room is kept for one message, so the panel moves only when two messages show at once.
- A full-screen panel covers the bottom panel, which is hidden while one is open.
- The F3 readout moved to the bottom left corner.
- The panel's outer margin and inner padding are smaller (24 to 12, 18 to 12), so the kept line costs the panel no height. At 1280 by 720 the research grid fits as it did before, without a scroll bar, and has more width.

With the research branch merged on top, one message above its panel:

[One message above the research panel, with the research branch merged on top](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-a159082a-c383-56f0-8063-a99f0c48cb0d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fmessage-line-above-panel.png)

## `main` taken in after the economy merged

[Pull request 24](https://github.com/patch-ops-llc/empire-earth-4/pull/24) merged first and this branch then conflicted with `main` in one place: the table of directories in `README.md`. The economy changed the row for `game/data/` and this branch changed the row below it, for `game/ui/`, and added one for `game/pieces/`. Each side changed a different row, so the merge keeps all three as their authors wrote them. Nothing else conflicted.

The economy's stores are in the state now, and the data has `resources.jsonc`, so the smoke test's two hashes moved: `content_hash` to `sha256:639ddf43…4423` and `state_hash` from `d9d9c1f36fbdd2ee` to `fff8c107c6969eeb`. `main` alone gave the same two. The match's six starting units are workers now and its deposits are entities without a body, which the world view does not draw; drawing them is 13v's.

## Decisions made

The first five were accepted by the coordinator on 2026-11-11 as they stood. The sixth came with the smoke test fix and was made under the standing rules.

- **An order click asks only for the kinds of target some row names.** So a deposit is found under the player's own units standing on it. Why: in the trial, with units asked first, workers standing on a deposit hid it.
- **The world view draws an entity as a unit when it has a body and a mover.** A structure or a deposit will have no mover, and the layer of its kind draws it. Why: it keeps the unit drawing out of every later piece's way without a list of kinds to maintain.
- **A modifier is an action held during the order click.**

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Overview

| TL;DR |
|---|
| Clarifai returns `modified_at` with nanosecond precision (e.g. `2026-10-02T17:05:11.904417302Z`), which the cursor format `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ` (max 6 fractional digits) cannot parse, so the cursor skipped every record and state for `applications`, `datasets`, `models` stayed at `start_date`. This PR truncates `modified_at` to microseconds before the cursor observes it, so state advances. |

Resolves https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-internal-issues/issues/19333:
- https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte-internal-issues/issues/19333

Close on merge: no — customer-filed; support confirms the fix with the customer before closing.

## Changes
- `manifest.yaml`: new shared `normalize_modified_at` `AddFields` transformation (guarded by `condition`, applies only when the value has more than 6 fractional digits), referenced by `applications`, `datasets`, `models`. Cursor `datetime_format` and state format unchanged.
- `unit_tests/mock_server/test_incremental.py`: mock-server `read` tests for the three streams (nanosecond, microsecond and millisecond inputs, per-app partition state, second-read carry-forward, missing/null/empty values).
- Version `0.0.77` → `0.0.78` (autopilot), changelog row.

## Behaviour note for reviewers
Emitted `modified_at` values with more than 6 fractional digits lose the sub-microsecond digits (`...904417302Z` → `...904417Z`). Field type stays `string`. The CDK `DatetimeParser` (7.47.0 and latest 7.48.0) delegates to `strptime`, which has no nanosecond directive; a parser-level CDK fix would be the cleaner long-term option.

## Breaking Change Evaluation
Not breaking: no schema type/field/PK/cursor/spec/state-format change and no records dropped. Patch bump.

## Declarative-First Evaluation
Used a declarative `AddFields` transformation with `condition`, defined once and `$ref`'d. Alternatives evaluated: extra `cursor_datetime_formats` entries can't match 9 digits via `strptime` (`%f`, `%f%z`, `rfc3339` all rejected on CDK 7.47.0); switching `cursor_field` to a helper field would change the state key. No custom Python component.

## Test Coverage
- `unit_tests/mock_server/test_incremental.py::test_modified_at_advances_state` (parametrized over streams and timestamp precisions): fails on the merge base for the nanosecond cases, passes with the fix.
- Full suite: `poetry run pytest` → 19 passed.

## Reproduction

<details><summary>Unfixed manifest output (CDK 7.47.0)</summary>

```
E     {'modified_at': '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z'} != {'modified_at': '2026-10-02T17:05:11.904417Z'}
FAILED mock_server/test_incremental.py::test_modified_at_advances_state[nanoseconds-applications]
FAILED mock_server/test_incremental.py::test_modified_at_advances_state[nanoseconds-datasets]
FAILED mock_server/test_incremental.py::test_modified_at_advances_state[nanoseconds-models]
```
Cursor log:
```
Skipping cursor update for stream 'datasets': failed to parse cursor field 'modified_at' value '2026-10-02T17:05:11.904417302Z': No format in ['%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ', '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ'] matching 2026-10-02T17:05:11.904417302Z
```
</details>

## User Impact
State for `applications`, `datasets`, `models` (and per-app partitions) advances to the newest synced `modified_at`. Side effect: `modified_at` is emitted with microsecond rather than nanosecond precision.

author: yuhaosimba
body:
## Problem

Constraint update groups reorder local atoms even in single-rank non-periodic runs. NO_PBC LJ kernels previously indexed immutable global LJ types using local coordinate indices; GB kernels similarly read the wrong intrinsic radii. Directed exclusion rows could also move to the opposite side of the local `i < j` traversal, allowing excluded pairs into LJ/Coulomb calculations.

This produced incorrect initial energies and rapid GB NVT instability with SHAKE/SETTLE. In the reproduced system, the incorrect initial LJ energy was approximately 112568 instead of -2137.72.

## Changes

- Pass `dd.atom_local` into NO_PBC LJ and GB calculations and use it for immutable global parameter lookup.
- Keep effective Born radii, derivatives, coordinates, charges and forces in their existing local order.
- Share a bidirectional exclusion lookup between the NO_PBC LJ and Coulomb energy/force kernels, preserving exclusions when local order reverses.
- Add `test_nopbc_atom_order` with 14 runtime combinations covering GB on/off, SHAKE, SHAKE+SETTLE, shuffled/reversed input, reversed exclusion ownership and force-only versus energy-output steps.
- Check all emitted forces/energies for finiteness and permutation invariance; also compare non-GB results to an independent analytical pairwise oracle.

## Scope

Target branch: `lab/sidereus-ai`; tested base: `5e4d7a9`.

PBC force algorithms and domain-decomposition ordering are unchanged. The changes in `main.cpp` only supply the mapping to NO_PBC calls. No Mokda frontend/backend changes, simulation defaults or installed engine binaries are included.

## Validation

CPU and CUDA builds succeeded. Each passed all four focused CTest tests:

| Test | CPU | CUDA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_nopbc_atom_order` | Passed | Passed |
| `test_hmr_runtime` | Passed | Passed |
| `test_rerun_cell_history` | Passed | Passed |
| `test_rerun_pme_boundary` | Passed | Passed |

The original installed engine failed the new atom-order regression; the fixed builds pass it.

### GB NVT reproduction

1EMA-derived input, 3866 atoms, existing 10000-step minimized restart, SHAKE/SETTLE, Middle Langevin at 300 K, 999 Å box. The original input's 95 water molecules were retained; no structure edits were made for this comparison.

| Time step | Steps | Duration | Mean temperature over final quarter | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.001 ps | 10000 | 10 ps | 299.97 K | Completed; all saved coordinates and printed observables finite |
| 0.002 ps | 10000 | 20 ps | 300.26 K | Completed; all saved coordinates and printed observables finite |

Initial LJ energy is restored to -2137.72, matching independent reconstruction with correct indices. Builds/tests ran with resource limits and no OOM kills.

## Validation boundaries

These are targeted correctness regressions and short stability runs, not production convergence or exhaustive GB/PBC validation. The old installed engine and the target branch also differ in upstream velocity initialization, so the fixed-coordinate regression and analytical oracle establish the mapping defect independently of the long-run comparison. The minimized input completed with finite values; a strict maximum-force convergence criterion was not established.

No long-duration PBC simulation was rerun. Existing PME-boundary and cell-history regressions pass on both CPU and CUDA.

author: elfenlieds7
body:
Windows-to-Mac Raft replication rejects a 5,442,995-byte message at tonic's default 4 MiB receive limit. `ServerConfig` already declares 64 MiB, but full-node and witness service construction never applies it. This connects that existing limit to full-node Raft/API and witness decoders and adds zone, message type and serialized Raft size to send-failure diagnostics without logging payloads.

Seven real mTLS cases cover all three Raft methods, explicit lower-limit refusal, sender identity refusal, actual large-entry replication, full-node snapshot restoration and full/witness snapshot persistence verified after closing and reopening storage. The existing three-platform node-control job runs the new target.

Exact head `58bf3cc1a4d7b67a89baa410515663e69e6212ab` has **47/47 successful checks and 9/9 successful workflows**. The original Linux, Windows and macOS jobs each pass the seven new cases plus two allocator cases: 21 new-case executions and six allocator executions, with no failures or ignored cases. The owning Cargo-program logs bind to test merge `d013cbf93af865598ac8455dff32ad37834df79d`, parents accepted main `53fa30b8` and this head. All main source and both-parent workflow steps are retained. The existing official Windows release candidate has verified archive/executable hashes and original checkout/build-log binding; it has not been installed.

The first CI head's witness fixture compile error is retained. The current fixture uses the existing empty witness roster and the actual witness durability interface: post-persistence commit plus cold-reopened exact snapshot, ConfState, HardState and first index. Full-node state readback and original time bounds remain. A separate offline log parser correction handles Windows path separators without rerunning any product test. No compiled old-source mutant, merged-tree CI or live recovery acceptance is claimed.

Original running-source analysis and timestamped failure evidence: https://github.com/sudoprivacy/sudocloud/issues/20#issuecomment-6816291176. The unused limit predates the member-address repair. The historical failed message's kind remains unknown; this change preserves a finite configured limit and does not establish support for arbitrarily large snapshots.

author: calv-io-n
body:
Tier: **red** (proposed). It adds kernel expiry, beside FAC-124's sweep. Kernel only: no UI change. Two independent reviews (r1 and r2) with `security-review`.

FAC-137 K1, the first of K1 → K2 → G1 → U1 on inferOS. The plan was approved as option A on the FAC-137 row. The design proposal is inferops#2643.

## What changes

**A person's temporary canvases, in their own operate session workspace.** Each is a set of widget placements in FAC-13's shape: references only, never a record or a credential.
- **Shapes:** `workshop-shared/src/temporary-canvas.ts`, with doc comments on every export: `TemporaryCanvas`, `TemporaryCanvasInput`, the limits, the TTL, the error codes and `parseTemporaryCanvasInput`.
- **Store:** `workshop-backend/src/temporary-canvas-store.ts`, `TemporaryCanvasStore`. It follows FAC-124's rules for dynamic definitions:
  - **Server-set expiry.** `expiresAt` is set at creation from `OPERATE_TEMPORARY_CANVAS_TTL_HOURS`: whole hours from 1 to 720; unset is 24, *proposed*. A malformed setting refuses to create rather than pick a duration.
  - **Save against expiry is deterministic.** Each read or write takes the clock inside one transaction. A save before `expiresAt` keeps the canvas; at or after it, the save is refused (`TEMPORARY_CANVAS_EXPIRED`), swept or not.
  - **The sweep deletes only expired, unsaved canvas records.** No saved canvas, no other record and no run is touched. A canvas names no run, and a run started from one of its widgets is that widget's own workspace's.
- **Overseer:**
  - a `temporaryCanvases` collection;
  - `#sweepTemporary` now sweeps canvases too, the hook the kernel reserved for FAC-137, each sweep in its own `try`;
  - `#updateAlarm` wakes for the next expiry.
- **Who can reach them.** Only through `OverseerImpl.temporaryCanvasesOf(userId)`: an operate session workspace, not retired by a company change, owned by that user. Anything else is `TEMPORARY_CANVASES_UNAVAILABLE`.
  - `Overseer` and `OperateSession` gain `listTemporaryCanvases`, `getTemporaryCanvas`, `saveTemporaryCanvas(id, expectedRevision)` and `removeTemporaryCanvas(id, expectedRevision)`.
  - `UseOverseerInterface` denies them. `OperateOverseerInterface` forwards after its retired check.
- **Creating:** `OverseerImpl.createTemporaryCanvasFor(userId, input)` is internal. No client or agent can call it: it is the path K2's approval effect takes.
- **No shared configuration.** Nothing here asks for `build`/`publish`, or writes a console, canvas page or the widget index.
- **Not the agent's.** No operate agent tool reads or writes temporary canvases. `OPERATE_AGENT_TOOLS` is exported read-only, as `OPERATE_AGENT_TOOL_NAMES`, for the check.

**Docs, in the same commit:** `docs/architecture/operate-mode.md` gets a new "Temporary canvases" section; the workflow-definitions section now points to it; and `covers` is updated.

## Proof (local, at cfe386aa, on main 63a373a5)

Everything ran through heavy-run, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm configs:generate`, on the head rebased onto main.
- **`__tests__/temporary-canvases.test.ts`** (new, listed in `test-projects.ts` under `BACKEND`): **10/10**. It covers N1, N3, N4, N5 and N9, plus the TTL's bounds, the input check, refusal outside the owner's live session, and the alarm set and cleared.
- **Nearby files: 9 files, 138/138:** `temporary-canvases`, `test-projects`, `rpc-target-validation`, `workflow-definition-expiry-alarm`, `workflow-dynamic-definitions`, `agent-widgets`, `operate-agui`, `shared-configuration`, `workflow-run-execution` (#442's alarm and run changes, now beside this sweep).
- **Mutations, each caught at cfe386aa** (source restored after each):

  | Mutation | Fails |
  |---|---|
  | Creation asks for shared configuration (N1) | 1 |
  | The sweep also deletes workflow runs (N3/N4) | 1 |
  | The sweep removes saved canvases (N3) | 2 |
  | Save ignores expiry (N5) | 1 |
  | The session check drops the owner | 1 |
  | An operate agent tool writes a canvas (N9) | 1 |

- **`pnpm lint`:** exit **0** (486 warnings, 0 errors). An earlier run failed on two things, both mine and both fixed:
  - a `//` comment on an exported method, where the house rule wants JSDoc;
  - the integration `workshop-use-role.test.ts` default-deny list, which must name every `Overseer` method. It now lists the four new ones.
- **Integration `workshop-use-role.test.ts`** (`--maxWorkers=2`, after `test:prebuild`): **1/1**. A use-role session is refused all four.
- **`pnpm docs:check`:** 0 errors.
- **Not run:**
  - the full backend group and the integration suite (K1 touches no integration path);
  - a browser pass (K1 has no UI).

## Security-review notes (my own code review, plus the executed tests above)
- **No new authority.** Reads and saves are the owner's own; creation has no external entry point yet.
- **Target can't be chosen.** The input names no workspace, console or company.
- **Expiry is a delete of the canvas record only.**
- **Second company:** a company change retires the operate session workspace, and its canvases with it (FAC-88). K2 adds the cross-company negative (N2) on the creation path.

**GrokBot proof:** not testable at K1, since nothing creates a canvas yet. The scenario comes with U1 (operate@grokbot).

Part of FAC-137

## Why

Switching OBS scenes loses the overlay's own transitions, and the script forcing overlay scenes overrode Auto (no Ban / Pick) and fought with 我要直播. Now OBS keeps one scene (game capture + the channel's overlay) and the overlay decides.

## What

- **Script** (`tools/wt-autoscene`): reports `hangar` / `battle` / `ended` per channel every 10 s and on changes (`POST /tournaments/:id/game-state`). A battle left within `minBattle` s (60) is reported as `hangar` (disconnect / wrong room). P pauses / resumes. OBS switching is optional (off by default). README and the .bat updated.
- **Server**: migration 052 (`live_channels.game_state`, `game_match_id`, `game_changed_at`, `game_seen_at`, `autoscene_paused`, `overlay_set_at`), `POST /tournaments/:id/autoscene {paused}`. Both routes are cache-neutral; pages get a `game_state` push on changes and at most every 30 s otherwise.
- **Overlay** (`#lib/game-scene.js`): battle → HUD, ended (for the live match) → bracket, only when the change is newer than the console's last scene pick. Auto with the script: Ban / Pick → reveal → versus until the battle. Paused or no check-in for 75 s: as before.
- **Console**: script online / offline + game state, pause / resume, "本局结束，请填写比分" toast with 录入比分. **我要直播**: prep waits for the battle while the script runs.

## Tests

- API: live channel game state / pause (repo), all 272 pass
- Web: `game-scene` (scene precedence), i18n
- Script: `reportState`, existing detection tests

author: matthew-dean
body:
A page that imports a stylesheet's `vars` now bundles only the code its exports need.

**Goals** (docs/perf/BENCHMARKS.md §10; size of the module Vite builds, unminified, with minified and gzip beside it):

| Goal | Target | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1. setter only | ≤ 1,500 B, ≤ 700 B gzip; next ≤ 450 B, ≤ 1,000 B with the unit check | 2,195 B, 1,010 B gzip | **381 B, 234 B gzip** (met); 906 B, 470 B gzip with a unit check |
| G2. `lightness(@brand)` | ≤ 15,000 B | 43,976 B, 12,532 B gzip | 31,736 B, 10,289 B gzip; 23,153 B, 7,776 B gzip once big.js is out of the bundle (not met) |
| G3. ratchet | ceiling = measured + ~5%, never raised | 2,400 / 45,000 B | 400 / 950 / 33,300 B |
| G4. setter speed | one `setProperty` per changed variable, 6.5 ms on 12,000 elements | | `writeVars` unchanged |

**What changed:**
- `@jesscss/core` builds each source module as its own lib file, so a bundler drops the modules a page never reaches.
- Each node constructor sets its own prototype, beside its definition. The node-copy table is built on the first `copyNode`. A page that copies no node drops both, and with them every constructor only the table names.
  - The table is not marked `@__PURE__`: the published build's minifier strips the mark, even with `comments.annotation` on.
- The 148 named colors are one `name rrggbb` string, read into a map on the first lookup. `color-name` becomes a dev dependency, for a test that holds the two tables equal.
  - This also drops the `alwaysBundle` CJS workaround.
  - A name such as `constructor` no longer reads `Object.prototype`.
- A recipe stylesheet's module takes `vars` from `createVars` and defines `set` beside it, so a page that calls only `vars` drops the writer. `createRuntime` stays, built on `createVars`.
- `exposedVars(spec, values, hold?)` takes the check as an argument: none, `checkUnit` or `holdRatio`. The generated module passes the least its exports need, so a stylesheet whose exports no CSS form reads ships only the key map.

**Not changed:**
- big.js and `value-operate.ts` are replaced in their own PR.
- `@jesscss/fns` stays built per dialect. Vite already keeps only the called function (0.8 KB of it for `lightness`). Building it per module also makes rolldown export a `less_exports` namespace from `@jesscss/fns/less`, which the compiler rejects.

**Cost on the compile side**, `benchmark.less`, with core's lib swapped between runs:
- CLI cold start, 21 interleaved fresh processes: 264.9 ms before, 264.4 ms after.
- Render (`measure:less:hotpath --stable`, 7 rounds, arm order rotated): base 41.40 ms (IQR 40.18–41.44), the same base build again 41.69 ms (39.92–41.74), this branch 41.89 ms (40.55–43.57). The change is inside the A/A spread.
- CJS: loading each subpath of core, fns, patch-css, jess and compiler before its root leaves no root export undefined, and `verify-cjs-smoke` passes.
- `--trace-deopt` over a CLI run shows no node-constructor deopt.

**Tests:** core, fns, patch-css, rollup-plugin-jess and vite-plugin-jess pass. The vite `rgb()` test now runs the built module and checks that it still rejects a value in the wrong unit. `check:guardrails` passes.

author: danielrjahn
body: ## Why Daniel's companion on a Jahn CPA task page answered "I have no tools" (#3855). Bridge 0.3.5 never declares the `firmary` tool in `hello.launch.tools`, so firmary-os (`prepareRoutedTurn`, `apps/web/modules/ai-relay/server/turns.ts`) never opens Firmary's tools for a Bridge turn. The Bridge side of P17 was built in #25 but never merged. This PR carries #25 rebased on 0.3.5, fixes the race its reviewers found, and adds the 0.3.6 release notes. ## What - **From #25 (unchanged):** `hello.launch.tools` is `["web_search","firmary"]`. A turn whose signed profile names `firmary` must carry `turn.firmary = {url, accessToken}`: prod/dev accept only `https` on `firmary.app` or a subdomain (production sends `https://os.firmary.app/api/mcp`, checked in the prod ECS task definition), and the token must be `fmcp_` plus 43 characters. A mismatch refuses the turn with `policy` / `firmary_tools_invalid`, which is logged as `turn_rejected`. Claude Code gets a 0600 `--mcp-config` file plus `--allowedTools mcp__firmary`, with `--strict-mcp-config` kept. Codex gets `mcp_servers.firmary` in `config.toml`, and the token only in its own environment. The token and URL are never logged or put on a command line (D657). - **Fix (review on #25):** the helper frees the turn slot when the terminal event goes out, but the Claude Code driver removed `firmary-mcp.json` in a `defer` after that, so it could delete the next turn's config. The file is now removed as soon as Claude Code exits (or before the error on an early failure). The test checks this at the terminal event; it fails on the old code. - **Honest fallback prompt:** a profile with no `systemPrompt` used to say "You have no tools" even with Firmary's tools on. The fallback now adds firmary-os's own `toolLine` exception after the required block. The server always sends a `systemPrompt`, so this is a safety net. - **Paragraphs:** text the model writes after a tool call now starts a new paragraph (both drivers), instead of "Let me look.The task is…". - **Release 0.3.6:** README status and `.github/release-notes.md`. The `firmary-link_*.deb` copies stop, as `release.yml`'s note asked once firmary.app links `firmary-bridge_*.deb` in production. It does: prod runs firmary-os `cba0b81717`, `apps/web/modules/ai-relay/downloads.ts`. ## Server No firmary-os change is needed for the protocol. The relay schemas in `internal/protocol/testdata` are byte-identical to firmary-os master, and the server's P17 code is in production. The server still gates tools on the `companion.byo-tools` feature for the firm and on Agent access allowing the `fm-bridge-claude-code` app (plan step 3). ## Verified - `go vet ./...` (linux, windows, darwin) and `go test ./...` pass. - Opt-in real-binary tests on the production pins (Claude Code 2.1.304, Codex 0.166.0): `TestRealFirmaryTools`, `TestRealLaunchProfile` and `TestRealMaxTurns` pass. The MCP tool is offered and called with no prompt, the bearer token arrives, and nothing is left in the profile. - Turn with grants → tools (`TestRunWithFirmaryTools`, `TestFirmaryTools`). Without grants → no `--mcp-config`, no `mcp__` tools. Refused credentials → `turn_rejected` with `firmary_tools_invalid` in the log, with no token or URL in it. Supersedes #25. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Chats can use Firmary tools to access firm records, with approvals and short-lived, chat-specific access. * **Improvements** * Responses after a tool lookup are separated into paragraphs for clearer reading. * **Changes** * Linux packages are no longer provided under the old `firmary-link` filenames. The current `firmary-bridge` package copies remain available.

author: zzj3720
body: A fix of #5697 (what is pressed in a page's list stays where it was): it did not hold where what the press opens **over** the pressed node makes its way in (a `show`, a `pick`, an `each`), only where its height changes at once (`By`), which is all `press_stays_test.mbt` has. ## What was wrong The pin measures what lies over the pressed node at each layout (`over_h`, flex's `measured_height`). A node on its way measures as tall as its way had it when it was last laid out, not as tall as it is at the moment read, so the pressed block's top was put by a height a layout behind, and at the way's start by none of it. ## The fix - `over_h` reads a node over the pressed one that is on its way (itself, or through its slots) at the height its way has at that moment (`@flex.come_tall_at`, the reading the list's `Places` uses). Where nothing over it is on a way it reads exactly what it read. - The pin lets go at the latest end declared by what that list set coming or going at the press's moment (a row's way, what a block holds, a group turned back), waited for as a moment (`View::at_moment`); `cause + move_most_ms` as before where nothing declares one. For that, a list keeps what its blocks set coming or going whether or not it joins them to its way (`Tree.list_inner`, a flag saying which; an `at_once` list still joins nothing). ## Tests - New `view/press_stays_ways_test.mbt`: a row's button pressed, a `show` of 300 opening over it, or under it: the button stays at its y at every 10 ms look from the press to 1.5 s on. Green at the default rate, 60 and 120 judged, 24 and 7; red at all five with `over_h` as #5697 had it. - `press_stays_test.mbt` unchanged, green at the five rates; `history_fold_wbtest`, `history_fling_wbtest` and the list files green at the five rates. - What the shipped lists draw is the same frame for frame against main (history_fold, history_fling, chats_list, job_sheet, home, history_steps_node, things_sheet, page_node, page_wide_node, link_row_panel_node, real_size at the default rate; the first five of those that move at 60), so no changelog line. ## Known, not mended here A second press on the same button while what the first opened over it is still on its way (the way turned back) reaches another row: the press's hit (`Tree::target_at`) is 160 points (four rows) off where the list draws its blocks while the pin puts the scroll at each layout. On main this cannot be reached (the first press does not hold, the row is out of sight by then). Its reproduction is kept out of the tree and goes to whoever takes it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## 第三层：输入在事件的 batch 外先把树带到它那一刻（`Tree::input`，c-811 叠上的提交） - **问题**：输入是在事件的 batch 里把树带到它那一刻的（`view_pointer`、`view_wheel`、返回手势取目标时，在事件的 `f` 里调 `Tree::bring_to`）。那一遍排版设的东西（列表的 slot），要等 batch 结束才传到由它算出来的绑定（留白的高）。上一帧之后过了 88 ms 以上才来输入时，行位要重找，块比画出来的低 120，按钮在画出来的中点按下去，按到的是别的行。 - **修法**：`Tree::event_said` 加了 `brings`：在事件的 `said` 之后、`f` 之前，在两个 batch 之外把树带到那一刻，和帧的排版走同一条路；`f` 里的 bring 这时就没事可做了。 - ui 的 `view_event` 加了 `input`，由宿主的 pointer、wheel、返回手势传进来（这三种原来就在事件里 bring）。 - 键、打字、拖放、核心消息照旧不 bring。 - Tree 层加了 `Tree::input`，给测试的路径用（`rc_walk` 的 `inputs`）。 - **验收**（Studio，wasm-gc）： - `press_stays_ways_test` 的第 4、5 条：没有这次的 bring 时红，加上后在默认、60、120、24、7 五档都绿。 - hit / hover / hand / scroll / key 相关的 40 个文件全过，app 的 `press_waits`、`account_open` 也过。 - mbui 和 app 的 native check 都是 0 错误，两份 detlint 都过。 - **instrbench 前后**（全部场景）：home 每帧 +0.2%（+2.0K，是 `f` 里那次没事可做的 bring 又把 timeline 扫了一遍），其余场景 −0.0% 到 +0.1%。

author: todd-skelton
body:
Fixes #1249 ([#1249 max_connections does not count a switched connection: a WebSocket or CONNECT tunnel releases its permit when hyper hands off the socket](https://github.com/corten-run/corten/issues/1249))

## What changed and why

`App::max_connections` is documented as the most connections `serve` holds open at once, and the app guide tells operators to size it from container memory. A switched connection (a WebSocket after its `101`, a tunnel after a `2xx` to `CONNECT`) was not counted: the accept loop moved the permit into the connection's task as `_permit`, and that task returns when hyper's connection completes, which hyper does when it hands the IO to the upgrade. So the permit was given back while the route still held the socket, and a client that opened and switched sockets was outside the cap.

The permit now lives in `Watched`, the wrapper around the accepted IO (`crates/corten/src/watch.rs`). hyper's `Upgraded` owns that IO after the switch, so the permit is released when the route drops the stream. Until the step before HTTP (`serve_wrapped`) finishes, the task still holds it, as before. No work is added per request or per connection: the permit moves one level down.

- `crates/corten/src/app.rs`: the accept loop passes the permit into `Watched`; the `max_connections` rustdoc says a switched connection counts until its route drops the socket.
- `crates/corten/src/watch.rs`: `Watched` holds `Option<OwnedSemaphorePermit>`.
- `crates/corten/src/tests.rs`: the tunnel test from [#1247 Keep a CONNECT tunnel busy so the header timeout does not cut it](https://github.com/corten-run/corten/pull/1247) now expects a second connection to wait while the tunnel is open and to be served once it closes; `a_switched_connection_counts_against_max_connections_until_it_closes` checks the same for a WebSocket after its `101`. Both failed on main (`a7e02c39`): the WebSocket test at "a second connection waits while a WebSocket is open", the tunnel test with the second connection answered `200` while the tunnel was open. `what_a_request_over_tcp_costs` takes `TCP_MAX_CONNECTIONS=n` so the path can be counted with the cap set.
- `docs/design.md#limit-protocol-switch`: no longer says switched connections are outside the cap; it says they count until the route ends them.
- `docs/guide/app.md`: the Connections row, the `max_connections` paragraph and the WebSocket section say a switched connection counts until its route drops it; sizing the cap from memory now includes the sockets an app keeps open (their per-socket memory is the WebSocket library's buffers, which the flood figures did not measure).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: an entry under Unreleased (Changed since review round 2, which says it breaks an app that keeps sockets open under the cap).

The skill (`skills/corten`) mentions `max_connections` only for TLS handshakes, which this does not change, so it is untouched.

## Measurements

callgrind, `tests::what_a_request_over_tcp_costs` (server and client in one process, over loopback TCP), release builds of main (`a7e02c39`) and this branch, `rust:1-bookworm` with valgrind on Docker Desktop. Instructions per request = (count at 1,200 requests - count at 200) / 1,000. Three runs per build, alternating builds.

| Path | main: median (range) | this branch: median (range) |
|---|---|---|
| keep-alive, `max_connections(64)` | 26,312 (26,307 to 26,315) | 26,309 (26,308 to 26,316) |
| a connection per request, `max_connections(64)` | 47,285 (47,162 to 47,335) | 47,278 (47,166 to 47,291) |
| a connection per request, no cap | 46,763 (46,692 to 46,767) | 46,566 (46,495 to 46,643) |

With the cap set, the two builds' ranges overlap and each build's runs vary more than the medians differ, so there is no difference to report. Without the cap the branch counted about 200 fewer instructions a connection (0.4%), with ranges that do not overlap; the code on that path changes only by `Watched` gaining a `None` field, so this is likely a layout or code-generation difference, not investigated.

## Checks

Each run separately. The full set ran on the fix commit `6c4ff03b` (branched from main at `a7e02c39`). main then moved by 39 commits (Origin scheme checks, MCP version header, `@scope` prefixing; none touches the accept loop or `Watched`), so it is merged in at `410a73a8` (a CHANGELOG conflict only, both entries kept), and `npm run check` and `cargo test --workspace --all-features` were run again there; the others were not re-run on the merge.

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: pass
- `corten fmt --check crates examples bench`: pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features`: pass (also re-run on the merge with main, `410a73a8`: pass)
- `cargo test --release --workspace --all-features`: pass
- CONTRIBUTING check 2 (no-default-features tests and checks, `corten new` app with `corten check` and `corten ui add --all`, `cargo publish --workspace --dry-run`): pass
- MSRV (`rust:1.88-bookworm`, `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-features --all-targets`): pass
- `npm run check`: pass (200 tests, 1 skipped by design; also on the merge: pass)
- watchlist smoke (`npm run smoke`, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit): all passed, 87 skipped by design
- watchlist dev smoke (`scripts/smoke-dev.mjs`): all passed
- card-market smoke: all passed

Not run: the ui-gallery, seller-desk, deck-builder, auction-room and listings-feed smokes. They share the accept loop but exercise no switched connection or connection cap.

## Review round 1

Fresh-agent review of `410a73a8`: the code change is correct (the permit is released exactly once on every path). Findings and what was done, in `95513ae2` (after merging main at `c31a9c89`, 6 commits, no conflicts):

1. Medium, idle switched sockets can hold every permit (neither timeout bounds them, and the earlier advice about bounding them was dropped). Fixed. `docs/design.md#limit-protocol-switch`, the header-timeout paragraph in `docs/guide/app.md` and WebSocket note 3 now say a route that accepts switched connections must end idle ones (a timeout on its reads, or pings the client must answer) and should bound how many it keeps, or they take the cap from every other request. The guide's WebSocket example wraps `socket.next()` in `tokio::time::timeout`. `examples/watchlist/src/socket.rs` had the same unbounded wait: it now pings every 30 s and closes with `1001 Going Away` once nothing has been heard for 60 s, tested by `a_client_that_answers_no_ping_is_closed_once_idle` (paused clock); its `/quotes` row in `app.rs` says so. The CHANGELOG entry adds that an app with long-lived WebSockets or tunnels that sets the cap now needs room in it for them, and its routes end idle ones.
2. Low, "every open socket is under the cap" was too broad. Fixed: the `max_connections` paragraph says every connection the app accepted counts until it closes; a relayed switch's upstream socket rides on the client connection's permit, and the app's own outgoing connections are not counted.
3. Low, tests. Added `a_switched_connection_stops_counting_when_its_route_drops_the_socket` (the route echoes once and returns while the client keeps its TCP open; the next connection is served and the server side reads EOF), and `a_switched_connection_after_a_step_counts_against_max_connections` (the same cap check over `serve_wrapped` with a greeting step).
4. Low, Limit 13 said a switched connection "still counts" next to a link titled as the bug. The link is now introduced as "(fixed by ...)". The `max_connections` rustdoc points to `docs/design.md#limit-protocol-switch` again, and says idle switched sockets are the route's to end.
5. Nits. Dropped `let permit = permit;` (the comment stays, now naming `permit`). Renamed `Watched::_open` to `open`; since a never-read field warns under `-D warnings`, it carries `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a doc comment saying it is held for its drop, as elsewhere in the crate.

Checks on `95513ae2`, e

author: vdimarco
body:
## Summary

I ran the QA checks listed in AGENTS.md on main in a cloud container. This branch fixes what failed. Most failures came from checks that no longer matched the game, or that waited a fixed time where software WebGL draws a frame every few seconds. Four were real faults: three Shore layout overlaps, and a Follow Suit build that dropped its analytics tag.

## Game changes

- **Shore, `combat-feel.css`:** Rift Jump is hidden under the death recap. At 844x390 the recap covered it. Rift Jump is disabled while the hero is down.
- **Shore, `command-bar.css`:** on upright phones the team chat sits 232 px up, above the point button. It overlapped the button by 10 px at 390x844.
- **Shore, `illustrated.css`:** at 320 px wide the objective box stops 145 px from the right edge, clear of the kill feed.
- **Follow Suit, `vite.config.ts`:** the arcade build adds `/arcade/analytics.js`. The tag was in `public/follow-suit/index.html` by hand only, so every `build:arcade` removed it. The rebuilt page is the same as the committed one.
- **Table Tennis and Lawn Tennis:** both load `/arcade/quiet.js` as their first script.
- **Mods, `mods/cabinet-spinner/hooks/cabinets.ts`:** the 21 games that had no cabinet now have one.
- **Spec, `openspec/changes/shore-hud-details`:** on a phone a tap on a skill casts it and shows no card, and the Spellbook explains spells. The owner chose to keep the game as it is.

## Check changes

- **Shore HUD suites** (`hunted`, `difficulty`, `hud-details`, `combat-feel`, `skill-targets`): they turn `renderer.draw` off once Play turns on, and wait for game time or for their condition.
- **Shore `desktop.e2e`:**
  - It follows the spec: a new desktop player sees the first-match guide, and touch play does not open the spellbook at the start.
  - The camera and motion parts draw real frames at quality 0.2.
  - The pixel budget read `#battle`, a 300x150 input canvas, so it could not fail. It now reads `#battle-3d`.
- **Shore `hero-select-3d`:**
  - It uses a real context loss and checks the `#graphics-error` dialog.
  - Play starts the match directly, because the draft is now optional.
- **Shore `render3d`:**
  - The round trip may meet a hill in front of a far point, as a player would see it. The centre point must still match exactly.
  - Unsupported graphics show the `#graphics-error` dialog.
- **First Breath `screens.e2e`:** the new tab checks read the address once the tab leaves `about:blank`.
- **First Breath `sound.e2e`:** each click is held to its own latency, within 3 ms plus one audio clock step.
- **Frostwing `smoke.e2e`:** the tap checks turn the drawing off during the tap, and count only the shots each tap starts.
- **Follow Suit `qa/arcade.e2e.mjs`:** it answers `/api/arcade-leaderboard`, as `machines.mjs` does.
- **`qa/arcade/quiet.mjs`:**
  - River Rush starts with "Start run", and a new `resume` page option taps "Resume run", because the game pauses itself when hidden.
  - The arcade entry opens the hall with `?view=classic`, because plain Chromium was sent to the silent Corridor.
- **`qa/arcade/machines.mjs`:** the Crimson credits part was fixed in #818.

## Checks

These ran in a cloud container. The Playwright copies in `qa/browser` and `follow-suit` were pointed at the installed Chromium 153 through `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `qa/arcade/machines.mjs` (full, after merging main) | 1193 ok, 0 failed |
| `node mods/check.mjs` | all passed |
| `npm run check --prefix follow-suit` | passed |
| All node tests, bots, `pop` (Rust), Olympus, Higgsfield, voice | passed |
| Pinball, Primordia, Moonwell, Ahead of the Light, Lake Brawl, Ledger smoke | passed |
| First Breath `smoke`, `boot`, `layout`, `input`, `perf`, `visual`, `screens`, `sound` | passed |
| Frostwing `smoke.e2e` | passed |
| Follow Suit `qa` and `qa:arcade` | passed |
| Shore: all 12 browser suites | passed (`desktop.e2e` takes 20 to 40 minutes here) |
| `qa/arcade/quiet.mjs` | 1099 of 1100; the miss (`vr`, hide, show and hide in one tick) passed 22 of 22 twice alone |

## Not fixed

- **First Breath `music.e2e`:** it failed in 2 of 3 runs, each time on a different timing check, by a few ms over limits of 5 ms and 40 ms. The third run passed. I did not loosen those limits without a closer read of the music engine.
- **Not tried:** real phones, real GPUs and phone speakers.

body: Checkout now matches the privacy collection notice and risk-warning section 6. The legal pages stay the current drafts, including the "(draft)" labels. Food-and-drink copy is unchanged. ## Consent Required before confirm: - Risk warning (section 6.2) - Hotel rules (section 6.3) - Group and children (section 6.4, new) - Terms: Customer Terms, Cancellation and Refund Policy, and the Privacy collection notice (section 6.5) - A separate sharing box: "I agree to Hotel Day Club sharing my name, email, mobile and booking details with {hotel} for this booking." Hot-day alerts are a separate box, left unticked, and are not required: "Send me hot-day alerts and offers by email/SMS. I can unsubscribe at any time." Each of those consents is logged with a policy version, a UTC timestamp (`...Z`), and the IP, in `consent_log`, beside the existing acceptance timestamps. The new log does not use `datetime('now','localtime')`. The older booking timestamps are left as they are. The full timezone fix is still for the later `today()` / day-closure PR. ## Versions (A11) `LEGAL_VERSIONS` in `consent.js` is the one shared config. This PR sets all four to `2026-10-23`, the "Last updated" date on the privacy draft that is served today. The terms, refunds policy and risk warning served with it have no separate date, so they share that draft date. The PR that publishes the new legal pages only needs to bump these four values. New bookings write `terms_version`, `refunds_version`, `privacy_version` and `risk_version` in the same INSERT (nullable for older rows). They show on the admin booking list and in the bookings CSV. A test checks that a new booking stores the current versions. ## Other forms There is no separate notify-me form. The homepage waitlist is also what "coming soon" destinations and "I'm a hotel" use. That form, and the contact form (the hotel-partnership enquiry), use the Schedule B notice, link to the privacy policy, and keep marketing as its own unticked box. ## Demo checkout fields The form no longer has card number, expiry or CVC fields, and it does not mention Stripe. The collection notice does not say "Payment is processed by Stripe". Personal fields the checkout form collects: - Full name (required) - Email (required) - Mobile (required) - Expected arrival time (optional select, "Not sure" preselected) - Hot-day alerts opt-in (optional checkbox, unticked) The server also stores the IP address on the consent log. It is not a field the guest types. "(demo)" prices, "Book your day (demo)", "Your demo booking", and the "Confirm booking · $X (demo)" button stay. ## Tags on www.hoteldayclub.com.au (checked 12 Nov 2026, current production, before this PR) No Meta Pixel, Google Ads, Hotjar, LinkedIn, TikTok or other remarketing tags were in the HTML. - Homepage: GA4 `G-9F5ZH1T4YN` (`googletagmanager.com` plus a preconnect), `/pickers.js`, the inline homepage script, and JSON-LD. Fonts are self-hosted. - Listing (`/h/saltwater-terrace`): the same GA4 tag and `/pickers.js`. An inline script can load `/vendor/leaflet/leaflet.js` and Leaflet CSS, then OpenStreetMap tiles (`tile.openstreetmap.org`), only after the map is opened. That is a map, not an ad tag. - Checkout (open date): the same GA4 tag and `/pickers.js`, plus the inline checkout script. No card-field scripts. This PR removes GA4 from checkout. - Confirmation: no live booking code was opened, so a successful confirmation was not fetched (that would have written a production row). `/booking/HDC-DEMO` returns 404 and loads GA4 with `page_path: '/booking'` so the code is not sent. The success page uses that same shell today. This PR removes GA4 from the confirmation page and from that 404. GA4 stays on the public marketing pages. ## Screenshots Checkout at 1280, marketing left unticked, no card fields: [Checkout at 1280](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-48e578e1-c957-5200-8cdf-f5edf7f4e777/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcheckout-1280.png) Checkout at 390: [Checkout at 390](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-48e578e1-c957-5200-8cdf-f5edf7f4e777/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcheckout-390.png) Validation at 1280 (required ticks empty, marketing still unticked): [Checkout validation at 1280](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-48e578e1-c957-5200-8cdf-f5edf7f4e777/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcheckout-validation-1280.png) Validation at 390: [Checkout validation at 390](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-48e578e1-c957-5200-8cdf-f5edf7f4e777/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcheckout-validation-390.png) `npm run check` passed. Do not merge. To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: hrudek
body:
### Goal
Adapt trusted aggregate touch aim across grip/posture changes without changing
immediate key attribution, and replace the easy P7 benchmark with discriminative
DE/EN/mixed evidence plus same-run search/latency baselines.

### Behavior
Full xy covariance with pooled shrinkage, tempered bounded Gaussian scores and
RAM-only stable/40/8 shared affine drift. Keep the existing learning control,
independent labels, protections/undo, static keys, DE/EN rules, punctuation and
Space/Typr semantics. Only bounded slow state persists with Full Access; schema1→2
migration and saved slow diagnostics remain. No new switch or keyboard network.

### Decisions
Use shared ridge residual fields rather than sparsely labeled per-key fast banks;
prequential .02 fixed share and stable no-drift memory recover on return. Separate
physical spread from decoder calibration; bound centers±.50 and eigen-sigmas
.22–.50. Add validated suffix-length/child-mask search indexes and frozen inverse
preparation without raising caps or granting below-literal auto authority.
Translate scoped MIT ideas at09a2e9c, not upstream files/resources or Student-t.

### Files
23 files: model/types/new TouchAimDrift, decoder, session/store/feedback integration,
thin saved-model ellipse diagnostics; pure covariance/ridge/privacy/migration/
oracle/evaluation regressions; learning/spatial/touch docs, feature row and MIT
provenance. No infrastructure, identity, signing or dictation changes.

### Tested
Swift6.4.2 Linux: **260 cases, 250 pass, 1 known backup metadata failure, 9 baseline
skips**. New aim/evaluation12/12, decoder46/46, learning29/29. Right-thumb recall@1
at10/20/30 trusted labels304/307/299 of312, old155/171/172; fast-disabled new
258/264/264 demonstrates46/43/35 additional fast-drift recoveries. Zero wrong
typo autos/valid-control changes; one-hand return59/59 throughout. Tilt DE loses
one result at zero return labels, recovered by5; no extra wrong auto.
Outside-B mean7.685ms/195.2 visits vs same-run original static10.133ms/422.3 and
new-density legacy10.912ms/454.8. Old learned diagonal remains faster at6.674ms,
though with291.2 visits: **+15.2% mean overhead is disclosed**, not a blanket speed
claim. Numeric slow/fast5184/320B, lexical file+indexes5,396,164B, not RSS.
Python76+25+4 pass; shell syntax, shellcheck, actionlint and diff checks pass.

### Not tested / needs iPhone
Apple SDK/UI compile, simulator, real DE/EN dictionaries/host callbacks and Full
Access/protected storage/Darwin delivery. Physical grip transitions and real
feedback coverage, rollover, device latency and extension RSS/pressure. Synthetic
fixtures do not establish human accuracy, universal reversal safety or old-learned
performance superiority.

### Screenshots
None. Optional settings-keyboard-diagnostics scene shows saved slow ellipses;
grip recovery needs physical typing, not screenshots.

author: elihu0211
body:
## 變更 邀請信、驗證信與 `mail test` 由純文字改成 `multipart/alternative`（純文字在前、HTML 在後），三者共用同一個版型。新增 `mail preview <輸出目錄>`，不寄信、不連資料庫就能看版型。 資料流是「呼叫端組資料 → `IMailComposer` 組成信 → `IMailSender` 只管傳輸」。 | 層 | 型別 | 職責 | |----|------|------| | 呼叫端 | `MemberCore`、`OperatorAdmin`（經 `IActivationMailer`）、`OperatorCli` | 只組資料：收件者、連結、有效期限、租戶、邀請或驗證；不碰文案與版面 | | 組信 | `IMailComposer`／`MailComposer` | 資料加文案、系統名稱、版型選項 → 主旨、純文字、HTML；**不寄信、不連網路** | | 傳輸 | `IMailSender`／`SmtpMailSender` | 收 `MailContent` 寄成 multipart；日誌不記收件者與內文 | | 註冊 | `AddPlatformMail()` | 傳輸、版型選項、系統名稱、本地化、組信、渲染器都在這一處；`Program.cs` 只呼叫它 | ### 設計決定、理由與取捨 1. **全走 DI，沒有 static 的組信類別。** `ActivationMail`（static）與先前的 `MailTemplate`（static）都刪了。取捨：多了 `IMailComposer` 與 `IActivationMailer` 兩個介面與一個實作，換來測試用 `ServiceCollection` 組真實服務、不手動接線；預覽命令與測試用的是同一個組信服務。`ActivationLinks`／`Activation`（權杖與網址的機制，不是信的內容）仍是 static，沒動。 2. **範本引擎：Razor 元件加 `HtmlRenderer`（第一方，沒有新增任何套件）。** 與平台 UI 同一套技術，參數是強型別的 `MailPage`，插入的值由 Razor 自動 HTML 編碼，所以不再有自己寫的編碼函式。Outlook 的條件註解與 VML 以 `MarkupString` 輸出，內容只有固定文字、整數與已驗證的顏色（規則寫進 `AGENTS.md`）。取捨：`SharedKernel` 改用 `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Razor`（沒有新的套件參照，`packages.lock.json` 不變）；沒有選第三方範本引擎，因為沒必要。 3. **渲染器用隔離的專用容器，不用主機的容器。** 後台（Blazor）註冊了 scoped 的元件服務，`HtmlRenderer` 從根容器解析它們，在驗證範圍的環境（Development）會失敗（整合測試抓到，211 個失敗）；也不該讓後台的 UI 設定影響信件。容器裡只有一個 `HtmlEncoder`。 4. **`HtmlEncoder` 放行 Unicode 全範圍。** 預設編碼器只放行基本拉丁字母，會把整封信的中文與全形標點變成 `&#x…;`（檔案大一倍、原始碼讀不了、更像垃圾信）。`< > & " '` 照樣編碼，安全性不變。 5. **版型的可調值走選項，不寫死。** `Platform:Mail:Template`（`MailTemplateOptions`）：`Culture`、`Width`、內距（桌面與手機）、`CompactBreakpoint`、兩組字型、淺色與深色各一組色票，全部有預設值、可由設定逐鍵覆寫。值會進內嵌樣式與樣式表，所以 `IValidateOptions` 在啟動驗證：顏色只收 `#rrggbb`、字型只收字母數字與少數符號、寬度與內距有範圍，**每組色票的文字對比度必須至少 4.5:1**（調色票不能把信調成看不清）。錯值在啟動停下並指名鍵，與其他設定群組同一個規則；與寄信是否啟用無關，一律驗證（預覽命令也用同一份）。系統名稱一律注入 `IOptions`。 6. **文案進資源檔，C# 與 Razor 沒有郵件用的中文字面值。** `MailTexts.resx`（繁體中文）與 `MailTexts.en.resx`（英文），鍵是領域鍵（`Mail.Heading.Invitation`）、帶參數用 `{0}`，用 `IStringLocalizer`。測試守住兩個語言的鍵與參數個數一致；缺鍵時組信丟例外，不會把鍵名寄出去。 - **信的語言取自 `Template:Culture`，不取自請求的語言。** 操作者可能用英文介面，收信的人還沒登入過、沒有「他的語言」可看，所以由部署決定。組信只在同步取字串的區段暫時換文化，不跨 await。 - **按鈕文字放資源檔，不放選項。** 它隨語言變；選項只放「長相」。 - 命令列（`OperatorCli`、`MailPreview`）自己的訊息仍是中文字面值（既有慣例，不是信件內容），沒動。 7. **沒有用 `TimeProvider`。** 組信不讀現在時間：連結期限是「一段時間」（`TimeSpan`，來自 `Platform:Mail:LinkLifetime`），不是時間點。 ### 沒變的 - **安全限制**：信裡唯一的外部網址是啟用連結；沒有遠端圖片、追蹤像素、點擊追蹤轉址、腳本或外部樣式；系統名稱、租戶識別碼、連結都編碼；日誌與稽核不記連結與內文；信裡沒有密碼；仍帶 `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated`。 - **純文字版**措辭與改版前逐字相同（既有的 `Assert.Equal`／`Contains` 一字未改）；主旨格式不變。 ### 與示意圖不同之處 - 租戶行寫「租戶識別碼：{識別碼}」，不是「租戶：…」。現有呼叫端只傳識別碼，且既有測試與純文字版都是「租戶識別碼：」，兩版保持一致。 - 純文字版沒有頁尾「這是系統自動寄出的信」：`mail test` 的純文字有既有的逐字斷言；HTML 版有。 ## 測試計畫 - [x] `dotnet build`（警告即錯誤）、`dotnet format --verify-no-changes`、`python3 ci/check-docs.py` 通過 - [x] `dotnet test`：742 個全過（含 Testcontainers 整合測試），既有測試的斷言未改弱（`BrandTests` 只改了建立被測物件的方式：static 呼叫改成經容器取得） - [x] `MailComposerTests`（經 `ServiceCollection` 取真實的 `IMailComposer`）：兩版含同一條連結、期限、提示、租戶；HTML 除該連結（三次：VML、按鈕、備用文字）外不含 `http`／`//`／` 預覽證據：邀請信（有租戶）的 HTML 與純文字（mail preview 輸出，連結是占位值） `invitation-tenant.html` ```html 邀請您啟用帳號 · 環境知識
連結 3 天內有效，只能使用一次‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

## In plain English (for Nimish)
One test about checking answers failed now and then and could keep main red, which blocks the live deploy. The site is fine; the test picked its sample answer at random from a set that included a bad one. It now always takes a sample that is really right, on a paper it can open.

## Cause (verified)
`tests/s4-validation-queue.spec.ts` "a right answer of a kind the reader is not yet trusted on waits, and settles in one click" took any answer marked `correct` and still a candidate, ordered by uuid, which is random per database.
- **One cause:** the spec's own fixture marks S4TEST-1's 7th answer `correct` with the reading "82", while its key is 62 (33 + 29). When the test presses "Yes, the child wrote 82", the engine marks that answer again against the key and calls it `wrong`.
  - That is CI's "Expected correct, Received wrong" (#707's run 43163733210).
  - I reproduced it by forcing that row to be picked: 1 failed, same message.
- **A second cause, found once the first was fixed with a fixed order:** S4TEST-1 and S4TEST-2 are both Asha's copies of the same worksheet. They share one paper-screen address, which opens the first copy. So an answer on the second copy is never the one in view; the panel showed another answer's id.

## Change (test only)
- The answer taken is one whose reading equals its question's key (`coalesce(i.spec->>'answer', i.responses->0->>'answer')`).
- It is on the child's only live copy of that worksheet.
- It is taken in a fixed order (`c.path, r.rid`), never by uuid.
- The assertions are unchanged, and the file stays at 400 lines.

## Checks run here
- Fresh database (`bin/testdb fresh`): the test repeated 10 times passes 10 of 10, and the whole s4 file passes 17 of 17.
- On a second database, the one where the first fix failed: 10 of 10.
- `bin/check`: 60 passed, 4 skipped.
- `npx eslint --max-warnings 0 .` in apps/web: clean.

## Noted, not changed
A child's second copy of the same worksheet can't be opened by its own address: the paper screen is keyed by assessment and Sr. No. The screen says "handed in two copies" (UI-4b), but an answer on the second copy has no direct link. That is the paper screen's, not this test's.

body:
Update to our target `mediceo1483` (catalogue 2309, ASF MAP XLVIII 214r, Siena no. 11 cipher). It takes up the gap "D1 untested" in NOTES.md.

**What it does.**
- A third pre-registered test of George Lasry's Siena no. 11 key on the "##" family. Portion: XLVIII 294 c. 306r, lines 1-16 (411 cipher tokens), never transcribed, decoded or measured before. Clear: the upper part of the clear copy c. 276r, up to where the clear of the 10 Nov test begins. The pre-registration, script, keys and a synthetic check were hashed before the transcription. Then the transcription, the three decodings and the clear were each frozen in turn, and the measure was run once.
- Letter agreement **0.6519** against at most 0.1854 for 200 shuffled keys (margin 0.467): **partial**, as on 10 Nov (0.6419). Lasry's key alone gives 0.6390.
- **D1 ("PLUS ODAG" = c) holds.** Of its 6 occurrences, 5 align on "c" in the clear and the sixth on nothing. The control is 200 random-position draws: p = 0.005 (e.g. "ci sia amico o inimico", "pratiche col cardinale").
- **TRI (▽) = "che" holds**: 4 of 5, p = 0.005 (e.g. "che sono capitoli", "che ognuno"). The other pre-registered candidates gave:
  - PLUS alone = o: **did not hold** (0 of 3).
  - PIBAR = n: no occurrence.
  - The proposed nulls DIV, OO and ST cannot be tested this way.
- 2309 was decoded again with `key/K_SIENA11_D1_TRI.tsv` (Lasry's key + D1 + TRI = che, nothing else) and re-read with your 95 % conventions:

| | certain | probable | restored | unresolved | letters read (certain + probable / with restored) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 Nov | 39 | 13 | 11 | 45 | 33 % / 43 % of 665 |
| 12 Nov | 46 | 13 | 11 | 46 | 35 % / 45 % of 683 |

  The gain is small: six "che" and one "e", e.g. "conte antonio che egli haueua", "che e utile a questo". The readings that use D1 ("conducti", "conte", "con", "ducati") now rest on a held test. The state stays **read in part**.
- Deviations are declared in `validation.txt`:
  - The upper c. 276r had been looked at for anchors on 10 Nov.
  - The transcriber knew the key and the candidates.
  - The candidates come from material already seen.
  - PLUS alone aligning twice on "c" is noted as an observation made after the measure, not a result.
- XLVIII 294 is now used up. A further value needs another letter of the family with a clear, and doubtful forms in 214 need an HD image from the ASF.

**Files**
- Changed: `NOTES.md` (Status line, key, test 3, reading counts, gaps, escalation), `profile.json` (two `solution` entries, validation note, gaps, reading_review, `decryption` path), `reading/xlviii214.md` (lines 2, 6, 12, 14 and counts), `validation.txt` (test 3 with hashes), `translation.md` (share read).
- New: `key/K_SIENA11_D1_TRI.tsv`, `decryption/xlviii214_D1_TRI.txt` (the D1 decoding is kept), `validation/xlviii294_306r_H3_{transcription,decoding,measure}.txt`.

The key is Lasry's. The clear of c. 276 is not reproduced, and there are no ASF images.

Checks:
- `_check_profile`: valid.
- `_check_reading`: 0.952, as before.
- `_check_writeup`: only the site build items are missing (page, `_dates.json`, findings), as on #375.

body:
**Tier 2: needs Frank's yes before merge.** It touches how pages are served and the structured data, not anything a visitor reads.

## What changes

**Speed.** Every service, treatment, product, practitioner, blog post and legal page (38 of 56) was rebuilt on every visit and never cached, answering in 170 to 250 ms on production against about 70 ms for the hub pages. The cause: a page type with a variable in its address and no `generateStaticParams` is rendered fresh every time. An empty list fixes it without fetching anything at build time, which is what stopped the earlier attempt noted under CH-104.

**Markup**, from the 2026-11-07 audit:
- the B Corp certification is attached to the organization on every page (`hasCertification`); before, only the B Corp page pointed at the organization
- the certification date is `2026-10` rather than "October 2026", which parsers cannot read
- phone numbers carry the `+1` country code, which Google asks for
- `/cafe/menu` names the cafe it belongs to, so its menu no longer points at something missing from that page

**CLAUDE.md**: the outstanding list gains the audit's items and the cafe items from the Owner.com grade; the three audit recommendations that were wrong are recorded so nobody acts on them.

## Verified on a local production build

- the six page types build as cached (`●`) where they were rendered per request (`ƒ`)
- each page renders once, then answers from the cache in 6 to 20 ms instead of 170 to 650
- unknown addresses still 404, Safa's switched-off page still 404s, the old redirects still 301
- `node scripts/audit-seo-complete.js http://localhost:3000`: **all 13 checks passed**
- `audit-security-headers.js`: all 8 paths pass
- `audit-render-baseline.js` against production: 56 pages changed, **structured data only**; no title, description, heading, text, image or link moved

**Not re-tested locally:** the publish webhook's purge, because `SANITY_REVALIDATE_SECRET` is not in `.env.local`. The webhook code is unchanged; I'll confirm on production after merge by publishing and watching the page refresh.

author: khunmaungaye
body:
## US-05 — Cancel Cleaning Booking

As a customer, I want to cancel a cleaning booking when cancellation is allowed so that I do not keep an unwanted service.

### How each acceptance criterion is met
| Acceptance criterion | How |
|---|---|
| 1. Cancel at least 24 hours before the service | **Cancel booking** button on upcoming one-time bookings. The rule is enforced by `POST /api/bookings/[id]/cancel` using Bangkok time (UTC+7). Exactly 24 hours is allowed. Inside 24 hours the card shows a note instead of the button. |
| 2. Cancellation confirmation message is displayed | A confirm step ("Cancel this cleaning on … ? You won't be charged.", naming the cleaner if one accepted), then a banner at the top of the page. |
| 3. Customer receives a cancellation confirmation | In-app, since there's no email service: the booking is listed under **Cancelled** in the Previous and All tabs. |
| Checklist: release the time slot | The booking moves to a new `cancelled_bookings` table and is removed from `bookings` in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction. This frees the `UNIQUE (service_date, time_slot)` window and removes the job from the cleaner's list and Available Requests. It follows the same pattern as the US-15 Skip feature. |

**Refused with a clear message:** less than 24 hours away, completed bookings, and recurring-plan visits (pointed to Skip in My plans). Another customer's booking returns 404.

### Files
- `src/lib/services.ts`: `CANCELLATION_NOTICE_HOURS`, `getServiceStartTime`, `isWithinCancellationWindow` (shared by the page and the API)
- `src/lib/booking-store.ts`: `cancelled_bookings` table (additive), `cancelCustomerBooking`, `getCancelledBookings`, `canCancel` flag
- `src/app/api/bookings/[id]/cancel/route.ts`: new route, `requireRole(["customer"])`
- `src/app/api/bookings/route.ts`: GET now also returns `cancelled`
- `src/app/bookings/page.tsx` and `globals.css`: button, confirm step, Cancelled list

### How to test by hand
1. Sign up a cleaner and a customer, then book two one-time cleanings as the customer: one tomorrow and one next week.
2. Tomorrow's card says it can't be cancelled within 24 hours. Next week's card shows **Cancel booking**.
3. Cancel it: the confirm step appears, then the banner. The booking leaves Upcoming and shows under Previous → Cancelled.
4. The same date and time can be booked again, and the cleaner no longer sees the job.
5. Repeat at 375px width.

### Test results
- `npm test`: 150/150 pass (21 new in `tests/us-05-cancel-booking.test.mjs`: 24-hour edges, ownership, double cancel, 401/403/404/409)
- `npm run lint`: clean
- `npm run build`: passes
- Checked by hand at desktop and 375px

### Notes for the reviewer
- The cleaner isn't notified, because the app has no notifications; the job disappears from their list.
- This touches the Previous and All tabs on the customer page, which US-14 also uses. Agree a merge order if US-14 gets its own PR.

## Summary by Sourcery

Enable customers to cancel eligible one-time cleaning bookings while preserving cancellation history and releasing the original appointment slot.

New Features:
- Allow customers to cancel eligible one-time bookings at least 24 hours before service and view cancelled bookings in their history.

Enhancements:
- Enforce cancellation eligibility, ownership, and role-based authorization through a dedicated cancellation API.
- Preserve cancelled booking records while freeing their service time slots and removing them from cleaner request lists.
- Add confirmation, error handling, cancellation status messaging, and responsive booking-history UI.

Tests:
- Add coverage for cancellation timing boundaries, authorization, ownership, recurring and completed bookings, retries, history, and released availability.

author: moveeeax
body:
Closes #15
Closes #16
Closes #17

## #17: report expired and untrusted certificates

What changed: `check` and `batch` no longer stop at a verification error. When the verifying handshake fails with `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError`, certcheck reconnects with verification off, reads the certificate and reports it. `status` is `expired` / `not_yet_valid` when the dates explain the failure, `hostname_mismatch` for OpenSSL codes 62/64, otherwise `untrusted`. The OpenSSL message goes to `verify_error` (JSON) and a `Verify:` line (text). Exit code is 1, not 2.

Behavior notes:
- `--insecure` keeps its meaning: only the unverified handshake runs, trust is not judged and never fails the check.
- New `--ca-file PATH` verifies against a private CA instead of the system store. Added so private PKI does not need `--insecure`, and so the hostname-mismatch path is testable offline.
- `fetch_cert` keeps its signature but no longer raises on verification failure; `fetch_peer` returns the cert plus verify info, presented chain, protocol and cipher.

## #16: `certcheck inventory` (from tls-inventory)

What changed: new `inventory --file hosts.txt` command. Per host: the `check` result, the presented chain with expiry/status per certificate, findings (`self_signed`, `hostname_mismatch`, `incomplete_chain`, `untrusted`, `chain_expired`/`chain_expiring`/`chain_not_yet_valid`, `protocol`, `forward_secrecy`), `protocols` from one pinned handshake per TLS 1.0-1.3, and with `--ciphers` the accepted suites with a forward-secrecy flag. `--min-version` (default `tls1.2`, per RFC 8996), `--require-forward-secrecy`, `--concurrency` (default 10, input order kept). Exit 1 on any breach or finding.

Decisions:
- Stays stdlib-only Python with argparse, not Go/cobra as the stub README said; it is a mode of this tool.
- Chain comes from `SSLSocket.get_unverified_chain()` (public in 3.13+), and on 3.11/3.12 from the private `_sslobj.get_unverified_chain()` that the public method wraps (checked in the CPython 3.11/3.12 `_ssl.c`).
- `incomplete_chain` = verify codes 2/20/21 with a non-self-signed leaf: the issuer was neither presented nor trusted. A private root not in the trust store looks the same to OpenSSL; the detail text says so.
- A protocol result is `null` when this client's OpenSSL cannot offer the version (`NO_PROTOCOLS_AVAILABLE`). `ssl.HAS_TLSv1_2` and friends are not used: on Python 3.15 with OpenSSL 4.1 they read False while TLS 1.2 works.
- Probe contexts use `@SECLEVEL=0` so the client does not refuse old versions/suites itself.
- Python cannot restrict TLS 1.3 suites, so only the negotiated TLS 1.3 suite is listed.
- Non-forward-secret suites are only flagged as findings with `--require-forward-secrecy`; `--ciphers` alone just lists them.
- Under `--insecure` no trust findings are produced.

## #15: `certcheck k8s` (from k8s-cert-expiry)

What changed: new `k8s` command. Lists `kubernetes.io/tls` secrets with `kubectl get secrets --field-selector type=kubernetes.io/tls -o json`, decodes the leaf from `tls.crt`, and when `certificates.cert-manager.io` is served (checked with `kubectl api-resources --api-group=cert-manager.io`) matches Certificates to secrets by `spec.secretName`, attaching Ready condition, issuerRef and `status.renewalTime`. Rows are sorted by days left, rows with no usable expiry first. Flags: `-n`, `-A`, `-l`, `--exclude-namespace GLOB`, `--exclude-issuer GLOB` (issuer CN or cert-manager issuer name), `--context`, `--kubeconfig`, `--kubectl`, `--warn-days`, `--timeout` (passed as `--request-timeout`), `--json`.

Decisions:
- Uses the `kubectl` binary instead of a Kubernetes client library, so the package keeps zero runtime dependencies and reuses kubectl's auth. Only `get` and `api-resources` are called.
- A not-Ready Certificate makes its row `not_ready` and a breach, unless the dates already make it expired/expiring. A Certificate whose secret is missing gets its own row.
- `-l` filters secrets only (Certificate labels need not match secret labels); with `-l`, Certificates without a listed secret are not reported, since the secret may just be filtered out.
- No separate `--critical` threshold: the exit codes 0/1/2 are already defined, so `--warn-days` stays the single threshold.
- Unparseable `tls.crt` is an `error` row and a breach; kubectl failure is exit 2.

## Testing

`python -m pytest -q`: 134 passed locally on Python 3.15 / OpenSSL 4.1. All offline:
- local TLS servers on 127.0.0.1 with generated root/intermediate/leaf chains (valid chain, missing intermediate, hostname mismatch, self-signed, TLS 1.2 max, restricted cipher list);
- core unit tests for verify-code mapping, chain findings, protocol policy and forward secrecy;
- k8s row building on fixture objects, a fake kubectl runner for argument scoping, and a fake kubectl executable for the subprocess wrapper.

Manually ran `inventory` against example.com and badssl.com hosts: expired, self-signed and incomplete-chain cases are reported as expected.

author: nyakuoff
body:
Game side of nyakuoff/New-Dawn-libultraship#3.

Adds a VRAM byte budget to the texture cache (issue #12).

- Each entry tracks its approximate size: level 0, plus a third more when it is mipmapped (OpenGL only; other backends report 0 and keep the entry-count behaviour).
- When the total exceeds `gNewDawn.Textures.CacheBudgetMB`, the least-recently-used entries are evicted. The default is 2048 MB, and 0 means unlimited. Textures bound in the current rendering state are never evicted. The 1024-entry cap is still enforced.
- Debug logging: `gNewDawn.Textures.CacheDebug=1`.

**Verified** (by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; the lead reviewed the eviction code):
- At the default budget and at unlimited, the full mods set is pixel-identical (RMSE 0) to the build before this change, with 0 evictions.
- Vanilla differs only within capture noise (0.012 and 0.018).
- With a 64 MB budget, four scenes produced tens of thousands of evictions with no crash and no missing or black textures.

Test-only (`MeshEditOpsPropertyTests.cs`, seeded `System.Random`, also built for net48, about 1 s). Second of two PRs for the gap-list operations with thin tests (first: #646).

- `VoxelSurfaceGenerator`: area and signed volume of random voxel sets equal the exposed faces and the filled voxels (both orientations); `CapAtBoundary = false` gives exactly the exposed faces off the grid boundary; `SkipInteriorFaces = false` gives all faces; `MaxMeshElementCount` splits without losing faces.
- `MeshInsertPolygon` on a flat grid mesh, circle with and without a hole, at 2^-10, 1, 2^10: valid mesh, total area unchanged, interior triangles cover exactly the polygon (area and centroid membership).
- `RegionOperator` on a sphere cap at 2^-10, 1, 2^20: a plain round trip changes nothing; an edit of the interior vertices puts each exactly `shift` along x (through the vertex maps) and leaves the border and the outside alone; an interior edge split adds two triangles, keeps the area and the closed mesh, and the vertex and triangle maps point to the right images.
- `MeshTrimLoop` cutting a cap from a sphere with the seed on either side: one boundary loop, valid mesh, the expected area share, no vertex on the removed side.

Mutants checked (library broken temporarily, tests must fail): no `SkipInteriorFaces`, `CapAtBoundary` ignored, flood fill of the inserted polygon without its edges as barrier, the triangle map of the region operator, the seed of the trim loop: each killed. No library change.

Finding: #647 (`VoxelSurfaceGenerator` exceeds `MaxMeshElementCount` by up to 17 vertices; pinned as a skipped test). The other operations passed their properties at all scales tried.
