author: dgatom
body:
Itens 2 e 3 da ordem recomendada da auditoria de eficiência de 12/11 (seções 3.1a e 1.2). Um commit por item.

## Item 2: compressão no Caddy

**Problema.** O site gerado pelo instalador era só `reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8300`, então nada saía comprimido: o `conversa.js` trafegava com 244 KB e a tela da conversa carrega uns 595 KB de scripts e estilos.

**O que mudou.**
- `bloco_caddy` (`lib/comum.sh`) passa a gerar `encode { zstd gzip match { ... } }` com uma lista explícita de Content-Type (html, css, plain, javascript, json, manifest, xml, svg). `text/event-stream` fica de fora de propósito, para a compressão não reter o stream da conversa.
- **Instalação existente.** O `dgclaw atualizar` roda o `install.sh`, que antes reescrevia o arquivo do site sempre (personalização se perdia). Agora o arquivo só é trocado se o conteúdo, sem comentários e linhas em branco, ainda é exatamente o que o instalador gerou (formato antigo ou novo). Arquivo personalizado fica como está, com um aviso dizendo o que acrescentar. O Caddyfile padrão do pacote (`:80` com `file_server`) continua sendo substituído na instalação nova.
- `dgclaw dominio trocar` grava o site gerado com o domínio novo, como antes, mas, se o arquivo foi personalizado, guarda antes uma cópia com modo e dono preservados em `/etc/caddy/<nome>.antes-dominio-<data>` (fora de `conf.d`, para não ser importada) e avisa onde ficou. A restauração depois de um `caddy validate` que falha passou a preservar modo e dono (antes voltava com 0644).
- `caddy validate` que falha restaura o arquivo anterior e não recarrega. Com a validação ok e o Caddy ativo, recarrega sempre.
- CHANGELOG com "Como atualizar" para quem personalizou o Caddyfile.

**Validação com Caddy de verdade** (Caddy 2.11.7 da VPS de teste, numa instância temporária em portas próprias, sem tocar no Caddy em produção, com o bloco gerado por este PR):

| | Bytes transferidos |
| --- | ---: |
| `conversa.js` sem compressão (hoje) | 244.276 |
| `conversa.js` com `Accept-Encoding: gzip` | 80.350 (`Content-Encoding: gzip`) |
| `conversa.js` com `Accept-Encoding: zstd, gzip` | 79.611 (`Content-Encoding: zstd`) |

- `caddy validate` do bloco: `Valid configuration`.
- SSE atrás do mesmo bloco, com o cliente pedindo `gzip, zstd`: os 4 eventos chegaram um por segundo, cada um na hora (sem acumular), e a resposta veio com `Content-Type: text/event-stream` e sem `Content-Encoding`.
- Estimativa para todos os `.js` e `.css` de `web/public` com `gzip -6`: de 1.001.755 para 284.958 bytes.

## Item 3: reflexão pula dia sem conversa

**Problema.** A reflexão das 23h30 acordava o modelo todo dia, mesmo sem nenhuma conversa: 17 reflexões em 15 dias na agente de teste, cerca de 0,9 milhão de tokens de escrita de cache.

**O que mudou.**
- `scripts/reflection.sh` conta, sem modelo, as mensagens do dono no dia em todas as sessões mexidas desde o começo do dia. Com zero, registra "PULADA" no log, `ok` no Pulso e sai, antes da cópia do MEMORY.md, do modo headless e da injeção.
- **Na dúvida, reflete:** pasta de sessões que não pode ser listada, transcript que não abre ou com linha JSON quebrada (só a última linha, ainda sendo escrita, é tolerada), leitura que falhou, pasta de sessões ausente, mensagem do dono com data ilegível ou provedor diferente de `claude`. Só o registro do Claude é lido aqui (o rollout do Codex fica em outra pasta, e a `PARIDADE-CODEX.md` já marca a reflexão como parcial), então agentes Codex continuam refletindo todo dia. Conferi que o `config.sh` dos agentes existentes já traz `DGCLAW_PROVEDOR='claude'`.
- Contam como conversa: painel, WhatsApp e Telegram (todos viram origem "owner"). E-mail e rotinas não contam.
- `DGCLAW_REFLECT_SEMPRE=1` força a reflexão.
- **Efeitos colaterais tratados:** o `audit.sh` das 23h50 deixa de acusar "reflexão não disparada" quando o dia foi pulado, e o `doctor.sh` conta o dia pulado (anotado em `.dgclaw/logs/reflexoes-puladas.txt`) como reflexão em dia. A working-memory das 7h já tratava a falta de diário.

author: olafura
body:
## What

Every non-exempt code block on a docs page runs beside its code and can be edited (SITE-2 goal 7), as a **general ljos-web feature** the current Astro site is the first user of.

### The general feature (`packages/runtime/codeblocks/`, docs in `docs/LJOS_WEB.md` A27)

- `ljos-web/codeblocks/parse` — the fence contract, shared by build and page: `qml` whole app, `qml harness=<name>` (snippet spliced at the harness's one `//! snippet` line), `qml before` (labelled old half), `file=`/`group=` multi-file examples (scripts included, folders as written — a `ShellLoader` example ships `user/Shell.qml` + fallback + app as three editable files). Exempt tags (`sh`, `rust`, `toml`, `json`, `text`, `xml`, `gherkin`, `javascript`, `diff`) stay plain; bare/unknown tags are named.
- `ljos-web/codeblocks` (build) — `checkExamples` holds every claimed block to compiling under `qmlc` (a block that claims to run and doesn't fails the build, with `file:line:` diagnostics); `hashExample` (content hash, prerender-format versioned); `renderPrerenders` makes each example's static half with **the merged prerender** (A26): one server bundle per batch over this runtime, `renderToString` from `ljos-web/server` in Node, split until a refusal names its own block, cached by hash — making an example runs it, so this is the run half of the check; `renderStatic` writes code + that prerendered markup in a stage sized by its root + the JSON payload.
- `ljos-web/codeblocks/remark` — a remark plugin for any unified pipeline. One example is one figure at its entry fence, however its fences spread through prose (as the docs write them); a group written as one run of fences is replaced whole. Untouched: exempt fences (the host highlights them).
- `ljos-web/codeblock` (+ `.css`) — hydration. Blocks mount only near the viewport (IntersectionObserver, 0 % idle, nothing fetched before). The first making **takes the prerendered nodes over with `hydrate()`** (A26; node identity asserted in tests). The editor is a labelled textarea per file (keyboard/AT reachable as any field); an edit debounces into the in-page compiler (A15) + `reload` (A13) — **state is kept**: a counter at 3 stays 3 when its colour changes, and editing a user's `shell.qml` keeps the app's contribution and count. A broken edit shows `file:line:column: message` inline (`role=alert`) and the last good result keeps running. The host element takes the root's size (it is the runtime's scene; pointer delivery needs it). `prefers-reduced-motion` stills transitions.

One core fix rides along: a canvas is no making in the hydration count on either side (`server/dom.js`, `object.js` `hydrate`). The font-measuring canvas is made at whatever making first measures — an anchored text's layout read decides that differently in a browser than in Node — and parted every anchored prerender at that element. Canvases are painted, not read; hydration remakes them and takes the prerendered ones out.

For the later move of ljos.dev to prerendered Ljós pages: use `assemble` + `renderPrerenders` + `renderStatic` at build time and `hydrateLiveCodeBlocks` in the page — a block inside a prerendered Ljós page is a prerender within the prerender, hydrated by the same `hydrate` (A27 spells this out).

### The site

`site/` wires the remark plugin into Astro's markdown (`harnesses` from the docs checkout `sync-docs` reads, prerenders from `scripts/codeblock-prerenders.mjs`), hydrates blocks from Starlight's Head on pages that have them, and prerenders in CI before the build (`mise run build:wasm-compiler` added). The site is built with Qt Quick Controls (`ControlsHost.qml`) and gives them to the compiler in the page, so Controls examples edit and run in the browser as they prerender at build; `ljos-web/compiler/modules` is exported for a page to extend the defaults that way. `pnpm --filter ljos-site test:codeblocks` builds the site from fixture docs **strictly** and holds the built page to: JS off = code + prerendered result; hydration, edit-keeps-state, broken edit inline, harness + ShellLoader examples live.

## What it proves (run locally, foreground, same commands as CI)

- `tests/codeblocks.spec.js` (20): contract/parse/splice/assemble/hash, qmlc check naming a broken block, **a `ShellLoader`/`Slot` example assembling and checking**, static HTML (and the committed test page being that HTML, not a copy), JS-off reading code+picture, hydration, edit-keeps-state (counter 3→colour change→still 3), broken edit keeps last good + inline `Main.qml:…`, harness snippet, group files editable, **editing `user/Shell.qml` keeps the app's state**, lazy mounting, exempt plain. The four committed picture PNGs were eyeballed.
- `site/tests/codeblocks.e2e.js` (2): same behaviour on a real Starlight build. Screenshots of the static and live built pages eyeballed.
- Full push gate on the rebased tree: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (23 suites ok), clippy `-D warnings`, `test:site` 104 (incl. the prerender lane's own spec after the canvas numbering change), `drop`/`live` 122 on both kernels, site pictures→prerenders + build + check-links (0 broken) + site tests 5 + fixture suite 2. **135 of the pinned docs' blocks prerender live** on the built site; 24 untagged stay plain. Built-page screenshots (JS off and live, incl. the Controls first-app counter) eyeballed.
- Measured against the docs lane's tree (`site2/docs-positioning`, which now has `docs/site/harness/` + tagged fences, via `LJOS_DOCS_DIR`, pin untouched): 271 fences → 165 distinct examples; **150 compile under `qmlc` today**; 101 exempt; 0 unknown. The 15 that do not: 8 `module "Ljos.Ui"/"Ljos.Layout" is not installed`, the rest single missing names/modules. Of the tagged examples, exactly 3 fail — the two on `start/index.md` + the `your-own-shell.md` shell group — all `import Ljos.Ui`.
- Also fixed: `compiler.spec` was red on main — the prerender merge added the `ljos-web/server` export without setting it aside as host-only; it joins that list here.

## DECISIONs

- DECISION: strict (every non-exempt block must compile) is a switch (`LJOS_CODEBLOCKS_STRICT=1`), never inferred from the docs tree — a docs pin must not by itself start failing this build. Tagged blocks (`harness=`/`file=`/`group=`/`before`) must compile always; untagged ones that don't stay plain and are counted in the build output. The fixture suite builds with strict on.
- DECISION: the site builds with Ljós's own control styles and no installed Qt (`styles: "ljos", qt: []`), as in CI: bundling the modules the in-page compiler may link must not depend on the building machine having a Qt (with one, Qt's own Imagine/Basic QML is compiled instead and does not pass `qmlc`).
- DECISION: no fake `QtQuick.Controls` mapping — the site gives real ones (above). On a page not built with them, a Controls example is reported at its import by the run check and left plain, never shown live-but-dead. Same for a `.ts` file imported by name from QML (compiler refuses; `.mjs` works — scripts still ride as editable group files).
- DECISION: the static half is the merged prerender (`renderToString` + `hydrate`), not a PNG from a headless browser and not `ljos render` — one path, the page's own markup. (This replaced an earlier PNG implementation mid-lane when #13 landed.) Cached by content hash; the manifest also records run failures so the embedding build leaves those blocks plain.
- DECISION: the editor is a plain labelled textarea (no syntax-overlay editor): the smallest keyboard/AT-honest surface; highlighting stays on the static code and on exempt blocks (the host's).

## Gaps (named, not hidden)

- **Dialect examples don't run yet**: `import Ljos.Ui` / `Ljos.Layout` / `Ljos.Controls` are not installed in ljos-web's compiler at this pin, so the docs' own-shell page examples check as not-installed. The machinery runs the same `ShellLoader`/`Slot`/`Contribution` API in the surface ljos-web speaks today (tests prove it); dialect e

author: alexhawat
body:
## Summary

Two agent-subprocess lifetime fixes. This is the first of two stacked PRs for wave W1.6 (agents lane). The second PR (failover classification, Codex auth, prompt transport, model ids) is based on this branch.

### W1.6-1: `MERGECRAFT_AGENT_TIMEOUT` now bounds a running, streaming agent (#1325)

- Before: every driver read stdout to EOF and only then called `wait_or_kill_process_group(timeout=agent_timeout)`. A CLI that kept emitting events ran to completion. Reproduced on `origin/main`: a 1 s cap with a child that streams for 5 s returned after 5.3 s.
- Now: `IdleWatchdog` takes a `deadline_s` counted from spawn. Its monitor thread checks it while the stream is still open and kills the process group when it passes. It also runs when the idle watchdog is disabled (`agentIdleTimeout: 0`). All four streaming drivers (Claude, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode CLI) pass `MERGECRAFT_AGENT_TIMEOUT`.
- A capped attempt returns `success=False`, error `"<label> timed out: it hit the wall-clock cap of Ns ..."`, and metadata `timeout=True, wall_clock_timeout=True, elapsed_seconds, cap_seconds` and `infra_reason=agent_wall_clock_timeout`, without `idle_timeout`. The existing chain logic treats `timeout` as retryable, the same as the old (unreachable) `"... CLI timed out"` text. Idle-stall reporting is unchanged. Because of the infra reason, the run reads as `infra_error`, as an idle stall does, never as a review that `failed`. This answers the reviewer finding; `tests/agents/test_agent_wall_clock_timeout.py` runs each driver's real result through `_classify_outcome`.
- Follow-up for the core lane: `main._promote_and_finalize_agent_result` copies the diagnostic into `tool_state.agent_diagnostic` only when `idle_timeout` is set. So a wall-clock diagnostic does not yet reach `run_metrics.agent_diagnostic` or the ledger's stall line. That is in `main.py`, outside this lane.
- Test: `tests/agents/test_agent_wall_clock_timeout.py`. It runs a real child process in its own session for each driver (`ids=claude/codex/gemini/opencode`) under a 1 s cap and asserts the driver returns in under 3.5 s, reports a timeout, and leaves the child dead. It also has unit cases for a deadline hit while events keep arriving, a deadline with the idle watchdog disabled, and idle stalls still reported as idle. All 4 driver cases fail on `origin/main`.

### W1.6-2: a timed-out secondary or file-group reviewer is killed, not abandoned (#1326, partial)

- Before: the roster `asyncio.wait_for` cancelled the coroutine, but the driver's `asyncio.to_thread` worker and its `Popen` kept running.
- Now: `agents/shared.py` adds `AgentProcessScope`, bound through a `ContextVar` that `asyncio.to_thread` copies into the worker. `spawn_agent_cli` adds every child to the current scope. `AgentImpl.run` closes the scope when the run returns, raises or is cancelled. Closing kills the process group of every child that is still alive (only live children, so a recycled pid is never signalled) and refuses any later spawn in that scope, so a worker thread that outlives the cancel cannot start a resume turn. This covers every `AgentImpl.run` caller: roster, file-group fan-out, and the main run.
- Test: `tests/review/test_roster_execution.py::test_a_timed_out_secondary_is_killed_not_abandoned` runs the real `run_pending_roster_reviewers` with a 0.5 s timeout around a real `AgentImpl`. Its `to_thread` worker spawns `sleep 30` through the real `spawn_agent_cli`. The test asserts the child is dead and the follow-up spawn is refused. It fails on `origin/main`.
- **Not done (why this is `Refs`, not `Closes`):**
  - *MCP session revocation.* All reviewers share one MCP bearer, and `X-MergeCraft-Agent-Id` is tracing-only (`mcp/server.py`). Refusing a timed-out reviewer's later calls needs per-dispatch tokens in `mcp/`, which is outside this lane. Killing the process before the timeout is recorded removes the caller. Only a tool call already in flight at the kill can still land.
  - *Cursor Cloud remote cancel (AGT-F13).* `integrations/cursor_cloud/client.py` has no stop/cancel call, and I could not confirm the Cursor `/v1/agents` stop endpoint from the repo. I did not add an endpoint I could not verify.

## Changelog

- **Fixed:** `MERGECRAFT_AGENT_TIMEOUT` now kills an agent CLI that is still streaming when the cap passes, counted from spawn. Before, the cap started only after the CLI closed its output, so a busy agent was never bounded by it.
- **Fixed:** A secondary or file-group reviewer that hits its timeout now has its CLI process group killed. Before, it was left running and kept spending tokens after it was recorded as timed out.

## Out of lane

None.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest tests/agents tests/review -p no:cacheprovider -q -n auto`: 1894 passed, 1 skipped (pinned opencode CLI not installed)
- `uv run ruff check` / `uv run ruff format --check` on `src/mergecraft/agents` and the touched tests: clean
- `uv run mypy src/mergecraft/agents/shared.py src/mergecraft/agents/activity_watchdog.py`: clean
- Red check: both new test groups fail on `origin/main` sources (drivers ran 5.3 s past a 1 s cap; roster child still running after the timeout).

Closes #1325
Refs #1326

author: csdev19
body: ## What this does Blur redactions now blur. The renderer's Content-Security-Policy blocked the `fetch(blob:)` that the Blur preview uses to read the pixels it blurs, so on a fresh capture or an added image the rectangle drew its handles and nothing else. The Redact tool also gets a tooltip and an accessible description that say what it is for. ## Why Owner QA on `main` at `e170edb3`: Redact, Style = Blur, drag over text, and the text stays fully readable. Root cause: `useRedactionTile` → `loadImage` (`redaction-preview.ts:54`) reads the source with `fetch(src)`. That path came in with `9d5caae6` and was only checked against `kaipu-media://` vault URLs. A fresh capture or an added image is a `blob:` URL, and the policy in `index.html` had no `connect-src`, so `default-src 'self'` refused the fetch. The tile never decoded and the preview never drew. The fix adds `connect-src 'self' blob:`. Runtime evidence: in headless Chrome, `fetch()` of a `blob:` URL fails under the old policy and succeeds under the new one. `annotations/redaction-preview.csp.test.ts` fails on `main` and passes here. ## What changes for you - Blur redactions on new captures and added images now show the blur on the canvas. - Hovering Redact shows "Redact — hide sensitive info" (es: "Censurar — oculta información sensible"). - Nothing else changes. Solid redaction and the export path don't use this fetch. ## What to review 1. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/index.html:9` — `connect-src 'self' blob:`.** Decide whether this is the narrowest grant. It allows fetch/XHR to same-origin and to `blob:` only: no `data:`, no remote hosts. Before this change, `connect-src` fell back to `default-src 'self'`. 2. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/screenshots/annotations/redaction-preview.csp.test.ts` — the test checks the policy string, not Electron's rendering.** It would have failed on `main`. It does not prove the pixels blur in the real app (see "What I did not verify"). 3. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/screenshots/annotations/annotation-toolbar.tsx:63` — tooltip copy.** Copy choice only. **Safe to skim:** the i18n pair in `packages/i18n/messages/{en,es}.json` (two keys, key-checked). ## Proof | Criterion | What was done | How to check it | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Reproduced: a failing test (or recorded repro in the real app) shows a Blur redaction leaving the covered pixels unchanged | CSP test written first (`582827a4`); it fails on `main` because the policy blocks `blob:` fetches | `git checkout 582827a4 && bun run test redaction-preview.csp` → red | Commit `582827a4`, then green at `1ea6ab03` | | Root cause identified with runtime evidence and written in the PR | Missing `connect-src` blocks `fetch(blob:)` in `loadImage` | "Why" above | Headless Chrome fetch: blocked under the old policy, allowed under the new one | | A Blur redaction visibly blurs the covered area on the canvas, while it is selected and after deselecting, and in the exported/copied PNG | Policy fixed | Step 1 below | **not verified** in the real app: the catalog's `redaction-blur` state opens a vault item (`kaipu-media://`), which never hit the bug. Before and after are byte-identical. | | Solid redaction still works as before | Not touched; full suite green | Step 2 below | 540 files / 6996 tests passed | | The Redact tool explains itself before use: tooltip/label names it as hiding sensitive information (e.g. "Redact — hide sensitive info"), localized like the other tool labels | `toolRedactTip` / `toolRedactHint`, en + es | Step 3 below | Diff of `annotation-toolbar.tsx`, i18n keys | | Real-app before/after screenshots in the PR | Catalog run on the Mac mini | — | **not verified**: see row 3. The only state the catalog has uses a vault source, so its before/after cannot show this bug. | ## Decisions - **Fix the policy, not the loader.** Options: (a) add `connect-src 'self' blob:`; (b) decode blob sources through an `` instead of `fetch`. Taken: (a). The loader reads bytes on purpose (comment at `redaction-preview.ts:37`), and (b) would add a second decode path. - **Copy "Redact — hide sensitive info".** It is the example from the ticket. es uses "Censurar". - **Name the Blur limit in the Redact hint (CodeRabbit, `90a3d796`).** Options: (a) leave the hint as written; (b) say Blur keeps a trace of the original colors. Taken: (b), because `redactionNote` in the same catalog already says only Solid hides content for certain, so the hint contradicted it. ## Verify it yourself **Setup** ```bash git switch feature/niw2-724-image-editor-redact-with-blur-does-not-blur && bun install cd apps/kaipu-record unset ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE # a T3 terminal sets it and dev crashes with isPackaged undefined KAIPU_FLAG_OVERRIDES='{"image-canvas":true,"image-inspect":true,"image-text":true}' bun run dev ``` **1. Blur on a fresh capture (the bug).** Take a new screenshot, or paste an image into the editor. Pick Redact, Style = Blur, and drag over text. Expect: the text is blurred while the box is selected, still blurred after you click away, and blurred in Copy / Export. Broken if: you see only the handles and the text stays readable (the `main` behavior). **2. Solid.** Same, with Style = Solid. Expect: an opaque box, as before. **3. Tooltip.** Hover the Redact tool. Expect: "Redact — hide sensitive info" ("Censurar — oculta información sensible" in Spanish). ## What I did not verify - The blur in the real Electron app on a `blob:` source: no catalog state redacts over a fresh capture. Step 1 is the check. - The exported/copied PNG with a Blur redaction over a `blob:` source. ## Checks - `bun run test` → exit 0, 540 files / 6996 tests passed - `bun run check-types` → exit 0 - `bun run lint` → exit 0, 0 errors - After `90a3d796` (copy only, two i18n strings): `packages/i18n` `bun run test` → exit 0, 5 files / 22 tests; annotations directory `vitest run` → exit 0, 21 files / 355 tests; push hook `verify-local` passed. The full suite was not re-run on this head. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * In canvas mode, the blur tool is labeled “Redact” and includes guidance on hiding sensitive image content with a solid cover or blur. The guidance notes that blur may retain traces of original colors and that redactions are permanent once saved. * **Bug Fixes** * Redaction previews now display images loaded from blob URLs correctly.

author: maks-sredniawa
body:
Closes #3 — A monitor that rejects writes on a fresh detection no longer makes every preset pick detect again (`extension/lib/monitors.js`). A display that another program holds, such as through the `ddcci` kernel module, is reported as busy instead of silent, and the notification names it separately, also when no monitor answers at all (`extension/lib/ddc.js`, `extension/extension.js`). A busy display does not make every pick detect again: it stays skipped until the monitor layout changes, so unloading `ddcci` mid-session takes effect after a monitor is plugged or unplugged, or the session restarts. Silent, invalid and DDC-disabled monitors are still re-detected on the next pick, since they may be waking up or have just had DDC/CI turned on. In preferences, the active preset's tick follows its row through a rename, and is cleared while the row's name is empty or duplicated (`extension/lib/presets.js`, `extension/prefs.js`).

## Screenshots
- Not captured. The changed notification text and preset tick live in a GNOME Shell extension and its preferences window, which need a running GNOME Shell session with DDC/CI monitors. No such app is reachable from this environment.

## Testing
- `make test`: 24/24, with new cases for the detection count, a newly failing monitor, busy and DDC-disabled displays, reuse of a detection with a busy display, no monitor answering because every one is busy, and the preset tick.
- The real `prefs.js` was driven in a virtual X display (GTK4/Adw, in-memory settings) by typing into its rows: a name clash clears the tick, removing the clash restores it on the same row, rename/empty/retype and a pick from the shell are followed. All steps pass; the same script against `main` fails at the first clash and leaves the tick on Day.

## Caveats
- The `DDC_disabled` header format the parser matches was inferred from the strings in the ddcutil 2.2.5 binary, not seen in live `ddcutil detect` output. `Busy display` is also present in that binary.
- The new busy-display notification sentence and the `extension/extension.js` change were syntax-checked only, not seen in a running shell.

author: eodgooch
body:
Closes #5

## Summary

`POST /api/match` now runs the real pipeline instead of `stub_match`:

```text
run_match(rec, req, *, model_factory, judge=no_judge)        pipeline/match_run.py
  _parse_patient            # parse_patient (#4); FHIR-only -> stub patient (HACK)
  search_cached_trials      # trial_search.py: recruiting, within radius, nearest 20
  match_trial  x N          # Semaphore(8) over trials
    compile_study           # cached; uncompilable trial -> failed trial:<nct> step, dropped
    evaluate_trial          # evaluate.py
      evaluate_criterion
        predicate?  rule_verdict   -> rule:<nct>:<id> event, Verdict.trace_event_id = it
        else        judge(...)     -> no_judge: unknown, skipped rule event   <- #6 plugs in here
    build_match             # rank.py: tier + counts
  rank_matches              # tier, then fewer unknowns, then distance
```

Outcomes are relative to eligibility, and exclusions are inverted in `outcome_for`. A missing fact gives `unknown`, never `fail`.

```diff
 <RunView>
   <TracePanel>
-  <Results>  one line per trial
+  <MatchResults>                tiers: Likely eligible / Needs info / Ineligible
+    <TrialCard>                 collapsible, counts, distance
+      <CriterionRow verdict>    icon + quote + evidence + rationale (badge slot for #6)
```

Seam for #6: `Judge = (nct_id, criterion, facts, rec) -> Verdict`, passed as `run_match(..., judge=...)`.

**Flagged for review:**
- **Parsing:** merged main after #4 landed, so a note is parsed for real by `parse_patient`. A FHIR-only request still gets `STUB_PATIENT` (HACK(demo), carried over from #4).
- **HACK(demo):** `condition` is recorded in the trace but doesn't filter. The cache was seeded for T2D/CKD, and the cached fields have no conditions module.
- **Product call:** a condition or med that the facts don't list gives `unknown` in both directions. So an exclusion `has X` is *not* a pass just because the note is silent. This is the conservative reading of SPEC's "`unknown` means the data is missing", but it pushes most trials to `needs_info` until the judge lands. Reverting it is a one-line change in `_membership`.
- Without an API key, only trials already in the compile cache can be matched. The others show as failed `trial:<nct>` steps and the run still finishes `done`.
- `GET /api/runs/{id}` was already wired. Its matches are now real, and the response schema is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `test_stub_match_streams_five_trace_events_then_done`. A fixed fake trial, and its verdicts pointed at one shared fake event.
  **After:** `tests/test_match_run.py`, which uses the fixture trials in the ctgov cache with a warm compile cache and no network:
  ```text
  demo patient -> 3 trials, sorted by (tier, unknowns), 0 LLM calls        PASS
  every verdict.trace_event_id -> rule:<nct>:<id> under trial:<nct>        PASS
  NCT07271186: T2D pass, HbA1c 8.4 in 6.5-10 pass x2, UACR missing -> unknown x2   PASS
  uncached trial + no key -> skipped, run done                              PASS
  radius 50 -> only the Sacramento site                                     PASS
  ```
- `tests/test_evaluate.py`: a missing lab gives `unknown`, not `fail`; exclusion inversion; unit mismatch gives `unknown`; whole-word name match; judge seam. `tests/test_rank.py`: tier edges (2 unknowns is likely, 3 is needs_info) and the full ordering.
- `make check`: ruff, mypy, **129 passed, 2 deselected**, web typecheck and lint all green.
- On the fixtures, all 3 nearby trials come out `needs_info` (6-20 unknowns, 0 fails), as expected for rule-only verdicts on a patient with 4 facts. The match page has not been checked in a browser.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No schema changes and no migrations. `web/lib/api-types.ts` only gains docstring descriptions.

**Blast Radius:** match-run

`/api/match` results and their trace shape change; nothing else consumes them yet. #4 and #6 will touch `match_run.py` (the parse swap) and `evaluate.py` (the judge). `stub_data.stub_matches` is now unused but was left in place to avoid conflicts with #4.

**HELD for the owner's sign-off.** The charts brief (§11, WP5) says the task corpus and grading adapter stay within the charts repository and that edits to sibling repositories are outside the assignment. This PR puts them here instead, in the harness that already runs live corpora. Please decide before merging whether the corpus belongs here or in opencode-charts.

## What it adds
- `cases/charts`: task corpus v1 with 13 tasks (sets `corpus`, `create` 7, `revise` 6), plus 2 `scripted` probes. The tasks are long labels in a narrow panel, explicit and ambiguous aggregation, count vs measure, misspelt fields, a brand theme, empty data, light→dark, inline→presentation→inline, adding x zoom, adding scatter brushing, an unsupported pie zoom, and a cosmetic change after the source CSV changed. Every item is decided by code. `evals.lock` is at epoch 2.
- `worlds/charts`: synthetic CSVs, and a build that saves the revision tasks' charts with the build under test, through its tools RPC on a stock host, with no model.
- `src/grade/adapters/`: per-plugin facts for `state:` clauses, derived from a run's own files. The Charts adapter recomputes each saved chart's group values from the rows it captured. The adapters are included in the grader hash.
- `packs/charts` sync (`charts.update`), `docs/charts.md`, `test/charts-corpus.test.mjs`.

## Evidence
- `node --test test/*.test.mjs`: 258 pass, 0 fail, 9 skips that were already there.
- Scripted model only (`--scripted --auth none`, containers): both probes pass. The 13 tasks run, trace and grade with 63/63 items testable, and all 13 fail, as they should with no tool calls.
- **No live model has run this corpus.** Agent success is unmeasured.

author: wildm-an
body:
## Summary

The play-button daemon listens on the Tailscale address since 0.1.74, but Windows Firewall dropped the connections of the other computers. A TCP connection to port 8765 of the remote computer got no answer, while `tailscale ping` worked.

- **Check** (`firewall.rs`, no administrator rights): after a start with Tailscale, the app looks for an enabled allow rule "Harness remote daemon" for the port, and for enabled inbound block rules of the daemon program. A block rule wins over an allow rule. Windows makes one when someone closes its firewall dialog.
- **Fix:** when the port is blocked, an outer PowerShell runs `Start-Process -Verb RunAs`, so Windows shows its administrator prompt one time. The elevated script removes the block rules of the daemon program and adds the allow rule: TCP 8765, inbound, only from `100.64.0.0/10`. The scripts go through `-EncodedCommand`, so the paths need no shell quoting.
- **Page:** "Checking Windows Firewall.", then a warning with "Allow in Windows Firewall" while the port stays blocked, for example after a closed prompt. When the page opens and the daemon already runs, the app checks with no prompt.
- **Other platforms:** macOS and Linux report "open", and nothing changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy --lib --tests` (one old warning in `browser.rs`)
- [x] `cargo test --lib firewall`: quoting, the Tailscale-only rule, the UTF-16 encoding, and the read-only check against the real firewall
- [x] The read-only check by hand: it found no allow rule and no block rules, so it reports "blocked"
- [x] `tsc -b` and `vitest run`: 562 passed
- [ ] On the remote Windows computer: play button with Tailscale, then accept the administrator prompt, then connect from another computer through Tailscale
- [ ] Close the prompt: the warning and "Allow in Windows Firewall" show

author: zubair-io
body:
Maple Cloud in the Android system Files app and every app's document picker: a production `DocumentsProvider` (`app.justmaple.aperture.documents`).

**Why:** #5836 — the Android counterpart of the Apple File Provider, on the same server contract.

## What changed
- `documents/MapleDocumentsProvider` + store/writes/API/caches: one root per connected server, its libraries, unified folder listings in cursor pages, `queryDocument`, path-keyed document IDs. IDs reject traversal and hidden segments, and `isChildDocument` covers tree grants.
- **Listings:** the provider never sends `stack=1`, so it always gets the unfolded listing: a RAW+JPEG pair is two documents and `createDocument` treats the JPEG's name as taken. A paged folder answers its first page with `EXTRA_LOADING` and finishes in the background, then notifies the folder.
- **Kinds:** a file's kind (photo/media/plain file/sidecar) comes only from the server listing. `file-meta` answers size and mtime only; an item not listed yet (persisted URI, tree grant after restart) is classified by listing its folder, never by extension.
- **Open:** `file-meta` stat, then the file streams to disk in 64 KiB chunks. The client gets a seekable descriptor; nothing is buffered whole. Concurrent opens of one version share one download. `CancellationSignal` drops the socket mid-transfer and leaves no partial file, for callers that hand the signal to the provider (`ContentProviderClient.openFile`; see CI below). Downloads are cached with a 512 MiB LRU across servers.
- **Thumbnails:** the server's 512 px AVIF through the app's existing ETag-revalidated cloud derivative cache, in the shared 64 MiB budget. On Android 10/11 the core converts it to PNG (`NativeBridge.cachePng`). Cache trimming moved from `PhotoLibrary` to `CacheTrim.kt` so the provider shares it.
- **Writes (where the server allows):**
  - Create folder uses mkdir.
  - Create or write a file goes through a durable pending-upload journal and uploads when the writer closes. The journal is keyed by **account** (origin + the access token's `sub`): signing back in as the same user resumes it, and another account on the same server never sees or sends it.
  - Upload outcomes: unreachable / 401 after refresh / 429 pause that account's queue; 408 / 5xx defer only that record; any other rejection (403, 400, 413, …) is terminal for that record, which stays listed with the summary "Not uploaded: <reason>" (rewrite retries, delete discards), and later records still upload. A writer that closes with an error marks its record failed, so torn bytes never upload. A writer that reopens a record mid-upload keeps it queued.
  - Rename: folders use move, files use relocate, and photos use their asset route so sidecars follow.
  - Delete is always trash: `intent=trash`, with 409 `trashed` treated as success.
  - `removeDocument` is supported.
  - Originals (everything the server lists under `images`, including GIF/PSB/MXF/BRAW) and existing `.xmp` files are read-only, before and after any read. A sidecar name collision (the server's 409) keeps both files and never replaces one.
  - Folder delete is not offered: `trash-folder` only trashes assets and the server has no way to remove a folder.
  - A photo the server has not indexed yet refuses rename/delete, because the plain-file route would separate it from its sidecar.
- **Change feed:** `/api/changes` is polled every 5 s while the provider is in use and stops after 10 min idle. The first poll adopts the journal head. A 409 resumes at `current` (never 0) and invalidates that server. Each change row calls `notifyChange` on its folder and document URIs. There is no FCM: the app has no push and the server only sends APNs.
- **Auth:** uses the app's Keystore credentials and `CloudHttp`. Refresh/logout now share one **process-wide** lane, because the app and the provider hold separate clients and refresh tokens rotate. Sign-out clears only that server's provider caches and cursor. Signed-out, unreachable or failed listings throw; they never return an empty cursor.
- **Tests/CI:**
  - JVM `CloudDocumentContractTest`: IDs, tree membership, flags/MIME/naming (incl. kdc/dcr/mos/rwl), and feed cursor/409 rules.
  - JVM `CloudDocumentWritesTest` (in-process server on a new `CloudTransport` seam that `CloudHttp` implements): listing kinds survive a read and classify unlisted items; RAW+JPEG pair = two documents and create never takes the JPEG's name; per-account journal; 403 terminal + later uploads still go; 401 pauses; torn writer never uploads; reopened record outlives an in-flight success; `EXTRA_LOADING` paging; concurrent opens download once.
  - Device `CloudDocumentsProviderTest` and `CloudDocumentsWriteTest` run against a **real `src/api` server** started by `scripts/with-cloud-api.sh`: fresh SQLite and library, `MAPLE_DEV_AUTH=1`, `adb reverse`.
  - The Android workflow now installs bun and the API deps, and `test-device-ci.sh` runs through the harness.
- **Docs:** `docs/android-documents-provider.md` (indexed in docs/README.md), a provider section in docs/caching.md, and src/android/README.md.

Local folder libraries are not re-exported: their own providers already show them, and proxying those grants would widen access.

## Review fixes (Fable review of #5873)
- P1 kind overwrite: `stat()` no longer classifies by extension; a read keeps the listing's kind, and uncached entries are classified by their folder's listing, so a GIF/PSB/MXF/BRAW never gets `FLAG_SUPPORTS_WRITE` and `openForWrite` refuses it.
- P2 journal: keyed by account; 403 terminal; one rejected record no longer blocks later uploads.
- Should-fix: unclean close clears `ready` and marks the record failed; upload success no longer removes a reopened record (generation check); permanently failed uploads show "Not uploaded: …" instead of looking saved.
- Nits: `EXTRA_LOADING` for paged listings; single-flight downloads; MIME types for kdc/dcr/mos/rwl.
- Cross-PR with #5850: resolved by the binding contract that the server folds only on `stack=1`; this provider never sends it (tested).

## Verification (local, this Mac, `src/android`)
- `./gradlew assembleDebug assembleDebugAndroidTest testDebugUnitTest lintDebug`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL; 150 JVM tests, 0 failures, 0 skips (CloudDocumentWritesTest 7/7, CloudDocumentContractTest 5/5).
- Fail-before (mutation runs, then restored): re-introducing the old behaviours — stat overwriting the kind with `File`, 403 in the retry/pause set, unclean close not failing the record, success always removing, synchronous full listing, no single-flight — fails the kind, 403/continue, torn/reopen, paging and single-flight cases; re-keying the journal by origin fails the per-account case. The pair test passes either way: it pins the unfolded-listing contract (`stack=1` never sent), which already held.
- Device: `scripts/with-cloud-api.sh ./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest` filtered to `CloudDocumentsProviderTest` + `CloudDocumentsWriteTest` on a local API 36 arm64 emulator against the real `src/api`: 6/6 passed, including mid-transfer cancellation. The first local attempt failed `createsWritesRenamesAndTrashesThroughTheServer` with HTTP 500 "not under root" on the rewrite: on macOS `TMPDIR` ends in `/`, so the harness registered `…/T//maple-android-api.*`. `with-cloud-api.sh` now canonicalises the work dir (`pwd -P`); CI (Linux `/tmp`) never hit this. The rest of the 95-test device suite was not run locally; CI runs it.
- `tools/check-file-budget.sh` / `check-budget-headroom.sh`: 0 violations; Prettier on the changed docs.

## CI (previous runs)
- `android-build` failed at `:app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` on `cancellingADownloadStopsTheTransferAndCachesNothing` ("expected OperationCanceledException … nothing was thrown") in runs 43168713303 and 43178904585, finishing in ~1–2 s. Root cause is the platform, not the link speed: `ContentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r", signal)` routes `"r"` through `openTypedAssetFileDescriptor(uri, "*/*

author: imshubham22apr-gif
body:
## Description
In Zarf v1.0.0 (`#5624`), the `--storage-class` flag was removed from `zarf init` in favor of per-component values configuration (`registry.persistence.storageClass`, `gitServer.persistence.storageClass`), and `State.StorageClass` was removed.

As noted in the v1.0.0 release documentation:
> *"New deployments now use the cluster's default storage class. Upgrades continue to use the existing storage class."*

To support this without breaking existing PVCs (which are immutable in Kubernetes), the Helm template in `packages/init/v1alpha1/zarf-registry/chart/templates/pvc.yaml` performs a dynamic cluster lookup:
```yaml
{{- /* Preserve an immutable storage class on upgrade; new claims use the Kubernetes default. */}}
{{- $claim := lookup "v1" "PersistentVolumeClaim" .Release.Namespace (include "docker-registry.fullname" .) }}
{{- if and $claim (hasKey $claim.spec "storageClassName") }}
  storageClassName: {{ $claim.spec.storageClassName | quote }}
{{- end }}
```

However, the existing end-to-end upgrade test in `src/test/e2e/20_zarf_init_test.go` (which initializes a cluster with `v1alpha1` and upgrades it to `v1beta1`) verified labels, services, secrets, and pods, but did not assert that the registry PVC's `storageClassName` and bound `volumeName` are preserved across the upgrade.

This PR adds assertions in `TestZarfInit` to capture the registry PVC's `spec.storageClassName` and `spec.volumeName` before upgrading and verify that both remain identical after the `v1beta1` init package upgrade.

## Reproduction / User Scenario
When upgrading existing clusters from previous Zarf releases to v1.0.0+, an accidental modification or omission of the PVC's storage class during Helm upgrade would trigger Kubernetes PVC immutability errors or attempt to detach/recreate the storage volume backing the internal Docker registry.

## Verification and Tests
Compiled and verified the e2e test suite:
```bash
go test -c -o test-e2e.exe ./src/test/e2e
```
(Compilation succeeds cleanly).

Verified unit tests across internal and external template rendering packages:
```bash
go test -v -count=1 ./src/internal/packager/template/...
go test -v -count=1 ./src/pkg/template/...
```
All pass cleanly.

## Related Issue
Follows up on [#5624](https://github.com/zarf-dev/zarf/issues/5624) and ensures regression coverage for storage class preservation during `zarf init` upgrades.

## Checklist
- [x] Tested changes locally with unit/compilation tests
- [x] Commit message follows Conventional Commits format

author: zxch3n
body:
Malformed change headers can make `import` and the checksum-free metadata pass in `import_batch` reserve tens of gigabytes before decoding a value. The issue's 94-byte update requested 34,359,738,360 bytes and aborted under a capped allocator.

This bounds change counts by explicit length bytes, validates dependency counts against the peer table, sums with checked arithmetic, and bounds the dependency total by the bits needed for its counter column. Metadata decoding also checks the count against the cached header before allocating. Checked integer conversions prevent length/counter truncation.

The three delta-of-delta columns used here (dependency counters, Lamports, timestamps) now use checked bit reads and arithmetic, since the upstream decoder also has unchecked reads on truncated prefixes. The wire format is unchanged. Batch metadata continues to skip the checksum for sorting; decoder bounds protect that path and crafted inputs with recomputed checksums without changing partial-success semantics.

Regression coverage includes all six issue reproduction paths in child processes capped at 1 MiB per allocation, unchanged document state/history after rejection, continued editing, and a later valid import. Module tests cover single-change oversized dependency counts, compressed dependency-total amplification, cached-header count mismatch, delta prefix widths, truncations, mutations, and arithmetic overflow. Includes a `loro-crdt` patch changeset and encoding context.

Validation:
- RED before the fix: capped regression child aborted requesting 34,359,738,360 bytes.
- `cargo test -p loro --test import_header_allocation --test import_batch_detailed --test contracts`: 187 passed, 0 ignored (allocation test exercises six child-process cases).
- `cargo test -p loro-internal --lib`: 508 passed, 4 existing ignored tests.
- `cargo clippy -p loro-internal -p loro --lib --tests`: passed with existing repository warnings.
- `cargo check -p loro-internal --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: passed; WASM runtime behavior was not separately executed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.

Commit `cdc216b7` contains the fix. A separate formatting-only commit resolves pre-existing rustfmt differences in six files so the requested workspace format check passes.

author: den-run-ai
body:
## Problem

`float` runs 37% slower in AOT since #1268 (#1300). listguard's loop copy gives `Point.__init__` a second call site; LLVM inlines an internal function's only call almost regardless of size, but each of two only if cheap, so the constructor stays out of line.

## Change

In the copy, a call of a function the program names nowhere else, as a callee or a value, is `alwaysinline`, and the callee's ops count toward listguard's 400-op limit. The loop's own call then is the callee's last, which LLVM inlines too. Coroutines and exported functions are excluded. A new `NAME.inline` check-IR fixture pins marked, unmarked and uncopied cases. Refs #1300. Prepared with Claude Code assistance.

## Validation

Local x86-64, LLVM 18. float AOT, 11 interleaved runs on one CPU: `0ec827ac` 35.03 ms, main 45.09, this PR 34.68. No `Point.__init__` symbol remains; instructions 355M → 344M (350M before #1268).

`irsame` against main (shared home, identical `lib/` and runtime): besides the new probe, 3 of 4,450 programs differ, each by one `alwaysinline`. Pass: `make` fixed points, `check-ir` (2,540), `check-runtime`, `lint`, `typecheck`, pass-contract and inspection tests, optimizations area JIT+AOT (256/256), affected cases GC-stressed. The fixture fails on main. Lean checks not run locally.

author: autonomyai-local[bot]
body:
## Summary
Adds one new self-contained component, `TestCard`, that renders a static replica of an attached Figma panel — a dark "UI magician Agent" settings card with an "Add New Design" section (two labelled inputs, two buttons) and a "Recent Breakdowns" heading. It was built as a smoke test of the Figma-to-component path: the goal was to prove a design frame can be turned into a component that renders, not to add product UI. Nothing in the app imports it and no route links to it, so there is no user-facing impact on existing screens.

---

## Key Changes
- Added `TestCard`, a prop-less, stateless component that approximates the Figma frame; its root element carries `id="testElem"` as a stable handle for the smoke test.
- Styled entirely with Tailwind utilities, using arbitrary-value brackets for the panel's off-system colours (dark surface, rust-orange buttons) because this repo's theme replaces the default palettes rather than extending them.
- No existing file was modified.

---

## Files Changed
- `src/app/components/test-card/TestCard.tsx`
  - New component. Named export `TestCard`, no props, no state, no data, no imports from app code.
  - Root `<div id="testElem">`; layout, spacing, radius and type in Tailwind; icons from `react-icons/fi` (`FiSettings`, `FiInfo`, `FiChevronUp`).

---

## Implementation Notes
- **Placement is load-bearing.** `tailwind.config.js` sets `content: ["./src/app/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}"]`, so a file placed outside `src/app/` would generate no CSS at all and the card would render unstyled with no error. It therefore sits at `src/app/components/test-card/`, following the repo's folder-per-component layout.
- **Why the colours are literals.** `theme.colors`, `theme.fontFamily` and `theme.boxShadow` are full overrides in this repo (not `extend`), so stock palette classes (`bg-gray-800`), `font-sans` and `shadow-xl` compile to nothing. The Figma panel's palette is off-system (dark surface, rust-orange buttons) and none of the semantic tokens express it; adding tokens would have meant editing `tailwind.config.js` or `src/app/styles/app.css`, which the request ruled out. The colours are therefore written as arbitrary values — `bg-[#1e1e1e]`, `text-[#d6d6d6]`, `border-[#6f6f6f]`, `bg-[#a34a1c]` — a deliberate, one-file exception to the repo's no-hardcoded-hex rule, contained to a component nothing imports.
- Typography uses the repo's `font-primary*` families rather than `font-sans`, which does not resolve here.
- The gear and info icons are decorative (`aria-hidden`), not interactive controls: the card is static and no settings behaviour exists behind them. Inputs are paired with `<label htmlFor>` and the repo's global focus ring is left intact.
- Approximate spacing, colour and typography were explicitly requested; the render is intentionally not pixel-accurate to the design. The design's exported assets and style guide were not available in the build environment, so values were approximated from the reference image.

---

## How to Test
1. `pnpm install && pnpm run storybook` — the script rebuilds `src/app/styles/app-compiled.css` first, which is gitignored and therefore not in this PR.
2. In Storybook, open **Components → TestCard → Default**.
3. Verify the card renders populated: the "UI magician Agent" title row with a gear icon, the truncated "From entire frame to a singl…" row, "Add New Design" with two labelled inputs, the two rust-orange buttons ("Awesome", "Prepare"), and the "Recent Breakdowns" heading.
4. Confirm an element with `id="testElem"` is present and has visible content, with no error overlay.
5. Differences in spacing, colour and type versus the Figma frame are expected — pixel fidelity was explicitly out of scope.

---

## Compatibility & Notes
- No new dependencies: `react-icons` is already in `package.json`.
- No breaking changes. Nothing imports the component and no route renders it, so it cannot affect existing screens.
- Only visible through Storybook; the app has no route for it.

---

## QA Checklist
- [x] Core functionality works as expected — the component renders with all its content present.
- [x] Visual/UI changes render correctly — rendered and checked once on Storybook.
- [ ] Hover/active/interactive states behave properly — not applicable: the card is static and its icons are decorative.
- [ ] Responsive behavior verified — not applicable: this is a fixed-width replica of a desktop panel and responsive behaviour was out of scope.
- [ ] Accessibility considerations addressed — labels, `aria-hidden` on decorative icons and the intact global focus ring are in place; a full accessibility pass was out of scope.
- [x] No unintended side effects or regressions — a single new file that nothing imports.

---

author: jonathan308
body:
SUPER-SLOT (0.10.12 fold): a Super request that arrives while the previous request's answer has ended, but its settlement has not, now **waits up to 1 s** for that settlement and is served. Before, it got an instant 429 `queue_full` (a coordinator bounce). Mid-answer arrivals are still refused at once. Targets `release/candidate-0.10.12d` (`0b52123a18`).

## Where Super's slots are released (file:line at `0b52123a18`)

Two slots, each refusing with 429 `queue_full`:

1. **Owner admission** (`NemotronSuperLocalBridgeBuilder.Owner.admitLocalRequest()`): text and images. **Corrected after review:** the managed slot admits **up to 8 requests at once** (`defaultConcurrentRequests`, halved by the load fit when memory is short). One at a time is only the qualification hook's default (`DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MAX_CONCURRENT`). Checked at `NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift:122-124`; returned in the request task's `defer` (`:173`), after `relay.complete()`.
2. **Image binding `active`** (`NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.swift:92,131`): one media request at a time, on every owner. This is the slot that bounces in production: since 11-11 14:00Z there were 5,864 image `queue_full` refusals against 1 for text. It is cleared in `settle`'s `defer` after the cleanup task. That task waits for the work's `execute`. `execute` reads the bridge stream, which closes at the engine terminal, **before native retirement** (`EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift:226-231`). It then waits for `usage.waitForTerminalObservation()` (native settlement), and the cleanup releases the media charges.

**End of one image request, in order:**

1. engine terminal
2. `.info` reaches the relay
3. the stream closes
4. native settlement
5. media charges released
6. `active = nil`
7. `relay.complete()` (the end the coordinator sees)
8. owner admission returned

On Super, then, the coordinator sees the end only after the slot is free. The provider-side window runs **from the engine terminal to the end of settlement**. A request that arrives in it is refused at once. Such a request either was stacked by the coordinator while the previous image was still visibly in flight, or follows a cancel or timeout whose settlement is still running.

## Before / after

**Behavior** (one Super Mac; the default owner serves one request, the image binding one media request):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    A1["next request arrives"] --> B1{"slot free?"}
    B1 -- yes --> C1["served"]
    B1 -- "no: previous one mid-answer" --> D1["429 queue_full at once"]
    B1 -- "no: previous answer ended, settlement running" --> D1
  end
  subgraph After
    A2["next request arrives"] --> B2{"slot free?"}
    B2 -- yes --> C2["served"]
    B2 -- "no: previous one mid-answer" --> D2["429 queue_full at once, unchanged"]
    B2 -- "no: previous answer ended, settlement running" --> W2{"settled within 1 s?"}
    W2 -- yes --> C2
    W2 -- no --> D3["429 queue_full after at most 1 s"]
  end
```

**Code:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph Before
    H1["SuperHTTPEngine.streamChatCompletion"] --> O1["Owner.admitLocalRequest: refuse when full"]
    O1 --> R1["text binding, or image binding run / runEncoded"]
    R1 --> G1["binding: guard active == nil else busy"]
    T1["request task defer"] --> F1["Owner.finishLocalRequest"]
  end
  subgraph After
    H2["SuperHTTPEngine.streamChatCompletion"] --> O2["Owner.admitLocalRequest waitingUpTo finishingWait: polls while every admitted answer has ended"]
    O2 --> R2["text binding, or image binding run / runEncoded"]
    R2 --> G2["binding.admit: polls while the active request's AnswerEnded is set"]
    Y2["SuperImageHTTPRelay receives .info"] -- onAnswerEnded --> N2["Owner.noteLocalAnswerEnded"]
    X2["binding.execute: engine stream closed, or cancel"] -- markEnded --> E2["AnswerEnded"]
    T2["request task defer"] --> F2["Owner.finishLocalRequest answerEnded"]
  end
```

## Fix

- `NemotronSuperServingPolicy.finishingWait` = 1 s.
- **Owner:** `admitLocalRequest(waitingUpTo:)`. When the owner is full and **every admitted request's answer has ended**, it polls every 5 ms for an admission, up to the bound. Otherwise it refuses at once, as before. An answer counts as ended once the relay has seen the engine's terminal usage (`noteLocalAnswerEnded`). `finishLocalRequest(answerEnded:)` keeps the count exact.
- **Image binding:** `admit()` does the same for the active media request once its stream has closed (or it was cancelled).
- **Memory:** a waiter proceeds only after the previous request's settlement and media-charge release. Memory is never admitted twice, so there is no new OOM path. The wait is bounded and stops on cancel or drain.

## Tests (Metal; red-first on CI)

- `NemotronSuperLocalImageBindingTests.imageArrivingDuringSettlementWaitsInsteadOfBouncing`: a second image arrives during a 300 ms settlement and must be served, with every charge released. With a 1.8 s settlement it is still `busy`, after about 1 s.
- `NemotronSuperLocalHTTPAdmissionTests.requestDuringAnImagesSettlementWaitsAndIsServed`: live HTTP on the default single-request owner. An image's settlement is held 400 ms; the next image, then a text request, must get 200.
- `NemotronSuperLocalOwnerTests.fullOwnerWaitsOnlyForARequestWhoseAnswerHasEnded`: owner unit test. Mid-answer: refused at once. Answer ended: admitted after the settlement. Bounded.
- `busyOwnerRefusesWith429BeforeAnyResponse` (existing) still pins the immediate 429 for a request held before its terminal.

Red: `8c60283222` and `9374a2e2b5` (DEBUG seam plus tests, no behaviour change). **CI red run 43169053879:** the binding test and the HTTP test were the only failures, refused with `busy` and 429. The binding test's bound check also failed, because the refusal came at once. The fix is `7bcff6e985`; `109fbaec75` only refreshes `direct-mode.md`'s freshness stamp.

## Other models

- **Gemma 4, Qwen 3.5/3.6 VL, Qwen3-VL:** no refusing slot. The tower runs under the container's serial lock, so a second media request queues.
- **MiMo and GLM (one Mac, native-tracked):** the client's terminal precedes native retirement, and the service allowance (plus MiMo's media reservation) stays charged for that moment. A refusal in that window is `media_memory_unavailable` (re-routed, no strike) or a capacity 503. **This PR does not cover them**: they take a different path, and the follow-up is a bounded wait in the bridge's admission.

## Expected effect: small, and honest about it

Production since 11-11 14:00Z (read-only): 11,375 Super image attempts, 5,841 of them bounced (`429 queue_full`).

- **99.7 % of the bounces arrived while the coordinator could see an image in flight on that Mac.** That is stacking, which coordinator #815 (Stage 5) addresses; only 18 bounces had nothing visible.
- The window this PR closes is the tail after an answer ends. About **90 bounces (1.5 %)** landed within the in-flight request's largest chunk gap before its end, a proxy for that tail. **At most 813 (14 %)** landed under 1 s before it. The GPU proof's first step measures the real window.
- Other provider-side causes are not changed here:
  - **Images sent to Macs without Super loaded** cause 84 % of the image 504s: 506 of ~600, plus all 75 `request_exceeds_node` and 69 of 70 `model_load` 503s; 2 of 656 such attempts were served. 456 of the 506 followed a bounce.
  - **Mac-wide stalls in acknowledging:** one M5 Ultra took 56 of the 63 never-acknowledged 504s on loaded Macs.
  - **Slow prefill on older chips:** about 33 acknowledged 504s on loaded Macs.
  - **`media_memory_unavailable`:** 43, all on one 128 GB Mac with Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.8 resident beside Super; the image size was not the cause.
- "Why a Mac stops acknowledging" is still open. The one clear case was Mac-wide, across all of that Mac's models, for about 40 minutes while it cycled models; it needs that Mac's provider log.

## Validation, limitations, refactor pass

- **CI red** run 43169053879 on `9374a2e2b5

body:
## Why
A review of the automatic trading (rules v1, #158) found five weaknesses. No order exists yet, so the account can start on v1.1 without rewriting any history.

## What changes
- **Post-earnings priority ignored the direction of the reaction.** A stock that fell on its report still ranked first. Now the close after the report is compared with the close before it: +2% or more ranks first, −2% or worse is skipped, and an unknown reaction gets no priority. The nightly build records closes for every universe member so the reaction can be read.
- **The 8-week hold was overridden by the label exit**, although the page said only the stop applies. The stop now comes first, then the hold.
- **Sector limit:** at most 2 positions per known sector.
- **Stale build:** no orders from a build older than 4 days, enforced in code instead of in the task instructions.
- **Trading costs:** every fill pays 0.10% for commission and slippage (`cost_rate` in the account file).
- `trade.html` shows the v1.1 rules.

The plan for 12 Nov is unchanged: GEN, CNX, GDDY, MO.

## Not changed, and why
- The rules are still not backtested: the committed history holds closes for paper-test symbols only, so a backtest here would not be meaningful. The universe closes recorded from now on make one possible later.
- Stops are still checked on closes and filled at the next close.

## Validation
- New tests: reaction ranking and skip, sector cap, stale build, trading costs, hold vs label vs stop

author: flotob
body:
The collection budget in main, as freedom-browser's B7 (#1190) measured it:

- **The charge is five times a collected result's JSON length**: the decoded text plus the parsed value. B7 measured every shape the service writes, at its cap in its worst form (a listing whose text V8 holds at two bytes a character; the densest object listings; `repo_info`, `node_info` and `identity` with one long two-byte string), after a full collection: 4.24× at most in Node, 4.09× in Electron. The design implied the bytes and the value fit the 16 MiB; a 2× charge didn't cover them.
- **The lists' cap is 3 MiB, not 4 MiB,** so the worst list's 15 MiB charge fits the 16 MiB budget alone (about 40,000 repositories in the densest form). The alternative, a 20 MiB budget, would raise main's memory bound instead.
- **Reserved at the head,** which gives the length, rather than piece by piece as bytes arrive, which could deadlock two calls each holding part of the budget.

Docs only.

author: eburgos
body:
A float map key written with an exponent (`1e3`) reached a Zod record as text no number check read, and an `f32` key beyond its range was refused by the Kotlin, Dart and Swift reads where serde reads it as an infinity. Zod now hands such a key on as plain decimal text, Kotlin's `f32` key serializer and Dart's read take an infinity, and Swift drops its finite-only filter on float keys.

Swift read an `isize` key through its native `[Int: Value]`, which read `01` and `-0` and named the key for the rest; it now reads it through the wrapped key read, as serde answers each case.

The Dart and Kotlin mcp servers recognised one of the four words serde refuses a number key with; `NOT_A_DOCUMENT_KEY` holds all four, so `01`, `-`, `1x`, `"1 "` and `1e400` answer `undeserializable-payload` with no field. The carillon matrix holds each case to the Rust dispatcher.

author: angryjay91
body:
story 4903 후속 (서버, 작은 PR) — **방 목록의 `latest_message`(한 줄 미리보기)가 «지우지 않은 가장 새 글»이 되고, 자기 `id`를 실어 줌.**

**왜**: 카디르 QA 바퀴(dev d097baf2a)에서 «마지막 글을 지우면 방 목록 미리보기가 옛 글이 남아 있는데도 메시지 없음»(PO 기준은 «남은 가장 새 글»). 원인은 코드로 확認 — 목록 쿼리가 `ConversationMessage` 중 가장 새 **행**을 고르는데 묘비(지운 글 행)도 행이라 선택됨 → `content: ""`가 내려가 화면이 «메시지 없음»을 그림. AC1 «후» 실측에서 «먼저 보낸 글»이 보인 것은 이 서버 동작이 아니라, 옛 글의 재전달 이벤트가 최신 자리를 덮은 우연이었음(5649의 순서 가드가 그 덮기를 막음 → 이후 일관되게 «메시지 없음»이라 이 어긋남이 드러남).

**무엇을**: `app/routers/conversations.py` 목록 빌더 — `latest_msg` 쿼리에 `ConversationMessage.deleted_at.is_(None)` 추가(전부 지웠으면 `None` → 빈 방과 같은 «메시지 없음»), `latest_message`에 `"id": str(latest_msg.id)` 추가(웹이 같은 마이크로초의 두 글을 구분하고, 삭제 알림을 id로 맞추기 위해 — 5649 codex가 LOW로 짚은 동시각 모호성의 서버 쪽 열쇠, 5627 한계 줄). 두 줄 + 주석.

**시험**(실 DB, `tests/test_4903_list_latest_alive_realdb.py` 3개 → 동률 시험 추가로 4개): ① 지우기 前 `id`로 자기를 가리킴 → 최신 글을 지우면 «남은 가장 새 글»(본문 + id) ② 모두 지우면 `latest_message`가 `None` ③ 더 오래된 글을 지워도 미리보기는 그대로. **변이 2 RED**: L1 묘비 제외 조건을 뺌 · L2 `id`를 뺌. 이웃 80 통과(이 PR이 건드린 목록 + 방 + MCP 목록 + 4846 조직 목록 + 4903 AC1·AC2 시험 전부, rc 0).

**알고 둔 것**: ① 한 방 마다 `latest_msg` 쿼리 한 줄 — 기존 구조(방당 1쿼리) 그대로, 조건 하나만 늘어 `conversation_id`+`created_at` 색인 위에서 삭제 행을 지나쳐 걸러냄(삭제 행이 최신 쪽에 몰려 있는 방도 한두 행) ② 웹은 이 PR만으로는 안 바뀜 — 5649(웹 AC3) 뒤 웹 후속 PR이 «최신 글 지움 알림 → 행을 즉시 비우고 목록을 다시 불러옴»을 얹음(그때 «남은 가장 새 글»이 화면에 보임) ③ 단건 대화 응답(`GET /conversations/{id}`)의 최신 글 필드는 이 PR 범위 밖(목록 미리보기만; 단건은 이 필드를 안 쓰는 걸 grep으로 확認).

**codex 1판 반영(새 머리 ea52451ac)**: ① **MEDIUM 같은 마이크로초 동률 → `id.desc()` 두 번째 정렬 키 추가**(방 자신의 메시지 목록 쿼리와 같은 동률 규칙) + 시험: 두 글을 같은 `created_at`으로 맞추고 **두 행이 «큰 id»를 번갈아 갖게**(UPDATE로 행 위치 이동) 두 경우 모두 큰 id가 뽑히는지 확認 — 처음 쓴 시험은 변이에 안 걸려(planner 순서 우연) 더 날카롭게 고침, 고정 uuid는 공유 시험 DB에서 부딪혀 매번 새 접미로 바꿈. 변이(`id.desc()` 제거) RED · 고친 코드로 2회 연속 초록. ② **MEDIUM 색인**: 맞는 관찰 — `conversation_messages`에는 `(conversation_id, created_at)` 색인이 `thread_id IS NULL` 부분 색인뿐이라 답글까지 포함한 «방 최신 글» 쿼리는 `ix_conversation_messages_conversation_id`로 방 전체를 훑어 정렬함. **이 PR 이전부터 같은 계획**(전엔 `deleted_at` 조건만 없었음)이라 새 회귀는 아니고, 지운 행이 많은 방에서만 훑는 양이 늘어남 → **후속 한 줄**(방 전체 최신 글 색인 `(conversation_id, created_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` 또는 방 목록 N+1 합치기) — 이 PR 병합 조건 아님. ③ **MEDIUM 정렬이 `Conversation.updated_at`**: 지운 뒤에도 방 정렬 기준이 «마지막 보낸 시각»이라 모두 지운 방이 최근 활동처럼 위에 있음 — 제품 판단(삭제가 방 정렬을 바꿔야 하는가)이라 이 PR 범위 밖, **후속 한 줄**. ④ **MEDIUM 웹이 id를 무시하고 방 + 시각으로 맞춤**: 이 PR이 id를 내려주는 이유 그 자체 — 웹 후속 PR(5649 뒤)이 id 우선으로 맞춤(시각은 폴백). ⑤ **LOW 시험**: (a) 동률 시험 추가(위 ①) (b) `test_conversations.py`의 «묘비 첨부 없음» 시험은 `MagicMock`으로 묘비를 주입하는 것이라 SQL 조건이 빠져도 통과함 — 맞음, 이제 목록 빌더의 묘비 분기는 도달 불가한 **방어 코드**(5641에서 넣은 것, 그대로 둠). 실 DB 시험 4개가 SQL 조건 자체를 지킴.

author: aaronjae22
body:
## Summary

This adds `POST /api/auth/token/`, login as ADR 0006 and ADR 0014 describe it:

- **The access token goes in the response body**, `{"access": "..."}` and nothing else, for the frontend to keep in memory.
- **The refresh token goes only into the `refresh_token` cookie**, never into the body. The cookie is:
  - httpOnly
  - `SameSite=Strict`
  - `Path=/api/auth/`
  - `Max-Age` of one day, the refresh token's lifetime
  - `Secure` whenever `DEBUG` is off. `DJANGO_REFRESH_COOKIE_SECURE` overrides it, for the prod image over plain http. It's documented in `.env.example`.
- **A failed login reveals no accounts.** A wrong password, an unknown user and an inactive user all get the same 401 body. Django's backend refuses inactive users the same way it refuses wrong passwords.
- **400** for missing fields, keyed by field. **415** for a form post: a cross-site HTML form can't log anyone in.
- **The `auth` throttle scope:** the 6th attempt in a minute is 429 with `Retry-After`. It counts failed attempts too.
- **Schema:**
  - Login requires no token.
  - It documents `LoginRequest`, an `access`-only 200, and its 400, 401 and 429 responses.
  - The API description says how to try it in Swagger.
  - `config/openapi.py` now documents a 400 as a field-to-messages map.

## Commits

- `test: add failing tests for logging in`: 404 on the route, and `AttributeError: REFRESH_COOKIE_SECURE` in the settings tests.
  - Test settings switch to Django's fast MD5 hasher, the usual practice for tests, because the real hasher is deliberately slow on every login.
- `feat: log in with the access token in the body and the refresh token in a cookie`
  - My first draft caught `TokenError` around the serializer, as simplejwt's base view does. For login it can never happen, since a token is only created after the credentials pass. Coverage showed the branch never ran, so I removed it.

## How to verify

Run from `backend/`, with the local Postgres for the database commands:

- `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .`: All checks passed, 93 files already formatted
- `uv run lint-imports`: 3 kept, 0 broken
- `makemigrations --check --dry-run`: No changes detected
- `spectacular --validate --fail-on-warn --file /dev/null`: exit 0
- Unit tests + domain/application coverage: 171 passed, 100%
- Full suite: 395 passed, total coverage 99.71%. `accounts/auth_views.py` is at 100%.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: all passed

## Out of scope

- Refresh, logout, rotation and the blacklist app (PR 03-08). Until then, the cookie set here has nothing that reads it.

author: profhepta
body:
## Why
The neuroscience reference uses logical steps for credit and matches feedback bit budgets without verifying the original information content. Repeated training seeds also do not establish independent task sources. These gaps prevent the four neuroscience research tracks from being interpreted as real-time, information-matched experiments.

## Changes
- Separate reward occurrence discount, state response, update interval and eligibility decay in real microseconds. Verify clock/boot envelopes before determining feedback availability.
- Add a frozen source roster with model/evaluator/opportunity binding; compare original unrouted information bytes and explicit routing assignments.
- Preserve UNKNOWN and missing tasks in the planned denominator and withhold incomplete paired statistics; report equal-weight declared-source differences without confirmatory p values.
- Record interval/right-censored learning-curve attainment so new-learning ability can be measured alongside old-task retention.
- Add the four-track protocol, verified primary references and explicit research/ordinary-owner execution gates.

## Validation and source
Stacked on #6097 at `1eac6794355fa01a3e051776c5598a13ac612073`.
New commit: `e263e7b01ca051ebc8c15b87ea6b9721169ba22e`.
Locally computed Git tree equals the GitHub-created tree: `cb1bb085c896abd7f89c64f51fd2efa314276fc1`.
- Python 3.12.14: **119/119 reference tests passed** (102 inherited + 17 new).
- `just fmt` from `codex-rs`: exit 0; upstream formatter has no applicable group for these qualification paths; source bytes unchanged.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- ai395 Python 3.14.4: **119/119 passed**, original job `1a1ce71e9da-2564-1678`, authoritative succeeded/exit 0, complete logs. All 24 executed Python source hashes equal the local tested source. Original native status/read payloads and stdout are committed; no test restart occurred.
- [Exact local execution and qualification boundary](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci/blob/e263e7b01ca051ebc8c15b87ea6b9721169ba22e/qualification/neuroscience-20261110/REAL_TIME_SOURCE_VALIDATION.md).
- [Four-track protocol](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/hepta-private-ci/blob/e263e7b01ca051ebc8c15b87ea6b9721169ba22e/qualification/neuroscience-20261110/FOUR_TRACK_PROTOCOL.md).

## Evidence boundary

author: eodgooch
body:
Part of #6. Wiring the judge into a match run comes after #5 merges (see **Integration** below).

## Summary

The LLM judge for criteria with no predicate, plus the quote-verification guardrail. Both are standalone modules; nothing calls them yet.

```text
judge_criteria(rec, items: list[JudgeItem], facts, note, *, semaphore, model_factory) -> list[Verdict]
  model = model_factory()                         # raises JudgeModelUnavailable if no key
  gather, each under the shared semaphore (8):
    judge_criterion -> step "judge:<nct>:<id>"    # = Verdict.trace_event_id
      llm call (with_structured_output(JudgeOutput), trace callback: prompt + raw output)
      malformed? -> retry once, adding the prompt's `## retry` turn that names the error
      still malformed -> unknown + error event "judge:<nct>:<id>:malformed"
      other model exception -> unknown + error event "judge:<nct>:<id>:error"
      verify_verdict -> guardrail event "verify:<nct>:<id>" (ok | failed)
        quote fails -> outcome=unknown, verified=false
```

```diff
 api/app/
 ├── pipeline/
+│   ├── judge.py          # JudgeItem, judge_criteria, judge_criterion, new_judge_semaphore
+│   ├── verify.py         # quote_present, render_facts, verify_verdict
 │   ├── compile_criteria.py   # _normalize -> verify.normalize
 │   └── fixture_model.py      # + `replies` script (malformed-then-valid tests)
 ├── prompts/
+│   ├── judge.md          # version: judge-v1, with an optional `## retry` section
 │   └── __init__.py       # loader accepts an optional `## retry` section
 ├── schemas.py            # RunTotals.guardrail_trips (additive; make types run)
 └── routers/runs.py       # compute_totals counts failed guardrail events
 web/
+├── components/UnverifiedQuoteBadge.tsx
 └── components/CriterionRow.tsx       # badge per verdict row (after merging #5)
```

**Quote matching** (`verify.py`): text is lowercased and whitespace-collapsed, and the match passes at `partial_ratio >= 90`. I used `partial_ratio`, not `ratio`. A quote is a span of a much longer source, and `ratio` compares whole strings, so a perfect quote from a long note would score about 4. Three guards sit on top of the ratio, each covering a case the ratio alone lets through:
- **Quote longer than its source:** falls back to `ratio`. `partial_ratio` swaps its arguments in this case, so it would score 100.
- **Numbers:** must match exactly. "eGFR 148" vs "eGFR 48" scores about 88.
- **Negation words:** must match the window plus the two tokens before it. Without this, "no history of pancreatitis" scores about 92 against "history of pancreatitis".

`patient_evidence` is checked against three sources: the note, each fact's `source_span`, and one rendered line per fact. The judge prompt shows facts in the same rendering, so FHIR patients with no note can still be quoted. A `pass` or `fail` with null evidence is downgraded.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no judge and no quote check. Totals have no guardrail count.
  **After:** `make check` passes: ruff, mypy, 135 passed, 3 live tests deselected, web typecheck and lint.

```text
test_judge.py
  fabricated patient_evidence          -> unknown, verified=false, failed guardrail event naming the quote   ✓
  malformed, then valid                -> 2 calls, retry turn appended, verdict from call 2, no error         ✓
  malformed twice                      -> unknown + error event (attempts=2), judge step failed               ✓
  llm event under the judge step       -> prompt messages, raw tool call, tokens, model                       ✓
  3 trials x 10 criteria, 1 semaphore  -> 30 calls, peak in flight == 8                                       ✓
test_verify.py
  exact / case+space / typo pass; fabricated, changed number, added "no", dropped "denies", too long fail ✓
test_totals.py
  ok guardrails and error events don't count toward guardrail_trips                                       ✓
```

**Not verified:**
- **<30 s demo run:** needs #5's orchestrator. I haven't measured it, and I'm not claiming it.
- **Live judge path:** there's no API key here. `tests/test_judge_live.py` is marked `live` and skipped.
- **Badge in a browser:** every verdict in the stub match is verified, so nothing would render the badge yet.

## Integration (after #5 merges)

In #5's evaluator, the no-predicate branch:

```python
from app.pipeline.compile_criteria import clean_eligibility_text
from app.pipeline.judge import JudgeItem, judge_criteria, new_judge_semaphore

semaphore = new_judge_semaphore()       # ONCE per match run, shared by every trial
...
trial_text = clean_eligibility_text(eligibility.get("eligibilityCriteria") or "")
items = [JudgeItem(nct_id, c, trial_text) for c in criteria if c.predicate is None]
llm_verdicts = await judge_criteria(rec, items, facts, note, semaphore=semaphore)
# verdicts come back in input order; merge with the rule verdicts by criterion_id
```

- **Trial text:** pass `clean_eligibility_text(...)`, not the raw field. Criterion text is verbatim against the cleaned text.
- **No API key:** `judge_criteria` raises `JudgeModelUnavailable` before making any call. Decide whether that fails the run or should become `unknown` per criterion.
- **Routes:** add a `judge_model_factory` dependency like `compile_model_factory`, so route tests can inject `FixtureChatModel(replies=..., tool_name="JudgeOutput")`.
- ~~**Verdict rows:** render the badge per verdict.~~ Done when main (#5) was merged in: `CriterionRow` renders `<UnverifiedQuoteBadge verified={verdict.verified} />`.
- **Totals strip:** show `totals.guardrail_trips`.
- **Concurrency:** the semaphore bounds judge calls only. Cold-cache compile calls can share it if you want them bounded too.

## Decisions to check (SPEC vs. brief)

- **File names:** I used `verify.py` and `prompts/judge.md`, the names in the SPEC.md layout and prompt-iteration section, instead of the brief's `quote_verify.py` and `judge_criterion.md`.
- **Semaphore:** injected and required, not module-level. A Semaphore created at import binds to the first loop that contends on it.
- **Error and malformed verdicts:** `verified: true`. They quote only the criterion text and claim no patient evidence, so they show no "unverified quote" badge. The error event and the failed judge step still mark them.
- **Other model exceptions:** network and API errors also become `unknown` plus an `error` event, so one flaky call doesn't fail a 20-trial run. The spec only covers malformed output.
- **Passing checks are traced:** each emits an `ok` guardrail event. `guardrail_trips` counts only the `failed` ones.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Additive modules with no call site yet. `RunTotals.guardrail_trips` is a new required response field, regenerated in TS. No consumer reads totals yet.

**Blast Radius:** small

Shared code that changed: the prompt loader now accepts an optional `## retry` section; the compiler uses `verify.normalize` (same behaviour); `FixtureChatModel` now raises if it gets neither `output` nor `replies`.
