## Summary

- Hosts can hide an event without affecting existing tickets. A removal request hides it while Tikatero reviews the request. Tikatero can approve or reject it, and hosts can withdraw pending requests.
- The admin event list shows every event and can be filtered by visibility, status and removal requests. The review page shows ticket sales, host verification, event history and the existing refund controls.
- Approval or an emergency cancellation opens a full refund for paid bookings. The payments job retries queued refunds with the original refund ID. A payment received after cancellation is queued for refund without issuing a ticket. Permanent deletion requires an admin and an event with no bookings.
- The ticket setup can limit seats across all ticket types. Checkout checks sold seats and active holds, and hosts can see how many seats are sold.

## Migration

`supabase/migrations/20261112120000_event_moderation.sql`. The migration adds request history, visibility fields and a durable image cleanup queue. Permanent deletion retains an audit snapshot. An admin or staff member who belongs to the organiser must confirm that relationship before acting as staff.

A rejected or withdrawn request leaves the event hidden until the host shows it again. If Tikatero also placed a hide, Tikatero must lift it. Cashfree refund requests retain the existing fees, reversal calculations and provider idempotency keys. author: juliusmarminge
body:
The review item was correct. The relay and client code are in this repo (infra/relay, packages/client-runtime); the earlier summary wrongly said they were not. The relay's HttpApiClient decodes the host's 401 as a typed EnvironmentHttpUnauthorizedError (not an HttpClientError), so diagnoseEndpointFailure returned invalid_response, and the client showed 'T3 Code on <host> sent an unexpected answer' with restart advice. This commit carries a machine-readable reason end to end. (1) contracts: EnvironmentHttpUnauthorizedError gains optional `reason: "host_clock_behind"` (optionalKey, so older relays ignore it), and RelayEnvironmentEndpointFailure gains "host_clock_behind" (ConnectionFailureCause derives from it). (2) server cloud/http.ts: CloudLinkProofRejectedError with hostClockBehind maps to a 401 that carries that reason; every other proof rejection is unchanged. (3) relay endpointFailure.ts: diagnoseEndpointFailure reports { endpointFailure: "host_clock_behind", endpointStatus: 401 } for that error, checked with a module-level Schema.is. EnvironmentConnector uses it for both the mint and health paths, and Api.ts already forwards endpointFailure on endpoint_request_failed. (4) client-runtime: errors.ts and diagnosis locate host_clock_behind on the server hop. The headline is '<host>'s clock is behind', the step is 'Turn on automatic date and time on <host>, then retry.', and the help section is the-clock-is-off. The host-side change from the previous round (clock-specific message plus logged warning) is kept. No new regex or parser. Compatibility: clients released before this change do not know the new endpointFailure literal; if they decode relay errors strictly, they show a generic failure instead of the old misleading one. AI-assisted; verified with the tests and tools listed above.

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#27989

## Reproduction on main

Commit a18a458f25 (origin/main). Ran `T3CODE_DEV_SEED=0 node src/bin.ts --base-dir <scratch> --port 38991 --host 127.0.0.1 --no-browser` from apps/server with a fresh data directory. Seeded a synthetic T3 Connect link into that home's secrets: a generated Ed25519 relay mint public key, relay issuer https://relay.test and linked user user-1. A driver script then POSTed signed t3-cloud-health+jwt proofs to /api/t3-connect/health, with iat set to real time plus the simulated host lag. Results: in sync -> 200; 30 s slow -> 200; 71 s slow -> 401 {"message":"Invalid cloud health request."}; 90 s slow -> 401 with the same message; forged signature (control) -> 401 with the same message. The server log recorded nothing about the rejection or the clock. The relay code that maps this 401 to the client's invalid_response/endpoint_request_failed is not in this repo, and T3 Connect is not available on the VM, so the desktop/Android error text was not exercised. Failing test: 'says a health proof was refused because of the host clock, not just that it was invalid' in apps/server/src/cloud/CloudLink.test.ts. It fails on main with 'Invalid cloud health request.'; the other 7 tests in the file pass.

## Evidence

_Being captured: before and after in the real app. This section is filled in before the pull request can merge._

## Tests

infra/relay: `vp test run src/environments/` 102 passed (new case: diagnoseEndpointFailure maps a host_clock_behind 401 to host_clock_behind and a plain 401 to invalid_response); `vp run typecheck` exit 0 after replacing instanceof with a hoisted Schema.is. packages/client-runtime: `vp test run src/connection/` 184 passed (new case: host_clock_behind diagnosis headline, steps, more-info section). apps/server: `vp test run src/cloud/` 22 files, 263 passed. Per-package `vp run typecheck` passed for contracts, client-runtime and server. Final `vp run check:changed` passed: format, lint, knip 1/2 and 2/2, graphql, typecheck (37 packages), tests (8 files). Earlier runs failed on format, then on lint (no-inline-schema-compile); both fixed.

## Not in this change

- `t3 connect status` does not report the clock problem, because nothing stores the last refusal for the CLI to read. Adding that means new persisted state and a contract field.
- The relay maps the host's 401 to the client's invalid_response/endpoint_request_failed. That code is outside this repo, so whether clients show the new clock message, or the existing 'the-clock-is-off' diagnosis, depends on a relay change.
- PR #19501 handles the other direction (the relay refusing the host's proofs because of host clock skew). It does not touch this path and does not conflict.
- hasBoundedCloudProofLifetime's iat-vs-now check in linkChecks.ts can never fail, because verifyRelayJwt already enforces it with the same 60 s tolerance. I left it as is.
- `t3 connect status` still does not mention the clock: its reachability check does not go through relay-signed proofs, and no state records the last refusal for the CLI to read.
- Clients released before this change get an endpointFailure literal they do not know; a forward-compatible fallback for unknown literals would be a separate change.
- PR #19501 covers the other direction (the relay refusing the host's proofs); it does not overlap with this path.
- hasBoundedCloudProofLifetime's iat-vs-now check in linkChecks.ts can never fail, because verifyRelayJwt already enforces it with the same tolerance; left as is.

AI-assisted; verified with the tests and tools listed above.

author: derrynknife
body:
One level for every interval the app shows: **90%**. Life quantities (B-lives, mean or median life, life left, time to a limit) get a 90% one-sided lower bound; a chance of failing a 90% one-sided upper bound; everything else (parameters, hazard and rate ratios, plot bands, rates, forecast ranges, availability) a 90% two-sided interval. Each result states its level. Pages that let you pick a level keep your pick and default to 90%.

Until now B-lives were 90% one-sided while parameters, plot bands, hazard ratios and most other intervals were 95% and forecast ranges 80%, so one page could show two levels side by side.

## What changed

- `backend/levels.py` and `frontend/src/levels.js`: the one definition (level, SurPyval `alpha_ci`, z, words).
- Life fits: parameter intervals, the probability-plot band, non-parametric bands, regression coefficients and hazard ratios (incl. robust and frailty θ), time-varying covariates, competing risks (bands and ratios), compare groups (average life and differences), recurrent (β, ROCOF, MTBF, MCF bands, rate ratios, repair effectiveness), accelerated life (parameters, coefficients, each level's own fit, the use-level calculator default), condition and life (parameters, hazard ratios, bands), degradation (band 90% two-sided; B-life and design-life bounds now off a 90% one-sided curve instead of the band's lower end), per-demand default, demonstration-test default, fleet and Maintenance forecasts (likely range P5–P95), RBD bands/uncertainty/next failure/phased missions/block check, simulated availability intervals, Explorer fit and plot band, the strategy sensitivity range.
- Saved fits are served at 90% on read, never rewritten: life and regression fits' parameter and coefficient intervals are rebuilt from the stored standard error, and the probability-plot band is moved on the scale SurPyval's Wald band is symmetric on (checked exact against fresh fits for Weibull, exponential, lognormal, normal, gamma, loglogistic, Gumbel, logistic, Rayleigh). Accelerated-life and condition-and-life fits likewise. Where a saved interval can't be moved without refitting (profile-likelihood θ, Buckley-James bootstrap, repairable fits, competing risks, non-parametric bands, a stored joint survival band, older per-demand models), it keeps its level and the page says "95%".
- Simulated availability: the interval shown is 90%; the run-to-precision stopping rule stays on its 95% interval, so run lengths and estimates don't change.
- A fix found on the way: the symmetric-interval check treated a tiny coefficient (an inverse-power `a` of 5e-26) as "about zero" and rebuilt its interval as [0, none]; the check is now relative to the numbers.
- Hypothesis tests (p-values, trend tests, the repair test, Gray's test), spares service levels, M_max's percentile and a library source's 5–95% spread are not intervals the app works out, so they are unchanged.
- MCP: result keys that named a level (`beta_ci_95`, `ci_95`, `rocof_ci_95`, `survival_95ci`, …) are now level-free (`beta_ci`, `ci`, …) with `ci_level`; guide text says the rule. `tools/list`: 7,988 characters before and after (only action schemas and guide topics changed).
- Guides and reference pages updated with the new numbers.

## Numbers that move (examples)

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Bearings Weibull β | 2.50 (95% 1.88–3.32) | 2.50 (90% 1.96–3.17) |
| Seal Weibull PH, temp_C | 0.138 (95% 0.093–0.183) | 0.138 (90% 0.101–0.176) |
| Pump bearings, +10% load | ×1.74 (95% 1.19–2.55) | ×1.74 (90% 1.26–2.40) |
| Pump modes, bearing wear by 5,000 h | 40% (95% 28–52%) | 40% (90% 30–51%) |
| Compare groups, seal life by load | +306 h (95% 54–557) | +306 h (90% 94–517) |
| One-shot, 3 failures in 200 | ≥ 96.2% at 95% | ≥ 96.7% at 90% |
| Brake pads B10 (degradation) | ≥ 3,210 h at 95% | ≥ 3,670 h at 90% |
| Truck fleet, failures in 12 months | likely 37–44 (80%) | likely 36–45 (90%) |
| Demonstration, R ≥ 95% (default confidence) | 59 units (95%) | 45 units (90%) |

## Tests

- `backend/tests/test_ninety_percent.py` (new): Weibull parameter intervals equal SurPyval's at `alpha_ci=0.1`; a fit saved at 95% is served at 90% (parameters and plot band) for four families, regression coefficients, accelerated life and condition and life; per-demand 3/200 gives 96.7%; forecast ranges P5–P95; degradation B10 bound 3,674 h; availability levels and stop rule.
- `frontend/src/levels.test.js` (new) and updated frontend tests (alt, competing risks, degradation, Explorer).
- Existing tests that pinned 95% (or 80%) now compare with SurPyval/RePyability at the new level.
- Ran: `node --test "src/**/*.test.js"` (all pass), `npm run build`, and the backend tests of every touched area (`pytest … -n auto --dist loadfile`). One failure, `test_mcp_findings.py::test_every_rbd_field_the_server_reads_is_in_the_published_schema`, also fails on `dev` without this change (`operating_interval` missing from the published schema); not touched here.

Guide screenshots will need recapturing on the release branch (the bands and labels changed).

author: rafalszypulewski
body:
## What changed

- `topics.yaml`: the flat `keywords` list is replaced by 19 weighted `keyword_groups` (core testing +10, frameworks +10, AI/API/performance/security testing +9, … general AI +3).
- `radar/prefilter.py`: new `build_terms()` / `keyword_score()`. `keep()` now keeps an item when its keyword score is at least `KEYWORD_MIN_SCORE` (new setting, default 4); `always_include` sources still skip the gate.
- Scoring rules:
  - matching is whole-word and case-insensitive
  - a keyword listed in several groups counts once, at its highest weight
  - where matches overlap, the longest keyword wins (`OWASP Top 10` hides `OWASP`)
  - `requires_anchor` groups (languages, CI/CD & DevOps, observability, architecture) only count when a keyword from another group matched too
- `matched_keywords` on raw items now lists the keywords that scored, in the order they appear in the text.
- README and PLAN are updated.

## Why

The old filter kept an item on any single keyword match, so most items got in only through `AI`, `LLM` or `agent`. A weighted score lets testing-specific terms count for more than generic ones. Part 2 (a separate PR) will also feed this score into pre-rank.

## Notes for review

- **Keywords curated from the proposed list:** generic terms are dropped (Latency, Throughput, Kanban, Jira, Linear, Jest — Polish "jest" means "is", …), `Go` is renamed to `Golang`, and testing-specific terms are moved out of anchored groups (flaky tests, test architecture, Selenium Grid, BrowserStack, …). Bonus and penalty lists from the proposal were left out on purpose.
- **Gate check on the 306 raw items from sources without `always_include`, at min score 4:** 98 are rejected, and only 3 of them were rated 7 or higher by the LLM (the old list at the same threshold lost 11). Adding `test`/`tests`/`tested`/`eval`/`evals` and AI plurals made that difference. The check only shows what would be lost: it can't show what the new list would newly let in, since these items already passed the old filter.
- **Takes effect on the next collect run after merge.**
- **Tests:** `pytest` (214 passed) and `ruff check` pass.

body:
## Description
The mocked Playwright script ended with `docker image prune -f`, which removes the dangling images of every project on a workstation, not only the one it built. A CI runner is thrown away after the job, so there is nothing to clean there either.

## Key changes
- `scripts/run-mocked-playwright.sh`: no image prune; the container is still stopped and removed. A comment says why.

## How to test
Prerequisite: Node 24 (`.nvmrc`, `.mise.toml`) and Docker.
```
npm ci
npm run playwright:run:mocked -- --project=chromium
docker images -f dangling=true
```

author: elematic-bot
body:
Fixes #812. `==`, `!=` and `is` on an inline binding were errors ("comparing it with '==' would box it"), because each lowered by reading the value whole. They now compare and test slot by slot.

```zena
function same(a: inline (i32, i32), b: inline (i32, i32)): boolean {
  return a == b;              // two i32 compares
}

function isGood(r: inline (true, i32) | (false, String)): boolean {
  return r is (true, i32);    // a test of the tag slot
}
```

## `==` and `!=`

When either operand is an inline tuple or union, both are lowered into the inline one's layout (`lowerIntoSlots`). That operand can be an inline binding, a call, a literal or a boxed tuple. `lowerInlineEq` then ands a comparison of every pair of slots:

- Each slot compares with the `==` of the type a member puts there (`valueFieldEq`): numbers by value, `String` by content, a class through its `operator ==`, nested records and tuples structurally.
- A slot a member can leave empty compares null-safely: both empty is equal, one empty isn't.
- Every write fills the slots its member doesn't use with defaults, so equal values agree on those too. The discriminant slots are among the pairs compared, which tells members apart.

Reachability notes what each slot's type needs to compare, instead of the inline type, which it couldn't map (the `typeToValType` crash #812 mentions).

An inline record's binding is a record held as its fields, so `==` on it already compared the fields in place. Only the use rule was in the way.

## `is`

On an inline union, `is` tests the members whose literals the tested tuples agree with (`#inlineIsTest`): an or of #1041's member tests. Destructuring a binding that `is` narrowed reads only those members (`#narrowedMembers`). Without that, `let (_, why) = r` after `r is (false, String)` read position 1 across both members' slots and bailed.

## Smaller changes

- A tuple literal written into slots no longer has to have an inline type. `make(1) != (1, 2)` has a boxed literal beside an inline result.
- The use rule allows `==`, `!=` and `is`.

## Tests

- `execution/tuples/inline_equality.zena`:
  - tuples, a nested tuple with a `String`, a union with a `String` member, inline records;
  - a stored tuple and a call result as operands;
  - `is` as a value and narrowing by it.
- WAT invariant: `comparing inline values allocates nothing`. It couldn't be seen failing on an allocation: before this change the program was rejected, and there's no boxing path to compare against.
- `semantics/type-system/inline_parameters.zena`: `==` and `is` no longer report.

author: dmachard
body:
When the dnstap collector receives compressed framestream frames (compression: gzip), DnstapServer.HandleConn immediately sliced the decompressed payload with frame.Data()[4:] to skip the framestream bulk header without checking its length.

If a peer sends a frame whose decompressed data length is less than 4 bytes, this triggers an unhandled runtime error: slice bounds out of range [4:x] panic inside the connection handler goroutine, terminating the entire collector process (DoS).

author: quixthe2nd
body:
## Problem
Restarting the hub isn't safe while an overlap restart is in flight, which defeats the point of overlap restarts. Reproduced today at 18:25: after a hub restart the predecessor reattached, but the successor was refused on every retry:

```
RuntimeError: overlap successor was not spawned by this transport hub
```

`OverlapSuccessorRegistry` was memory-only, so the hub forgot every successor it had spawned. `DiscordSessionRouter._undelivered` (events held for a dead/absent generation) was memory-only too and silently dropped on restart.

## Fix
- **Successor registry** mirrors to `<hub dir>/hub-overlap-successors.json` on spawn, attach and prune. On load, a record is kept only if `get_process_start_time(pid)` still matches the stored fingerprint, so PID reuse or a hand-written entry still can't vouch for a process. Boot grace carries over via wall-clock age.
- **Held events**: each router binds a store (`hub-undelivered-discord-<token>.json`, `hub-undelivered-matrix-<key>.json`), saved on every hold and after replay, and deleted when empty. Reloaded events replay on the next attach as before.
- Files are written atomically, mode 0600, inside the existing 0700 hub directory (same trust boundary as the hub socket).

## Tests
New `tests/gateway/test_hub_persistent_state.py`: registry reload lets the successor attach; a wrong fingerprint is dropped; held events survive a router restart and the file clears after replay. Hub, Matrix-hub and registry suites pass (24).

## Deploy
Needs a hub restart to load. After this lands, hub restarts are safe at any time.

author: technolojin
body: ## Description Launching a system whose compute units run in several execution environments (ECUs, or containers on one ECU) from one studio workbench. One daemon runs per execution environment; a daemon given the others as peers serves their units as well, so the browser and any API client talk to it alone. A Docker environment stands in for a multi-ECU bench and tests this in five topologies, including devices that freeze, lose power or drop off the network. ### Studio: peers - `serve --peer =`, `--peer-ssh =`, and a site file (`--site-file` or `$AUTOWARE_SYSTEM_DESIGNER_SITE_FILE`, YAML `peers: {unit: url | {url, ssh}}`); a `--peer` replaces the site file's binding of the same unit. - A peer's address is `http://127.0.0.1:` (its own loopback port, or a forward that keeps the port), never the port of the daemon given the binding. - `serve/peers.py`: one link per peer address reads the peer's health, systems, sessions and jobs, follows its event stream, and reconnects with backoff (0.5 s to 10 s). A stream silent for three heartbeat intervals counts as lost. Stdlib only, like the daemon. - A peer on another device is reached through an SSH forward the daemon keeps as a job of kind `tunnel` (`ssh -N -L`, `BatchMode=yes`, `ExitOnForwardFailure=yes`, keepalive 5 s x 3), restarted 1 s to 15 s after it ends. User, port, keys and host key checking come from the SSH configuration of the daemon's user. - Through the daemon with peers: - `systems.list`: a peer's unit is `available`, `running` or `unreachable`, with the peer record under `daemon`; `health` lists `peers` with state, version and `mismatch`. - `launch.*`, `measure.*` and `monitor.*` naming a peer's unit are forwarded; `launch.status`, `jobs.list` and `launch.runs` include the answering peers'. - A peer's job and run ids read `/`. - `launch`, `member`, `member.log`, `member.activity`, `monitor` and the `job`/`job.log` events of launch jobs are relayed; follows are released on the peer when this daemon's last event stream closes. - A system runs one mode at a time across all daemons; a mode is refused while another mode of the system runs or is starting. Sessions last reported by an unreachable peer still hold the mode, until the peer answers again or `launch.forget {compute_unit}` drops them; `launch.status` answers them for a peer that gives none. - A `systems.changed` about a peer's own links is not relayed, so daemons linked to each other do not echo it. - `build.start` is refused for a peer's unit. - A mismatch (version, method set, units served, modes/units/deploy variants of the exported systems) is shown, not enforced. ### Studio: launches - A session and its run name their launch (`launch`). A unit started while another unit of the system runs or starts the mode joins that unit's launch (a peer's units as last reported); the first unit opens a new one. `launch.start` takes `launch` to name it. - The runtime takes it as `--launch-id` and records it in `run.json`; the runs of one launch stay in their own directories on their own units. - `launch.runs` leaves the runs of peer units out before it truncates. ### Studio: workbench - Launch > Control: each unit shows the daemon serving it; an `unreachable` unit's controls are disabled; "Launch all" / "Shutdown all" in the Control head (`web/js/activities/launch/units.js`). - A unit that cannot launch names the session holding it (`unitHolder`, `holderLabel`): `in use · `, ` runs on `, or ` shutting down`. A mode shutting down on any unit of the system ends on all of them before it launches again. - Launch > Logs: the selector lists one entry per past launch (first start, mode, deploy variant, compute units) and shows the members of all its runs on one tree (`web/js/activities/launch/sessions.js`). A member with a directory in several runs of the launch shows their tails in start order, each under its run's label. A run naming no launch is an entry of its own. - Launch > Topics: the selector lists the runs, grouped by launch. - Status bar item for the peers' state. ### Runtime - Each run owns its log directory: a run starting within the second of another gets a numbered one (`_2`, ...). Two runtimes on one host previously shared `run.json` and the tracer counters. - `ControlChannel.close` closes the clients before waiting for the server. From Python 3.12 on `wait_closed` waits for open connections, so `launch.shutdown` over the control channel did not end the runtime on Jazzy. `ServeDaemon.stop` of the studio waits for its server after its connections for the same reason. - Graceful shutdown sends `SIGINT` to the process group (was `SIGTERM`), then `SIGKILL` after the grace. rclcpp and rclpy leave the ROS graph on `SIGINT`; a glog failure handler takes `SIGTERM` as a crash. - A member is its whole process group: it has stopped once its leader has exited and no process of the group is left. The children of a launch file that ends before them are waited for and killed the same way, and a member whose leader exits by itself takes what is left of its group with it. - An actor stays responsive while an exited leader's group is ended: a kill and a respawn toggle apply, and stopping the member ends what it left in its group. Groups polled together share one `/proc` scan per poll. - A restarted or respawned member appends to its `out` and `err`. ### Demo packages (moved under `demo/`) - `autoware_system_design_examples` is now `demo/autoware_system_designer_demo_systems`. `TypeAlpha` has three onboard units: `sensing_perception` (sensing, perception, robot state publisher), `map_localization` (map, localization, vehicle), `planning_control` (planning, control), each subscribing topics published on the other two. - New `demo/autoware_system_designer_demo_nodes`: the dummy node designs, each built into a real node that does what its design declares (`scripts/generate_dummy_nodes.py` generates one `DummyNode` subclass per design at configure time; `std_msgs`, `tf2_msgs`, `std_srvs` only). The node designs previously pointed at a package that did not exist, so `TypeAlpha` could not be launched. - `demo/autoware_system_designer_demo_systems/ee_architecture/TypeAlpha..compose.yaml`: where each unit runs, one file per topology. ### Multi-unit environment (`demo/docker_multi_unit`) - Image (`ros:-ros-base`, `build_depends.repos` as an underlay, `sshd`), entry point, shared compose services, the runner `run.py` (stdlib; `topologies`, `up`, `down`, `url`, `units`, `compose`, `ssh`) and the tests. Humble by default, Jazzy by `ASD_ROS_DISTRO`. - `run.py` derives the main daemon's peers from the bindings of the topology file and writes them as its site file; only the main daemon's port is forwarded to the host. | Topology | Stands for | Main daemon reaches its peers by | | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | | `host` | containers of one ECU | the shared loopback | | `bridge` | separate ECUs | SSH forwards | | `local_pair` | two containers of the main ECU and a second ECU | the shared loopback, an SSH forward | | `remote_pair` | the main ECU and two containers of a second ECU | two SSH forwards from one destination | | `shared_environment` | the main ECU and one environment of two units | one SSH forward, one link for two units | ## How was this PR tested? - Studio `pytest`: 163 passed, including `test_serve_peers.py` (several daemons in one process against a fake runtime: routing, merged lists, eve

author: chs-haple
body:
## Root cause
`CcRenderSession` duplicated the same pair of actions in **six** exit/cancellation paths: cancel the `PendingPrearm` listener receipt first, then clear the owner reference *only if it is still the same receipt*. These two actions are one ownership invariant; keeping them separate in six catch/exit paths creates a maintenance risk where a later edit could clear ownership despite a failed unhook.

## Bounded refactor
Add one owner-local `cancelPendingPrearm(pending)` with exactly the existing cancellation→identity-check order; reuse in `detach`, `abortPrearm`, detached host, successful prearm, failed prearm, and `onPendingPrearmDetached`. Existing `@Synchronized` outer owners, failure suppression and rethrow, callbacks and native/hook behavior stay unchanged. The retry condition is displayed on one line, with the same boolean operands and evaluation order. No new state, listeners, allocations, user settings, or ABI.

**Deliberately excluded:** `prearmAfterNextNativeLayout` cancellation of an old receipt checks for reentrant replacement *before creating a new one*, while `restoreAfterHotReload` deliberately discards the entire pending slot after cancellation; they are **not** equivalent to these six paths. `PendingPrearm.cancel()` retains its `Releasing` phase if listener removal fails, and this patch does not clear the owner reference in that case. Verified the relevant checked-in CC owner contract, available private read-only SystemUI reference note for fake-carrier/layout-listener boundaries, and actual source; no new device/binary observation or complete target lifecycle claim.

## Full base→HEAD review
Source `dev=9dd8dd4c52da41b0f3b6f7e5212f62d565f1178c` → one commit `710b23a616759dfbd49836bb2502dccc620bef73`: one file, +12/-15 lines. Independently inspected the full patch; no duplicate comments, stale references, new reflection/resource strings, changed event diagnostics, extra wrappers/owners, or missing cleanup path. Source-only test/build and static analysis are gating; real-device tests are not represented as performed.

## CI and permission
Require Codacy no new issues, actual Android/JVM tests, pinned target/MIUIX checks, exact PR-head mergeability and postmerge dev CI. No Build bump, sign, IT/main promotion, or Codacy dashboard/export refresh.

body:
Plain project content search treats text such as `needle *.ts` as `needle` plus a filename filter. With `words.txt` containing `needle *.ts` and `code.ts` containing only `needle`, it returns the wrong file and misses the literal match.

Use native `multiGrep` with a single literal pattern and no filename constraints for plain searches and invalid-regex fallback. Keep valid regular expressions on the existing path and retain case, whole-word, ranges, limits, and pagination behavior. This is a focused correction to the existing plain-text search contract; it adds no feature and qualifies as a small obvious bug fix without a prior issue. The separate per-file whole-word cap problem is outside this PR.

Verification:
- The native-backed service regression failed on upstream: it returned `code.ts` with a six-character range instead of `words.txt` with the full eleven-character range. The focused workspace suites pass all 30 tests with the fix, including literal glob/bracket text, whitespace, case sensitivity, whole words, regexes, fallback, ranges, and pagination.
- `vp run check:changed --concurrency 1` passed format, lint, both knip scans, GraphQL generation, all three affected package typechecks, and 32 tests.
- The real Browser panel showed `words.txt` with the entire `needle *.ts` phrase highlighted, with no result for `code.ts`.

`vp run scenarios:prove scripts/scenarios/content-search-keeps-literal-query.e2e.ts --base 31a108c195f6f720c1d3232e3fb0ae9ef1e66554 --head 99c8775cc72a33202011ccc901e4c66417479289` proved the bug in the real app: the base fails the missing-`words.txt` assertion; the head passes both file assertions.

| Plain search for `needle *.ts` | Upstream base `31a108c195` | Fixed head `99c8775cc7` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Result | `code.ts`, line 1: `needle` | `words.txt`, line 1: `needle *.ts` |
| Highlight | `needle` only | Entire literal phrase |

author: gausejakub
body:
## Summary

Completes the remaining open backlog issues.

- **OAuth2 (#35, #34):** Gmail Authorization Code + PKCE over a loopback callback (bring-your-own Desktop client ID); Outlook uses the per-account `oauth_client_id` and XOAUTH2 for IMAP and SMTP. Rotated refresh tokens are saved, revoked grants are cleared from the keyring, and access tokens are refreshed before each (re)connect so long-running TUI/MCP sessions keep working past token expiry.
- **Cache verification (#36):** `:verify [folder|full]`, MCP `verify`, and a periodic pass (`[sync] verify_interval`, default 6h). Reconciles UIDs/flags with IMAP; runs SQLite quick/integrity check, a decrypt sample and an orphan sweep once per pass. Pending writes, and writes that finish mid-pass, are protected; dead-lettered ops are not.
- **Flag / unread / move (#15):** TUI `f`, `U`, `:move <folder>`; MCP `flag_message`, `unflag_message`, `mark_unread`, `move_message`. Cache updates optimistically, server delivery goes through the durable op queue.
- **Motion layer (#27):** spinner, progress bar, transient status messages, adaptive tick; `general.motion = false` disables animation.
- Fixes: sync timer storm from duplicate completions; ordering across timezone offsets.

### Review fixes included
- Optimistic move rows live in a reserved UID range (≥ `0xF0000000`), excluded from `HighestUID`, so moves no longer stall incremental sync of the destination or collide during reconciliation; an unmapped move no longer purges the destination folder.
- Queued ops replay in queue order (batched mark-reads are flushed before later ops), with an `id` tie-breaker.
- Verify takes message existence from `UID SEARCH`, so a FETCH parse failure can't delete a cached row.
- OAuth loopback ignores forged callbacks with the wrong `state`, and the code exchange has a timeout.
- MCP `move_message` returns the source folder plus `destination`, instead of labelling source UIDs with the destination folder.

### Not in scope
- #34: no built-in public Outlook client ID ships yet (needs an Azure app registration), so users configure their own. The issue stays open.

## Test plan
- `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...` all green
- New tests: OAuth flows/rotation/refresh, XOAUTH2, verification reconcile, placeholder/HighestUID/reconcile collisions, dead-letter handling, status motion, sync completion dedup

author: physicsqoo
body:
## Goal

Measure the **actual relationship between optional retained logical cache payload quotas, cache reuse, solve WallTime and Linux process peak RSS**, without changing the Full WMC solver or its public API.

Existing scientific reference: main at `66a1b22a5e128bb37735c4959d6c3ba91bb18532`, with opt-in logical quota API admitted only after A0, exact medium-CNF tests and native CodSpeed passed.

## New source-pinned research cohort (additive)

- Preserve the **existing 28-row** independent Linux cache-cap profile, its original CSV header, negative-resource controls, and historical artifact filename.
- Add a **separate 21-row CSV**: both analytical CNF families (equality chain and independent forced pairs) at 16, 32, and 64 variables, plus one 3-variable cache-hit positive control; each uses source-pinned **legacy / tight / roomy** cumulative logical-payload quotas.
- Each run is launched in a fresh Linux process under the existing parent-enforced five-second deadline and `prlimit` **512 MiB RLIMIT_AS virtual address-space**, not an RSS cap.
- Confirm independent exact Gaussian-rational Full WMC oracle and SAT for **every case**, tight quota actually rejects cached entries, roomy quota rejects none, and cache-hit control exercises reuse.
- Record cache entries, hits, logical key/bit totals, rejected admissions, wall time and Linux `VmHWM` per case. Fail the workflow on incomplete/malformed output, worker failure, missing controls, timeout, oracle mismatch, or a broken quota contract.

## Safety and performance interpretation

This is research-only instrumentation. `VmHWM` includes program/runtime/input allocations; logical quotas are **not byte caps**; `RLIMIT_AS` is a virtual address-space bound, **not physical RSS**. There is no production cross-platform supervisor, no Projected WMC and no comparison/ranking against GPMC or Ganak.

Do not infer sustained RSS savings from one Linux runner or claim an algorithm speedup without repeated controlled measurements. The existing 22 CodSpeed identities remain untouched.

## Acceptance

Check exact-HEAD Linux research workflow CSV shape and 21 source-locked oracle cases, original 28 cases and both guard negative controls; Rustfmt/strict Clippy/full native science, five platform coverage, and CodSpeed 22/22 unchanged. Review public scope and CI evidence before deciding merge.

## Verified exact-HEAD science and performance admission

- [Research Linux source cohort #43176457190](https://github.com/PhysicsQoo/RaWMoCS/actions/runs/43176457190): **SUCCESS**. Original **28** independently checked rows, plus new **21** logical quota rows, each in a separate Linux worker with source-pinned independent exact Full WMC oracle, SAT assertion, payload admission checks and VmHWM; **both** standalone modes individually passed memory-denial and timeout negative controls. No malformed or missing rows were accepted.
- [Source-pinned QuPRS A0 and Rust science #43176457196](https://github.com/PhysicsQoo/RaWMoCS/actions/runs/43176457196): **SUCCESS 6/6** at exact HEAD, covering Linux core, A0, Windows, Ubuntu ARM64 and both macOS platforms.
- [Rust benchmark / official CodSpeed #43176457180](https://github.com/PhysicsQoo/RaWMoCS/actions/runs/43176457180): **SUCCESS**, including cargo fmt, strict clippy, all fixed tests and actual upload. [CodSpeed result](https://app.codspeed.io/PhysicsQoo/RaWMoCS/runs/6af56ca82b3926b5b3224470) **22/22 identities**. [Comparison with immutable main run](https://app.codspeed.io/PhysicsQoo/RaWMoCS/runs/compare/6af56aa3f89dfd50840903e9..6af56ca82b3926b5b3224470): **22 unchanged**, no new benchmark IDs. CPU changed from AMD EPYC 7763 to Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C; do NOT infer CPU-time percentage improvements.
- The completed first isolated cohort showed on 64-variable independent-pairs CNF: legacy/roomy cache 97 entries versus tight 2; VmHWM 2480 / 2520 versus tight 2448 KiB; all three have 97 solver nodes, **zero cache hits**. Chain64 cache 3 / tight 0 / roomy 3, VmHWM 2476 / 2468 / 2472 KiB, zero hits. The cache3 positive control has one actual hit under each policy. **No general RSS or WallTime saving is established**: single process-cohort run, allocator/page granularity, source-specific synthetic structure and noisy elapsed times.
- GitHub diff is restricted to the **research-only example, workflow, and profiling document**; original solver implementation, 22 benchmark IDs, QuPRS default solver and published APIs are untouched. No private tracking IDs appear in public artifacts. PR has no submitted reviews or unresolved review threads at last check.

**Decision:** suitable to merge as reproducible *measurement and guard-qualification infrastructure*, not as a speedup or production hard RSS limit.

author: launsion-boop
body:
## 問題

真機（iPhone Air，2026-11-12）：Bot 回合裡 bash 觸發結構審批，等用戶點卡時 Worker `postApproval` 經宿主 `/v1/http` 打到 Bot listener `/approval`；listener 要等用戶決定才回響應頭，llm-bridge 的 60 s 響應頭看門狗（`PDSH_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT`）先觸發，工具 60 s 後被判 NOT executed。宿主出口在消費者離開後仍讀完上游，App 看不到；Worker 的配對 `/identity/cancel` 到了但不取消審批，卡片 pending 到 300 s 超時才記為 deny——殭屍卡。用戶感受：Bot 卡一分鐘才回覆。

## 修法（契約 PC-20261112-bot-approval-keepalive）

- **App `/approval`**：`Accept` 顯式含 `text/event-stream` 且 5 s 未決 → 沿用 `/mcp` 長調用的 SSE 形式（5 s 回頭、每 15 s `: keepalive`、恰好一個 `event: message`）。快結果或無 SSE accept 仍 JSON。審批等待只受 300 s 審批超時約束；60 s 看門狗本身不放寬。
- **Worker `postApproval`**（`approval-gate`／`sandbox-approval` 共用）：發 `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`，嚴格解析恰好一個 message 事件，其他形態 fail closed。
- **App `/identity/cancel`**：級聯取消該 (sessionId, callId) 仍 pending 的交互審批（既有 `cancelled`/`consumer_cancelled`），卡片收起；持久待辦不動。

author: devrochy
body:
## Qué hace

Primera parte visible del rediseño **«habilidades por agente»**: **fase 5a** de la SPEC nueva y de **ADR-0190 (en preparación)**. Comercio, agenda, cobranza y suscripciones pasan a ser tipos de agente; el dueño controla dentro de cada agente sus acciones, una por una.

Solo usa lo que ya existe: los bindings `tools` del AgentSpec v3 (`ToolBindingV3`) se editan en el borrador con el proxy `/api/agent-editor/[id]/draft` y se publican como hoy. No hay endpoints nuevos.

### Editor del agente: paso «Acciones» (nuevo paso 4)
- Lista las acciones del agente agrupadas por lo que hacen: Pedidos, Catálogo, Citas, Cartera, Suscripciones, Pagos, Leads, Clientes, Conversación y «Otras acciones».
- Por acción: encendido, «Ponerle un tope por conversación» (1 a 10.000) y «Pedir confirmación antes de hacerla».
- Un binding sin cambios sale **idéntico** (no se agregan `enabled: true` ni `requiresConfirmation: false`), así que guardar otro paso no ensucia el contenido.
- `buscar_conocimiento` no aparece aquí: lo sigue controlando «Memoria y conocimiento» (si no, `aplicarConocimiento` pisaría el cambio). La pestaña lo explica.
- Los errores `tools[i]` (de la API o de referencias retiradas) ahora van a este paso, junto a su acción, y ya no a Superpoderes. Una acción retirada bloquea publicar aunque esté apagada (`lint_agentspec` / `referencias_retiradas`), así que tiene **«Quitar del agente»** (con «Deshacer»).

### Agrupación temporal
`lib/grupos-de-acciones.ts` es un mapa local nombre → grupo y nombre legible, armado con los nombres reales de agent-core `develop` (`packages/pack-*/pack_*/skills.py` y las acciones del core). Tiene fallback por prefijo (`cob_*`, `sub_*`, `*calendar*`…) y «Otras acciones» para lo desconocido. **Se borra cuando el backend exponga `grupo`.** El test recorre todas las acciones del backend y comprueba que ninguna cae en «Otras».

### Configuración › Herramientas del agente
Muestra el aviso «Ahora se controla en cada agente…» con enlace a /agentes. La sección no se quita todavía.

### Texto
Dice «acción» y «habilidad»; nunca «tool», «pack» ni «plugin» (manual de marca §9.3). Hay un test que lo revisa.

## Cómo se probó
- `vitest` completo: 246 archivos, 2118 tests en verde. Hay tests nuevos de la lógica, de los grupos y del componente (con axe). Se ajustaron los tests que iban a «Paso 5» para publicar (ahora es el 6) y el de referencias retiradas (la acción retirada se muestra en Acciones).
- `tsc` y `eslint` limpios.
- En el preview con el backend de prueba (`RETIRADAS=1 ACCIONES=1`, opción nueva del script): apagué una acción, marqué confirmación en otra, quité la retirada y guardé. El `PUT` del borrador mandó `tools` con exactamente esos cambios y el resto intacto. El aviso de Configuración se ve, y el paso cabe a 375 px sin desplazamiento horizontal.

## Fuera de este PR
- La clave `grupo` y los nombres legibles en la API, y luego borrar `lib/grupos-de-acciones.ts`.
- Asignar acciones a opciones de plantillas (SPEC-40).
- Quitar la sección «Herramientas del agente» de Configuración.

No mergear ni desplegar hasta que lo revise el dueño.

author: aa-monts
body:
**To be reviewed by @mustafab0.**

## Why do we need this?
`dimos --simulation=mujoco run coordinator-xarm7` exits 1 a few seconds after start with `ValueError: sim_mujoco reports 8 joints, expected 7`. The shipped `xarm7/scene.xml` has 8 joints (7 arm joints and the gripper) and `MujocoSimModule` reports all of them, but the blueprint's hardware is arm-only (`dimos/robot/manipulators/xarm/blueprints/basic.py:151`, 7 joints), and the sim adapter requires the two counts to match (`dimos/hardware/manipulators/sim/adapter.py:86-90`). `coordinator-teleop-xarm7` declares the gripper joint, so its count matches and it starts.

## What is this feature?
In simulation only, `coordinator-xarm7` now declares the gripper joint: `xarm7_hardware("arm", gripper=bool(global_config.simulation))`. The simulator is given the 7 arm joints as its `dof`, so the adapter sees the scene's 8 joints and the sim detects the gripper and drives it through the scene's own gripper range. Without `--simulation` the hardware is the same arm-only xArm7 as before, so the real-arm path and `test_standalone_xarm7_has_only_arm_tasks` are unchanged.

For the owner to decide: in simulation the trajectory task now spans 8 joints (`joint1..joint7`, and `arm/gripper` in the scene's range, 0 to 0.85), on hardware still 7. If `coordinator-xarm7` should look arm-only in the sim too, the alternative below is the way.

Alternatives not taken:
- Let `ShmMujocoAdapter` accept hardware that declares only the arm joints and leave the scene's gripper alone. It keeps 7 joints in the sim, but it loosens a shared check that today catches a scene and hardware that disagree.
- Declare the gripper on hardware too (`gripper=True`, as `coordinator-xarm6` does). That changes what the blueprint does on a real xArm7.

No test added: one composition line, evaluated at import time from the global config.

## How to manually run this
```bash
dimos --viewer none --simulation=mujoco run coordinator-xarm7
```
Before: `MujocoSimModule: gripper detected ... idx=7`, then `sim_mujoco reports 8 joints, expected 7` and exit 1. After: `ShmMujocoAdapter connected dof=8 gripper_dof=1` and `Blueprint started`; Ctrl-C stops it.

On macOS the arm sim also needs #5200 (DIM-469); without it both main and this branch stop earlier at `launch_passive requires ... mjpython`. What was checked, on macOS 27.2 (Apple Silicon) with #5200's `mujoco_engine.py` change applied locally:
- main `17b0763a36`: exit 1 with the error above.
- this branch: connects with the gripper detected, starts, runs 40 s until Ctrl-C, exit 0.
- headless and in-process (the blueprint's coordinator on its own sim module, no launch): a trajectory that moves only `arm/gripper` to 0.4 puts the gripper actuator at 135 of 0..255 and the scene joint at 0.42 rad.

Not checked: Linux, the MuJoCo window, moving the arm joints with a trajectory (only the gripper was moved), real hardware.

## Which issue(s) does this PR close?
Fixes [DIM-477](https://linear.app/dimensional/issue/DIM-477)

- [x] I have read and approved the [CLA](https://github.com/dimensionalOS/dimos/blob/main/CLA.md).

author: naveen-konda
body:
## Problem
Every time a user leaves a folder view in Browse (opens a document or another folder), the previous view stays in browser memory and is never released (about 1.3–3.5 MB, ~11k–25k DOM nodes and ~2.7k–4k listeners per switch), so the tab slows down over a working day. Jira: [WEBUI-2411](https://hyland.atlassian.net/browse/WEBUI-2411)

## Root cause
`nuxeo-selection-toolbar` declared `disconnectedCallback()` inside the legacy `Polymer({...})` object. There `super` is `Object.prototype`, so Polymer's own disconnect logic never ran and the behaviors' `detached()` was skipped: `I18nBehavior` never removed its `i18n-locale-loaded` listener from `document`. The Ctrl/⌘ + . shortcut listener added in `ready()` was an anonymous function and was never removed either. Through `__dataHost`, those listeners retained the whole detached folder view. Introduced by WEBUI-1750 (#2727).

## Changes
* **`elements/nuxeo-selection/nuxeo-selection-toolbar.js`**: add the `document` listeners in `attached()` and remove them in `detached()`, replacing the `disconnectedCallback()` override so Polymer and the behaviors tear down normally. The shortcut handler is now kept in `_onShortcutKeydown` so it can be removed.
* **`test/nuxeo-selection-toolbar.test.js`**: unit tests that attach/detach the toolbar and assert no `document` listener is left (including after repeated cycles) and that the shortcut no longer fires once detached. They fail without the fix.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm test` passes (3159 tests)
- [x] New tests fail on the unfixed code (`keydown` and `i18n-locale-loaded` left on `document`) and pass with the fix
- [ ] Manual: in Chrome DevTools run `getEventListeners(document).keydown.length` and `getEventListeners(document)['i18n-locale-loaded'].length`, open a document from a folder and go back 10 times, then collect garbage: both counts should stay flat instead of growing by 10 each

## Notes
Backport pair: develop-2023 (same fix on the other LTS line).

author: imojenisys
body:
Slice 6 of #3411: the gap #3732 records. A format whose rules didn't decide a whole replacement got no protection for its read-only regions. The incoming text was taken as it was.

**The shape.**
- `IReadOnlyRegionRules.Replace` returns `ContentReplacement?`. Null leaves the decision to the IDE, which is also what a format with no rules gets. Its remarks say how the IDE reads the incoming text (with the current prefix's length when it starts with that prefix, otherwise 0), that the IDE never puts the prefix back, and that an added region is refused.
- `HexIDE.Core/Language/ContentReplacementRules.Replace` asks the format first. Otherwise it accepts the text only when the reader's regions keep their text and order, and the hanging regions their keys and order.
- A change, drop, addition or reorder is refused with "The content would change {P}, which only the IDE changes. Nothing was changed." {P} names the changed or dropped regions through the format's `DescribeRegions`. An addition is named from the incoming text, and anything else is "read-only text".
- `CodeEditorViewModel.ReplaceContent` and `DocumentContent.Write` both go through it, and their docs say so.

**Nothing a VB6 user or caller sees changes.** `Vb6ReadOnlyRegionRules` keeps its own decision. So there's no changelog fragment, no spec requirement and no `MISSING_FEATURES.md` change. The rule is internal, as slices 6a to 6e kept theirs.

**Tests.** `ReplacementWithoutAFormatRulePreservesTheReadersRegions` covers each site (`set_file_content`, `TrySetContent`, the closed writer), each policy (no rules, rules without `Replace`, rules with a phrase) and each change (changed, dropped, added, reordered, line renamed, reordered without hanging). Every case is named, so a failure says which one. Bypassing the fallback at the call sites fails 54 cases, and round 2's added-region wording failed 3 before its fix. `RunningCodeEditTests`' eight rows now get VB6's rules for their setup write, with assertions unchanged.

**Design read by hexide-gen** over both rounds. Its changes are in: an added region named from the incoming text, the four docs, the named cases, and the removals. Totals reconcile against main's CI: HexIDE.Tests gains the new cases, Integration is unchanged at 3,088, and CI should show 66 skips where WSL shows 69.

body:
The maintainer asked what a user is supposed to do with `dev.json` and a `.minisig` beside every archive. Nothing, but the release text did not say so.

`tooling/release-notes.sh <channel> <dist>` writes three short sections in Markdown:
- **Installing**: unpack, put on the `PATH`, from then on `toolchain install` / `update`; zig via `toolchain install zig`; a link to the Book.
- **The other files**: none of them is needed to install. What the index, the signatures and `SHA256SUMS` are, and that the command checks them itself, from GitHub or the mirror alike.
- **Checking a download by hand**: the `minisign -Vm <archive> -P <key>` line with the channel's key (from `tooling/release-keys`, which a test holds equal to the keys in the binary), the reserve key, and why `sha256sum -c` alone finds a broken download but not a forged one.

The command's name (`lyric5` now) is read from the linux-x64 archive, so the text cannot drift from what the archive holds. The script refuses (exit 1) when there is no such archive or no command in it.

Where it goes:
- `dev.yml`: after the dev prerelease's intro (the half sentence about the index and signatures moves into the new section).
- `release.yml`, dry run: after the draft's line. A real release: the tag's own text first (`--notes-from-tag`), then this, by `gh release edit`. The publish job gets a checkout for the script and the keys; it signs nothing.

Checked locally against a made-up dist with an archive packed the way `package.yml` packs it (`tar -czf … -C out .`, so `./lyric5`): the text for dev and stable, the dev.yml assignment as bash runs it, both refusals. The dev prerelease shows the result after the next merge to main; the dry run and a real release are not run here.

author: ericvh
body:
Part of #39. Replaces #159 (rebased onto next after #158 and #161).

Replaces #167, rebased onto next after #162 (mcpd stages 4 and 5) and #166 (Styx tools). The conflicts were in README.md (the `sh` row keeps `<>` and adds `-e`; the system tools row gains the disk and install commands) and Cargo.lock (regenerated). After the rebase: fmt, workspace clippy, build-root, clippy-guests, kernel clippy, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask kernel --kvm` and all four TCG configurations of `cargo xtask kernel` pass.

Three commits, in the issue's priority order.

**mk and sh -e**
- `sh -e`, as Inferno's sh source has it (the man page leaves it out): a command that fails anywhere but at the end of a sequence raises its status; sub-shells inherit it.
- mk runs each recipe with `sh -e`, so it stops at its first failing command, and runs up to `$NPROC` recipes at once (default 1), with the job slot in `$nproc`. On a failure it waits for the running recipes before it stops; `-k` carries on. Corpus: `mkpar.sh`.

**Disk tools and `#S` partitions**
- `#S` takes sd(3)'s `part name start end` and `delpart name` on `ctl`; a partition is a file beside `data`, and `ctl` lists it. The partitions live in the kernel only, as in Inferno. Errors are Inferno's (`bad process or channel control request`, `i/o error`).
- `disk/fdisk [-abfprw] [-s sectorsize]` (PC table, primary partitions, in sectors), `disk/prep [-bcfnprw] [-a name]... [-s sectorsize]` (Plan 9 table in sector 1; `w`/`-w` also update the device), both with prep(8)'s editor (`a d . p P w q h`, fdisk's `A e t`, expressions with `. $ n% + - * /`). `disk/mbr [-9] [-m file]` writes sector 0's boot code (default: our own 22-byte stub that prints "not a bootable disk").
- The kernel's disk steps add, read, write and delete partitions on sdV1 and run `disk/prep -bw -a nvram -a fs` on one (expected.out updated). Corpus: `diskpart.sh` on image files.

**install/**
- `create [-uvxo] [-p proto] [-r root] [-s source] [-N uid] [-G gid] [-d desc] [-t time] name`, `inst [-chtuvF] [-r root] package [prefix...]`, `info [-r root] package`, `wrap2list [-i] [-r root] [file...]`, `updatelog [-c] [-p proto] [-r root] [-t now gen] [-x path]... log [path...]`, `applylog [-cegnsuv] [-T timefile] clientlog clientroot serverroot [path...]`.
- Formats are Inferno's: mkfs archives with a `/wrap/name/stamp/{package|update,desc,proto,md5sum,remove}` header (stamps in decimal, `update` as `%22ud`), and applylog(8)'s log lines `time gen verb path serverpath mode uid gid mtime length [sum]`. Shared code in `appl/lib/wrap`; `/lib/proto/all` added. Corpus: `install.sh`.

**Not done, and why**
- `disk/format` (FAT12/16 maker) and `kfscmd` for purgfs: not started. kfscmd fits purgfs (sync, check and usage exist in `purg_fs::dev::DevFs`); it needs a control file, which means a small change to `#K` (for example an attach spec giving a `cmd` file, served at `/chan/kfs.main.cmd` as Inferno's kfs does) and kernel tests.
- `ftl`: not meaningful here (no flash translation layer on virtio-blk); `kfs` is the purgfs device itself.
- `install/mergelog`, `wdiff`, `wfind`, `install` and create's `-U` (hybrid package): not done.
- fdisk: extended (secondary) partitions are listed by their primary entry, not followed; units are sectors, not cylinders.
- `man2txt`/`man2html`: out of scope until the project has its own man pages. `sendmail`: out of scope (no mail system).

**Bugs seen, not fixed**
- `sed` handles only `s///` (`sed 1q`, `sed -n 2p` fail with `only s/// scripts`).

author: sziller
body:
Refs #5 (Local Command Interface and Proof-of-Concept Request Processing, 2/6). Implements the approved technical refinement. The issue is intentionally not auto-closed.

## Summary

Extends the existing Engine IPC and `ape` CLI. No second communication architecture, thread, or Engine loop is introduced.

- **`ape --ping`** and **`ape --echo TEXT`**: stateless diagnostic queries answered by the running Engine. `ping` returns the execution id, Engine pid, completed operating cycles and Engine UTC time. `echo` returns Engine-validated text (at most 256 characters, counted in Unicode characters).
- **Protocol v1, extended additively:** optional correlation id (at most 64 characters), optional argument object, response id and result object, new error codes `invalid_arguments` and `invalid_correlation_id`. Requests without the new fields remain valid. `ape` generates a correlation id per request and rejects an answer that does not carry it.
- **Dispatcher:** `Engine._handle_administrative_request` stays the single entry point (authorize, dispatch, answer). Operations are classed explicitly as `QUERY` or `LIFECYCLE_CONTROL`. There is no operational-command class, because none exists yet.
- **Responsive idle wait (D7):** a new `idle_wait.py` (`selectors` plus a wake-up `socketpair`) lets socket readiness interrupt the idle wait. One thread, one loop. Requests are answered while idling without starting extra cycles, and the monotonic cycle deadline is unchanged. A wake byte written after the stop flag makes STOP and handled signals wake the wait with no lost wake-up. Readiness without progress (for example `accept()` failing with `EMFILE`) makes the Engine ignore the socket for 0.25 s instead of spinning. Idle servicing is limited to the time left before the next cycle. Wake-up resources are closed during cleanup, and a failure to close either the endpoint or the wake channel does not skip the other.
- **CLI:** `-x`, `--ping` and `--echo` are mutually exclusive. `peer_not_authorized` maps to exit 4. The default timeout stays at 5 s.
- **Diagnostics:** `INFO` traces for request received, processed and answered, naming the operation, the (quoted) correlation id and the outcome. Request arguments, in particular echo text, are never logged. Queries are not lifecycle audit events.
- **Docs:** new "Request Classes" section and an idle-servicing note in the architecture document. In the operations document: protocol fields, error codes, `ape` usage and exit codes, bounds, traces, tests, and the replaced "once per cycle" latency statement.

## Architectural decisions

- `ping` and `echo` are queries: no journal, nothing persisted or replayed, no "accepted" wording. STOP remains a lifecycle-control request: audited, not journaled, not replayed.
- The same authorization (Linux permissions plus Engine-side peer check) applies to every operation, queries included.
- Readiness only lets the Engine answer earlier. It never makes a cycle start earlier or later beyond bounded servicing time, and external communication is still never the clock.
- A handler exception during idle servicing follows the existing failure path, as inside a cycle.

## Verification

Full suite: **279 passed** (85 existing Issue #4 tests unchanged, plus 194 new). The new files were also run three times in a row and once under extra CPU load, without failures.

New tests cover the 14 verification points of the refinement:

| Refinement point | Where |
|---|---|
| 1 Engine-side `ping`/`echo` | `test_engine_lifecycle.py`, `test_request_processing.py` (the answer carries the Engine's pid and execution id) |
| 2 Argument validation (Unicode, 256/257 boundary, JSON escapes, missing/wrong types) | `test_engine_lifecycle.py`, `test_request_processing.py`, `test_ipc_protocol.py` |
| 3 Malformed/unsupported requests rejected safely | `test_request_processing.py`, `test_local_ingress.py` |
| 4 Authorization | `test_engine_lifecycle.py` (queries and STOP), `test_cli.py` (exit 4) |
| 5 Engine runs without requests | existing tests plus idle-CPU tests |
| 6 Requests trigger no extra cycles | `test_request_processing.py`, `test_engine_lifecycle.py` |
| 7 30 s interval does not mean a 30 s answer | `test_request_processing.py` |
| 8 STOP and signals interrupt idle waits | `test_request_processing.py`, `test_engine_lifecycle.py`, `test_idle_wait.py` |
| 9 Stalled clients and bursts | `test_request_processing.py`, `test_engine_lifecycle.py`, `test_local_ingress.py` |
| 10 Readiness without progress cannot busy-loop | `test_engine_lifecycle.py` |
| 11 Wake-up resources released | `test_idle_wait.py`, `test_engine_lifecycle.py` |
| 12 Issue #4 tests still pass | whole suite |
| 13 No query persisted or replayed | `test_engine_lifecycle.py`, `test_request_processing.py` |
| 14 No hardware | `test_engine_lifecycle.py` (no hardware modules involved) plus design (no adapters exist) |

Sanity check of the tests themselves: I temporarily broke the implementation five ways (no wake byte on stop, no back-off, time limit not passed to servicing, no servicing while idle, wake channel not closed). Each break made the relevant tests fail.

### Manual verification

```
# terminal 1
aquaponics-engine --cycle-interval 30
# terminal 2
ape --ping                 # answers in milliseconds despite the 30 s interval
ape --echo "héllo"         # prints the text back
ape --echo "$(printf 'x%.0s' {1..257})" ; echo $?   # refused (invalid_arguments), exit status 1
ape -x                     # shutdown initiated; the Engine exits promptly
```

Measured locally with a 30 s interval: `ape --ping` about 55 ms and `ape -x` about 40 ms.

## Behavior changes to be aware of

- STOP latency is no longer up to one cycle interval (the documented Issue #4 limitation is replaced). The remaining bound is an in-progress cycle plus bounded ingress time (at most 0.5 s per call, plus about 0.4 s worst case from a stalled client's read and write deadlines).
- `peer_not_authorized` now gives `ape` exit status 4 for every operation, including STOP (previously 1). This follows the refinement.
- `stop` now refuses an `args` object (`invalid_arguments`). `ape` never sends one.
- Hardening outside the literal scope but within "malformed requests are rejected safely": the decoder turns `RecursionError` on very deep JSON nesting into a protocol error (relevant to the Python 3.11 baseline).
- The `ScriptedIngress` test stand-in gained `readiness_source = None`.

## Remaining limitations

- Responsiveness is bounded by the operating cycle in progress. Issue #6 must keep each control-loop phase time-bounded, as the refinement states.
- In the `EMFILE`-style fault case, requests are delayed by up to 0.25 s between retries, and the ingress logs a warning per failed `accept()`.
- A real permission denial for a different Linux user is still not automated (it needs a second account). The Engine-side check and the CLI mapping are tested separately.
- Python 3.14 was used for testing. The 3.11 baseline was not run here.
- AsciiDoc was reviewed by reading. No renderer is installed, and generated HTML is not tracked.
- `ape --echo -text` needs `--echo=-text`, which is standard `argparse` behavior and is documented.
- Unchanged and out of scope: synchronous `fsync` of the audit file (#8), the general logging architecture (#7), systemd (#9), phase restructuring (#6).

No hardware access, REST endpoint, scheduling, operational command, journal or database is added. `production`, rulesets, Actions policy, and the Issue and Project status are untouched. `documentation/media/` and `engine-launcher.py` are untouched.

author: xianhong1208
body:
1.3, part 4: image generation at `POST /v1/images/generations`, OpenAI's request shape, images back as base64 only.

## Engines (new recipes)

- **`vllm-omni-image`**: diffusers pipelines (Z-Image-Turbo, SDXL, FLUX.1-schnell, Qwen-Image) on NVIDIA with the `vllm/vllm-omni:v0.32.0` image text to speech already pins. `--max-generated-image-size` repeats the deployment's pixel cap in the engine; VAE slicing on; model offload and VAE tiling as options.
- **`sd-cpp`**: stable-diffusion.cpp's `sd-server`: `vulkan` for every AMD GPU/APU (render node only), `cuda`, and `cpu-process` without Docker. Its images exist only under rolling tags (`master-vulkan`, `master-cuda`): pinned by digest, entered in the lock file, and `pin_images.py` now keeps such a pin (reports the move as information) unless `--move-rolling`. The CPU process is release `master-1043-3be2378`: later Linux releases are built on Ubuntu 26.04 and need glibc 2.43. Its OpenAI API is the same. It is a `.zip`: the agent now unpacks zips (feature `engine_zip`; placement refuses agents without it). sd-server has no API key, so placement also requires the key guard.

## Gateway

- Checks before sending: prompt, `n`, `size` (`WxH` or `auto`), `output_format`, steps, seed, guidance. **`response_format: url` → 400 `response_format_not_supported`** (no images are kept); `stream` → 400. `<sd_cpp_extra_args>` in a prompt is refused.
- Per-deployment caps with working defaults: images per request (4), largest side (the model's own), sizes a multiple of 16 (64 for UNet models), most steps (50), longest prompt (4,000).
- Only known fields reach the engine (vLLM-Omni's `lora` path, `extra_params` and system prompts never do); for sd-server the extras are built into one escaped `<sd_cpp_extra_args>` block.
- **Queue per deployment**: `concurrency` (1) per replica, FIFO waiting in the gateway up to `queue` (8), then 429 `queue_full` with Retry-After; 503 `queue_timeout`; a client that gives up leaves the queue. Image requests use the deployment's own read timeout (600 s / 1,800 s).
- Answer in OpenAI's shape without engine extras; engine errors as `engine_error`. `/v1/images/edits` and `/variations` → 404 `endpoint_not_supported`.
- Usage: `images`, `kilopixels` (from each image's header), `busy_ms` (replica time × GPUs). No tokens, no cloud, no prompt filtering (documented).

## Catalog, estimate, UI

- `image` task, `diffusers` format; the inspector reads model_index.json + components' safetensors headers (one set of weights, nothing from the top level), and GGUF/safetensors repos for sd.cpp with text encoder / VAE files found by name or named (`components`).
- Estimate method `diffusers`: components (16-bit for vLLM-Omni), activations for the caps, one VAE decode, offload.
- Recommended *Images* group, Apache-2.0 / OpenRAIL only, pinned to commits. FLUX.1-dev, SD-Turbo, SDXL-Turbo, SD3.5 left out by licence.
- Playground **Image** tab; Usage columns; Try it.

## Verification

- Backend: full suite on SQLite and on PostgreSQL 17 (927 passed, 1 skipped on PostgreSQL); `ruff check .` clean. New `tests/test_image_generation.py` (FY-IGEN-001 to 024) with fake engines in both request styles: generation, caps, url refused, only known fields sent, the queue (two at once on concurrency 1, 429 when full, a client that gives up leaves, a newcomer does not jump), usage, engine errors, keys / allowlists / rpm, no cloud, rendering, estimates, the inspector against a fake Hub, the recommended list, zip unpacking, placement gates, Try it and the Playground options, rolling-tag pins, the acceptance decoder.
- Mutation check: 72 mutants on the new guards, all killed.
- Web: lint (0 errors), typecheck, 209 tests (FY-WEB-171 to 173 new), build.
- Real run on a throwaway HTTPS server with a CPU agent (process runtime, no Docker): the `cpu-process` zip engine downloaded, verified and unpacked; Stable Diffusion 1.5 Q8_0 (single checkpoint, `-m`) and Z-Image-Turbo Q4_0 with its Qwen3-4B text encoder and VAE (`--diffusion-model --llm --vae`) both made correct images through the official SDK (`client.images.generate`). `scripts/accept_img.py` on the CPU: 16 passed, 1 skipped (no vision model). Seconds per image on 16 to 32 cores of a busy host: SD 1.5 512x512 20 steps about 100 s (5 steps 35 s); Z-Image 8 steps 121 s at 512x512, 517 s at 1024x1024. `num_inference_steps` and `seed` through `<sd_cpp_extra_args>` work (same seed, same bytes); `n` images are made one after another.
- Memory, measured on the CPU and used to calibrate `sd-cpp`: linear, about 6.3 GiB per megapixel beyond the weights for both models.
- Screenshots of the Image tab, the catalog, the recommended list and Usage at 1440 and 390 px: no horizontal scroll, no console errors.

Not verified here (no GPU): vLLM-Omni image serving, sd.cpp on CUDA and Vulkan, the `vllm-omni-image` memory constants. The A100 and AMD acceptance runs follow.

author: marioernestovaldes
body:
Fixes **T2** of the off-target GUI review.

> The first Vina run completed **with no Vina binary installed** while the Programs step showed **Backend = binary**. The Python `vina` module was used instead. Nothing in the UI or in the stored protocol says which backend produced the numbers.

The fallback itself is intended (`_vina_here`): without a binary, Vina docks through its Python bindings. What was wrong is that nothing recorded it.

**Resolved where it docks.** The job carries the backend that was *asked for*. Each worker resolves it on its own host (`constants.vina_here`), so a worker with a binary uses it even if the submitting machine has none, and the reverse. (An earlier revision of this PR resolved it at submit; review showed that pinned remote jobs to the submitting machine's backend.)

**Recorded through the result path.** The Vina runner stamps the backend it used on each row it returns (`extra.vina_backend`). The parent records it on the run as `docking_runs.protocol["executed"]["vina_backend"]`, a sorted list (`["python"]`, or `["binary", "python"]` if workers differed):
- sharded runs and campaigns: from each shard envelope, in `ShardHitWriter.handle`;
- docking, redocking and row campaigns: from the written rows, at finalize (`_supersede`).

`protocol["config"]["vina_backend"]` keeps the request, so a re-run asks again instead of inheriting one host's fallback.

**Shown.** The Programs step's Backend combo lists `binary` and `python`, and both stay selectable. Without a local binary the list reads **"AutoDock Vina - no binary"** and the panel says that a run docked here falls back to the bindings, while a worker that has the binary still uses it.

**Not in the label/hash.** As `protocols.py` already decides, the backend is an execution detail. Hashing it would split existing Vina results from a re-run after installing the binary.

Tests:
- `test_vina_backend_executed.py`: worker with binary uses it whatever the submitter had; worker without one falls back and stamps `python`; `record_executed` merges hosts and keeps the request; rows reach the run at finalize; the shard handler records the envelope's backend.
- `test_the_submitting_machine_does_not_resolve_the_vina_backend` (test_docking_rerun).
- `test_vina_without_a_local_binary_says_so_and_keeps_the_requested_backend` (test_docking_phase4).

74 passed across these and the shard, campaign, skip-existing, redock, screening-backend and hit-materialization test files.

author: olyasir
body:
Linear: PRO-123 (tech-debt, no visible change)

## What

A cold first visit to the landing or the quiz painted one network round trip late: `styles.css` and the Google Fonts sheet were both render-blocking, so paint waited for a second round trip after the HTML.

- **Fonts sheet no longer blocks render.** Loaded with `media="print"` and switched to `all` on load, with a `<noscript>` fallback. The fonts already use `display=swap`, so the fallback face was already what painted first; layout shift is unchanged.
- **`styles.css` is inlined into the four pages at image build.** `inline-styles.sh` replaces the `<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css" />` line with a `<style>` block holding the file. `styles.css` stays the single source and the source HTML is untouched, so opening a page over `file://` or `python3 -m http.server` still works. The build fails, naming the page, if a listed page has lost that link line.

## Measured (pre-merge, same model as PRO-114's local check)

Main vs this branch, each built from git (`origin/main` as is; the branch through the real `inline-styles.sh`), served under the live hostname with modelled Slow 3G (2000 ms, 500 kbps) and live Google Fonts under DevTools throttling. 390x780, cold.

| Page | FCP main | FCP branch | CLS main / branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| index.html | 4704 ms | 2584 ms | 0.002 / 0.002 |
| en.html | 4536 ms | 2524 ms | 0.008 / 0.008 |
| quiz.html | 4600 ms | 2460 ms | 0.006 / 0.006 |
| quiz-en.html | 4596 ms | 2440 ms | 0.026 / 0.026 |

- First paint now follows the HTML, at the same floor as the app since PRO-114 (2.45 s live).
- Same computed body/heading fonts, background and 390 px width on every page. Final screenshots are pixel-identical on both quizzes; on the landings they differ only by the animated SOS demo's timing (side by side looks the same).
- Inlining adds `styles.css` (about 6 KB gzipped) to every HTML response and drops it as a separate cached file. On Slow 3G that's about 0.1 s of transfer; repeat visits revalidate the HTML anyway.
- Removing the link line breaks the build: checked with a page that lacks it (exit 1, message names the page).

author: naveen-konda
body:
## Problem
Every time a user leaves a folder view in Browse (opens a document or another folder), the previous view stays in browser memory and is never released (about 1.3–3.5 MB, ~11k–25k DOM nodes and ~2.7k–4k listeners per switch), so the tab slows down over a working day. Jira: [WEBUI-2411](https://hyland.atlassian.net/browse/WEBUI-2411)

## Root cause
`nuxeo-selection-toolbar` declared `disconnectedCallback()` inside the legacy `Polymer({...})` object. There `super` is `Object.prototype`, so Polymer's own disconnect logic never ran and the behaviors' `detached()` was skipped: `I18nBehavior` never removed its `i18n-locale-loaded` listener from `document`. The Ctrl/⌘ + . shortcut listener added in `ready()` was an anonymous function and was never removed either. Through `__dataHost`, those listeners retained the whole detached folder view. Introduced by WEBUI-1750 (#2727).

## Changes
* **`elements/nuxeo-selection/nuxeo-selection-toolbar.js`**: add the `document` listeners in `attached()` and remove them in `detached()`, replacing the `disconnectedCallback()` override so Polymer and the behaviors tear down normally. The shortcut handler is now kept in `_onShortcutKeydown` so it can be removed.
* **`test/nuxeo-selection-toolbar.test.js`**: unit tests that attach/detach the toolbar and assert no `document` listener is left (including after repeated cycles) and that the shortcut no longer fires once detached. They fail without the fix.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm test` passes (3159 tests)
- [x] New tests fail on the unfixed code (`keydown` and `i18n-locale-loaded` left on `document`) and pass with the fix
- [ ] Manual: in Chrome DevTools run `getEventListeners(document).keydown.length` and `getEventListeners(document)['i18n-locale-loaded'].length`, open a document from a folder and go back 10 times, then collect garbage: both counts should stay flat instead of growing by 10 each

## Notes
Backport pair: develop-2025 (same fix on the other LTS line).

This supersedes the 0246 rule "CREATIVE_MEDIA is never trial-funded". Migration **0275** was allocated by the coordinator. The trial program stays **CLOSED** and the creative program stays **INACTIVE**, so nothing can spend until the owner opens both.

1. **Grant at trial start.** Inserting a trial enrollment (any path) grants one creative lot in the trial school's own wallet, in the same transaction:
   - new lot kind `TRIAL`, 1,500 credits (the assumed $0.01 provider cost per credit);
   - it expires exactly when the trial ends;
   - it is linked to its enrollment by `trial_enrollment_id`, which the lot CHECK requires.

   `hon_os_trial_creative_grants` snapshots the credits and the cost stop for each trial. `hon_os_trial_creative_policy` holds the amounts in force (migration owner only; an HQ setting can come later).
2. **Spending** goes through the existing `reserve_saas_creative_credits` path, so Creative Studio images, video and avatars (`avatar.create`, later `avatar.video`) work at HQ-published rates.
   - TRIAL lots are spent first (rank 1).
   - A trial school is eligible for the trial window only (index 0, trial start to end, no subscription).
   - A trial school never opens an included monthly window.
3. **Two stops.**
   - Credits: never more than 1,500.
   - Real cost: `ai_trial_funding_available(..., 'CREATIVE_MEDIA')` is true only while the trial is live and the creative provider cost recorded for the organization during the trial is below $15.
   - Reservations already held when the cap is reached can still finish (at most one request each).
   - Agent-inference funding is byte-for-byte the 0246 rule.
4. **Receipt and screens.**
   - The trial receipt now has `creativeCreditsIncluded: true` and `creativeCredits` (granted, left now, expiry = trial end).
   - The wallet's `byKind` lists `TRIAL` after `INCLUDED_MONTHLY`, but only when the school has a trial lot, so every other wallet reads exactly as before.
   - The start page shows the creative credits. Its "Creative Studio is not included" wording is replaced (EN/KO/ES).

- `packages/database/migrations/0275_hon_os_trial_creative_credits.sql`, checksums, staging repin (0275), `verify-rls.mjs` (2 new tables), `ai-spend-entrypoints.json` (new spend reference `hon_os_trial_creative_funded`)

- `apps/api/test/hon-os-trial.test.cjs`, `saas-creative-wallet.test.cjs`
- `packages/database/scripts/test-hon-os-trial-runtime-integrity.mjs` (new group 5, plus updated creative assertions)

## Evidence (local disposable PostgreSQL 16)

- Trial proof **15/15 PASS**. New group 5 covers:
  - grant row, lot and ledger GRANT match the trial; no lot for a school without a trial;
  - the real wallet JSON passes the closed contract, with `TRIAL` in byKind;
  - a forged TRIAL lot is refused, and the grant is immutable;

author: iurisilvio
body:
The process-wide usage collector retries failed usage sends from a daemon thread until the test process exits. Every 10 s its sender looks up each queued API key's plan with `requests.get` and POSTs the usage with `requests.post`. Tests point both at `http://127.0.0.1:9`, so both fail and the usage is queued again. A tick that lands while a test has patched `requests.post`, `requests.get` or the transport (`requests_mock`) adds calls to that test's fake and breaks exact call counts and `call_args` reads. #3393 fixes two such tests one at a time; this removes the cause for the whole suite.

Before each test, `tests/conftest.py` stops the collector's two threads if the collector module is loaded. It looks the module up in `sys.modules` and never imports it, so suites that run without `inference`, such as the SDK job, are unaffected. It skips the threads' final enqueue and flush, so stopping them sends nothing. Tests that exercise flushing already call it directly.

## Tests

- A local pytest plugin seeds a leftover usage record whenever a test patches `requests.post` or `requests.get` (`monkeypatch` or `unittest.mock`), then runs a sender tick on another thread at the start of the window and right after the first patched call. Over the 15 test files that patch them and check calls, it fails 42 tests in 14 files on `main`, among them `test_roboflow_api.py`, `test_session_lifecycle.py`, `vision_events/test_v1.py`, `test_collector.py`, `test_inner_workflow_dispatch.py` and `test_roboflow_platform_blocks_legacy_compat.py`. With this change they all pass (786 passed, 12 skipped), because no sender is alive to tick. Forcing the tick anyway still fails the same 42.
- Holding one window per file open for 11 s, so the real `_usage_sender` fires on its own schedule: on `main` all 14 tests fail on its POSTs to `/usage/inference` and GETs to `/usage/plan`; with this change all 14 pass and the sender makes no calls.
- `tests/inference/unit_tests` (`-n auto --dist loadfile`, as in CI), `tests/workflows/unit_tests`, `tests/inference_sdk/unit_tests` and `tests/inference_cli/unit_tests` pass.
- black, isort and the flake8 gate pass.
