### Playwright downloads and installs browsers without verifying the authenticity of the SSL certificate
[CVE-2025-59288](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-59288) / [GHSA-7mvr-c777-76hp](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-7mvr-c777-76hp)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
Use of `curl` with the `-k` (or `--insecure`) flag in installer scripts allows attackers to deliver arbitrary executables via Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks. This can lead to full system compromise, as the downloaded files are installed as privileged applications.

##### Details
The following scripts in the `microsoft/playwright` repository at commit [`bee11cbc28f24bd18e726163d0b9b1571b4f26a8`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/commit/bee11cbc28f24bd18e726163d0b9b1571b4f26a8) use `curl -k` to fetch and install executable packages without verifying the authenticity of the SSL certificate:

- [`packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_chrome_beta_mac.sh`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/bee11cbc28f24bd18e726163d0b9b1571b4f26a8/packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_chrome_beta_mac.sh)
- [`packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_chrome_stable_mac.sh`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/bee11cbc28f24bd18e726163d0b9b1571b4f26a8/packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_chrome_stable_mac.sh)
- [`packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_msedge_dev_mac.sh`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/bee11cbc28f24bd18e726163d0b9b1571b4f26a8/packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_msedge_dev_mac.sh)
- [`packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_msedge_beta_mac.sh`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/bee11cbc28f24bd18e726163d0b9b1571b4f26a8/packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_msedge_beta_mac.sh)
- [`packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_msedge_stable_mac.sh`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/bee11cbc28f24bd18e726163d0b9b1571b4f26a8/packages/playwright-core/bin/reinstall_msedge_stable_mac.sh)

In each case, the shell scripts download a browser installer package using `curl -k` and immediately install it:

```shell
curl --retry 3 -o ./<pkg-file> -k <url>
sudo installer -pkg /tmp/<pkg-file> -target /
```

Disabling SSL verification (`-k`) means the download can be intercepted and replaced with malicious content.

##### PoC
A high-level exploitation scenario:

1. An attacker performs a MitM attack on a network where the victim runs one of these scripts.
2. The attacker intercepts the HTTPS request and serves a malicious package (for example, a trojaned browser installer).
3. Because `curl -k` is used, the script downloads and installs the attacker's payload without any certificate validation.
4. The attacker's code is executed with system privileges, leading to full compromise.

No special configuration is needed: simply running these scripts on any untrusted or hostile network is enough.

##### Impact
This is a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability due to improper SSL certificate validation (CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation). Any user or automation running these scripts is at risk of arbitrary code execution as root/admin, system compromise, data theft, or persistent malware installation. The risk is especially severe because browser packages are installed with elevated privileges and the scripts may be used in CI/CD or developer environments.

##### Fix

 - https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/commit/72c62d840247d9defd87c6beb0344d456794b570
 - [https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/37532](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/37532)
 - https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.56.0

- This vulnerability was confirmed by @​evilpacket
- This vulnerability was reported by @​JLLeitschuh at Socket

author: tengtium-tech
body:
## The problem

The same `docs/` ships to `main` and to every stack branch. Any sentence about what has been *built* is therefore true on at most one branch — and four places asserted that nothing exists:

| File | Claimed |
|---|---|
| `docs/README.md:43` | "Not started; no implementation exists" |
| `docs/12-delivery/readiness-dashboard.md:43` | "No production source, tests or build exists" |
| `docs/01-project/documentation-standard.md:56` | "no application code exists" |
| `docs/01-project/documentation-structure.md:55` | "no application code, test execution or deployment exists" |

True on `main`. Wrong on `csharp` and `react`, where work has started. A document must not imply implementation it lacks — and it must not deny implementation it has.

## The fix

Implementation status is now reported where it can be true: a `STATUS.md` at the root of each stack branch, **outside `docs/`**, so a docs sync can never collide with it.

- `docs/README.md` and the readiness dashboard stop stating a code status and point at the stack branch.
- The standard and the structure document say that Approved covers the specification, and that implementation is neither claimed nor denied here.

## The rule this establishes

> Documents under `docs/` describe intent and are identical on every branch. Files at a branch root describe state and belong to one branch.

That is the seam the stack-branch model already draws, written down so the next person doesn't have to infer it.

## Follow-ups

Three small PRs add `STATUS.md` to `csharp`, `react` and `react-csharp`. This one should merge first; the sync will then carry it to the stack branches and the follow-ups rebase on top.

author: devopsinterviewcloud
body:
Adds the A03 keyword post for "ai infrastructure engineer interview questions": the system design round for an AI platform. It covers requirements and GPU sizing, training vs serving cluster layout, the serving path and inference-aware routing, KEDA autoscaling on vLLM queue depth, cold starts, cost per request, and model rollout and rollback. The CTA is the bundle alone, naming the AI/ML questions the books actually list, plus the AI infrastructure page link.

Claims corrected during review:

- Default rolling updates don't always stall on a full GPU pool. maxUnavailable 25% rounds down, so four or more replicas can free a GPU first. Now scoped to small Deployments or `maxUnavailable: 0`.
- A KEDA cron trigger raises replicas, it can't lower the floor. Now `minReplicaCount` is the overnight floor and cron raises it by day.
- Least-connections does track open streams; it just doesn't see token counts or KV-cache pressure.
- The HPA scale-down window slows a queue-only signal but doesn't stop it oscillating.
- `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` has to cover the preStop delay as well, since the clock starts before preStop.
- GPU utilization wording softened: it measures kernel time, so it can read high at low concurrency.
- Cost formula relabelled as GPU cost per 1,000 requests.
- The AWS Spot two-minute warning is best effort; streams that outlast the drain are cut and the replacement may cold start.
- Capacity Blocks end on a fixed date, so the serving floor now points at On-Demand Capacity Reservations.
- Kueue's required-topology annotation applies per PodSet; added `podset-group-name` for keeping a leader and workers together.
- Opening sentence no longer generalises about how every interview is structured.

Codex review: 3 rounds, SOUND on round 3. `npm run build` passes with /blog/ai-infrastructure-engineer-interview-questions in the route list.

The scheduled agent merges this PR once the preview build passes; if it is still open, a merge gate failed and ops/blog-agent-runs.log says which.

author: nandurpm
body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the weekly Gemini Tracker audit and adds a separate, non-production smoke test.

### Changes
- Distinguish static source inspection from executed tests; require evidence, exact commit SHA and command/workflow before any audit area is labelled PASS.
- Run the existing `tracker-quality.yml` suite even when Gemini correctly proposes no source-code changes.
- Run the suite against the exact audited commit; block stale `main` snapshots and identify the corresponding workflow run by commit SHA and dispatch time.
- Upload a final audit-report artifact that records the independent CI result and URL.
- Record the configured primary Gemini model accurately in the report/Telegram audit notification.
- Keep Telegram audit-notification verification fail-closed when its required secrets are unavailable; this includes the latest main-branch notification behavior.
- Add a controlled smoke workflow that injects an integer-paise remainder defect into an ephemeral fixture, asks Gemini to repair only that fixture, then applies the patch on a clean runner without API credentials and executes regression tests.

### Evidence
- Earlier full smoke run: [Gemini repair + independent tests](https://github.com/nandurpm/portfolio/actions/runs/43174869398) — PASS, 3/3 tests.
- The latest smoke run also validates the hardened weekly workflow YAML and expected pipeline controls before running the synthetic fixture: [latest smoke run](https://github.com/nandurpm/portfolio/actions/runs/43175787385).

### Safety
- No Tracker application source, financial calculations, production records, Supabase schema, signing identity, package identity, deployed assets, or release artifacts are changed.
- The deliberate defect exists only in the temporary GitHub Actions runner workspace; it is not committed into the repository or shipped.
- The audit smoke workflow cannot deploy, publish releases, create PRs, or write to repository contents.
- No automatic merge is enabled. This PR is draft pending final workflow validation and review.

author: justinehler
body:
Replaces #2928; same commits re-cut onto main after the census ledger repair (#2922); no other change.

Review: full

Replaces #2909. Same three commits, re-cut on main be0010c9f. The only change is in the third commit: the series-rule types and routes move unchanged into `internal/api/dvr_rules.go`, because on #2909 that commit took `internal/api/dvr.go` to 1,012 lines and failed `TestBudgets` (limit 1,000). `dvr.go` is now 678 lines and `dvr_rules.go` 344. Commits 1 and 2 are as they were on #2909 (957 and 969 lines).

What people get (definition 11, rules 42, 48, 51, 55, 57, §5; brief from the lead and app lane B, 12 Nov):
- **Recordings** (`GET /v1/dvr/recordings`, `/{id}`) say their size on disk (`bytes`: the file and the guide's details beside it, the files Delete removes; it grows while recording, and a booking not yet recorded says 0). With the title, they also carry `libraryId` and this profile's `positionMs`, `durationMs` and `watched`. The single read adds `playingNow`, how many people Delete would stop. Together these make the delete preview, so there is still no separate delete-preview route.
- **Storage** (`GET /v1/dvr`): `usedBytes`, `floorBytes` and `capBytes`, and `keepDays` / `keepNewest` (the keep rule behind `keepRule`). There is also a forecast, `upcomingBytes` / `upcomingHours`, for every booking of the next 14 days at the same rate as `hoursLeft`. The forecast is space only, never titles. There is no "reserved": `floorBytes` stands in for it (lead's ruling), and API.md says so.
- **Series rules**: `PATCH /v1/dvr/rules/{id}?preview=true` previews an edit and saves nothing. `POST ?preview=true` now previews too; before, it only echoed the rule. A preview is `preview: {matches, airings[first 10: title, episode, channel, times, alreadyBooked]}`, built by the same matcher the recorder books with (`dvr.RuleAirings`, split out of `followRule` with no change in behaviour). A preview lists only airings on channels the viewer may watch and within its rating limit.
- A rule's **channel** can be changed (`channel` on `DvrRuleSave`, same source only), and `anyChannel` is honoured on PATCH. A rule that matches by title is refused `anyChannel` with a plain field error. A saved edit books what the rule now matches straight away, as a new rule does. Rule reads now carry `source`, `channel` and `channelName`; the list used to send none of them.
- A **keep choice** on a rule is cleared with `0`, after which the owner's default applies.
- **Conflicts** carry `tuners` and `tunersUsedBy` (rule 42). Recordings booked by the asker's own account are named by title, except a title above the asking profile's rating limit; anyone else's read "A recording" (area 7 rule 38).
- The **Recorded tab** has its own read: `state=recorded` lists made recordings by title, then newest first, by cursor, so one show's recordings stay together across pages. `scope=everyone` (rule 48) already existed, and every row already says who booked it.
- **More airings** (`GET /v1/live/programmes/{id}`) gives each airing its episode where the guide has one.
- A recording that **captured nothing** (the source answered but sent no picture) now ends `failed` with the reason and leaves no file and no title behind. Before, it was listed as Partly recorded and could not be played.

- Recordings, airings and reminders carry `channelId` beside `channel`, which stays the display name (app lane B reads it as one).
- A series rule moved to one channel lets go of its bookings not yet started on the channel it left. Each passes to whoever else asked for it, as a cancel does.
- Every recording and booking row says what this profile may do with it, decided by the same helpers the routes use: `mayChange` (change, stop, delete what was recorded: the booker, the owner, administrators) and `mayCancel` (a booking not yet started: a profile that asked for it, the owner, administrators). `GET /v1/dvr` adds `everyonesRecordings`: whether the profile may see the Recorded TV library, so the Mine / Everyone's switch can be left out when both lists are the same.

Tables: no new table or index. `RecordedTitles` reads the page's titles by primary key, with the profile's row in `user_item_state`. The Recorded tab's title order sorts the made recordings, as many as the Recorded TV library holds, an accepted cost written beside the query.

Cost: the new reads do not grow with the catalogue. Query plans and timings on a 60,000-item load-tool fixture (`portico-load -mode import -items 60000`; mini-1 runs nothing larger locally):
- `RecordedBytes` (Storage's used total) is index-only all the way (library_paths → directories → files). Over the fixture's largest library, 31,877 files, it took 0.01 s, well beyond any real Recorded TV library.
- `RecordedTitles` is 50 primary-key lookups per page, the same cost at any catalogue size.
- Size on disk is one `stat` of the file and one of its `.nfo` per listed recording.
- The rule preview is the recorder's own 14-day guide read (at most 2,000 airings) plus one channel lookup per distinct channel.
I did not run a 400,000-item load run: no read here touches the catalogue beyond lookups by id.

Contract files left to the merge desk's regeneration. New and changed shapes: `DvrRulePreview`, `DvrAiring` (new). Fields added to `DvrRecording` (also `channelId`, `mayChange`, `mayCancel`), `DvrOverview` (also `everyonesRecordings`), `DvrRule` (`preview`, `channelName`), `DvrRuleSave` (`channel`), `LiveAiring` (episode fields, `channelId`) and `LiveReminderOut` (`channelId`).

Verified:
- `go build ./...` and `go vet` (api, db, dvr) on this branch, cut from main be0010c9f.
- `go test ./cmd/portico-contracts/` passes.
- Focused tests through test-slot: every DVR, Live programme, assistant and channel-exclude test in `internal/api`, plus `internal/dvr` and `internal/db`.
- New tests in `internal/api/dvr_facts_test.go`: size and place and the Storage forecast; edit preview, channel change and keep clearing; a conflict's tuners as the owner and as a 13 profile on the same account; the Recorded read; an empty capture failing with no title; the old channel's booking let go after a channel change; each row's `mayChange` / `mayCancel` for the owner, another profile and a profile that also asked, and `everyonesRecordings` with and without Recorded TV.
- Engineering ratchet in queue mode through ratchet-slot over all three commits (base be0010c9f); `TestBudgets` passes: holds. The client census was skipped: Go only, no contract files.

author: pranc1ngpegasus
body:
## Why

Delegating a Linear issue to an AI agent had no local side. kuroko receives the Linear webhook for a delegated issue and dispatches it to a local coding agent over stdio or websocket, exactly once, with the lifecycle model-checked.

## What changed

- `crates/kuroko-core` holds the task book and the one pure `apply` transition function, shared by the tokio engine and a stateright model that checks six invariants over all interleavings.
- `crates/kuroko-engine` runs the single-writer dispatch loop with JoinSet panic recovery and a shutdown that stops starting new dispatches.
- `crates/kuroko-linear` verifies the `Linear-Signature` HMAC over the raw body, checks freshness, and distills the payload into admit, withdraw, or drop.
- `crates/kuroko-transport` implements the stdio child process and the websocket transports.
- `apps/kuroko` is the axum daemon with TOML config, `GET /tasks`, and graceful shutdown.

## Scope

Covers webhook intake, dispatch, and result capture in memory. Reporting results back to Linear, persistence across restarts, and superseding a re-delegated issue are deliberate follow-ups. Mutation testing stays in CI rather than `nix flake check`, per the documented tradeoff in `mutants.yaml`.

## Tradeoffs

Task identity is source, issue, and trigger, so a re-delegation to a different agent runs as a second task, serially per issue. The 60-second freshness window can reject Linear's own late retries when a retry preserves the original timestamp. A startup reconciler is the follow-up for both.

## Blast radius

Greenfield repository with no callers. The flake gains a `packages` output and an `apps.kuroko` entry, and `nix flake check` gains a `cargo fmt` gate. Existing checks are otherwise unchanged.

## Verification

- `nix flake check` green at every unit commit and at HEAD. Clippy `--deny warnings`, doctest, nextest 101 of 101, fmt, treefmt, pre-commit.
- `cargo mutants --workspace --exclude 'apps/**' --jobs 2`: 111 mutants, 78 caught, 33 unviable, 0 missed, `missed.txt` empty.
- Release binary end to end: a signed delivery answers 200, the stdio agent writes the rendered prompt, `GET /tasks` shows `Succeeded`, a tampered signature answers 401, and SIGTERM exits the daemon in 53 ms.
- Stateright model: 393 unique states across 4 tasks, all invariants hold.

author: pranav-32
body:
## Problem and change

`main` CI failed twice on Intel macOS (runs 42879740843 and 42995627998) in
`clutch.watch` > `test_bursts_outputs_and_ignored_paths`. In both logs the six burst edits,
written 20 ms apart, produced **two** build cycles instead of one (the second run fails at the
quiet check after the burst; the first run's split satisfied `cycle(3)` early, so the asset
reconfigure landed in the final quiet check).

Watch builds after a quiet debounce window, so two builds are correct when the editor pauses
longer than the debounce. With four heavy suites sharing a 4-core runner, the test's writer can
stall longer than the 120 ms debounce. This is a test timing assumption, not a watch defect.

- The burst test uses an 800 ms debounce.
- `quiet()` always covers two debounce windows (default sessions keep 0.45 s), which also
  strengthens the 1000 ms-debounce timestamp-restore test.

The commit carries `Release-As: 0.6.0-beta.1` so the next version proposal is the first
release to publish the per-user installers as a prerelease.

## Checks

- Windows (MSVC, Ninja): `clutch.watch` 3/3; full `ctest --parallel 4` 39/39 twice.
- Linux (Docker gcc:14, 4 CPUs with a busy loop per visible core): watch suite 3/3.
  The unmodified test also passed under that load, so the local runs show no regression
  but did not reproduce the macOS stall; Intel macOS CI is the deciding check and will
  be run twice.

author: ax128
body:
## 为什么要改

控制台保存配置时，字符串只做 `strip()`，再按 `KEY=value` 写入 `config/.env`。值里只要含有回车、换行或空字节，这一行就会被拆开。管理员会话因此可以写入控制台刻意不开放的键，例如 `AEGIS_GATEWAY_KEY`、`AEGIS_ENFORCE_LOOPBACK_ONLY`。

打到这个接口需要管理员会话。

## 复现

在还没改生产代码时跑：

```
pytest -vv aegisgate/tests/test_ui_config_center.py::TestConfigRoute::test_control_character_in_string_value_is_rejected aegisgate/tests/test_ui_config_center.py::TestEnvWriteGuard::test_write_env_updates_rejects_control_characters --tb=short
```

6 failed。失败原因是行为还没拒绝这些字符，不是导入或拼写错误。

- `test_control_character_in_string_value_is_rejected` 的 `lf`、`cr`、`nul`：`assert 200 == 400`。含 `\n`、`\r`、`\0` 的字符串被接受。
- `test_write_env_updates_rejects_control_characters` 的 `lf`、`cr`、`nul`：`Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError`。落盘函数直接把这些值写进文件。

摘要：`6 failed, 1 warning in 0.12s`。

## 改动

- 字符串和枚举在 `strip()` 之前拒绝 CR、LF、NUL。错误信息沿用现有校验：`invalid value for <字段>`，接口返回 400 `invalid_field_value`。
- 落盘函数在写文件前对键和值再检查一次。绕过字段校验的调用方会得到 `ValueError`，文件字节不变。
- 测试对这三种字符分别断言 HTTP 400，以及 `.env` 字节与提交前一致。
- CHANGELOG 的 `[Unreleased]` 增加一条 Security。这一段可能和其它 PR 的 `[Unreleased]` 文本冲突。

计划没有写到的取舍：只拒绝这三种字符，不把垂直制表符、换页或 Unicode 行分隔符算进去。数字和布尔仍走原来的解析，写回去的文本不会带上这些字符。落盘函数抛出的 `ValueError` 不在路由里另接成 400，因为请求路径先被字段校验拦住，已经是 400。

## 行为变化

- 控制台保存的字符串或枚举只要含有 CR、LF 或 NUL（含以前会被 `strip()` 丢掉的首尾空白），返回 400，`config/.env` 不被改写。
- 不含这些字符的值，保存、热重载和重启提示与原来一致。

## 测试

```
pytest -q aegisgate/tests/test_ui_config_center.py
# 41 passed, 1 warning

pytest -q aegisgate/tests/test_streaming_router.py aegisgate/tests/test_doc_alignment.py
# 120 passed, 1 skipped

pytest -q
# 2266 passed, 12 skipped, 78 warnings

# Python 3.10.21，同一测试文件
pytest -q aegisgate/tests/test_ui_config_center.py
# 41 passed, 1 warning
```

基线是 2260 passed / 12 skipped。新增 6 个测试，没有新增 skip。

body:
## Summary

### Product and settings correctness
- Verify the authoritative `products.weights` read/write when an admin changes a product variant's stock or price.
- Verify whole-product availability updates actually affect a row; report RLS/no-row failures instead of false success.
- Require an explicit product name and at least one valid weight/price; do not silently insert sample prices when the form has no valid variants.
- Do not silently substitute seeded demo products/categories or stale cached shop settings when configured Supabase reads fail.
- Treat an empty production catalogue as empty, not as a reason to show sample data.
- Do not cache proposed shop settings before Supabase confirms the save.

### Checkout reliability
- Reuse a persistent idempotency key for retries of the same checkout payload, with a hashed fingerprint so customer details are not stored in the key record.
- Block duplicate submit events while the current checkout request is in flight.
- Add regression coverage for stable keys across identical retries and new keys for changed payloads.

### Security hardening
- Remove the published default local admin credentials from documentation and code; remove the legacy seeded local admin record from existing local store files.
- Disable unauthenticated local password-recovery/reset endpoints; secure recovery requires Supabase Auth.
- Disable legacy public order-number and phone-only history endpoints that could expose customer personal information. Production tracking remains on the token-protected Supabase Edge Function.
- Remove the fabricated fallback UPI intent and fail clearly while UPI integration is pending.
- Restrict administrator allow-list management to super admins and limit ordinary admins to viewing their own admin record. Includes a new SQL migration and updated fresh-install SQL.
- Fail closed if an administrator record has an invalid or missing role.
- Update API documentation to describe the secure production flows.

### Tests added
- Variant stock write success and RLS-denied write.
- Whole-product stock update with zero rows affected.
- Missing/invalid product weight validation.
- Production catalogue errors do not fall back to demo data.
- Empty live catalogue remains empty.
- Shop settings errors do not use stale cached settings.
- UPI helper does not fabricate a payment session.
- Checkout idempotency key reuse behavior.

## Safety
- All changes are on `fix/admin-stock-update-errors`; `main` is unchanged.
- No production Supabase data, existing orders, or Vercel production deployment was manually changed.
- The new migration `20261112120000_restrict_admin_user_management.sql` is a proposed SQL change only; it has not been applied to the live database.

## Validation
- Tests/build have not been executed in a local runtime in this review because the GitHub source could not be cloned in this environment.
- GitHub Actions workflow runs were not present for the reviewed commit.
- Vercel preview check is being monitored; no production deployment was requested or performed.

author: pkgdemon
body:
The Wi-Fi Dock extra (E36, nextbsd/nextbsd#623), on the interface from #12.

- **Tile:** three arcs lit for the signal (≥ −60 dBm: 3, ≥ −70: 2, else 1, wlan(8)'s steps). All dim when not connected; an ellipsis while joining (SSID set, not Authenticated yet).
- **Tooltip:** `Wi-Fi: <SSID> (−58 dBm, channel 36, WPA2)` / `joining …` / `not connected`.
- **Data:** wland's `State:/Network/Interface/<if>/AirPort` (Authenticated, SSID, BSSID, RSSI, Channel, Security), watched with `SCDynamicStoreSetNotificationKeys` + `SCDynamicStoreSetDispatchQueue`; the callback wakes the Dock's run loop through a pipe. No polling. The SC/CF code is plain C, built without GNUstep's headers.
- **No radio:** no AirPort entry and nothing from `wlan list`, so no tile.
- **Menu:** Disconnect from the current network; the networks of the last scan, each with a signal glyph and strongest first (a new scan starts when the menu opens and the list is older than 20 s, so the next opening is fresh); Scan Again. Open networks join directly, secured ones ask for the passphrase in a panel (8–63 characters), and 802.1X ones are shown but left to `wlan connect --eap`.
- Scans, joins and disconnects run `/usr/sbin/wlan` asynchronously. wlan(8) says it's the supported way for anything above the Mach line, including the desktop, to drive wland.

What wland lacks for the rest of the ticket:
- **No Wi-Fi on/off:** wland's MIG interface has no radio power call, so there is no "Turn Wi-Fi Off". Disconnect, which also stops autojoin, is the closest thing.
- **No rejoin without the passphrase:** `wlan connect <ssid>` with no passphrase means an open network, even for a known one, so rejoining a saved secured network asks again.
- **Passphrase on argv:** wlan(8) takes the PSK as an argument, so it shows in `ps` while wlan runs. A stdin option or a client library would fix that.
- **Scan results need a second look:** `wlan scan` returns once the sweep is done, but the menu is already open by then, so the fresh list shows the next time it opens.
- **"Network Preferences…"** waits for that pane.

**Tested** on the arm64 VM, which has no Wi-Fi (`wlan list`: no WLAN interfaces): no tile. The drawing, tooltip, menu, glyphs, Disconnect, the network list and the passphrase panel were checked with `DockExtrasTestData`. Joining a real network wasn't tested (no radio).

**Why.** `Job.progress`, `created_at` and `completed_at` are read and written by `openai-videos` only: `gemini-veo` and `openrouter-videos` never set or read them. By the kind rule they move to `openai-videos`' native. Fields most formats have stay, with a `// WARN:` naming the format that lacks them:
- `model`, `seconds`, `size`, `error.code`: openrouter-videos lacks them.
- `expires_at`: gemini-veo lacks it.
- `videos`: openai-videos lacks it, since it serves them at `/content`.

**Change.**
- Kind: the three fields go.
- `openai-videos`' `job_of` leaves them in the job's native, and `job_json` writes them back from there.
- A job of another format still gets them as `null` (with `remixed_from_video_id`), as OpenAI's SDK schema expects.

**Wire changes.**
- openai → openai-videos client: the values are unchanged. In a job object, `created_at`, `progress` and `completed_at` now come after the typed fields instead of in OpenAI's order. JSON key order only.
- gemini-veo / openrouter → openai-videos client: unchanged (`null`, as before).
- Every gemini-veo client path: unchanged (it never wrote them).

**Tests.** `openai-videos` had no job read/write test to fold into, so one compact test was added: `a_job_is_written_back_with_its_times_and_progress`, an OpenAI job round-trip plus a foreign job's `null` placeholders.

**LoC** (`git diff --shortstat origin/main...HEAD`: 2 files, +37 −23): code +17 −23 (−6, including 6 WARN lines), tests +20, docs 0.

Checks: `cargo test -p respan-gateway-media -p respan-gateway-media-http`, `cargo clippy -p respan-gateway-media --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the same for `-p respan-gateway-media-http`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`.

author: sanskarin
body:
## Why
The new 16 kHz WebView2 microphone PCM encoder computes a windowed-sinc low-pass for every output sample of up to 30 seconds. At common 44.1/48 kHz input rates that repeats tens of millions of trigonometric calculations on the UI thread during **Stop recording**, causing a potential unresponsive interval.

## Changes
- Reuse a per-conversion bounded Map of phase-quantized Float64 kernels (1025 phases at most, ~1 MiB worst case) instead of re-evaluating sin/cos for every resampled frame.
- Preserve native 16 kHz path, stereo downmix and the low-pass filtering that prevents aliases folding into speech.
- Add deterministic reference-filter numerical comparisons for 44.1/48/96 kHz, plus instrumentation asserting trig calls stay bounded for a 2-second sample.
- Update offline STT documentation to distinguish source optimization from real-device quality verification.

## Validation / release boundary
- Source-only performance change; no model downloads or microphone activation, storage, release tag or published binary.
- Await exact-head CI for React/TypeScript, Python, Windows Rust/Clippy and the unsigned Windows candidate.
- CI cannot certify playback responsiveness or Hindi recognition accuracy on Windows 11; manual acceptance remains required under #3 and #129.
- This PR does **not** publish v0.5.7.

author: marpaia
body:
Fixes #40.

## Problem

A crowded colony pressed cells through device walls. Once a cell center crossed a wall face, the coupled nutrient step failed with `signal sample position is inside a grid obstacle`. `examples/microfluidic_trap.py` stopped this way at about step 510 (128 cells) on every seed tried, on CPU and Metal; the Danino clock and biopixel trap examples stopped the same way.

Two causes:

- **Contact rows.** For an outside box, cylinder, or sphere, a rod whose nearest point was an endpoint got one row at that end only. With both ends inside a flat face, the solve answered with a rotation that drove the other end deeper, and the cell rocked through the wall.
- **Soft walls.** The regularized solve weighs a wall row against the cells pressing on it, so walls always gave a little under pressure. The trap's back wall lies on a lattice plane, so the solid mask starts exactly at the wall face and half a micron of give was enough to fail sampling.

## Changes

- **Contact generation (CPU, Metal, CUDA):** when the centerline minimum lies at an endpoint, every endpoint within the activation margin emits a row.
- **Wall projection (host code shared by all backends):** each relaxation pass ends by moving mobile cells out of the external constraints. Each centerline end moves along the normals of the contacts it is inside and the cell is rebuilt at its own length, so a tilted rod comes to lie along the wall and a rod wedged upright in a low cavity is turned flat.
- **No tunnelling:** a correction longer than a cell's radius is applied in up to sixteen parts with a projection after each, so it cannot carry a cell past a wall's mid-plane.
- **README:** the quick start now builds the viewer and opens the trap model in it.
- Architecture docs, tutorials, and example comments that described soft walls are updated.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Native tests, Metal-enabled build, incl. CPU-vs-Metal conformance | 30/30 pass |
| Python suite | 512 passed, 32 skipped |
| pre-commit | clean |
| Trap, 1,000 steps, CPU | 8,103 cells, deepest wall penetration 0.0009 |
| Trap, 1,000 steps, Metal | 8,114 cells, deepest wall penetration 0.0010 |
| Biopixel trap, 1,100 steps, CPU | runs, 17,007 cells |
| Pillar channel, 3,000 steps, CPU | runs, 93 cells |

New tests cover the two-row contact rule, the projection (tilted rod, corner, wedged rod, fixed cells), a thin-wall tunnelling case, a CPU-vs-Metal fixture for tilted rods against a box and a pillar, and a 620-step crowded-trap regression.

## Not covered

- **CUDA is not compiled or run.** The kernel edit mirrors the Metal one, but no NVIDIA hardware or toolkit was available. The CUDA compile workflow should run before merge.
- **The Danino clock still stops, on a different error.** At step 748 (1,024 cells) it raises `Implicit coupled signal solve did not converge after 10000 iterations`, with cells inside the walls and all values finite. Not investigated here.
- **Cells still overlap each other when crowded.** At 8,000 cells the worst pairs overlap completely. This predates the change; suppressing growth under pressure, which #41 attempts, is not part of this PR.
- **Residual wall penetration is about 1e-3** in a very crowded trap, where the projection's eight sweeps do not fully settle.

author: matthew25187
body:
Closes #809.

Without a header line, `CsvFileWriter` only looked for new field names when a record line had more fields than it had seen so far. A line with the same count under different names, such as `{A=3, C=4}` after `{A=1, B=2}`, was written as `3,` and the `4` was lost without an error.

Now any field the first record line doesn't have makes the line inconsistent. The line goes to `InconsistentFieldCountHandler` or throws `CsvFileException` (`Expected 2 fields; found 3 fields.`). A handled line doesn't change the fields of later lines. A later line that lacks one of the first line's fields is still written with a blank value for it, which is documented and tested now.

The issue's first point (a handled wider line spoiling the lines after it) was already fixed by #874. This PR adds tests for the same-count case as well.

The common case, where a line has the same names in the same order, compares each name to the one at the same position, so it doesn't do a hash lookup for every field.

Release note is declared on the commit.

author: jamiefuller320
body: This is the runner for the UK/Europe point-in-time replay. It is stacked on the design PR #1378. Until the owner seals the registration, it makes no EODHD calls. **Safety and licence** - `docs/data/strategy_book_uk_replay_registration.json` is committed with `sealed: false`. Every EODHD call raises `UnsealedRegistration` until `seal` records the owner stamp and the registration doc's sha256. `reveal` refuses to run without a committed development result and an owner reveal stamp, the same gate as the US rehearsal. - The repo only ever receives the aggregate store `docs/data/strategy_book_uk_replay.json`. The workflow commits that one path via `gha_commit_artifacts.sh`. A test rejects price and statement keys, per-episode rows, and any float of 1000 or more. - Licensed raw data sits in a gitignored cache that is deleted after develop/reveal. Between Actions runs it is stored only as an AES-256 tarball encrypted with the `EODHD_API_TOKEN` secret. This matters because Actions caches in a public repo can be restored by fork-PR workflows, which never receive secrets. **Reuse** - The walk is `strategy_book_observe.walk_book` with the US-rehearsal options and the registration windows. - Delisting haircuts use `strategy_book_us_tape.with_variant`. - Aggregates and the family test use `strategy_book_us_rehearsal` (a family of 4, adding `trend_not_falling`). - HTTP goes through the existing `EodhdClient`. - Failed-name years come from `ch_failed_name_statements`. - Every constant is in one `REGISTRATION_CONSTANTS` block that mirrors the draft registration. **Fetch plan** (`fetch_plan()`, no calls): 6,678 LSE names (active plus delisted). That is 86,818 weighted calls (13 per name) under a 90,000 soft cap, with a resumable cursor across UTC days. When the budget runs out the run reports `partial`; it is never silently truncated. A probe stops the job if EODHD reports a call weight different from the planned one. **Units:** `GBp` (pence) is divided by 100 before the rank, and `GBP` is used as is. The check reads the code as written, because `"GBp".upper() == "GBP"`. **Wiring** - Dispatch-only workflow `strategy-book-uk-replay.yml` with phases fetch, development and reveal. If the secret is missing it exits 0 and commits nothing. - Ops-monitor check `check_strategy_book_uk_replay`, with `auto_fixable=false`. - Runbook `docs/ops/strategy-book-uk-replay-runbook.md`. - CLI `ftse-strategy-book-uk-replay`. **Tests** - `tests/test_strategy_book_uk_replay.py`: 16 passed, all with mocked HTTP. - The strategy_book, ops_monitor, gha_commit, human_tasks, glossary, deferred and eodhd suites: 452 passed. - The uk_replay, gha, workflow and ops_monitor suites, re-run after the cache encryption change: 245 passed. - ruff is clean. - The sealed plan hash is unchanged. Not run here, because this VM has no token and the registration isn't sealed: the real fetch.

body:
Fixes BT-4704

Pure move / extract refactor of `beamtalk_object_class.erl` (3430 -> 2917 lines). No behaviour change; `beamtalk_object_class`'s exported API is unchanged.

## What moved where

**New `beamtalk_class_session`** (session and group-leader seeding): `seed_session_context_from/1`, `seed_caller_session_context/1`, `restore_dict_key/2` (exported: also used by `dispatch_class_method`), plus private `adopt_entry_group_leader/1`, `set_group_leader/1`.

**New `beamtalk_class_publish`** (record-free outbound publication): `register_xref/2`, `register_state_var_xref/2`, `refresh_xref/2`, `put_method_xref/4`, `safe_xref/1`, `announce_class_lifecycle/2`, `notify_compiler_server_register/2`, `sync_identity/6`, `sync_direct_constructors/2`, `sync_constant_class_methods/2`, `sync_caller_safe_primitives/2`, `sync_class_process_facts/3`, `warn_stale_subclass_constructors/3`, `is_runtime_fun_info/1`, `seed_runtime_class_methods/2`. All are exported only because `beamtalk_object_class` calls them.

**In `beamtalk_object_class`:**
- `read_published/3` carries the shared `*_safe` accessor shape; `module_name_safe`, `superclass_safe`, `instance_methods_safe`, `instance_variables_safe`, `local_class_method_selectors_safe`, `local_instance_method_infos_safe` are now thin over it.
- `init/1` delegates to `join_class_registry/0`, `class_meta/2` (also reused by `apply_class_info/2`), `init_is_internal/2`, `publish_init_identity/7`, `cache_self_dispatch_state/2`, `register_class_indexes/2`, `publish_init_state/3`.
- `handle_call` clauses `new`, `rename_class`, `put_method`, `put_class_method`, `update_class`, `get_class_var` delegate to `call_new/2`, `call_rename_class/2`, `call_put_method/4`, `call_put_class_method/4`, `call_update_class/2`, `call_get_class_var/2`.

Comment-only reference updates in `beamtalk_repl_eval`, `beamtalk_repl_shell` and `beamtalk_session_primitives_tests`.

## Accessor drift
`superclass_safe`/`module_name_safe` called `class_name_for_pid` directly while the others used `reflection_class_name`. For any pid other than `self()` the two are identical (`reflection_class_name` delegates), and `self()` was already handled by a dedicated clause in both, so the drift was not behavioural. All accessors now go through `reflection_class_name`; no separate fix or test needed.

## Seams left alone (and why)
The issue's target of ~2,300 lines is not met (2917). `publish_reflection/1`, `method_record/4`, `notify_hot_patch/1`, `apply_class_info/2` and the remove/shadow logic (~600 lines) all read or build the private `#class_state{}` record, which lives in this module. Moving them means extracting the record to a shared header, which is a design change rather than a pure move, so they stay. Happy to follow up if wanted.

## Verification
`rebar3 fmt --check`, `rebar3 xref` (no new warnings), `rebar3 dialyzer`, `just test-runtime` (9063 + 2190 tests, 0 failures) and `just test-stdlib` (233/233) pass locally. Existing tests unmodified.

author: akinz-bobo
body:
## Summary

Makes the pull request check wait for the slowest environment and not for the sum of all three.

Closes #83

## What changed

- `infrastructure.yml`: the single `Plan, policy and rehearsal` job becomes three parallel `Rehearse <environment>` jobs from a matrix, each with its own emulator. Module apply tests move to a job of their own and run once. A `Plan comment` job joins the three plan reports
- `.github/actions/setup-terraform`: the pinned Terraform, the provider cache and the pinned tools, as one composite action used by every job. The same five steps were repeated in each job before
- `scripts/plan-report-merge.sh`: joins per-environment reports into one. An environment whose job failed before planning gets a row that says so, so it cannot drop out of the comment
- The apply on merge is unchanged and still sequential. On merge the order is the point: each environment gates the next
- The pipeline guide describes the new shape

## Why

The rehearsal job grew with every store added to the data layer. Durations of the whole workflow run, from the run history:

| Pull request | State of the environments | Run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #70 and earlier | Foundation layer only | about 7 minutes |
| #79 | Plus an empty data layer | 8.3 minutes |
| #80 | Plus a bucket | 13.5 minutes |
| #81 | Plus two tables | 16.3 minutes |
| #82 | Plus a database | still running at 15 minutes when a new push cancelled it |

A cache and backups are still to come in this milestone, and three more layers after that.

**Correction.** The issue, the first version of this description and one commit message say "more than twenty minutes". That was my estimate while waiting, not a measurement. The longest completed run was 16.3 minutes. The guide and this description now carry the measured figures. The commit message cannot be changed without rewriting pushed history.

## How it was verified

- The merger was run locally on two real reports and one missing one: rows and details in order, and a "no report" row for the missing environment
- Both YAML files parse
- This pull request is the test of the workflow itself: it must show three rehearsal jobs, one module test job and a single plan comment

## Note

The check names change from `Plan, policy and rehearsal` to `Rehearse dev`, `Rehearse staging` and `Rehearse production`. Nothing depends on the old name: there is no branch protection rule that names it.

- [x] Checks pass
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] No secrets, account ids or personal data added

author: jitsusama
body:
### 💡 TL;DR

Health's lines about slow moments now say where a pi session's time went, by cause, and what a slow Chrome page was. The four secret-ask measures are judged on the security axis, beside its readings of them.

### 🧩 Problem

The pain-points detector now splits a pi message's time into the model, the provider's errors, pi's own work and tools, and writes Chrome's reloads and visits back as goes of their own. Health read every go as a launcher's, so a pi line said only that time was lost to waiting, which reads as the model's fault, and a Chrome line said nothing of what happened. Separately, cadence judged the four asks measures on the polish axis, while the security quest set them on security, where cadence axes security now reads them, so a finding and its reading would sit under different axes.

### 🔧 Solution

A pi line now says its loss is to waiting on pi, then adds where the time went, most first. A cause under a second is left out, and a minute or more reads in whole minutes. For example: "a pi session took 2100 s over 3 messages, 2 min or more lost to waiting on pi (19 min on tools, 14 min on the model)". A Chrome go reads "reloading a page in Chrome took 82 s over 5 reloads", or "going straight back from a page in Chrome lost 6 s". A launcher line is unchanged. The new signs default to zero, so a day file written before the detector's change still reads.

The four `health.asks.*` measures move from polish to security, and a test holds every asks measure there.

### 🔬 Validation

- Red: with Chrome's branch and the causes taken out, both feel tests failed (62 passed, 2 failed); with one asks measure back on polish, the axis test failed (134 passed, 1 failed).
- Green at the merged base: `health-tallies-the-days-warnings` (64 tests), `cadence-asks-when-a-target-slips` (137), both crates' clippy, and `formatting`.
- `nix-offload there --lent-only --changed` passed 22 checks before the rebase; `merge-net needs` names no VM tests.
- Not covered: real pain-points lines on a machine, since health isn't imported on one yet.

author: oodinhoo
body:
## What and why

**Column lineage through stored procedures.** SQL tasks are often `EXEC dbo.usp_…`: the table lineage already followed the `.sql` scripts of those procedures, but the column lineage stopped at each call. It now follows the `INSERT … SELECT` of the procedure body, and of the procedures it calls in turn (a loop of calls is read once), in the database of the procedure. A procedure defined in several scripts is still not traced, as in the table lineage.

- `sql.rs`: while reading a procedure body, keep its `INSERT … SELECT` (`projection::insert_select`, extracted from `insert_selects`)
- `inventory.rs`: `SqlDefinition.inserts`
- `columns.rs`: `task_inserts` adds the procedure inserts to those of the task query; `mod.rs`: definition lookup shared (`defined_in`)

**Fix found on the way.** The step of an SQL task was keyed by (package, task, column): a task filling `dbo.Clients.courriel` then `dbo.Archive.courriel` had a single step for both, so each column seemed to come from the other (loop in the trace). Procedures do staging-then-target all the time. One step per written table now.

**Package list on the lineage map.** Next to the project list, a second list picks one package of the project, to keep big projects readable. Left empty: the whole project. Hidden for "All projects". Kept in the address (`#map/PROJECT/PACKAGE`); a package of another project falls back to the whole project.

## How it was tested

- New fixture `tests/fixtures/columns_procedures/`: SQL task → `dbo.Charger` (column list, SQL expression) → `dbo.Archiver` (`SELECT *`). Test of the full column trace in `tests/columns.rs`, plus the existing `procedures` fixture (duplicate definition: no column; UTF-16 script read)
- Procedures calling each other (read once) and a procedure named with its database (`EXEC Archives.dbo.Copier`: its tables are in Archives), checked to fail when `body_database` ignores the name
- `the_map_narrows_to_a_project_then_to_one_of_its_packages` in `html.rs`
- Report of `tests/fixtures` in a browser (Playwright): project `columns` 18 blocks, one package 10, back to the empty choice 18; hash updated; list hidden for all projects; French label
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`: 177 tests pass

Known limits: the column step carries the SQL task name, not the procedure name; procedures called from a Data Flow (OLE DB Command, source `EXEC`) are not followed (`shortcut:` comment); temp tables and dynamic SQL give "unknown origin".

## Checklist

- [x] No real customer package, server name or secret anywhere in this pull request
- [x] `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` pass
- [x] Snapshot changes reviewed with `cargo insta review` (no snapshot changed)
- [x] New HTML report texts translated in `src/render/i18n.js`
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` (`[Unreleased]`) and README updated if behavior changed

author: i-hun
body:
## Why

A one-shot cron alarm's entire job is `hermes kanban unblock <id>`. When the card was already closed, archived or purged before the alarm fired, the CLI exited non-zero (`cannot unblock <id> (not blocked/scheduled?)`), the run was recorded as failed, and the owner was paged over an empty board. Every alarm had to be wrapped in a status-checking shell script — a rule that only works for alarms someone remembered to wrap.

## What changed

`hermes_cli/kanban.py` — `_cmd_unblock`:

- missing card, `done`/`archived`, and a lost race with a concurrent unblock/complete all print a line and exit **0**;
- `blocked`/`scheduled` are still unblocked exactly as before;
- the `--reason` comment is written **only after** the parking actually went away, so a no-op never annotates a closed card's history;
- a failed comment write is a warning on stderr, not an error exit — the unpark has already landed.

`hermes_cli/kanban_parser.py` — the `--reason` help text now says "on a successful unblock".

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_unblock_idempotent.py` — 9 cases: scheduled → ready, blocked → ready with exactly one `UNBLOCK:` note, done/archived/missing → rc 0 with a message, no note on a closed card, lost race → rc 0 and no note, failed comment write → rc 0 + warning, and the literal CLI shape via `python -m hermes_cli.main kanban unblock <id>`.

Mutation probes (in a throwaway copy): dropping the comment write, writing it before the transition, and removing the warning guard each fail exactly one test.

Work by Hermes agent on behalf of @i_Hun.

author: adrian-lee-dev
body:
## Problem

Step 3 of the booking workflows plan (`docs/workflows.md`, "Implementation plan") needs the execution storage that capture, dispatch, mail admission and history (steps 7–16a) will write: enrollments, due runs, per-recipient claims, minimal history and workflow mail reservations, plus a nullable `notification_email_sends.workflow_reservation_id` without a foreign key. Concurrent duplicate capture must fail on unique keys, deletion and retention must never make a dispatch possible again, and existing ledger rows and core count queries must stay unchanged. The definition-storage review also left four proof gaps (hard-off pin through the package entry, off-scan exemptions, whole-minute binding, revision lock order).

Workflows stay hard-off behind `WORKFLOWS_IMPLEMENTED = false`. This PR adds no transport, read path, REST, MCP, CLI or web surface.

## Change

**Migration `0079_workflow_execution.sql`**

- `workflow_enrollments`: a booking's capture of one workflow revision at one lifecycle occurrence (`created`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled`). Unique per (booking, occurrence, workflow); each occurrence takes only its own triggers; immutable; insert needs a live definition and a stored revision with that trigger. Booking FK with cascade.
- `workflow_runs`: the one due run of an enrollment. Due and expiry instants are immutable, a claim token and a lease, states `pending`/`claimed`/`completed`/`skipped`/`retired` with fixed skip reasons; finished runs are final. A partial index holds only unfinished runs for the due scan.
- `workflow_recipient_claims`: an attendee or host plus the workflow-purpose address digest (never the address), unique per run and digest. A timer email's winning recipient holds its intent (category, offset, digest), which only one workflow can hold on a booking. `dispatching` is the marker, set only while the run is claimed; it shares the run, so a retirement that commits first prevents it and a marker that commits first holds the retirement back. A partial index finds markers for the repair of stopped attempts.
- `workflow_run_history`: one immutable, content-free record per finished run, not linked to the run or booking; it goes with its workflow and has page and retention indexes.
- `workflow_mail_reservations`: one per admitted claim, charged to the owner organization, without FKs to run or claim; restamped only forward; removed only after its ledger row or with its organization.
- `notification_email_sends`: nullable `workflow_reservation_id` (no FK, no default, existing rows keep NULL), a CHECK that a workflow charge carries a recipient digest, and a partial unique index (one ledger row per reservation). Core rows are unaffected.
- `workflow_definitions`: a purge guard refuses deleting a tombstone while one of its runs is pending or claimed.
- Every guard locks the organization before any parent row, with a pinned `search_path`. Child tables carry the organization in composite FKs, as revisions do.

**Tombstone decision.** Execution rows are the "minimal non-content terminal identity tombstones". They name the workflow and revision without an FK to the definition and hold no content. A later purge of a tombstoned definition with its revisions (and history) therefore keeps every booking's enrollment, run and claim, and replayed capture or repair meets the same identity and final state. The purge is refused while a run is unfinished, and no enrollment or run is added for a tombstoned or purged workflow. 0076 is unchanged.

**Step-2 review follow-ups**

- Hard-off: the guards are imported through `@hourmere/workflows` and must be identical to `hard-off.ts`. The package `exports` map and the entry's export names are pinned. The child process also calls each wrapped function with `true` and `{ whileOff: true }`.
- Off scan: exact storage-support files instead of a wildcard, the five new table names and row types, and a scan of every workspace manifest's `main`/`exports`/`imports`. A comment states that built names are a known limit of a name scan.
- Whole minutes: fractional offsets and delays are refused by both the contract and `workflow_revisions_trigger`.
- Lock order: while another session holds the organization, a revision insert waits without having locked the definition. A mutant reverses the order.
- The comment on `REMINDER_MIN_GAP` now says the timer rules avoid the notifications and jobs packages, and that the scheduling root still loads mail.

**Docs:** `docs/workflows.md` (status, persistence and tombstones) and `docs/data-model.md` (new "Workflow execution storage" section).

## Tests

| File | What it proves |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/db/src/workflow-storage-execution-protections.ts` | 12 behavioural checks, each with its own fixture, plus 125 source-copy mutants |
| `workflow-storage-execution.test.ts` | Every constraint, index, trigger, NOT NULL column and the 20 trigger rules are named by a check, and every check passes (13 tests) |
| `workflow-storage-execution-mutations.test.ts` | Each mutant applied to 0079 on a predecessor copy fails its check with an AssertionError (126 tests) |
| `workflow-storage-execution-coverage.test.ts` + `testing/migration-objects/0079_workflow_execution.json` | `checkConstraintCoverage`: 81 objects, 79 covered, 2 allow-listed |
| `workflow-storage-execution-upgrade.test.ts` | Populated predecessor (every migration before 0079, including 0078) with reminders, follow-ups, workflow definitions and revisions, and the mail ledger: every row unchanged down to xmin/ctid, ledger rows NULL, fresh install equals upgraded, rerun is a no-op |
| `packages/notifications/src/workflow-ledger.test.ts` | On the same rows before and after 0079, the unchanged `mail-limits.ts` functions return the same instance, booking-recipient and sign-in counts and purge the same rows. A workflow charge counts only in the instance hour |
| `packages/workflows/src/execution-storage.test.ts` | Occurrence triggers, skip reasons, intent categories and offsets bound both ways to the contract |
| `scripts/workflows-off.test.ts`, `packages/workflows/src/hard-off.test.ts`, `packages/workflows/src/storage.test.ts`, `packages/db/src/workflow-storage-protections.ts` | The step-2 follow-ups above |

Concurrency: two connections race every capture identity (enrollment, run, recipient, intent, reservation, ledger charge, history record), and exactly one row wins. Capture and the workflow's deletion take turns on the definition, and a marker and run retirement take turns on the run, in both orders.

author: eiei114
body:
Multica Issue: DOT-3456

## 概要

`/new` で起動時に使うモデルピッカーを、既定オフの opt-in として追加しました。設定はユーザーグローバルの `~/.pi/agent/pi-startup-picker-settings.json` の `showOnNewSession` で、`/startup-picker:settings` から切り替えます。ピッカー本体は既存の検索可能・recent-first のものを再利用しています。

## 実装

- `lib/settings-store.ts` — `showOnNewSession` を読む/書くだけの小さなストア。ファイル欠落・不正 JSON・真偽値以外はすべて `false`、読み取りは絶対にファイルを書き換えません。書き込みは一時ファイル + `rename` で、ユーザーが足した他のキーは保持します。
- `lib/settings-command.ts` — 引数なしの `/startup-picker:settings`。「Ask on /new: on / off」を選ぶだけで、キャンセルは現状維持（書き込みなし）。書き込み失敗は error 通知で「保存できなかった」と明示し、保存済みとは表示しません。`/startup-picker:about` は現在の on/off を必ず表示します。
- `lib/startup-picker.ts` — `session_start` の `reason === "new"` 分岐を追加。設定がオンなら既存ピッカーを出し、ベースラインは「ピッカーを開く前の現在モデル」です。キャンセル・UI なし・レジストリ空・未知の recent・`setModel()` 失敗（例外含む）はすべて現在モデル維持 + warning のみで `/new` は継続し、起動時の既定モデルフォールバックは通りません。recent store への保存はモデル切替が成功したときだけです。`resume`/`fork`/`reload` は設定に関係なくピッカーを出さず、`startup` の挙動とキャンセル時のフォールバックは変更していません。
- `extensions/index.ts` — RPC モードでは従来どおり UI を非同期に遅延。`/new` のハンドラ失敗は warning に留め、ctx が stale になった後の通知も安全に無視します（RPC では `/new` 1 回で `session_start` が 2 回発火するため、同一セッションでの二重起動もガード）。

## 確認シナリオ

1. 設定ファイルなしで `/new` → ピッカーは出ず従来どおり（no-op）
2. `showOnNewSession: false` で `/new` → 同上
3. `showOnNewSession: true` で `/new` → provider → model のダイアログが出て選択が反映
4. 設定オンで `/new` のピッカーをキャンセル → 現在モデル維持、`/new` は継続、recent store 不変
5. 起動時（`reason === "startup"`）→ 従来どおりのピッカーとキャンセル時フォールバック
6. `resume` / `fork` / `reload` → 設定 on/off いずれでもピッカーなし
7. `/startup-picker:settings` で on に切り替え → 保存、`/startup-picker:about` が `on` を表示
8. `/startup-picker:settings` をキャンセル → 値は変わらず、ファイルも不変

## 操作手順

```txt
/startup-picker:about          # 現在の on/off を確認
/startup-picker:settings       # "Ask on /new: on" を選ぶ
/new                           # 設定オンなら provider/model ピッカーが出る
```

## 期待結果

- 設定が無い/壊れている/真偽値以外のときは `/new` が完全に no-op
- 設定オンでも、キャンセルや失敗時は「ピッカーを開く前の現在モデル」が維持され `/new` は止まらない
- 起動時（startup）の挙動とキャンセル時フォールバックは不変
- 書き込み失敗時に「保存した」と表示されない
- recent store は切替成功時のみ更新され、recent-first の順序が保たれる

## 確認コマンド

```txt
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run smoke:pi
npm run ci
npm pack --dry-run
```

実行結果（この checkout、Windows / Node v26.12.1 / Pi SDK 1.5.0）:

- `npm run typecheck`: pass
- `npm test`: 80 tests / 80 pass / 0 fail
- `npm run smoke:pi` (`pi-sdk-behavior-v2`, 実 Pi 1.5.0 RPC プロセス): 8/8 pass
  - `extension_load`, `happy_path`, `error_path`, `reload_cleanup`, `new_session_default_off`, `new_session_disabled`, `new_session_enabled`, `host_shell` すべて exit 0、unhandled error 0、extension load error 0
  - `new_session_default_off` / `new_session_disabled` は `/new` のダイアログが 0 件、`new_session_enabled` は provider → model の 2 ダイアログを経て `get_state` が選択モデルを返すことを確認
- `npm run ci`: pass（typecheck + test + smoke + pack）
- `npm pack --dry-run`: 22 files / `pi-startup-picker-0.4.0.tgz`、`lib/settings-store.ts`・`lib/settings-command.ts` を含む
- 追加の実機プローブ: 実 Pi RPC 上で `/startup-picker:settings` → on、`/startup-picker:about` が `on` を表示、再度 settings をキャンセルしてもファイルが不変であることを確認

## 注意する失敗パターン

- 設定ファイルの読み取りで例外を投げる（欠落・不正 JSON は off として扱うこと）
- 読み取り時にユーザーの設定ファイルを書き戻してしまう
- `/new` でキャンセル/失敗時に起動時の既定モデルへフォールバックしてしまう（現在モデル維持が正しい）
- `setModel()` が例外を投げた場合に `/new` が失敗扱いになる
- `/new` 1 回でピッカーが二重に出る（RPC の `session_start` 二重発火）
- 書き込み失敗を「保存済み」として通知する

## バージョン

- `package.json` / `package-lock.json`: `0.3.12` → `0.4.0`（後方互換の opt-in 機能追加のため minor。canonical `main` = `b63e575` の 0.3.12 から再計算）
- `CHANGELOG.md` に 0.4.0 エントリを追加、README / ROADMAP / `docs/examples.md` / `docs/pi-sdk-compatibility.md` も既定オフと opt-in フローに更新
- publish / tag / release / workflow dispatch / deploy は実施していません


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **New Features**
  * Added an opt-in model picker for `/new`, disabled by default. Enable or disable it with `/startup-picker:settings`, and check its status with `/startup-picker:about`.
  * If selection is canceled, unavailable, or fails, `/new` keeps the current model. Recent model combinations are saved only after a successful switch.
  * The picker remains unavailable for resume, fork, and reload sessions. Missing or invalid settings default to off.
* **Documentation**

body:
## What and why

The standards say only the env modules read import.meta.env. Three reads lived elsewhere:

- `VITE_EXPOSE_MAP`, in the map's test hand-outs, is now `isMapExposed` in `shared/config/env.ts`. It stays a plain comparison the build works out, so the hand-out is still dropped from a production build; the build guard that proves it passes.
- `VITE_CONTRIBUTIONS`, in the studio's `flags.ts`, moves into the studio's `env.ts` beside the other values it parses. `flags.ts` goes.
- `VITE_EMULATOR_RIDE` moves from `shared/config/env.ts` into the contributor page's own `env.ts`, parsed with its other values. The one read in `app/contribute/main.tsx` stays in place, with a line that says why: there the build must see it to leave the emulator driver out of every other build.

ESLint now refuses import.meta.env outside the four env modules, by name or handed on whole. MODE, DEV and PROD may be read anywhere. docs/architecture.md is regenerated for the two new import edges.

## Two things that had to stay as they are, and why

- **`VITE_EXPOSE_MAP` is not parsed with Zod.** I tried that first: the production build then carried the code that hands the map out on `window`, and the build guard "no production file hands out the map as window.__map" failed. A value parsed while the page runs cannot be dropped by the build; a plain comparison can. So `isMapExposed` in `shared/config/env.ts` is a plain comparison, with a comment that says so, and the guard passes.
- **One read stays in `app/contribute/main.tsx`**, with a one-line lint exception and its reason. Read from the env module instead, the tester's app build gained a file for the CI emulator's driver (an orphan nothing loads, but it should not be in a tester's APK at all). Read in place, the app build is as before: no emulator file in the tester build, one in the build made with `VITE_EMULATOR_RIDE=1`. Both were built and checked.

## Shown failing, then removed

A scratch file with `import.meta.env.VITE_SOMETHING`, `JSON.stringify(import.meta.env)` and a line reading `DEV`, `MODE` and `PROD`: the first two are refused with the new message, the third passes. The scratch file is deleted.

## Proposed line for the standards (not edited here)

`.claude/CLAUDE.md`, "Validation with Zod", after "Nothing else reads `import.meta.env`": **"`MODE`, `DEV` and `PROD` may be read anywhere, for a branch the build works out."** That is what the code does and what the new rule allows. It is the owner's file to change.

## Checked

`npm run check` passes on the branch merged with today's staging (1,802 unit checks), the build's size budgets and guards among it. The suites that use these flags run in this PR's CI.

## Worth knowing

`eslint.config.js` changes, so this counts as touching every file it governs. `docs/architecture.md` is regenerated here; a change that regenerates it too runs `npm run docs:architecture` again after this merges.

## Linked issue

None.

- [x] No new `any`, `!` or `as`
- [x] New and changed files follow the naming and folder rules (kebab-case, in the right feature)

author: owaiskhan-ash
body:
## Why

A scan is the one action that costs money and queries the open web on someone's behalf, and `/api/swarm` is a public URL. Hiding the form in the browser was never a gate — anyone could POST to the route. This ties the scan to a signed-in Google account on **both** sides, and brings the copy back in line with the behaviour.

## How the check works

`lib/scan-auth.ts` verifies the Firebase ID token the client sends. Two steps, no service account, no new dependency:

1. **Shape and claims** — three segments, `iss = https://securetoken.google.com/<project>`, matching `aud`, unexpired. Anything invented locally dies here.
2. **Issuer** — one call to Identity Toolkit `accounts:lookup` with the same token, returning `users[0].localId` as the caller.

`POST /api/swarm` now answers `401 { code: "auth-required" }` before the rate limit. If Identity Toolkit is unreachable the token's own claims still have to check out, so an outage cannot lock every signed-in user out of the product.

## Interface

- **`/scan`** — signed out shows a sign-in panel ("A scan runs on your account, not on the open internet") with one Google button and an aside on what the account is for; no inputs, no submit. The form appears the moment auth restores. While the session is being restored, a skeleton holds the space so the gate never flashes at someone already signed in.
- **Dashboard scanner** — same rule: the button reads *Sign in to scan* and starts Google sign-in; the request carries `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>`; a 401 surfaces the server's message. Stored reports stay visible.
- **Copy** — the landing FAQ ("Do I need an account?"), both "Your data" cards, the cost answer and the privacy policy (§ Information you provide, § Google Sign-In) no longer promise that a scan runs without an account.
- **`GoogleMark`** — the Google G SVG now lives in one component instead of two.

## Verified locally

| Request to `/api/swarm` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| no `Authorization` header | `401 {"error":"Sign in with Google to run a scan.","code":"auth-required"}` |
| `Bearer not-a-real-token` | `401` same body |
| forged JWT with a foreign `aud` | `401` same body |
| forged JWT with correct `iss`/`aud` (sandbox has no egress to Google) | passes the gate, then fails downstream for the local missing `GEMINI_API_KEY` — the outage path logs `Scan auth: Identity Toolkit unreachable` |

Headless: `/scan` signed out shows the gate, `#phoneInput` absent, submit absent, overflow 0 at 390 px; `/dashboard` shows a stored report with the button reading "Sign in to scan". `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` clean.

body:
The escrow-release retry test in svc-p2p (`saga.money.test.ts`) failed once on a CI runner. It ran out of time, though the money it checks was never wrong (#7158). It replays the release several times, and each replay rebuilds the trade in Postgres from scratch, so all of them together can take longer than vitest's default 5 s on a busy runner.

**Fix:** the shared money-door test (`describeMoneyDoor` in `packages/ledger-client/src/testing/saga.ts`) takes an optional `timeoutMs`, and svc-p2p's escrow-release door sets it to 30 s. No assertion, replay or invariant changes. Every other door keeps the default.

Closes #7158.

**Proof:**
- Reproduced locally before the change: `TEST_DATABASE_URL=… pnpm exec vitest run src/saga.money.test.ts` in services/svc-p2p failed with `Test timed out in 5000ms`, the same error as the issue.
- After the change, the same run stops at `Test timed out in 30000ms`, which shows the budget reaches the test. On this Mac it still ran out of time: the load average was 170 to 260 during the run (`uptime`), and one earlier run with a 120 s budget passed in 75 s. A local run proves nothing; CI's Tests job on this head is the proof.
- CI on this head: run 43201464771, job "Tests (10/16)": `✓ src/saga.money.test.ts (1 test) 1193ms`, svc-p2p 618 tests passed. The CI review passed on this head.
- `pnpm --filter @intafaced/ledger-client exec vitest run src/testing`: 90 passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean for ledger-client and svc-p2p. Prettier clean on both files.

Left-or-replaced: none (no journey step).

Decisions:
- The budget is per door, not a new default for every door, so only the door that failed changes.
- 30 s is about 6 times the 5 s default this test normally finishes inside on CI. A real hang still fails, now after 30 s.

Revert: revert this one commit.

author: hooop
body:
## Summary

Claudex is now entirely in English, ahead of its open-source distribution: UI, agent prompts, slash commands, files written into users' projects, tests, comments, docs, this repository's `.claudex/memory`, and the demo GIF. The git history is not rewritten.

Behaviour changes:
- **Answer language**: agents write their debate messages and the consensus summary in the language of the human's messages, English when they cannot; everything else they write (code, comments, commit messages, files, including after `/implement`) is in English. Three new tests pin the rule.
- **`/sujet` is now `/topic`**, with no alias.
- Welcome-screen date in `en-US`; English number formats (`8.2 s`, `30,000 characters`).
- New `.claudex/.gitignore`, scaffolds and handoff headings are in English, and the gitignore no longer overclaims that agents re-read the memory "at the start of every debate". Existing French memory files in users' projects keep working (nothing parses their headings).
- The repository agent `memoire-claudex` is renamed `claudex-memory`.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-english-pass-design.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-12-english-pass.md`.

## How it was tested

- `npm run check`: typecheck, lint, 40 files / 702 tests (699 on main + 3 language-rule tests). Matchers kept their strictness; two near-empty guards were made meaningful again.
- Each task was reviewed separately. The agent prompts and both memory files were compared with the French originals rule by rule and line by line (same headings, dates and numbers). A final whole-branch review was followed by one fix wave, which was re-reviewed.
- Final case-insensitive grep for French over every tracked file. Remaining justified hits: the English-pass spec and plan (they quote what was translated), the deliberate `café` test inputs, the old heading quoted in the README, and one real local file name in `limits.md`.
- Demo GIF regenerated with `vhs` from the translated tape. Frames were checked: English throughout, 53 MB (was 57 MB).
- **Not tested**: a real debate. Please run the smoke test from the design: start one debate in French and one in English, check that the agents answer in your language, and check `/topic`, `/help`, the welcome date and a handoff file.

## Decisions taken

Listed in the design's "Decisions taken" sections: one language and no i18n layer; no `/sujet` alias; fixed `en-US` locale; users' existing memory not migrated; our own translation (not the external fork's); the memory and old plans keep commands and numbers byte for byte, with translated quotes marked "(translated from French)".

## What to review closely

1. `CONSENSUS_INSTRUCTIONS` and `SYNTHESIS_PROMPT` in `src/orchestrator/scheduler.ts`: the wording of the language rule.
2. `src/memory/store.ts`: the `CLAUDEX_GITIGNORE` text written into users' projects.
3. `.claudex/memory/decisions.md` and `limits.md`: spot-check a few entries you know well.
4. README: the paragraph on the agents' language.

author: stevenjpx2
body:
## You can Run atelier's service without macOS ever asking about `~/Documents`: `atelier add StevenJPx2/chauffeur` makes atelier's own copy of the project, and the daemon works only from it. Your checkout is never read or changed. Part of #1 ([atelier's own clones](https://github.com/StevenJPx2/atelier/issues/1#ateliers-own-clones), approved by the owner). ```sh atelier add StevenJPx2/chauffeur # watching StevenJPx2/chauffeur, cloned in /Users/me/.local/share/atelier/clones/StevenJPx2/chauffeur.git ``` ## Why Under launchd, git in a checkout in `~/Documents` waits on macOS's folder prompt, and each release, a new binary, brings it back. rc.5's daemon logged `git ran past 120s` for 40 minutes until the owner clicked Allow. CI runners and coding agents keep their own copies (GitHub Actions runners, Buildkite's git mirrors, Renovate), which also keeps atelier independent of where and how you keep your checkouts. ## Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR Add["atelier add owner/name"] --> Clone["clones/owner/name.git
bare, origin only"] Poll["each poll"] -- "makes it if missing" --> Clone Clone -- "fetch base, worktree add" --> Tree["worktrees/owner/name/issue-n"] Yours["your checkout
~/Documents/…"] -. "init only, from your terminal" .-> Init["atelier init"] ``` ## Builds - `refactor(git)`, a separate mechanical commit: `Checkout` becomes `Repository`, and the `checkout` fields of `Project`, `WorktreeRequest` and `Worktrees::remove` become `local`. No behaviour change. - `Repository::under(root, repo)` → `//.git`, with the same folder-safety checks as worktrees. `create(url)` makes a bare repository with `origin`, fetches nothing, and refuses one with another `origin`. Branches are fetched on demand into `origin/`; its only local branches are the issues'. - `GitHub::clone_url`: GitHub's URL over the protocol `gh` uses for github.com, as `gh repo clone` does (HTTPS unless set to SSH), so pushes use the same sign-in as today. - `atelier add owner/name` (no `--path`) makes the clone, checks it can reach `origin`, and removes a clone it just made if not. Each poll makes a missing clone, so projects added before move over on the next poll; their `path` is accepted and no longer read. `status` shows the clone and never makes one. `init` still runs in your checkout, from your terminal. - `Git::remove` runs git inside the worktree, so a worktree made from your checkout before this change is removed too. - No new dependencies. Structure: [slice 1 page](https://github.com/StevenJPx2/atelier/blob/feat/own-clones/docs/plans/slices/slice-1.md#worktrees-cratesgit). ## Proofs - Git, real repositories: the fixture's local repository is now the bare clone made by `Repository::create`, so every worktree test runs from the production layout. New: the clone is bare with its `origin`, holds only `origin/v2` after a fetch, and refuses another `origin`; a worktree made from a separate checkout is removed through `Git::remove`; unsafe names are refused for clones too. - GitHub: `clone_url` against what real `gh` 2.103.3 printed for `git_protocol` (fresh config: `https`; after `set ssh`: `ssh`), and HTTPS when `gh` fails. - Real binary: `add` makes a bare clone with GitHub's URL; refuses an unreachable repository leaving no clone, an unsafe name, and a second add. With an old entry naming your checkout and no clone, the daemon makes the clone, the builder's worktree belongs to it (`--git-common-dir`), and your checkout gains no worktree and no ref. The sandbox's home sends every `https://github.com/` URL to a local folder, so tests never reach the network. ## Gates Local: fmt, Clippy -D warnings, nextest (97; CLI suite 4 runs), doc tests, rustdoc -D warnings, MSRV 1.96, cargo-deny, cargo-shear, Prettier. cargo-mutants on the diff: 41 mutants, 35 caught, 6 unviable, 0 missed. After merge and the rc: restart the service and check over several polls and a claim that no daemon process touches `~/Documents`.

author: welshofer
body:
## What

W1 dogfood 15 was a Japanese 10-minute keynote, made by `scaena generate` against scripted Anthropic and OpenAI endpoints. On main, all 8 slides' notes were dropped as too short for their share of the talk. The cause is two mismatches:

- **The prompt** asks each slide's notes in words, at 145 a minute ("about 60 words").
- **`notes::counted`** splits on whitespace, so Japanese notes written to their budget count as a word or two. `read_all` then drops them as `Short`.

Health already times a talk set without spaces at 300 characters a minute (`CHARACTERS_A_MINUTE`, `by_character`). The notes now use the same rule:

- `duration::CHARACTERS_PER_MINUTE` (300) and `duration::by_character` (kana, Han, Hangul) sit beside `WORDS_PER_MINUTE`.
- `counted` counts each spaced word as one, and each run of CJK characters as the words they take to say: characters × 145 / 300.
- For a deck in Japanese, Chinese, or Korean, by name or tag:
  - the notes' prompt asks "spoken at about 300 characters a minute" and each slide "about N characters";
  - its rule says "Run to about the characters given for the slide".

  English prompts are byte for byte as before.

## Evidence

On the dogfood's deck, with the same scripted answers:

- **Main:** 0 of 8 slides keep notes, and every beat is held at Narrato's 15 s estimate.
- **This branch:** all 8 keep notes (263–329 characters each), each beat timed 69–76 s. Health says "About 10 minutes of talk, where its brief asks 10 minutes."

## Test

`a_talk_said_by_the_character_is_asked_and_counted_in_characters` (`scaena-narrato` notes):

- The Japanese prompt asks in characters.
- The English prompt still asks in words.
- 132 characters of Japanese count as 64 words, and `read_all` keeps them.
- An English sentence counts as before.

Without the fix, it fails: `left: 1, right: 64`.

Checks run: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; clippy `-p scaena-narrato -p scaena-ops --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`; `cargo test -p scaena-narrato`; `cargo test -p scaena-ops --features narrato,shipped --lib --tests`.

## CLAUDE.md

In "Deck generation", after "…at 145 words a minute less the change and its own words on screen,": add "a talk in Japanese, Chinese, or Korean asked and counted at 300 characters a minute, as health times it (`duration::by_character`, W1 dogfood 15),".
