author: braghettos
body:
Fixes #233, with the design the maintainer chose: follow each component's upgrade policy.

## Defect (measured on GKE, 0.3.47 → 0.3.48, core-provider 2.13.82)
The umbrella emitted every existing child at its **origin** version (`osh.pinVersion`, #166), whatever the component's `upgradePolicy`. That was supposed to be inert under `Automatic`, because the engine used to prune the old version (measured on 0.3.28). core-provider 2.13.82 keeps a version that a release revision still uses, so on an upgraded install:
- all 32 children were still emitted at `v0-3-47` an hour after the upgrade, and `v0-3-47` was never retired;
- `componentValues.keystone.oidc.caBundleRef` was **rendered** by the umbrella and **missing** from the stored child, because the child is written through the narrower v0-3-47 schema. So #220 and #217 do nothing on upgraded installs;
- the engine (writing v0-3-48) and the umbrella (writing v0-3-47) were two writers on every child (core-provider#462).

The positive control on a fresh 0.3.48 install stored the same value and keystone-api mounted it.

## Fix
- `osh.migrationApproved(policy, upgradeTo, current)`, a pure function, is the engine's own predicate (`CompositionDefinition.MigrationApproved`, types.go:258-269 at 2.13.82, confirmed with core-provider):
  - `Paused` → no;
  - `Manual` → only if `krateo.io/upgrade-to-version` equals the current **served version name** (`v0-3-48`); any other value, an older version included, approves nothing;
  - `Automatic` or unset → yes.
- `osh.migrationApprovedFor` reads the component's **live** CompositionDefinition with one named GET in the release namespace, so an operator's `kubectl patch ... upgradePolicy` counts.
- `osh.effectiveOrigin` drops the origin when migration is approved. `osh.resolveVersion` is unchanged: it emits the current version once served and the newest served version before that, so #166's protection at the bump instant holds.
- Offline (`helm template`) the lookup returns nothing, the policy reads as unset, and the origin was already empty offline, so the offline render is unchanged. `validate-origin-version-pin.py` still asserts it is byte-identical.

## Gate (`hack/validate-upgrade-does-not-prune.py`)
- 7 policy cases checked against the engine's answers: automatic, unset, paused, Manual without the annotation, Manual→current, Manual→older, and Manual with the chart-version form `0.3.33`.
- For each case, emission of an existing component born at the old version: with **both versions served** it goes to current iff approved; at the **bump instant** it goes to the old version whatever the policy.
- Structural checks that `osh.emitVersion` routes the origin through `osh.effectiveOrigin(..., osh.migrationApprovedFor ...)`, and that the policy is read from the live CompositionDefinition and compared with the current version.
- Mutations:

  | mutation | result |
  |---|---|
  | pin regardless of policy (main's behaviour) | **FAIL**, 3 cases (automatic, unset, Manual→current) |
  | Manual always approves | **FAIL**, 6 problems |

- On this branch, these all pass: `validate-upgrade-does-not-prune`, `validate-origin-version-pin`, `validate-docs-wait-for-served-kind`, `validate-capability-roles`.

## Not yet verified live, and why
The engine pulls charts from GHCR, so the live proof needs a release containing this fix: a cold 0.3.47 install upgraded to it, then a 0.3.48-only value set, which must be **stored** on the child, and every child's `krateo.io/composition-version` must equal the version emitted after the roll. I will run that before this is called done.

author: agon252009
body:
- [ ] Full review cycle run: the review-cycle skill, every phase, through its closing conformance pass

## Summary

Panels cannot use the clipboard, and the orb skill never said so, so agents kept giving panels copy buttons that silently copied nothing. The skill now says to give panels no copy button, and to copy text on the host and tell the user instead.

## Key changes

- `skills/orb/SKILL.md`: panels cannot use the clipboard; copy on the host (`pbcopy` on macOS) and say so

## Technical implementation

Two lines in the panel rules, next to the existing statement that panels run sandboxed. Panels are iframes built by `sandboxedFrame` in `web/orb.js`, with an opaque origin and no `allow` attribute, so the `clipboard-write` permission is never delegated and `navigator.clipboard.writeText` fails.

## Rationale

Making the button work instead, with `iframe.allow = "clipboard-write"`, would let any panel write to the user's clipboard on a click. That is a security decision for the orb-security work, so it is recorded as a follow-up in #228 and not made here. Until it is made, the skill has to stop agents from shipping a control that cannot work.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run python -m pytest -q orb/test_skill_speaker.py`: passes, so the skill text still parses for the speaker test
- [x] Confirmed the cause: `web/orb.js` `sandboxedFrame` sets `sandbox` with no `allow` attribute; a panel copy button copied nothing in use on Thu, Nov 12, 2026

Closes #228

author: andrebrait
body:
## What

Give programs that embed omp, like ompweb's runner, a supported way to start a session without going through RPC.

`runRootCommand` takes an optional `runSessionHost` dependency. With it, a launch goes through the normal startup (settings, auth, `--resume`/`--model`/`--tools`, extensions, MCP, session creation) with the protocol-host behaviour of `--mode rpc-ui` (stdin left to the host, tool UI enabled, a session without a model still starts), then hands the session and its tool-UI setter to the host instead of the TUI, print or RPC modes. `SessionHostContext` and `RunSessionHost` are exported for embedders.

## Why

An embedder that drives `AgentSession` directly today has to either reimplement omp's startup or run omp as an RPC child and translate its protocol. This hook keeps the startup in omp and leaves the session's transport to the host.

## Testing

`packages/coding-agent/test/main-session-host.test.ts` covers the handoff (session started with the CLI's options, tool UI setter delivered, TUI/RPC modes not entered). Used by ompweb's runner in production through a patch of 18.19.0.

---

body:
Yukon submission `9f7fa0d9-d2eb-4eed-92b8-a1590b23cf55` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/flock-challenge at `7a5a4ab92532d52c9b6f0b53cac875bbb90ffb47`.

Current best score: 2322204.58380192. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: GPT
Harness: Codex

This candidate is based on promoted source 7a5a4ab92532d52c9b6f0b53cac875bbb90ffb47, associated with submission bb23c183-315e-4d00-a518-4026cafffb88. It changes only crates/flock-core/src/gpu_commit.rs. The executable change is confined to LC_FACTORED_B4_MSL_SOURCE and removes the intermediate threadgroup equality-generator array from lc_fold_stripes_factored_b4. The existing table is built directly from the immutable equality buffer, so the producer-consumer barrier for that intermediate array is no longer required.

The production selection was traced before making the change. launch_fold_prefix selects pso_lc_factored_b4 for the zerocheck arm when byte folding and the factored route are enabled and the pipeline object exists. It otherwise falls back to the incumbent byte-B4 pipeline, then the nibble-B8 pipeline. The lincheck arm also prefers the factored B4 pipeline when available. The candidate therefore affects both arms when they select this shared shader. It does not optimize only the nibble fallback. The official workflow does not explicitly enable the relevant rollback variables. Actual pipeline creation and selection on the official runner have not been observed locally, and source-level preference is not presented as runtime instrumentation.

The baseline shader processes at most four stripes per loop iteration with a group of 256 threads. It first copies ns*8 equality generators into tg_eq, synchronizes the group, and assigns 64 builder threads to each active stripe. Each builder forms the low-six-bit subset XOR, then emits four table entries by selecting neither of the two remaining generators, generator6, generator7, or both. The resulting table has 256 entries per stripe. A second producer-consumer synchronization publishes the table before the witness bytes are looked up.

The changed shader retains the same builder ownership and XOR expressions. For builder lane lid, the stripe is s=lid>>6 and the low-six-bit selector is h=lid&63. Instead of indexing a staged array at s*8, the builder directly reads the device equality buffer at (sb+s)*8. The low-six-bit while loop, its ctz index, the two high generators and the four output addresses remain equivalent. No multiplication, reduction polynomial, field representation, bit order or table-value formula is changed.

For a given active stripe, the output indices are s*256+h plus offsets 0,64,128,192. As h runs from zero through63 these are disjoint and cover every table entry exactly once. The builder guard lid<ns*64 prevents inactive stripes from writing or reading generators. Each referenced generator index lies between sb*8 and (sb+ns)*8-1. This is the same equality-input extent that the baseline staging copy read. The change does not access generators belonging to a later stripe or require extra input padding.

Two converged threadgroup barriers remain inside every loop iteration. The first precedes table writes and ensures that all previous-iteration table lookups have finished before storage is reused. The second follows all table writes and ensures that every current table entry is visible before lookup. The removed middle barrier existed to publish tg_eq, which is no longer written or allocated. The eq buffer is populated before dispatch and remains immutable during that dispatch under the unchanged host ownership and command-buffer lifetime contract. There is no newly introduced cross-thread producer for eq that would require an in-kernel staging barrier.

Both remaining barriers are outside the live-column and builder-lane conditionals. Every thread in a group executes the same stripe-loop bounds, so inactive columns and lanes beyond the short final stripe count still rendezvous. A short final block consumes only tables below ns. The final loop iteration needs no additional table-reuse barrier after its lookups because the table is not reused after that iteration. Partial-output stores remain disjoint and unchanged; the subsequent reduction dispatch and its ordering are unchanged as well.

The useful-column test and witness loading are unchanged. A thread owns four adjacent columns and either contributes to those useful columns or leaves their accumulators at zero. Full B4 blocks retain their existing up-front word loads, and shorter blocks retain the incumbent per-stripe word path. Chunk offsets, stripe_hi, stripes_per_chunk, i_groups, output positions and the partial-reduction algorithm are untouched. Host GPU/CPU prefix partitioning, staged-prefix adoption, fallback pipeline selection and failure behavior are also untouched.

The source-level savings are one of the three barriers per stripe block and the staging writes for up to32 uint4 generators. The threadgroup storage decreases from16896 bytes to16384 bytes by removing the512-byte generator array. No occupancy improvement is claimed from that size change. The tradeoff is more source-level device reads: a full stripe had eight initial device generator loads, whereas its64 builders now issue192 low-six-bit selected reads plus128 high-generator reads, or320 total. Those accesses refer to the same eight generator values. Cache, broadcast and compiler behavior determine the actual memory transactions and latency;320 is not a DRAM-transaction count. The candidate may regress if the additional loads outweigh the removed synchronization.

No timing result or speedup estimate is attached to this candidate. The optimization hypothesis is that direct access to the small shared read-only generator set can reduce staging and synchronization cost while preserving the existing factored table lookup. Official execution is needed to determine the whole-proof effect. The change does not modify the challenge, nonce, proof transcript, accepted input domain, scoring, verification requirements or benchmark harness in order to obtain a favorable result.

Bounded independent checks compared30720 table entries to a separate eight-bit subset-XOR definition. These cases cover all256 byte values, both high generator bits, active stripe counts zero through four, multiple stripe offsets, and zero, all-one, high-bit and random generator families. The checker verified complete disjoint table writes and exact equality-index bounds. It then compared480 folded-output cases with a direct scalar per-bit reference, covering empty and short stripe ranges, full and partial B4 iterations, nonzero offsets, and useful-column limits0,8,56,64. Padding outputs remained zero.

Two negative controls deliberately used the wrong stripe offset or removed generator6. Both were detected. The arithmetic and indexing checks took approximately0.15 seconds and did not run a native benchmark. Arithmetic equivalence alone cannot establish GPU race freedom; the retained-barrier and immutable-buffer argument is provided separately above. Rustfmt parsed the exact baseline and candidate without syntax errors; both retained the same121 existing formatting-difference hunks. The patch applied and reversed byte-for-byte against the exact baseline, and git diff --check passed. The checker passed Python compilation and Ruff.

Rust type checking, Metal shader compilation, GPU execution, native proof verification and performance measurements have not been run locally. Rustfmt does not parse the embedded Metal string. The candidate is intended for the normal official evaluator with these limitations disclosed. Existing fallback behavior remains available if the supplemental pipeline cannot be created; fallback execution would not establish that this changed kernel was exercised succe

author: vigani1
body:
## Summary

Fixes a real worker bug behind an intermittent For Each fan-in failure: attempt leases could expire while their worker was still working on them.

**Causes, found by tracing dispatch, claim and publish:**
- A handler started its lease heartbeat only **after** reading the executable and inputs, so a slow preparation could let the claimed lease expire.
- Claims, reads and renewals shared one connection pool. Blocked work could occupy every connection, so an attempt that still owned its lease couldn't get one to renew it.
- Unused cold For Each spare preloads weren't cancelled promptly.

With 100 fan-in sources, the fan-in step then waited on source attempts whose leases had expired without ever being renewed.

**Fix:**
- The heartbeat is owned from the claim onward, preparation included. Every exit path (success, failure, cancellation, drain and shutdown) awaits its cleanup. Renewal stays fenced: it never extends an expired or replaced lease.
- A one-slot renewal runtime uses the worker role and shares the worker's monitor, so it costs **one** extra connection per attempt runtime (measured: 4 connections, not 5). The default connection budget is 39 per instance, or 75 with two overlapping instances plus ops and migration, under PostgreSQL's 100.
- Preload startup deadlines are charged only when requested, and unused cold spares are cancelled promptly. An assigned spare is never cancelled.

No retries were added, no deadlines lengthened, no fencing relaxed, and no schema or role changed.

## Moved / Removed

None.

Lines: 662 insertions(+), 209 deletions(-).

## Commits

- `374f366bf` fix: retain preparation leases and defer worker preload deadlines
- `2942eabd5` fix: reserve a connection for attempt heartbeats
- `080267de8` fix: cancel unused For Each worker preloads promptly
- `d5359a53f` fix: share the worker monitor with attempt renewals
- `3b77a3807` test: cover preparation lease fencing and large For Each fan-in

Replayed (cherry-picked) onto main with no conflicts. Commits that fail checks on their own: none known.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm check`; 1,173 worker unit tests
- [x] Regressions that fail on the base: a preparation lease crossing its original expiry, which also refuses a competing claim; renewal under a saturated pool; the connection count (5 before, 4 after); stale renewal rejection; a 100-item For Each with exact ordered results
- [x] Worker integration: 100 tests in the attempts, For Each, fan-in, pending-task and recovery files; 16 Calls tests
- [x] Full worker recovery and resilience with faults enabled: 146 tests, including J1's Code deploy-drain regression and SIGTERM, kill, freeze and thaw recovery
- [x] Two full worker integration runs at 2,365 passed each (diagnosis)
- [x] Fresh review (ready; P3 fixed), independent test writer (mutation-proven, no bugs), final review (ready)

author: zmeigorynych
body:
DEV-2280 — the SLayer 2.0 breaking half of Ossie expression coverage (the additive half is DEV-2282).

## What changes

**A date compared with a timestamp is its midnight, as in SQL and Ossie.** On 1.x, `created_at <= '2024-12-31'` read the whole day; now it stops at `2024-12-31 00:00:00`. This holds in every position: filters, `FILTER (WHERE …)` and `CASE` in measures, saved measures, column filters and dates bound through variables. The whole day is still one spelling away: `created_at in '2024-12-31'`, or `created_at < '2025-01-01'` as an upper bound. `date_range` bounds and the other period literals (`'2024'`, `'2024-Q4'`, `'2024-12'`, relative tokens) keep their period meaning, and DATE columns, `>=` and `<` come out the same either way.

```json
{"source_model": "orders", "dimensions": ["id"], "filters": ["created_at <= '2024-04-10'"]}
```
With an order at `2024-04-10 09:30`, 1.x returned it and 2.0 does not.

**The change is announced.** Where the new reading gives different rows (`<=`, `>`, `=`, `!=`, `BETWEEN` against a TIMESTAMP), the response, or the save, carries one `date_only_midnight` warning per spelling. It names the whole-day spelling, and the variables that bound the date at that comparison, if any. It is a structured warning (also a Python `UserWarning`), not a `FutureWarning`, and the removal tripwire reads its new `scheduled_notice` marker, which schedules it for removal in 3.0.

**Stored documents keep their rows.** On load, the stored versions bump to SlayerModel 24, SlayerQuery 15 and Memory 11 (after DEV-2021's and DEV-2281's bumps). Each Mode-B comparison of a TIMESTAMP column with a date is rewritten to its 1.x meaning:

| stored | loads as |
|---|---|
| `x <= '2024-12-31'` | `x < '2025-01-01'` |
| `x > '2024-04-10'` | `x >= '2024-04-11'` |
| `x = '2024-04-10'` | `x in '2024-04-10'` |
| `x BETWEEN 'A' AND 'B'` | `(x >= 'A' and x < 'B+1')` |

On `9999-12-31`, which has no next day, the bound is that day's last microsecond (`x <= '9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999'`). Column types are read from the datasource's stored models, walking joins in either direction and matching names case-insensitively; they are read only when the document holds a date literal. Each nested query is upgraded according to its own stored version. A comparison whose column can't be typed is left as written and logged. The rest of the text stays byte-identical.

**Ossie export.** A comparison with a fixed date or time now exports as a standard-SQL comparison, so the metric is no longer dropped as SLayer-only. Period and relative comparisons stay SLayer-only.

**SQLite casts.** `CAST(x AS TIMESTAMP)` (and `DATETIME`, `TIMESTAMP_NTZ`, `::TIMESTAMP`) returned the year on SQLite. It now converts as `TRY_CAST` does. `TIME`, zoned timestamps and timestamps with a precision are refused at plan time with the typed cast error.

**Numeric pins.** Library-matrix cases pin true division of integers (`5 / 2` is `2.5`) and away-from-zero DECIMAL ties under two-argument `round` on every Tier-1 dialect. The server dialects are verified by CI.

## Also in this PR
- `basedpyright` locked at 1.40.2, the version `la-typecheck` verifies.
- Docs: `concepts/time.md`, the agent help, the MCP query description, the dbt and Ossie import/export pages, `formulas.md` (numeric semantics) and a `docs/upgrading/2.0.md` entry.

The full spec is in `openspec/changes/dev-2280-ossie-expression-coverage-every-valid-ossie/`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Date-only strings now represent midnight in temporal comparisons, while `in`, `not in`, and `date_range` continue to cover the whole day.
  * SQLite timestamp casts now normalize valid dates and timestamps and return NULL for invalid values; unsupported cast types are rejected.
  * Integer division preserves fractional results. Decimal rounding ties round away from zero; floating-point tie behavior remains database-specific.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Older saved queries and models are upgraded to preserve their previous whole-day date-comparison results.
  * Date-only comparisons with timestamp fields may display an informational notice when midnight semantics could affect results.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated guidance explains date-only comparison and range behavior, numeric semantics, SQLite casts, and compatibility changes.

author: vde-dis
body:
Part of the CI programme (0.5.0). Fixes a hole in the docs-only rule, and moves that rule into a script that a test can call.

**The hole.** A diff made only of Markdown sets `code=false` and skips the heavy jobs. But six documents are asserted on by harnesses: `docs/network.md` and `docs/network.fr.md` (`test-flow-matrix.sh`), `docs/status.md` (`test-evidence-age.sh`), `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.github/pull_request_template.md` (`test-rung-receipts.sh`), `infrastructure/opentofu/cluster/README.md` (`test-bootstrap-in-state.sh`). A pull request editing only one of them skipped the harness that catches the break; it surfaced only on the push run after the merge. Those six now count as code.

**What changes**
- `scripts/dev/classify-changes.sh` holds the rule (the old pattern, unchanged, plus the list of the six). The `Classify the diff` step calls it. It also uses `git diff --no-renames`: a moved file is listed under both names, so moving away a document a harness reads is code too (the default prints only the new name).
- `scripts/dev/test-docs-only-rule.sh` (about 0.4 s, 14 cases, picked up by the `test-scripts` glob): pure documentation is docs-only, a script or a workflow is code, each listed document alone is code, a stale line (a listed file that is not tracked) fails, and a real two-commit git history shows the moved-document case. Without `--no-renames` that last case is red.
- The step reads the event and the base branch through `env:` instead of interpolating them into the shell.

**Replay.** Over the 194 commits since 2026-08-15: 22 were docs-only under the old rule, 7 of them now run the tests, all 7 because of `docs/status.md` (the other five listed files flip none by themselves). The new script agrees with the replay on all of them.

**Side effects to know.** A pull request that edits only one of the six files is a code pull request: it declares a rung (`CONTRIBUTING.md` says so). That is one word once the `Rung: mocked` receipt rule of #462 is in. The scan for new readers is deliberately absent: a harness that reads a document written some other way than the list is caught by the push run on `main`, not by the pull request, and the fix is one line in `classify-changes.sh`.

**Not changed:** the `rung` and `test` jobs (other pull requests of the programme are on those hunks).

author: haillucifer666
body:
Issue: Large-repo scans read as hangs: "Analysing / Progress — / Elapsed 2:00" then "Still running in the background", while the database showed the scans COMPLETING (scans 21/22). Causes: progress written only in the analyzer loop; serial worker with no queue position; a 120-second client give-up; ingest blocking the event loop (starving the heartbeat).

Fix: Ingest moves to asyncio.to_thread so the heartbeat beats during the clone; the worker emits cloning/reading phases; the detail endpoint reports queue_position while queued (0 = next up; a running scan counts for nobody); SSE frames carry it; ScanConsole polls to terminal with a 30-minute honest cap instead of a 2-minute give-up; AnimatedScan learns all phase labels, shows "Queued · N ahead", keeps elapsed ticking while queued/running, and surfaces "No heartbeat for Xm — worker may be stuck" from the heartbeat it was already being handed.

Verified: pytest -q 528 passed in api/; npm test 69 passed in web/ (6 new, red-first). Dedicated reviewer found no CRITICAL; its IMPORTANT (one failed poll aborted the 30-minute wait) is fixed with a failure-tolerance streak + unmount guard.

Merge order: after feat/dashboard-overhaul (this PR's base). A running worker predating this branch must be restarted at merge time.

author: plarsa
body:
Closes #136. Replaces #189, which was built on the branch of #186 before that was merged; this one is on current `main` and carries only this change.

A name carrying a character the realm's user profile refuses, such as `<` or `>`, answered **500 with a full Java stack trace**. Keycloak answers 400, and the application passed that on as an unhandled exception.

## A 4xx from Keycloak is a 4xx for the caller

`KeycloakErrorAdvice` answers a `KeycloakAdminException` carrying a 4xx with that same status and `{"reason":"KEYCLOAK_REJECTED"}`, and anything else with 500 and `{"reason":"KEYCLOAK_ERROR"}`. Neither what Keycloak said nor where the call failed goes into the response, and `application.yml` sets `include-stacktrace`, `include-message` and `include-exception` to off.

This is what closes the issue: whatever the realm refuses, for whatever reason, the caller is told it was their request and not the server.

## The form says which characters are the problem

The user form and both "add user" dialogs check the name before sending anything, with the pattern of Keycloak's `person-name-prohibited-characters` validator, and report it on the name field with the characters named.

That is the **only** copy of the rule. An earlier revision mirrored it in Java as well, checked it in both user endpoints and in the import dry run, and pinned all of it with tests — about 350 lines more, and the same rule to keep in step in two languages. The backend's message never reached the user interface anyway, which reports its own error for a failed save. If the copy falls behind the realm, the form lets the name through and the advice above answers 400 rather than 500.

## Verification

The rule is Keycloak's, not a guess at it. I pulled `PersonNameProhibitedCharactersValidator` out of `keycloak-services-26.8.1.jar` from the running Keycloak and read its `PATTERN` reflectively: the pattern here is that one, with `\p{Cntrl}` written out as the control ranges since JavaScript has no such class. The two agree on 26 sample names, including the payload from the issue, every listed character, a tab, an empty string, `Martin Lindström`, `Anna-Maria O'Brien` and `Ole-Johan Dahl`.

Backend: 493 tests. Frontend: 152 tests, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Not in this PR

A name the realm refuses inside an import bundle still stops the job part-way, as it does today. That is a defect of its own and belongs in its own issue rather than here.

author: lukacf
body:
## What was wrong

Some console timeline records were stored without the attributes of the member they are about and were
then decided by the member's name instead. Records of a member that is private to one person could
therefore be shown to other people who had signed in and, on a console where sign-in is optional, to a
caller who sent no token. Separately, records on the system page that speak of an agent or of memory records
without being that agent's own (the memory steward's conflict signals, quarantined writes, taint
transitions, promotions) were readable by everyone who may view that page. And the session of a private
side chat that had ended could, on some consoles, be attached by a caller other than its owner.

Affected: 0.9.11 through 0.9.14 (the system page records: releases through 0.9.14).

## What changes

1. Read rule: a frame stored without a witness is shown to an administrator only (a person listed under
   `admins`), on every console that can identify a person. Only a console that can identify nobody is
   exempt; a caller who sends no token on a console that verifies tokens is treated like any person who is
   not an administrator.
2. Witness rule: a frame's witness comes only from what its record names: the session it names; for a
   console send to a member with no session, the member the send is made to, captured at the send; for a
   record that names a console send, the witness stored on that send's frame. No projection reads a member
   by its name, also not when retained records are projected again.
3. Spawn kickoff: written only when the spawn tool's own outcome names the session of the member it made
   (`fork_off`, `delegate`). The copy derived from the spawning agent's history is no longer written, and a
   refused call leaves nothing under the name it gave.
4. System page: the memory steward's conflict signals, quarantined writes, taint transitions, promoted
   records and promotions that await approval are decided as a record with no witness: administrator-only,
   on every timeline surface. The decision a timeline read keeps for one request is keyed by everything the
   decision reads.
5. With no runtime registered, a stored frame whose member sat in a nested mob is not served.
6. Gating: on a console that can identify a person, audit entries carry neither a memory conflict's reason
   text nor the error text of a failed conflict lookup for a caller who is not an administrator (the stored
   entry is unchanged), and an audit entry or pending request whose origin the console does not know is
   shown to an administrator only.
7. A realm's dream history in the memory panel also consults a deny on an agent the console does not know.
8. Whether a console can identify a person is read in one function from the console's own configuration;
   a view taken for no subject anywhere else is kept apart by default.
9. Until a console has read who its runtime's agents are private to (right after a start, and for as long
   as that read fails), it keeps every caller who is not an administrator apart, a console that can
   identify nobody included. A request made while the first attempt of that read is running waits for it,
   at most five seconds.
10. Session attach: the console takes the private owner of a session from the labels the session was
    created with, also after its agent has ended. A session Core still serves is read as before. A session
    Core no longer serves (an ended agent's session is archived) is read through the runtime's session
    service with the read an attach loads the session through, and the owner is taken from the peer labels
    in its session metadata, where the agent's build writes them. Such a session is answered as one that
    does not exist to everyone but its owner and an administrator, on every console. A session no agent
    holds whose owner cannot be established (the read fails, the stored session names an agent and no
    labels, the runtime has no session service, or Core's member history does not answer) is attached for
    an administrator only: every other caller is answered "access denied: the session has no established
    owner" where access rules are enforced, and as for a session that does not exist otherwise. The read
    builds, seats and wakes nothing. An ordinary
    ended agent's session is attached as before, whether or not the runtime was composed with a durable
    session store of its own.

No field is added to a public type and nothing changes on the wire except two additive `session_id` values
(member memory events that name their session, live image records) and the kickoff records that are no
longer written. No Core path, manifest or lock file changes.

## What operators see

- No backfill: a frame stored without member attributes is shown to administrators only, whichever release
  through 0.9.14 stored it. Nothing is removed from the console log.
- People who are not administrators no longer see retire, reset, respawn and delete markers, memory harvest
  records, the system page's conflict signals, quarantined writes, taint transitions and promotions, the
  failure record of a send the console's log does not hold, a send to an identity that has no member yet,
  and image or memory records that name no session.
- A console that can identify a person and has no access configuration has no administrator and shows
  these frames to nobody. A console that can identify nobody serves its one operator as before once it has
  read who its agents are private to.
- Given up on purpose: the owner of a private side chat no longer sees its lifecycle markers, harvest
  records and some failure records; `mob_spawn_member`, `spawn_member` and `spawn_many_members` write no
  kickoff record; a console that can identify nobody shows no frame without member attributes until that
  first read has landed.

See Security, Upgrade, Changed and Known limitations under Unreleased in `meta/CHANGELOG.md`, and the access
guide's Known limitations.

## Limits

- A runtime built with `MobRuntime::from_handle` has no session service, so its Console cannot tell who an
  ended session was private to: it attaches an ended session that no agent holds for an administrator only.
  Every other caller is answered "access denied: the session has no established owner" where access rules
  are enforced, and as for a session that does not exist otherwise (documented on the constructor, noted
  under Upgrade and Changed, pinned by a row for both answers). A stored-session read on the mob handle
  would let such a runtime decide; it is not part of this change.
- The read of an ended session for the attach decision loads that one session's stored document,
  transcript included, as the attach itself does next.
- A frame stored without member attributes cannot tell two agents that held one name apart (access guide,
  Known limitations).
- A gating audit entry or pending request is decided by the agent that holds the name of its origin now;
  only a host supplies an entry's origin (CHANGELOG and access guide, Known limitations).
- The last-activity time shown for an agent name is kept per name (CHANGELOG, Known limitations).

## Rows

The row files are `src/console_frame_witness_tests.rs`, `src/console_kept_apart_tests.rs`,
`src/console_aggregator/conflict_signal_replay_tests.rs`, `src/access/controller.rs`,
`src/private_owners.rs`, `tests/console_uncaptured_frames.rs` and `tests/access_control.rs`; each commit
message names what its rows state.

author: s-m-saifullah
body:
## What

Three small privacy fixes.

**1. `RATES_ENABLED` (default `true`).** The daily exchange-rate fetch is the server's only outside call (currency codes and a date, for ledgers that pinned other currencies). With `RATES_ENABLED=false` nothing leaves the server:

- the hourly job skips the rate step (the other steps still run);
- a manual "refresh rates" answers 200 with every currency listed in `failed`, the way an outage already looks, so the API contract is unchanged;
- setting a rate by hand still works.

`buildApp` now picks its rate source from the config, and `server.ts` no longer passes one in. `.env.example` has the new line. The documents are updated in a separate docs pull request.

**2. Web sign-out forgets everything.** It removed nine named cache keys, so budgets, reports, loans, currencies, recurring rules, imports and other answers stayed in memory for up to five minutes. It now removes every cached answer except the session entry (set to nobody, so a page watching the session sees the sign-out) and clears finished changes, which hold what was typed. This is deliberately not `client.clear()`: a test with a page watching the session guards that.

**3. The hourly helper saves no rate while amounts are hidden.** "Use this total" wrote `"3.5 h at $40.00/h"` into the saved description even in privacy mode. With amounts hidden it now fills the amount and leaves the description alone. Same fix on the web and on the phone.

## Tests

- Written first (the new API and web tests failed on the old code): config, provider, tick, an integration test with a fetch spy (plus a positive control so it cannot pass vacuously), the cache wipe with every key family, a watching page, finished changes, and the helper on both clients.
- 20 deliberate mutations, all caught.
- API 773, web 1,474 and Android unit tests pass locally, with type check, Biome and Android lint. `pnpm openapi` produces no change.
- One existing web test changed on purpose: it asserted that `forgetSession` leaves unrelated cache entries alone. One call in `LogServiceViewModelTest` changed from a trailing lambda to a named argument because the function gained a parameter.

Ships at the next server tag; the phone change ships with the next Android release.

## What was wrong
- Opening a window didn't move keyboard focus, so Ctrl+V went to the desktop icon list. It pasted to the desktop (a no-op) and cleared the clipboard.
- The Recycle Bin wasn't a drop or paste target, and only custom folders could be recycled.

## What changed
- **Paste goes where you are.** Ctrl+V targets the window you last clicked:
  - Recycle Bin window: recycles the cut items.
  - Folder window: moves them into that folder.

- **Recycle anything** except the bin itself: apps, built-in folders and custom folders. Ways to do it:
  - Press **Delete** on a focused icon or a multi-selection.
  - Right-click → **Move to Recycle Bin**.
  - **Drag** onto the bin icon or into the open bin window. The drag caption reads "Move to Recycle Bin".
  - **Cut** (Ctrl+X), then **Ctrl+V** in the bin, or right-click the bin → **Paste into Recycle Bin**.
- **Restore puts it back:** each item returns to its old folder slot or desktop position. Restore all runs in reverse so the original order holds.
- The bin window lists newest first, each with an app or folder tile and "App · From X" or "N items · From X".
- Copy updates in README, the README.txt app and help text.

author: tannevaled
body:
```go
const guestZpkgDir = "/pkgx"   →   "/zpkg"
```

Our prefix is `zpkg`. The user store is already `~/.zpkg` (`bottle.Dir`, whose comment explains at length why we got out of upstream's directory), the environment variable is `ZPKG_DIR`, the binaries are `zpkgx` and `zpkgs`. **Only the guest root inside the build container still carried `pkgx`** — the mount point that the stubs, the loader symlinks and `ZPKG_DIR` must all agree on.

A build container that mounts somebody else's directory name has not been renamed, it has been relabelled. That is `bottle/zpkg.go:373`'s own sentence about what a command *prints*, and it applies here too.

## This is a product change

**Published bottles are to be rebuilt if needed** — that decision is the user's, taken 2026-11-12.

What makes it survivable is the relocation stage: `fixup/` rewrites rpaths at install time, so the guest root is a **build-time location rather than a promise to the artifact**.

## Measured rather than argued

The constant was changed first, and the suite was asked what depended on it. Exactly **two** tests went red, both because they hardcoded the old value:

| test | expected |
|---|---|
| `TestGuestPath` | `/pkgx/gnu.org/bash/v5.3/bin/bash` |
| `TestWriteLdSoConf` | four `/pkgx/...` directories |

**Nothing in the product did.**

Both now build their expectation from `guestZpkgDir`, because what they are about is that the staging root is *replaced* by the guest root, and that `ld.so.conf` names guest paths rather than staged ones — not what the root is called. Hardcoding it made them go red for a reason that says nothing about either property.

## One test pins the value, once, on purpose

If every expectation is built from the constant then nothing asserts the constant, and it can drift back with a green suite. That matters here, because the whole reason it moved is that upstream's name had been deciding it.

```go
func TestTheGuestRootIsZpkg(t *testing.T) {
	if guestZpkgDir != "/zpkg" { … }
	if strings.Contains(guestZpkgDir, "pkgx") { … }
}
```

## No x

This is the **store**, like `ZPKG_DIR` — not the `zpkgx` runtime. The same distinction #461 made between `ZpkgDir` and `ZpkgxBin`.

`go build`, `go vet` and the full suite pass; `gofmt -l` silent. The three affected tests were re-run by name through `gotest`, which refuses to call a selection a pass when part of it matched nothing.

## What is left elsewhere

This is one of five repositories carrying the path. A census counted the occurrences that are a path of **ours** rather than an address of somebody else's: zbk 153, bottle 47, packages 22, zpkgx 14, pantry-overlay 2. `pkgxdev/pantry` and `dist.pkgx.dev` are excluded and stay — renaming those would point at nothing.

author: schalappe
body:
## Summary

Release of the 27 changes merged into `develop` since `v0.2.0`. The non-merge commits include `feat` commits, so `scripts/next-version.ts` computes `0.3.0` on `main`.

```text
v0.2.0..develop
  features
    twinny-style visual pass, then thread, accent user message, and decision block (#60, #117)
    copy and insert buttons on code blocks (#84)
    add a provider from the panel, with an Ollama preset (#85)
    leave old tool results out of a full request, fold finished turns (#86)
    Plan, Ask, and Auto-edit modes (#88)
    @problems, @diff, and @selection mentions (#89)
    add selection to chat, fix with broke-code from the editor (#95)
    queue messages while a reply is in flight (#96)
    /compact and opt-in automatic compaction (#97)
    undo the file changes of a turn (#98)
    retry, continue, and edit the last turn (#114)
    History filter by title (#77), commit message from the staged diff (#78)
    extension logo (#119)
    prompt: one command covers a whole folder tree (#121)
    changed files of the latest turn, with a diff per file (#126)
  fixes
    inline code spans end at fenced blocks (#61)
    conversation temporary names checked in linear time (#62)
    consecutive user messages joined in the history (#115)
    Gemma and Qwen output on vLLM (#116)
    Open VSX publishing through trusted publishing (#127)
    eval: bench commands in a macOS sandbox (#123)
  docs and tests
    bench against any OpenAI-compatible server (#113), bench results (#124),
    behavior spec moved out of AGENTS.md (#125), README rewrite with install section (#128)

push to main (merge commit, never squash)
  release.yml
    next-version.ts                          -> 0.3.0
    lint, typecheck, test, build, package    -> broke-code-0.3.0.vsix
    tag v0.3.0 on the merged commit
    publish to Open VSX (now OIDC, #127), then the VS Marketplace, then the GitHub Release
```

## Evidence

- Each change passed CI on its own PR. CI on the `develop` head (`aae7881`) is green.
- `git merge-tree origin/main origin/develop` reports no conflict, and `main` holds no commit that `develop` lacks.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way

Once the release runs, `0.3.0` is published to Open VSX and to the Visual Studio Marketplace, and that version cannot be published again.

**Blast Radius:** users

Every installed copy updates to 0.3.0. This is the first release with Open VSX trusted publishing (#127): if the trusted publisher is not registered on Open VSX, the run fails at the Open VSX step after the tag is created, and the Marketplace and GitHub Release steps do not run.

**Revert:** `git revert` of the merge commit on `develop`, then a release `0.3.1` (a `fix` commit) with the old behavior. Versions already published stay published. For a failed Open VSX step, register the trusted publisher on Open VSX, then re-run the failed release run, which reuses the tag (a re-run uses the workflow of the merged commit, so reverting #127 would only help the next release).

author: obviyus
body:
## Problem

A Control UI (or TUI) session renders one system prompt for the user's own turns and a different one for turns that arrive from elsewhere: `sessions_send` from another session, subagent settle, cron, wakes. Every alternation re-writes the whole conversation at Anthropic cache-write price.

On a production gateway the `[prompt-cache]` detector repeatedly reported `systemPromptSuffix` changes in the **Tooling** and **Session routing** sections on `trigger=user provenance=inter_session:*` turns. A fix that merged earlier for completion wakes (run-granted `skill_library`) covered part of the Tooling difference; it did not cover this one.

## Root cause

`suggest_task` and `dismiss_task` are offered only when the turn's **requesting client** is an operator UI with `operator.admin` and the `task-suggestions` capability:

- `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-request.ts` (`supportsTaskSuggestions`) and `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-execution-phase.ts` set `taskSuggestionDeliveryMode: "gateway"` from the client connection.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` adds the two tools only in that mode.

A turn without that client (inter-session, cron, wake) does not have the tools. The cached system prompt changed in two places:

1. The deferred-tool directory in **Tooling** lost the `suggest_task` / `dismiss_task` rows.
2. **Session routing** (`src/agents/delegation-guidance.ts`) lost its `suggest_task` bullet.

## Fix

Use the mechanism that already exists for run-granted tools:

- Both tools are marked `runGranted` in `core-tool-facts.ts`, like `skill_library`. The cached directory omits them, and the turn that holds the grant lists them in its own runtime context ("Deferred tools granted for this turn"). The flag also stops "unavailable core tool" allowlist warnings for them, which is correct because they are absent on some turns by design.
- Session routing no longer renders the `suggest_task` bullet. The tool's own description already carries that guidance (records a card only; not for explicit requests to start a session).

Which turns get the tools does not change. The Codex app-server thread prompt, which renders its own delegation section, is not changed.

## Proof

**Real route, before vs after.** Isolated throwaway Gateway (scratch state, no channels), real Anthropic-compatible provider route, `cacheRetention: short`. A logging proxy recorded the provider's own `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` and the system-prompt digest. User turns were sent as an operator UI client (TUI identity: `operator.admin` + `task-suggestions`, through `chat.send`), the same gate the Control UI passes. Target session: UI turn, UI turn, then another session's `sessions_send` into it, then a UI turn.

| target-session request | before: read / write | after: read / write |
|---|---|---|
| UI turn 1 | 11,640 / 19,589 | 11,640 / 19,623 |
| UI turn 2 | 12,785 / 19,411 | 12,921 / 19,445 |
| **`sessions_send` turn** | **12,785 / 20,310** | **32,366 / 1,097** |
| UI turn 3 | 32,196 / 2,065 | 33,463 / 1,307 |

- Before: 2 system prompts in the session. The `sessions_send` turn's prompt differed exactly by the two `suggest_task`/`dismiss_task` directory rows and the Session routing bullet (diffed from captured bodies), and re-wrote 20.3k tokens.
- After: 1 system prompt for every target-session request. UI turns still list both tools in their own runtime context. The `sessions_send` turn does not.

Separate from this change, the second request of a fresh session (UI turn 2 above) re-wrote ~19k in both arms. I reproduced it with plain UI turns and no inter-session input, and found no byte difference in system, tools, parameters or message prefix. It happens once per session, on this route only. I did not investigate it further here.

**Focused tests:**
- `tool-search-directory.test.ts`: the cached directory is identical with or without each run-granted tool (`skill_library`, `suggest_task`, `dismiss_task`). The grant is listed separately.
- `delegation-guidance.test.ts`: Session routing renders the same with or without the task-suggestion grant.

## Not covered

`Skills`-only suffix changes in production also happen on ordinary user turns (8 of 15 with no provenance). They track environment changes (skill catalog edits and the remote-node availability line inside the Skills section), not the trigger. Separate follow-up.

author: codeware-agent[bot]
body:
A sign-in that still owes its TOTP code could land on "The service is temporarily unavailable" instead of verify-totp (Sentry CMS-23 and CMS-24).

The multi-tenant plugin's `TenantSelectionProvider` is nested outside our `TotpEnrolmentRedirect` and payload-totp's `TOTPProvider`, so on every admin page it reads `tenants` as the pending user before either can redirect, and on `/admin/verify-totp` it reads anyway. That read is refused, and `payload.find` throws `Forbidden`. The dashboard is the same pattern one level further in.

- `totpEnrolmentPlugin` swaps the plugin's provider entry for `PendingSafeTenantSelectionProvider`, which renders the plugin's provider with no user while `isSecondFactorPending(user)`, so it reads no tenants. Otherwise it passes everything through. The tenants access stays a hard refusal.
- `AdminDashboardView` renders nothing for a pending session, before any read.
- Audited: `AdminNavWrapper` (counts and tenant icons already return null or catch), `AfterLogin` (reads with `overrideAccess`), the setup view and its issuer lookup (catches). None needed a change.

author: jitsusama
body:
### 💡 TL;DR

A line Joel says to The Void from Agents now shows as one quiet card from The Void saying sent, replaced in place by the reply. The card never takes focus and is held under Quiet like any notice.

### 🧩 Problem

When Joel talks to The Void from Agents, the launcher closes and nothing says the line went anywhere or what came back. He has to reopen Agents and find The Void's row to read the reply, which is the spammy, hard-to-follow feel his brief for agents calls out. VKCF3Z ruled the answer is a notice rather than a launcher held open: one card, quiet, that never takes focus and that the reply replaces.

### 🔧 Solution

When Return gives a line to the session standing at Agents' top, the shell sends one low-urgency card from The Void: his line, muted, with a foot reading sent and the time. When that talk's reply comes, the same card is replaced in place, its foot reading answered, the reply cut at whole words with a pointer to the rest in the talk. A card put away is sent once anew; an answered card that closed is never sent again. Only his own line's reply makes a card, and only Agents' talk act sends one.

- Notices daemon: a hint `x-from` names the sender, keeping its mark and hue, and `x-said` carries a key the daemon words, put before the time on the side and the card's foot.
- Shell: `Told.qml` sends through `notify-send` as Arrivals does, its logic in `Told.js`, and logs how long the card took to reach the notices.

The agents daemon takes the sending next, once it speaks to the bus. The card's default action opens Agents, not the talk itself.

### 🔬 Validation

- Red then green: notices-holds-what-the-bus-says (64 tests), a-live-notice-asks-the-daemon, and the new the-void-answers-on-one-card, each failing first at a test-only commit.
- cc4 gate at 23e622d2 passed: changed-checks, qmllint, formatting, words, verbs and the agents niri check.
- vm-desktop-shows-then-rests, starts-clean and takes-calls whole at the head.
- No 50 ms pair: no Return-to-card time existed before, as there was no card; after the switch the journal's told line gives it in ms. On-screen time isn't measured.

author: tanishqbaweja
body:
## Problem
`ast_grep_replace` makes an edit for every match that `root.findAll(pattern)` returns and applies the edits to the file text from the end of the file. `findAll()` also returns the matches inside another match. When one match contains another, the second edit is applied to code that the first one already replaced, and a replacement of a different length corrupts the file. #5050 listed this under "Not changed" as a follow-up.

Repro on dev (9fd477ed7): Windows 11, Node 24.20.0, @ast-grep/napi 0.31.1 (the version package-lock.json installs). The `bridge/mcp-server.cjs` that `npm run build` makes on dev runs over stdio with an isolated home and no `CLAUDE*`/`OMC_*` variables, and `tools/call ast_grep_replace` gets `language: "typescript"`, `dryRun: false` and a folder with one file:

- `$X + $Y` -> `add($X, $Y)`: `const s = a + b + c;` becomes `const s = add(a, b) + b, c);`. `a + b + c` is `(a + b) + c`, so both sums match, and both start at `a`.
- `foo($A)` -> `barbaz($A)`: `foo(foo(1));` becomes `barbaz(foo(1))1));`
- `foo($A)` -> `f($A)`: `foo(foo(foo(1)));` becomes `f(foo(foo(1)))`, without the `;` and the line break.
- `$X` -> `w($X)` on `foo(1)` (no `;`, no line break), where the program, the statement and the call have the same range: `w(foo)oo(1))1))1))1))1))`, with "Found 6 replacement(s)".

A dry run of `foo($A)` -> `barbaz($A)` on `foo(foo(1)); foo(2);` reports "Found 3 replacement(s) in 1 file(s)", lists `- foo(1)` / `+ barbaz(1)` for the inner call, and shows `- foo(barbaz(` as the code that the outer call replaces. A replacement of the same length can leave the file right, but the count still includes the inner match: `console.log($$$ARGS)` -> `logger.info($$$ARGS)` on `console.log(console.log(1), 2);` writes `logger.info(console.log(1), 2);` and reports 2 replacements.

## Fix
`src/tools/ast-tools.ts`, in the `ast_grep_replace` handler: the edits of a file are sorted by start, and an edit that starts inside an edit already kept is dropped. The kept edits are applied from the end of the file, as before.
- The outer match is replaced, and the matches inside it are left as written. `findAll()` lists an outer match before the matches inside it and the sort is stable, so the outer match is kept also when both start at the same place (`a + b` in `a + b + c`). Of matches with the same range, the first is kept.
- Separate matches, and adjacent ones (one ends where the next starts), are all still replaced.
- The count ("Found N replacement(s)") and the change list show only the applied edits, in a dry run too, and the code after `-` is the matched code.
- Each file is checked on its own.

`ast-grep run -p <pattern> -r <replacement> -U` (@ast-grep/cli 0.31.1, the same version as @ast-grep/napi) also replaces only the outer match. For all 13 inputs that the end-to-end check below writes, the files this branch writes are the same as the CLI's; with dev, 9 of them differ.

## Tests
`src/__tests__/tools/ast-tools.test.ts` gets four tests next to #5050's, with its `replaceInFile` helper (the real handler with @ast-grep/napi 0.31.1 on a temp folder):
- `$X + $Y` -> `add($X, $Y)` on `const s = a + b + c;` gives `const s = add(a + b, c);`
- `foo($A)` -> `barbaz($A)` on `foo(foo(1));` gives `barbaz(foo(1));`
- separate and adjacent matches on one line are both replaced: `foo(1); foo(2);` gives `barbaz(1); barbaz(2);`, and `foo($A);` -> `bar($A);` on `foo(1);foo(2);` gives `bar(1);bar(2);`
- a dry run on `foo(foo(1)); foo(2);` reports "Found 2 replacement(s) in 1 file(s)", shows `- foo(foo(1))` / `+ barbaz(foo(1))` and `- foo(2)` / `+ barbaz(2)` and nothing for the inner call, and leaves the file unchanged

Results (`npx vitest run <files> --testTimeout 120000`):
- `src/__tests__/tools/ast-tools.test.ts`: 22 passed. With dev's `ast-tools.ts`, 3 of the 4 new tests fail; the one for separate and adjacent matches passes on dev too.
- All of `src/__tests__/tools/`, plus `ast-tools-path-restriction`, `omc-tools-contract`, both `omc-tools-server.test.ts` files, `omc-tools-server-interop`, `standalone-server` and `src/mcp/__tests__/standalone-listtools.test.ts` (11 files): 302 passed and 1 failed. With dev's `ast-tools.ts`, 299 passed and 4 failed. Compared by test id, the only differences are the three new tests that fail on dev. The other failure is the same on both: trace-tools "should auto-detect latest session from multiple replay files" writes two files 50 ms apart and expects the second to be newer, but this exFAT drive records modification times in 2-second steps.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint` (0 errors and 21 warnings, the same as on dev; none in the changed files), `npm run build`: pass
- `npm run generate:inventory:verify`: passes without regenerating
- The full `npm run test:run` was not run.

End to end: the setup of the repro, with the `bridge/mcp-server.cjs` that `npm run build` makes on dev and on this branch. ast-grep's CLI ran on a copy of the same files. The number in brackets is the "Found N replacement(s)" count; every file ends with a line break except `foo(1)`.

| pattern -> replacement | file | dev | this branch (the same as the CLI) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$X + $Y` -> `add($X, $Y)` | `const s = a + b + c;` | `const s = add(a, b) + b, c);` (2) | `const s = add(a + b, c);` (1) |
| `$X + $Y` -> `add($X, $Y)` | `const s = a + b + c + d;` | `const s = add(a, b) + b, c) + c, d);` (3) | `const s = add(a + b + c, d);` (1) |
| `$X + $Y` -> `add($X, $Y)` | `const s = a + (b + c);` | `const s = add(a, (b + c)) c));` (2) | `const s = add(a, (b + c));` (1) |
| `$X + $Y` -> `add($X, $Y)` | `f(a + b, c + d);` | `f(add(a, b), add(c, d));` (2) | the same (2) |
| `foo($A)` -> `barbaz($A)` | `foo(foo(1));` | `barbaz(foo(1))1));` (2) | `barbaz(foo(1));` (1) |
| `foo($A)` -> `barbaz($A)` | `foo(foo(1)); foo(2);` | `barbaz(foo(1))1)); barbaz(2);` (3) | `barbaz(foo(1)); barbaz(2);` (2) |
| `foo($A)` -> `barbaz($A)` | `foo(1); foo(2);` | `barbaz(1); barbaz(2);` (2) | the same (2) |
| `foo($A)` -> `barbaz($A)` | two files: `const x = foo(foo(1));` and `foo(2); foo(foo(3));` | `const x = barbaz(foo(1))1));` and `barbaz(2); barbaz(foo(3))3));` (5 in 2 files) | `const x = barbaz(foo(1));` and `barbaz(2); barbaz(foo(3));` (3 in 2 files) |
| `foo($A)` -> `f($A)` | `foo(foo(foo(1)));` | `f(foo(foo(1)))` (3) | `f(foo(foo(1)));` (1) |
| `outer($A)` -> `wrap($A)` | `outer(function () {` / `  outer(1);` / `});` | `wrap(function () {` / `  outer(1);` / `})` (2) | `wrap(function () {` / `  outer(1);` / `});` (1) |
| `foo($A);` -> `bar($A);` | `foo(1);foo(2);` | `bar(1);bar(2);` (2) | the same (2) |
| `console.log($$$ARGS)` -> `logger.info($$$ARGS)` | `console.log(console.log(1), 2);` | `logger.info(console.log(1), 2);` (2) | the same (1) |
| `$X` -> `w($X)` | `foo(1)` | `w(foo)oo(1))1))1))1))1))` (6) | `w(foo(1))` (1) |

The dry run on `foo(foo(1)); foo(2);` reports 3 replacements on dev, as in the repro. This branch reports 2, lists `- foo(2)` / `+ barbaz(2)` and `- foo(foo(1))` / `+ barbaz(foo(1))`, and leaves the file unchanged.

Also with this branch (the handler from source, run through tsx): running `foo($A)` -> `barbaz($A)` again on `barbaz(foo(1));` gives `barbaz(barbaz(1));`, as a second CLI run does. In Python files, `foo(foo(1))` and `s = a + b + c` become `barbaz(foo(1))` and `s = add(a + b, c)`, the same as with the CLI.

## Not changed
- A match inside a replaced match is left as written, as with ast-grep's CLI; running the tool again replaces it. The report does not mention the matches it leaves out.
- The replacement text of each match, including the `$$$` substitution from #5050, is unchanged. The edits are still applied from the end of the file, and the change list still shows a file's last change first.
- `ast_grep_search` is unchanged.
- Tested with TypeScript and Python files only; the new step compares only the offsets of the matches.

author: stavroskasidis
body:
## What and why

On macOS, Check Environment's **Install .NET** always ran `dotnet-install.sh` into `~/.dotnet`. The IDE then put that folder first on its own `PATH` and reported the new SDK. A terminal whose `dotnet` is Microsoft's `.pkg` install (`/usr/local/share/dotnet`) never saw it: `/etc/paths.d/dotnet` and `path_helper` put that folder first in every shell. So `dotnet --list-sdks` showed no 11.0 while Check Environment showed 11.0.100.

Install .NET now detects the `dotnet` on the login shell's `PATH` and offers every way to install it on the machine. The recommended way installs where that `dotnet` is, and it's already selected.

`ShellHost` records that `PATH` before `UseUserDotnet` puts a .NET root first. Each option's `dotnet` folder is compared with the terminal's real one, its links resolved.

- **macOS**: Microsoft's `.pkg` into `/usr/local/share/dotnet` (`curl`, then `sudo installer` in the integrated terminal), `dotnet-install` into `~/.dotnet` (or into the terminal's own root when that is in the home folder), or the download page. The `.pkg` is recommended unless the terminal's `dotnet` is in the home folder.
  - The `.pkg` comes from `aka.ms/dotnet/<channel>/[preview/]dotnet-sdk-osx-<arch>.pkg`, or the exact version from `builds.dotnet.microsoft.com` when `global.json` pins one.
- **Linux**: the distribution's `dotnet-sdk-X.Y` when apt, dnf or zypper has it. It is asked from local metadata only (`apt-cache policy`, `dnf -C info`, `zypper --no-refresh info`), and never offered for a pinned version. Also the `dotnet-sdk` snap's channel when the terminal's `dotnet` is that snap, `dotnet-install` into `~/.dotnet`, and the download page.
  - The package is recommended when the terminal's `dotnet` is a package's, or there's none. Otherwise `~/.dotnet` is recommended: nothing installs into a package manager's folder.
- **Windows**: winget, or the download page.

What changes for the user:

- **Warnings:** an option whose SDK the terminal's `dotnet` won't see says so.
- **The dialog:** the dialog gains a radio-list mode (`DialogRequest.Alternatives`), with each option's description, exact command and note. The setup wizard's .NET rows open the same dialog.
- **Terminal installs are awaited:** the command's exit code is passed through (`exit $status` after the "press Enter" prompt). A failure is reported. On success the IDE takes the new root (`AddsToPath`), checks again and restarts the hosts that failed, as it does after installs it runs itself.

Docs:

- **User guide:** "How it installs" in `getting-started.md` is rewritten. `troubleshooting.md` gets a row for "Check Environment shows an SDK that `dotnet --list-sdks` doesn't".
- **Website:** a line on the Features page.
- **Smoke test:** a gallery shot of the dialog (`dialog-alternatives`).

## How it was tested

- `DotnetInstallOptionsTests` (new, 14 tests) covers the options and the recommended one on each OS:
  - the macOS `.pkg` with a terminal `dotnet` from the `.pkg`, from the home folder, from Homebrew, or none;
  - pinned and preview `.pkg` URLs, and the x64 IDE on Apple silicon;
  - Linux with the distribution's `dotnet`, a `dotnet` in the home folder, or the snap;
  - winget's note on Windows;
  - the package managers' answers parsed.
- `HostRuntimeSetupTests` is updated for the new recommendation.
- `EnvironmentShellTests` has three new headless UI tests:
  - the picker lists the three macOS options, the recommended one selected and the notes shown; Cancel runs nothing, and the option picked is what runs;
  - the dialog renders radio buttons whose commands wrap inside the frame;
  - a terminal install is awaited, and its exit code decides (non-Windows).
- `FirstRunSetupTests`: the setup wizard's .NET row opens the dialog (Cancel runs nothing, the yes runs the way picked). The inline confirmation is tested on a missing git row.
- **Linux (this container)**:
  - `Codalus.Workbench.Tests`: 1142 passed, 18 skipped for missing prerequisites (Docker and the like).
  - `Codalus.Website.Tests`: all 19 passed.
  - `Codalus.Shell.Tests`: 1088 passed and 15 skipped for missing prerequisites. Two failed:
    - `FirstRunSetupTests` still expected the inline confirmation on the .NET row; it is fixed in the second commit, and all 9 tests of its class pass.
    - `LanguageTests.A_declarative_plugin_adds_a_language…` needs the `TodoLanguage` sample built. The solution build does that, but this run only built test projects. With the sample built, it passes.
- **macOS and Windows: not validated.** No Remote Control session for the Mac or Windows was reachable. On the Mac, Install .NET should:
  - pick the `.pkg`;
  - after `sudo installer`, let a terminal's `dotnet --list-sdks` list the new SDK;
  - have Check Environment show `/usr/local/share/dotnet/dotnet`.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests cover the change, and `dotnet test --solution Codalus.slnx` passes locally (new tests added; the test projects ran separately, as above; CI runs the solution)
- [x] No new warnings (builds treat warnings as errors); the shell still publishes with Native AOT (compiled bindings only, no reflection)
- [x] New dependencies are MIT-compatible and recorded in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (none added)
- [x] Docs updated (user guide, website Features page)
- [x] No performance budget regressions
- [ ] Commits are signed off (`git commit -s`, DCO)

author: datazuul
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"datazuul"} -->
_Requested by **Ralf** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VajHxoMpjg2u43YzaGY7La?thread=cmsg_01VajHxoMpjg2u43YzaGY7La3RPuZVsDfUtuBiXTL2sMQx)_

## Why

After #120 Ralf asked to give all amadeOS Java programs and games the same memory settings. Java's defaults reserve a quarter of the RAM for each program and keep what they once used. A parallel thread also needs `-Djdk.lang.Process.launchMechanism=FORK` in every launcher, so that a Java upgrade does not break running programs ("Spawn helper ran into version mismatch"). Both now live in one shared place.

## What

- **`/etc/amadeos/java/app.options`** and **`game.options`**: Java argument files (one option per line, `#` comments), shipped by **amadeos-session** as conffiles.
  - app: `-XX:+UseSerialGC -Xmx256m -XX:MinHeapFreeRatio=10 -XX:MaxHeapFreeRatio=30 -Djdk.lang.Process.launchMechanism=FORK`
  - game: `-XX:+UseG1GC -Xmx512m -XX:G1PeriodicGCInterval=10000 -XX:MinHeapFreeRatio=10 -XX:MaxHeapFreeRatio=30 -Djdk.lang.Process.launchMechanism=FORK`
- Every launcher the shared build generates (including amadeos-dm and amadeos-session's worker) now reads:
  ```sh
  OPTIONS=/etc/amadeos/java/app.options
  [ -r "$OPTIONS" ] || OPTIONS=/dev/null
  exec /usr/bin/java "@$OPTIONS" <module options> -jar ...
  ```
  A module's own options come after the file and win (e.g. a larger `-Xmx`). Without the file (a plain Debian system without amadeos-session), Java runs with its defaults.
- Software's own heap options from #120 move into the shared file.

The app and game repos follow with one PR each. Each one switches its launcher the same way. Programs that handle big images or documents get their own `-Xmx`, and so do Cruise, Pinball and Templar.

## Measured (startup, Xvfb, JDK 25, `-XX:MaxRAM=8g`)

The system modules (wm, panels, settings, task manager, disks, log viewer, widgets, sysinfo, print, software) keep 3–45 MB of live heap after a full GC, so 256 MB is plenty. `java @app.options -Xmx1g` gives a 1 GB heap (a later option wins), and `#` comment lines in the files work.

---

author: imweeriyasinghe
body:
Fixes two defects found during DEV acceptance. DijiAtWork only: no Platform Core, shell or migration changes. **Merging deploys nothing.**

## 1. Overdue attendance counted as worked hours
A session open for 60 hours added 24-hour days to history, reports and exports.

**Rule:** a session longer than the missed check-out threshold (default 12 hours) is **unverified**.
- Its time is kept separately as `provisional_seconds` and labelled Unverified. It is never counted in confirmed gross, break or net totals, reports or export hours.
- An open session becomes unverified when it passes the threshold. A completed one stays unverified, even after a late check-out, until Management approves a correction.
- A genuine long session is confirmed by an unchanged correction, which is allowed only in that case.
- Sessions within the threshold, including cross-midnight ones, are unchanged.
- No session, timestamp or audit record is modified.

**Exports:** a new `Unverified hours (not included)` column, plus an `Unverified` flag on the sessions export.

## 2. Missed check-out alert never delivered
`atwork-api` gave Platform Core 3 seconds; a cold start took longer, so every attempt timed out.
- Delivery now waits 30 seconds.
- A run stops after 3 consecutive failures, so it stays within the job timeout.

author: h-east
body:
vim-patch:9.2.1336: sort()/uniq() compare function can free list items still in use

Problem:  sort() and uniq() build an array of pointers into the list
          being sorted and then call the user-supplied compare function
          for each comparison.  The list itself is not protected, so the
          compare function can call remove(), insert() or extend() on
          the same list.  do_sort() and do_uniq() then read and relink
          already freed list items, a use-after-free confirmed with
          valgrind.
Solution: Lock the list with VAR_FIXED for the duration of do_sort() and
          do_uniq(), the same way reduce() already protects the list
          while its callback runs, and restore the previous lock
          afterwards (Yegappan Lakshmanan).

author: mrc4tt
body:
## Why

A server rejected a good `gamedata.json` (build 14197, all 38 signatures resolving) for good after two early deaths, and the log could not say why:

```
The server died early 2 starts in a row after a gamedata update. Rolled back: .../gamedata.json.
Gamedata update skipped: this gamedata.json (sha256 810f075a…) was rolled back after the server died early with it twice
```

The guard cannot see why a start died, so it now errs towards letting updates through and says what it knows.

## What

- **Stop signals are not deaths.** SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP while an update is pending writes `gamedata/update.stopped` (async-signal-safe open/write/close, handler installed after the CLR's and chaining to it); the next start logs `stopped (SIGHUP) … not counted as a crash` and keeps the update.
- **Suspect keys.** On rollback each pending file is diffed against its backup (`plugin_gamedata::DiffEntries`); only keys whose own-platform signatures/offsets (or platform-neutral fields, or added keys) changed count. They are logged per file. A file with none is kept and not rejected (`Outcome::Innocent`: "Gamedata is not the cause … look at plugins or the map").
- **Rejections expire.** 1 h, then 6 h, then 24 h per repeat of the same sha256 (`strikes`, `until` in `update.rejected`). A rejected file that later survives a start is unrejected; entries are forgotten 7 days after expiry and an empty `update.rejected` is deleted. Entries written before this get one hour from first read.
- **How far the dead start got.** The confirm timer writes uptime into `update.pending` every 10 s and the map at map start; rollback/retry logs say `after about 10s on de_dust2`.
- **`GamedataCrashGuard`** (default `true`, native + managed config + `core.example.json`): `false` turns the guard off and clears its files.

## Verified

- `css_unit_tests`: all 84 cases pass (7 new guard cases: suspects, stop marker, innocent, expiry/backoff, unreject, legacy entries, disable).
- `cs2-smoke-test --local`: 214 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped; Windows DLL builds.
- By hand on the smoke server:
  - SIGTERM: CS2 unloads cleanly (pending confirmed, exit in 2 s), so a plain panel stop was never the problem.
  - SIGHUP with a pending update: marker written, next start "not counted as a crash".
  - 2× SIGKILL, unchanged file: kept, "Gamedata is not the cause".
  - 2× SIGKILL, changed signature: rolled back, `1 key(s) changed … UTIL_ClientPrintAll (signatures.linux)`, "tried again in 1h".
