author: nschatz
body:
## What

The FHIR adapter now reads a `Device`'s identifiers and serial numbers as Safe Harbor category (M), so Safe Harbor and the Limited Data Set both remove them, each with a `DEID_CATEGORY_REMOVED` row (category `DEVICE`, transform `redact`) at its locus that carries no value.

- `src/fhir/locus-map.ts`: `FHIR_DEVICE_IDENTIFIER_ELEMENTS` (internal), an explicit list of R4 element paths: `Device.serialNumber`, `Device.lotNumber`, `Device.distinctIdentifier`, `Device.udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier`, `Device.udiCarrier.carrierHRF`, `Device.udiCarrier.carrierAIDC`. Also `FHIR_DEVICE_IDENTIFIER_PATH` (`Device.identifier`) and `FHIR_DEVICE_CATEGORY`.
- `src/fhir/extract.ts`: a primitive at one of those paths becomes an `identifier` locus of category (M), written back in place (`set-primitive`), so the policy decides it. A value of any other shape is blocked whole. This check runs before the embedded-content rule, so `keepEmbeddedContent: ["base64-binary"]` no longer keeps a `carrierAIDC`. On a `Device`, `identifier` now defaults to category (M) instead of MRN. The SSN system still routes to SSN.
- The paths are matched by element path, not by name, so `Medication.batch.lotNumber` is not touched. The rule reaches a `Device` on its own, contained in another resource, or in a `Bundle` entry.
- Kept, because these describe the kind of device and not the one device: `deviceName`, `modelNumber`, `partNumber`, `type`, `status`, `manufacturer`, and the UDI's `issuer`, `jurisdiction` and `entryType`.
- Docs: the FHIR guide (a table row and a new section, "Device identifiers and serial numbers", with a runnable example), `limitations.md`, `what-the-caller-still-owns.md`, the `fhir` module TSDoc and the regenerated API page. The `embedded-content.ts` TSDoc no longer lists `carrierAIDC` under `base64-binary`.
- Changesets: a new patch changeset states each change to the default output. The pending `fhir-embedded-content` changeset ships in the same release, so it no longer lists `carrierAIDC` among the elements `base64-binary` keeps.

## Why

A serial number on a FHIR `Device` came through Safe Harbor unchanged. Safe Harbor lists device identifiers and serial numbers as category (M), and the Limited Data Set rule lists them among the direct identifiers it removes.

On main (04e8ee8), we ran the probe `{"resourceType":"Device","serialNumber":"ZZLEAK"}` through `deidentifyFhirJson` under `SAFE_HARBOR_PROFILE` and `LIMITED_DATA_SET_PROFILE`. Both returned it unchanged with an empty manifest, and the only record was `{"locus":"Device.serialNumber","code":"DEID_POSITION_UNEXAMINED"}` in `unexaminedResiduals`. A second probe, with every field filled in, gave this on main:

| Position | On main, both presets | After this change, both presets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `serialNumber`, `lotNumber`, `distinctIdentifier`, `udiCarrier.deviceIdentifier`, `udiCarrier.carrierHRF` | kept verbatim, no row, only in `unexaminedResiduals` | removed, category (M) row |
| `udiCarrier.carrierAIDC` | removed as embedded content, category (R); kept when the caller names `base64-binary` | removed, category (M) row, whatever kind is kept |
| `identifier.value` | Safe Harbor: removed as MRN (H). Limited Data Set: keyed surrogate as MRN | removed, category (M) row, under both |

## Proof

Locally, in the worktree:

- `harness gate deid --fast` passed all 18 checks: install, typecheck, lint, format, phi-scan, build, attw, smoke, examples, test-selection, no-emdash, no-internal-refs, readme, claude-card, catalog, process, docs-content, docs-reference.
- `harness gate deid --run "pnpm exec vitest run test/fhir test/corpus test/leak-property/fhir.test.ts test/leak-property/found.test.ts test/codes.test.ts test/deidentify.test.ts test/enumeration-closure.test.ts test/docs-content.test.ts --maxWorkers=2"`: 34 files, 1690 tests, all passed.

Red first. We stashed `src/` back to the base, kept the new tests, and ran them:

- `test/fhir/device-identifiers.test.ts`: 24 of 29 failed. Every field failed under both presets, and so did the probe case, the all-fields case, the Limited Data Set identifier case, the contained and `Bundle` case, the `carrierAIDC`-with-keep case, the `_serialNumber` sibling case, the custom-policy case and the locus-shape case. The 5 that passed are guards that should already pass: a Patient identifier is still MRN, an SSN system on a Device is still SSN, `Medication.batch.lotNumber` is untouched, a misfit `carrierAIDC` is blocked, and an object at `serialNumber` is blocked. After the change: 29 of 29 pass. The two residual cases added later, for `DeviceDefinition` and `Observation.device.identifier`, record behavior that has not changed.
- `test/leak-property/fhir.test.ts`: 10 of 270 failed. Both generated properties failed (`fhir` and `fhir-animal`), and so did 8 of the 9 new per-spot cases. The ninth, `identifier[0].value`, passed on the base because Safe Harbor already removed it as MRN. With the change, all pass.
- `test/corpus/leak-corpus.test.ts`: 4 of 255 failed. These were the new `fhir-device-identifiers` and `fhir-device-identifiers-keyed` cases: the no-leak check, plus the tamper check, which fails when the sentinels are still in the output. With the change, all pass.

The leak property has a new arm, `devices`, in both generated properties. It places a sentinel at each of the following on a contained `Device`, and on the resource itself when the generated type is `Device`: `serialNumber`, `lotNumber`, `distinctIdentifier`, `udiCarrier[0].deviceIdentifier`, `carrierHRF`, `carrierAIDC` (as base64), `identifier[0].value`, and a second `udiCarrier`. A stricter rule applies there: the sentinel must be gone from both the output and the manifest. A fixed per-spot block also runs each spot on four resource types, alone and in a `Bundle`, three ways: default, `keepPatientAnimal`, and every embedded-content kind kept.

The leak corpus adds a Device case under each preset. The survivors are the device name, the model number, the type code, `entryType` and the clinical values.

CI on this pull request runs the full suite, coverage, the changed-line mutation job and the perf gates. This change measures nothing, so the body gives no numbers.

CI took two fixes before going green:

- First head (66bd28e, run 43295432898): `ci / coverage-ratchet` failed in `pnpm test:coverage`, which requires 100%. The cause was the non-primitive branch of the device rule's type guard. It cannot be reached, because a structure or a list at one of these elements is blocked before the walk (`findUnknownKeys`). The second commit marks it `v8 ignore if` and disables `ConditionalExpression` and `BlockStatement` mutation, following the existing `replaceElementId` guard. It also adds tests showing an object, a list and a list of objects at `serialNumber`, `carrierAIDC` and `deviceIdentifier` all blocked whole with no category.
- Second head (8fbf9cc, run 43296158964): coverage passed. `ci / mutation` found 1 surviving mutant in changed code: `src/fhir/extract.ts:846 CallExpression (NoCoverage)`, the `blockNode` call inside that same guard. The third commit adds `CallExpression` to the guard's disable.
- Final head (db3dfc2, run 43298837377): every check is green, required or not. `harness wait deid#157 --all` exited 0, and `ci / mutation` reports 0 surviving mutants in changed code.

Exceptions in changed code, as the mutation job lists them on the final head:

- `src/fhir/extract.ts:843-846`: the device rule's type guard. `v8 ignore if`, plus `ConditionalExpression`, `BlockStatement` and `CallExpression` disabled for mutation. The reason is the one given above: the walk never reaches this guard with anything but a primitive.
- `src/fhir/locus-map.ts:472-478` and `:488`: static mutants in the `FHIR_DEVICE_IDENTIFIER_ELEMENTS` set and the `FHIR_DEVICE_IDENTIFIER_PATH` constant, skipped by `ignoreStatic`. The tests still check each path: every listed element is removed under both presets, `Device.identifier`

author: jeisenback
mkofler96
body:
## Summary

Since #554 the viewport renders on demand, so world matrices only refresh when a frame renders. A click that lands before the frame after a camera move, or after a new marker appears, raycast from the old camera pose and picked nothing. Two click-to-pick e2e tests failed at random in CI because of it. R3F's event `compute` now brings the matrices up to date before each raycast.

```diff
 <Canvas
   frameloop="demand"
+  events={pickingEvents}
```

```diff
 // pickingEvents.ts — wraps R3F's default pointer events
 compute(event, state, previous) {
+  state.scene.updateMatrixWorld();
+  state.camera.updateMatrixWorld();
   compute(event, state, previous);   // R3F default: pointer → raycaster.setFromCamera
 }
```

This PR also unblocks CI. Clippy 1.100, the current stable that CI installs, fails `develop` and every PR on two `needless_range_loop` lints in `amg.rs`. The second commit fixes those loops (details below).

Fixes KOF-344

## Evidence

The CI failures it explains:

* `split-geometry.spec.ts` › "a split that lands during a BC pick ends the pick session" on PR #556: `picked: 0`, expected 1.
* `couplings.spec.ts` › "a reference point is picked by clicking its marker clear of the model" on `develop` @ 5ff732f ([run 43163044389](https://github.com/mkofler96/KoFEM/actions/runs/43163044389)): `selectedFace` undefined.

Both depend on timing and did not reproduce locally, so I added a deterministic test. `viewport-picking.spec.ts` turns the camera with `lookFrom` and dispatches the click in the same task, so no frame can render in between.

**Before** (`develop` @ 796adcc plus the new test, without `pickingEvents`):

```text
bunx playwright test tests/viewport-picking.spec.ts
  1) viewport-picking.spec.ts:100:1 › a click right after a camera turn picks the face under the cursor
    Error: the click picked no face
    Received: null
  1 failed
```

**After** (this branch):

```text
bunx playwright test tests/viewport-picking.spec.ts tests/couplings.spec.ts tests/split-geometry.spec.ts
  16 passed (57.3s)
bunx playwright test            # full suite
  286 passed (8.5m)
```

**Clippy.** On `develop` @ 796adcc ([run 43292531264](https://github.com/mkofler96/KoFEM/actions/runs/43292531264)), "Rust (native)" fails at the Clippy step, and every job after it is skipped:

```text
cargo +1.100 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
error: the loop variable `row` is used to index `here.scratch`   --> crates/kofem-fem/src/amg.rs:966
error: the loop variable `row` is used to index `here.solution`  --> crates/kofem-fem/src/amg.rs:1009
```

On this branch, clippy is clean on both 1.100 and 1.97, and `cargo test --workspace` passes all 87 tests.

Also run: `bun run typecheck && bun run lint && bun run format:check` — pass.

There are no screenshots because nothing looks different: the change is only which face a click picks.

## Key Changes

- **web `viewport/pickingEvents.ts`** (new): R3F's pointer events with a `compute` that updates scene and camera world matrices before raycasting.
- **web `viewport/Viewport.tsx`**: the canvas uses `events={pickingEvents}`.
- **web `viewport/ViewportTestHooks.tsx`**: `project()` projects with an updated clone of the camera instead of updating the live camera. The old side effect hid this bug in tests.
- **web tests**:
  - New `viewport-picking.spec.ts`.
  - `couplings.spec.ts` drops its double-`requestAnimationFrame` wait. It never guaranteed a rendered frame under `frameloop="demand"`.
- **crates/kofem-fem `amg.rs`**: the V-cycle's restriction and prolongation loops iterate the level's work vectors instead of `0..prolongator.row_count()`. It is the same loop, because P has one row per unknown of its level.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** small

Every viewport pointer event (click, hover, pointer move) now walks the scene graph to update matrices before raycasting. The scene holds few objects, so the cost is small. Matrices only change where they were stale, so rendering itself is unchanged. This touches every face, node, geometry and reference-point pick, and the full e2e suite covers them. The `amg.rs` change only rewrites two loops; the Rust tests cover the V-cycle.

## Checklist

- [x] **No silent fallbacks** — `pickingEvents` throws if R3F's events have no `compute` to wrap.
- [x] Every input accepted by the UI or an API is actually consumed downstream

author: lance0
body:
Hosted CI picked up Rust stable 1.100.0, which turned main red in three jobs.

## Cargo artifact layout

Cargo 1.100 no longer places test and bench executables in `target/<profile>/deps/`. They now live at `target/<profile>/build/<pkg>/<hash>/out/<name>-<hash>`. Final artifacts such as `target/debug/rustbgpd` stay where they were.

- `tools/gobgp-bridge/tests/daemon.rs` located the daemon at `current_exe()/../../rustbgpd`. That path now resolves inside `build/`, so the test failed in `core tests (shard 2)`. The daemon belongs to another package, so `CARGO_BIN_EXE_rustbgpd` is not available here. The test now searches upward from its own executable for the nearest `rustbgpd` file, which works with both layouts and with `--target <triple>`.
- `bench/tests/test-vpn-query-receipt.sh` searched `target/release/deps` for the `vpn_query_timing` bench, which failed `scale / receipt checks`. It now gets the executable path from `cargo bench --no-run --message-format=json-render-diagnostics`.
- `bench/run-vpn-query-campaign.sh` and `bench/compare-route-paging.sh` searched the same directory (neither runs in CI). Both now read the path from Cargo's JSON output. Each requires exactly one matching executable, as before.

## New clippy 1.100 diagnostics

- `needless_bool` fired in `allocation_permitted` in `crates/rib/src/manager/update_groups/{admitted_recovery,recovery_provenance}.rs`. The `#[cfg(test)] if … { return false; } true` tail is now split into a test version and a non-test version. Behavior is unchanged.
- `needless_range_loop` fired in `bench/scale/reloadstall/src/main.rs` (2 sites), `bench/scale/reloadstall/src/recovery_mass_dirty.rs` (1 test) and `tests/config_persistence_lifecycle.rs` (1 site). These now iterate slices. The slices keep the original out-of-range panic instead of truncating silently.

## Consumers audited

| Consumer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/gobgp-bridge/tests/daemon.rs` (sibling path from `current_exe`) | fixed |
| `bench/tests/test-vpn-query-receipt.sh` (`find target/release/deps`) | fixed |
| `bench/run-vpn-query-campaign.sh` (`find $target_dir/release/deps`) | fixed |
| `bench/compare-route-paging.sh` (`find $target_dir/release/deps`) | fixed |
| other `current_exe()` callers (api, cli, evpn-linux netns, rib fault corpus, transport, `src/`, root `tests/`, rrtransport, mcp) | unaffected: they re-execute or report the test binary itself |
| `scripts/check_ci_test_shards.py` and its test | unaffected: they only test that `executable` is present; the `/deps/` path in the fixture is cosmetic |
| `docs/perf/event-history-host-fence.sh` and its test fixture | unaffected: matches on `comm`, not on the path |
| `tests/birdwatcher_adapter_smoke.rs`, `docs/perf/run-lean-daemon-build-flavors.sh` | unaffected: they read `out_dir` and `executable` from Cargo JSON |
| `tests/support/mod.rs` `rbgp_binary()` (parent of `CARGO_BIN_EXE_rustbgpd`) | unaffected: Cargo still reports the final artifact, and hosted shard 1 passed on 1.100 |
| workflows, justfile, Dockerfile, release packaging, fuzz scripts | unaffected: they use only final artifacts (`target/<profile>/<bin>`, `target/<triple>/release/<bin>`, `target/ci/<bin>`) |

## Validation

| Check | 1.99.1 | 1.100.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cargo clippy --locked -p rustbgpd-rib --all-targets -- -D warnings` | pass | pass |
| `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | pass | pass |
| `cargo test --locked -p rustbgpd-gobgp-bridge --test daemon` (daemon built first) | pass | pass |
| same test on the previous code | pass | fails with the hosted error (`missing target/debug/build/rustbgpd-gobgp-bridge/<hash>/rustbgpd`) |
| `bash bench/tests/test-vpn-query-receipt.sh` | pass | pass |
| `bash bench/tests/test-vpn-query-campaign.sh` | pass | pass |
| `build_bench` from `run-vpn-query-campaign.sh` | pass, resolves `release/deps/…` | pass, resolves `release/build/rustbgpd-api/<hash>/out/…` |
| `locate_benchmark_binary` from `compare-route-paging.sh`, including a zero-match rejection | pass | pass |
| `cargo test --locked -p reloadstall` | pass | pass |
| `cargo test --locked --test config_persistence_lifecycle` | pass | not run (clippy-only change) |
| CI rustdoc command | pass | pass |
| `just check-fast` | pass | pass |

On 1.100.0, `target/debug/rustbgpd` is still produced as a final artifact.

author: aaltaay
body:
## What

**Held: a design for approval, not a build.** This adds ADR 071 as *Proposed*: the three Level 2 lines become three lanes with one owner each (yours, Claude's seat's, the bots'), your lane stays on the last stock you opened with no timer, and recording follows the lanes instead of recording stocks nobody watches. No code changes yet; the build lands on this same PR after the operator approves the record.

## Why this approach

- **What went wrong (2026-11-12, `backend/logs/blast.log`).** The operator held 100 XLAB on Paper from the phone. The page went to the background at 12:14:50; the Level 2 line was let go 0.75 s later and auto-record took it for TGHL at 12:15:02; the tape line was cancelled at 12:15:04 (the 16 s linger). Back at 12:15:06, Level 2 returned in 2 s but the tape could not be asked for until 12:15:20: IBKR allows one tick-by-tick request per instrument per 15 s and Nova counts 16 s from its own cancel. The phone showed "Resubscribing in 10s".
- **The operator's shape, verbatim:** "I need one empty lane for me! One empty lane for Claude training and one lane for bots trading .. keep it simple", and "the recording only starts when bots, Claude, or I are watching at level 2. We don't need random recorders when nobody's watching anything". Asked whether they may borrow an idle lane, they chose strict lanes.
- **Why not a smaller fix.** Any timer that cancels the operator's line meets IBKR's 15 seconds on the way back, and seven kinds of holder each have their own take / keep / give-up rule today. Fixed owners remove the lending, the room-making and the yield rules instead of adding an eighth exception.
- **What a cold reader would miss.** Auto-record does two jobs: its `trade` / `near` / `armed` tiers are how a bot's setup gets the Level 2 it must have to fire (`BOT_NO_DEPTH_LINE`), so that picker becomes the bots' lane; only its `leader` tier is the recorder nobody watches. And a resting Paper order holds a tape line of its own (`practice/tape_hold.py`): with strict lanes it must fill from Level 1's Last off-lane (the existing `l1_last` stand-in), which is still an open question for the operator (ADR decision 9).

## Verified by

- `py -3 tools/doc_invariants.py` -> `doc_invariants: OK (live-doc claims)`
- The timeline in the ADR is read from the desk's own log lines for 12:07-12:17 ET; IBKR's wording is quoted from its TWS API tick-by-tick page.
- Not verified: whether IBKR counts its 15 s from the previous request or from the cancel. A measurement after 20:00 ET on a stock nobody watches is step 1 of the build order.

none yet. ADR 071 (Proposed). Roadmap: desk reliability for the phone work (ADR 070).

author: neptunus0001
body:
Fixes #267.

## Problem

`copy_file` creates an empty placeholder at the target path and then copies. The placeholder was only removed when the copied size did not match. When `fs::metadata`, `fs::copy` or `set_file_times` returned an error, the empty file stayed behind. On the next run it counted as an existing target with different content, so the real file was stored under a `{dup}` name next to the empty one.

## Change

In `src/action.rs`, the steps after the creation of the placeholder are moved into a helper, `copy_file_contents`. If it returns an error, `copy_file` removes the target and returns the error. The successful path is unchanged.

## Result

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| copy of an unreadable source file fails | empty `IMG_...-a.jpg` left in the target directory | target directory stays empty |
| same, run again after fixing the permissions | `IMG_...-a-1.jpg` (real file) and `IMG_...-a.jpg` (empty) | `IMG_...-a.jpg` only |
| move falls back to copy but the source no longer exists | empty `IMG_...-a-1.jpg` left behind | nothing left behind |

Also checked: a successful copy still has the same content and modification time as the source, `hardlink` and `move` work as before, and a multi-threaded copy of several files produces all of them.

## Testing

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` and `cargo doc` pass for default features, `--no-default-features` and `--features video`.

author: derek73
body:
The first of two PRs implementing #659's decision, as amended after the measurement gate. The amendment is the issue's comment of 2026-11-12 (https://github.com/derek73/python-nameparser/issues/659#issuecomment-6836211654); the "Specification" section below is that wording as the reviews settled it. The second PR turns the switch on from `Parser.suggest` and follows this one.

## What it does

**A new opt-in switch, `Policy.capitals_as_family`, off by default (rules/O9).** It reads the words a name writes in capitals as its family name, wherever they stand:

| Input | default (1.4.0, 2.0.0, 2.8.0, 3.0.1 and this tree) | `capitals_as_family=True` |
|---|---|---|
| `DUPONT Marie` | given `DUPONT`, family `Marie` | given `Marie`, family `DUPONT` |
| `Ayla BURSALI AKSOY` | middle `BURSALI`, family `AKSOY` | family `BURSALI AKSOY` |
| `Jeffrey LAM Kin-fung` | middle `LAM`, family `Kin-fung` | given `Jeffrey`, middle `Kin-fung`, family `LAM` |
| `Hugo LAC` | suffix `LAC`, reports `given-or-family` | family `LAC`, no report |
| `DOYEN Hugo` | title `DOYEN`, family `Hugo` | given `Hugo`, family `DOYEN` |

The `Jeffrey LAM Kin-fung` row is #1181's answer under the switch: the other words keep their written order.

## Specification (the decision as amended 2026-11-12)

- **A capitals word** has two or more letters in capitals, after any lowercase prefix glued in front: `O'BRIEN`, `ALLIOT-MARIE`, `McDONALD` and `d'ESTAING` count. A word holding a full stop, slash or digit does not (`DR.`, `N/A`), nor does anything in brackets or quotes, initials joined by a hyphen (`J-P`), or a word whose capitals are one letter (`PhD`).
- **One run:**
  - runs joined only by particles or conjunctions are one run (`Aude BROSSARD de VILLEMONT`), a listed one-letter conjunction written bare included (`Ana LOPEZ Y GARCIA`; `Y.` is an initial);
  - a run neither opens nor ends in a conjunction (`Mary SMITH AND Jones` → family `SMITH`);
  - a lowercase particle written right before the run joins it (`Jean de LA FONTAINE`);
  - a run of particles alone is no run, and neither is a lone roman numeral (II to X); the name then reads by position (`Karim AL Haddadi`, `John Smith III`).
- **Two runs:** where a name word divides two runs, the last is the family (`PETER Okello MUWANGA`).
- **Which names it reads:** a name is in mixed case only where a word no run took, other than a title, a suffix, or a particle or conjunction written in lowercase, holds a lowercase letter. `Dr. ANITA ROY`, `MARIA de SOUZA LIMA`, `JOHN McCAIN` and `JAN Van DER BERG` are unaffected; `MORRISON Van` is read.
- **The other words:** in written order, the given name the first unit holding a word that may be one. A lowercase particle or conjunction outside the run is a joining word, so a lowercase particle stays with the word after it (`de Marie DUPONT` → given `de Marie`) and a unit of nothing else is a middle name (`JEAN y Perez` → given `Perez`); a particle written with a capital may be the given name (`De Marie DUPONT`, `Van Mary DUPONT`).
- **Peel:** a listed credential or numeral ending the run comes off where a capitals word that is no particle is left (`Marie GRAJALES III`, `Jean DUPONT MBA`), but never leaves only particles (`Anna DE CARO`), and only at the end of the name.
- **Commas:** the switch reads only the part before the first comma; a family comma names the family (`Dupont, MARIE`).
- **Construction:** setting it with `unlisted_caps_suffixes=CapsSuffixes.EVERYWHERE` raises `ValueError` naming both values and offering `Policy(capitals_as_family=True, unlisted_caps_suffixes=CapsSuffixes.AFTER_COMMA)`. A test executes the offered code. It raises from `Policy(...)`, from `patched()` on either side, from `dataclasses.replace` and from `parser_for` with a pack.
- **Accepted costs**, stated in rules/O9 with their counts:
  - joined initials in the middle of a name read as the family (`Jan GM Brouwer` → family `GM`; 4,246 ORCID records);
  - a credential after the surname with no comma reads as the family (`John Smith MD` → family `MD`; 757 ORCID records, none from a source that writes families in capitals).
- **Left open:** a bare `DR` in capitals at the head reads as the family (`DR Anna Berg`; 204 ORCID given boxes). It is recorded as rules/O9's last Accepted bullet and decisions/O9's `Open:` line.

## Where it runs

`_post_rules._family_in_capitals`:
- **Position:** after H1, M4, P1, O1, O2 and P6, so none of their moves undoes it. Before O6, which stands down where it acted. O7 and O3 then read the words it leaves. O8 needs no stand-down, since the capitals family is never a single initial.
- **What it reads:** the tokens before the first comma whose role is a name, a title or a suffix. A word S6 read as a credential, or H1/H9 read as a title, is in reach; nicknames and maiden clauses are not.
- **Cost:** with the switch off it is one attribute test. Frame counts for `John Smith`, `Smith, John` and `John Q. Smith` are 125, 135 and 176 on this branch and on the merge base.

`_vocab.is_capitals_word` is the word test, shared with PR B. A new internal tag, `capitals-family`, which reaches no published token, makes `Token.reading` give the family words' source as `shape`, the source the type already names for "a word in capitals".

**Ambiguity reports** (decided by `nameparser/_pipeline/AGENTS.md`), where the rule acts:
- dropped, since the capitals settled the fork, as S6 already says of a credential its capitals settle: `particle-or-given` and `given-or-family` reports (the capitals said where the family is), and any `suffix-or-name` or `title-or-name` report on a word of the run (`DEAN Hugo`, `Hugo JUNIOR`);
- kept, under every order: a title or suffix fork on any other word (`Dean Mary DUPONT` keeps `title-or-name`).

The rule emits nothing of its own, since the caller declared the convention, as O6 and O8 do.

`capitalized()` leaves a name in mixed case as written, so `DUPONT Marie` renders `Marie DUPONT` and keeps its capitals. `capitalized(force=True)` gives `Marie Dupont`: the family is named by its field by then.

## Measurements

### The gate (before code; scripts and outputs in the 3.1 session notes, `659-gate/`; dated snapshots in decisions/O9)

The capped `orcid-researchers/raw.jsonl` the decision read was no longer cached. I read the full ORCID 2025-10 dump instead (24,990,909 records), with a 20,000-a-country cap to approximate the corpus. Not measured: France's register and LegCo (not cached), and the parliament datasets fetched after 2026-11-08 (Korea, Indonesia, Ethiopia, Israel).

**ORCID: which box holds the capitals** (records where one box is wholly capitals words and the other holds none):

| | family box | given box | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| capped, 4+ letters | 44,952 | 4,882 | 90.2% |
| capped, 2–3 letters | 5,336 | 787 | 87.1% |
| whole dump, 4+ letters | 327,396 | 40,175 | 89.1% |
| whole dump, 2–3 letters | 69,550 | 15,522 | 81.8% |

The coordinator's figures were 90.1% and 87.3%. Where the family box is in capitals, the prototype read both fields right in 396,793 of 396,946 records, composed either way.

### Parliaments, capitals taken as the family, the shipped switch (`parliaments_shipped.py`; cache refreshed 2026-11-12, 23 datasets)

| | default | switch on |
|---|---|---|
| `tr_parliament` | 549 / 591 | 591 / 591 |
| `az_parliament` | 0 / 124 | 124 / 124 |
| `kz_mazhilis` | 152 / 152 | 152 / 152 |

The refreshed cache adds `kr_assembly`, which the gate could not measure. Of its 297 names in Latin script, 293 are written wholly in capitals (`PARK SUNGHOON`) and 4 in mixed case with no word in capitals, so the switch reads none of them.

### Switch off

- **Committed snapshot:** changes only by 96 example names new to the rules corpus (rules/O9's and the Precedence bullets naming it); no existing name moves.
- **CLDR agreement:** `cldr_agreement.py` matches every record.
- **Local corpora:** `snapshot.py --local <source> --base <checkout of 670b3498>` "matches the bas

author: hrustalq
body:
Refs #998, refs #1000, refs #986. Follow-up to #996: these two commits were pushed to its branch a minute after it merged, so they are not in `dev`.

## fix(memory): recall and reflect have a per-key rate (#998)

Reflect is a model call on a viewer's request, so a read-only key could call it without bound; the only brake was the workspace budget, which does nothing unless the workspace enforces one. Recall had no limit either.

- `MemoryRateService` counts retain, recall and reflect per key (or per person), asked by the REST routes and the per-bank MCP tools after the resolver and before the work. The bank is resolved first, so a caller from another workspace still gets a 404, over the rate or not.
- `MEMORY_RECALL_RATE_PER_MIN` (300) and `MEMORY_REFLECT_RATE_PER_MIN` (30), each with a default.
- Over the rate: a 429 with a `detail` and `Retry-After` over REST, a refused tool call over MCP. No model is called.
- With the limiter unreachable, retain and recall stay up and reflect is refused.

## chore(ci): run the Hindsight compat spec in CI (#1000)

The spec that defines compatibility ran only by hand. It is now a step of the `coedit-e2e` job, on that job's Postgres, Redis and ArcadeDB, before the worker and the API start. Stub embeddings and a stubbed reflect model: no provider is reached. #986's criterion is reworded to match.

## Verified

- `make verify` (3,858 API tests) and `make deps`.
- `hindsight-compat.e2e-spec.ts` locally: 46 tests, including the new one (both verbs refused on both surfaces, `Retry-After: 60`, no model call).

## Not verified

- **The new CI step has never run.** This PR's own `coedit-e2e` run is its first; if ArcadeDB is not ready in time or the runner lacks something the spec needs, it fails here.
- The fail-closed path for reflect against a real Redis outage: covered by a unit test on the argument passed to the limiter.

author: soliskit
body:
# Pull Request

## What this changes

Brings the repository's four Python GitHub check scripts under the same pinned Ruff lint and format setup already used in litlmoz, with all findings fixed and enforcement added to the commit hook and CI. 8 files changed.

1. ruff.toml: new, copied from the approved litlmoz pattern - target py310, rule sets E4, E7, E9, F, W, I, UP, B, C4, RUF.
2. .github/workflows/test.yml: the test job now installs the pinned ruff==0.17.4 and runs ruff check . and ruff format --check . before the existing lint step.
3. lefthook.yml: pre-commit gains python-lint (ruff check) and python-format (ruff format --check) over staged Python files.
4. Python fixes, all mechanical: import sorting, regex flag aliases and formatting. The scripts' validation logic is untouched.
5. .gitignore gains __pycache__/ and *.pyc.

No rule overrides, no noqa, no new JavaScript dependencies; Ruff is a free pinned tool.

## Class

* [ ] **Refactor:** project code changes, behavior does not. Requirement entries are unchanged and the tests pass; tests change only to follow renamed or moved code.
* [ ] **Bug Fix:** project code is brought back in line with an existing requirement. Which requirement, and which test failed before the fix?
* [ ] **Intentional Change:** behavior is added, changed or removed. Which requirement entries changed in the same commit, and which tests now check them?
* [ ] **Clarification:** requirement entries now describe behavior the project already has. Which entries, and which tests check them?
* [x] **No Class Needed:** no project code and no requirement entries change. The review questions still apply.

## Review questions

* **Behavior:** No. The Python scripts' observable behavior is preserved - every fix is formatting or an equivalent spelling, and all four byte-compile.
* **Protection:** No runtime check is loosened, removed or moved. The check scripts keep their exact validation logic; the PR metadata workflows load them from the trusted base, so this PR's own checks ran the base versions.
* **Gates:** No gate is lowered or removed. This change raises the gates: Python lint and formatting are now enforced in the commit hook and CI.
* **Description:** No new behavior is added, so no requirement entry is needed.

body:
## Why

The libraries in the stack build on each other, but their agent skills do not.
Eight repositories ship a use skill, none of them knows about the others, and installing one installs nothing below it.
This page is the design for linking them into a tree, so an agent working high in the stack reads a short card about each library below it and opens that library's skill only when it needs to.
It is the page for the design issue #151, under the epic #150, and it is the bottom of a stack: one page per library's shelf follows, starting with gaussx.

## What changes

| | Today | After this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The skill tree's design | in #151 only | `docs/design/skill_tree.md`, in the Design section of the site |
| How the geotoolz ⇄ pipekit cycle was broken | spread over Report 16 and #116 | one section, with the three steps and the rule they follow |

The page covers the units by band of the role ladder, the contract card, the shared `role-ladder` skill at the root, the three install options, the rules that keep the tree acyclic, gates ST-1 to ST-6 and the risks.

## What stays the same

- No code, no skill and no plugin changes. The decision in #151 is still open.
- The dependency graph, its rules and its generated page.

## Tests

- `myst build --html` builds the page with no warning from it (mystmd 1.12.0; a two-sentence rewording of items 1 and 2 of "The tree" was made after that build).

author: air
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"air"} -->
_Requested by **Aaron** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Gp19T8C3QMJyauZZiCPWvp?thread=cmsg_01Gp19T8C3QMJyauZZiCPWvpNkygdu3nCpspa6E86y4MQP)_

This is the first of six pull requests that bring Wasteland's pages up to what Pool of Radiance got. It adds seven sections to the front of the Dice and combat tab. The three sections that were there are untouched and now come after them, numbered 08 to 10.

## What a reader gets

Six of the new sections have a fight the reader can run. The page does not use a port for these. It loads the listings of the engine, the game and one map (the same files the Source tab shows), lays them over each other as they sit in the C64's memory, and runs the game's own battle round on the kit's 6502. The browser supplies the random bytes, and the game's text comes out as text.

1. **Secret: a Ranger who is down cannot be hurt by any monster.** A shot that lands on a fallen Ranger is printed as a miss, and monsters in melee only pick Rangers on their feet. In 400 rounds, 1,847 blows aimed at two fallen Rangers cost them no CON.
2. **Bug: the Guards under the Temple of Blood cannot fire while one of their Bloodbeasts is alive.** A line of monsters without guns ends its whole group's turn to shoot, where an empty line is only skipped. The patrol's record lists the Guards first, so the Bloodbeasts are reached first. A switch on the page moves that one branch, and the Guards fire.
3. **Bug: a lone gunman runs away easily, and a line of ten gunmen never runs.** This one was found while building the page. The code keeps "how many times to halve the party's CON" in a byte that another routine overwrites with the number of monsters in the line. One monster halves the CON once, ten halve it ten times.
4. **Secret: a party left behind heals twice as fast as the party you lead.** Measured in the emulator as well: over 64 steps on the world map, the party left behind healed 16 points and the walkers 8.
5. **Bug: fists, knives, and chainsaws can never hit the Chopters outside Base Cochise.** Their skill byte is 0, and the code turns 0 into −256 when it subtracts it. 1,800 blows, none landed.
6. **Bug: a single shot that kills the last Ranger outright can freeze the game.** Rare: 3 rounds in 3,000 for a lone Ranger at 1 CON. The first button plays one of the three.
7. **A round is fought in four passes, and every gun fires before any blade.** A table and three paragraphs, no widget.

## How it was checked

- `games/c64/wasteland/test_combat.js` runs the page's two script blocks in node with fixed random bytes. It makes every figure the page prints again from the committed listings, and fails if the page's text does not hold that figure. 75 checks pass.
- Sections 1 and 4 were also tried on the real game in VICE before the page was written. The notes are in `agent-history.md`.
- All six widgets were driven in Chromium on the built page, at desktop and phone widths, with no errors.
- `check_binaries.py`, `check_docs.py`, `check_listing.py`, `test_kit.py --changed` (10 passed) and `build.py` (118 games) all pass.

## Other files

- `parts/game/symbols.json` and `listing.json`: the comment on `line_weaker_than_party` (`$869F`) said what the code sets out to do. It now says what the code does. One record changed.
- `parts/game/facts.md`: the same correction, and the live and simulator results beside the facts they confirm.
- `reference/wasteland-page.css`: styles for the new plates.

## Before

author: vacwave
body:
Non-MT, MT version: #857
If `dev` gets merged into `dev-mt`, #857 can be closed.

The A-Life scheduled update has no time limit. Each update runs `objects_per_update` objects however long they take, and `bind_stalker.script` sets that to 20. `process_time` only applies to the online/offline switch pass.

In GAMMA after a load, one update of 20 objects took 28 ms on average and up to 73 ms, about twice a second. It runs through `seqParallel`, so the main thread waits for it at the end of the frame, which shows up as a regular stutter.

Adds an optional time limit to `[alife]`:
```ini
scheduled_time_limit = 2000 ; microseconds, default 0 (off)
```
Scripts can also set and read it:
```lua
alife():set_scheduled_time_limit(microseconds) -- 0 = off
alife():scheduled_time_limit() -- gets current value, 0 = off
```

When set:
- A scheduled update stops once the limit is exceeded and continues from the same object next time. At least one object is always updated.
- `objects_per_update` stays the maximum.
- Scheduled updates run at the `schedule_min` interval (30 ms engine minimum), so the same work is spread over more, smaller updates.
- The online/offline switch pass keeps its usual interval.

Default is 0, nothing changes unless the key is set.

Testing:
Make a MO2 mod `mods\modname\gamedata\configs\mod_system_perf_alife.ltx`
```ini
![alife]
schedule_min                             = 1 ; GAMMA sets this to 170, make it minimum
scheduled_time_limit                     = 2000 ; 2 ms
```

Built DX11-AVX and played in Anomaly and GAMMA, the constant stuttering while moving was mostly gone.

Unrelated to this PR: `process_time` is passed to the switch pass as seconds instead of microseconds (`CALifeUpdateManager::set_process_time`), so that limit never triggers. Not changed here, since fixing it would change switching behaviour for existing configs.

author: caleb-bb
body:
Closes #329. Part of #325.

## Summary

Adds the `cake.laws.candidates` LawSpec unit: 13 laws over `Cake.Candidates`' four public functions. Two laws went red against the code, and this PR resolves both. It also adds a Claude Code hook that loads the LawSpec prelude into a session during LawSpec work.

## Contract changes

Both were decided on the issue's terms before any Cake code changed; the laws and tests for each are in an earlier commit than the fix.

1. **A `Cake.Citable` `:id` is a `String.t()`** (was `term()`). This resolves B4.
   - Before: the moduledoc allowed tuples, and a tuple id with no `source_ref` crashed `Candidates.group_by_document/1` with `Protocol.UndefinedError` in `to_string/1`.
   - Why narrow instead of making `doc_id_for` total: `Conversation.select_docs/2` is already specced `[String.t()]`, both implementations return a UUID, and a text encoding for arbitrary terms could collide with a real string id.
   - Follow-on: `Cake.Candidates` and `ChatLive` drop their `to_string/1` calls, `Responses.Result.citation`'s `id` is `String.t()`, and the Citable fixtures in `responses_test.exs` and `citations_test.exs` use string ids instead of tuples.
2. **The candidate page label counts distinct pages.** Two chunks on page 5 used to read `"PDF pages 5-5"`; they now read `"PDF page 5"`. This was not in the issue: the laws surfaced it, and several chunks per page is the normal case for books.

`document_metadata/1`'s spec now takes a non-empty list, which its doc and its use of the first result already required.

## The laws

| Function | Laws |
| --- | --- |
| `group_by_document/1` | Equals a reference model (one group per document id, first-seen order, input order within a group, text keys); every group is non-empty and holds one document; flattening is a permutation of the input; every candidate gets a group whatever its id |
| `all_chunk_ids/1` | Each candidate's own id, in group then member order; count equals the input length |
| `expand_to_chunk_ids/2` | Equals a reference model of a selection; selecting every document equals `all_chunk_ids/1`; an empty selection gives `[]`; distributes over appended selections |
| `document_metadata/1` | Title; preview cut to 100 characters; page label; a group all on one page is labelled `PDF page N` |

Three laws go beyond the issue's table: the title (first candidate's `book_title`, else its label), the selection reference model, and group well-formedness.

Two generators are built by construction because random data did not reach the case:
- Generated text topped out at 19 characters, so the preview law builds previews up to 169 characters to cross the 100-character cut.
- Generated page numbers rarely coincide, so a dedicated law puts one to six candidates on the same page.

## Also in this PR

- **LawSpec prelude hook** (`.claude/hooks/lawspec-prelude.sh` and `.mjs`, registered in `.claude/settings.json`). The first tool call in a Claude Code session that touches `lawspec/` or a `.lawspec` file gets the prelude's operation names and laws injected, read from the installed compiler so it matches the pinned version. It loads once per session and per subagent, reloads after a clear or a compaction, and cannot block or fail a tool call. Documented in `lawspec/README.md`; one sentence added to `CLAUDE.md`.
- **`lawspec/README.md`** gains the specification's row and four authoring notes (short generated text, global definition names, refined record fields, literal-only example expectations).
- **`README.md`** describes `Cake.Candidates` and names its specification, and says a Citable id is a string. No Cake structs are added, so the struct inventory is unchanged.

## Not changed

- `Cake.Support.FixtureGDS.Record` (test support) still types its `id` as `term()`. It builds ids from whatever shape a test's hit has, so narrowing it needs a look at each caller.
- An unpersisted `Chunk` or `ParsedDocument` has a `nil` id, which its `Cake.Citable` implementation returns as it is. Retrieval units come from the database, so this is documented in `Cake.Citable`'s moduledoc and not guarded.

## Verification

All on the head commit:

- `laws` job steps under Erlang/OTP 29.1.2 and Elixir 1.20.5: `npm run check`, `npm run fmt:check`, `npm run generate:check` pass; `mix test` reports 1688 passed.
- `mix precommit`: 146 properties, 1021 tests, 0 failures.
- `mix docs --warnings-as-errors` passes, and `mix dialyzer` reports 0 errors.
- `mix xref graph --label compile-connected --fail-above 3` and `mix coveralls.json --exclude integration` (84.0% against a minimum of 70) passed on the commit before the last; the last commit changes no module dependencies and adds no code paths.
- Red first: before the Cake changes, the B4 law failed with `Protocol.UndefinedError` on `{"alpha", 4}`, and the page-label laws and two ExUnit tests failed on `"PDF pages 5-5"`.
- On the first version of the spec, eight deliberate bugs in `Cake.Candidates` were each caught by at least one law. That check was not repeated after the spec was rewritten for text ids.
- The hook was observed firing in a live session. Its subagent and compaction behaviour was tested only by piping hook input to the script.

author: williamhpark
body:
crypt_alloc_buffer() allocates the bio for an encrypted write with bio_alloc_bioset(), which associates it with the blkcg of the current task. The ioprio of the original bio is copied over, but its blkcg association is not.

For page cache writeback, the original bio is associated with the cgroup that dirtied the pages (wbc_init_bio()), but the task submitting it is a flusher kworker in the root cgroup. The encrypted bio therefore ends up charged to root on the underlying device. io.cost and io.max don't throttle root, so the writer escapes both. Writes issued from the writer's own context (fsync(), O_DIRECT) keep the right cgroup, and so do reads, since kcryptd_io_read() uses bio_alloc_clone(), which copies the association.

We hit this on ext4 over dm-crypt (no_write_workqueue) over NVMe with io.cost enabled. On the encrypted volumes, the containers' io.stat wbytes added up to 0-16% of the bytes written to the disk, against ~95% on an unencrypted disk on the same host.

Fix it by copying the association from the original bio, as is already done for the ioprio. This follows commit 5d8d40815314 ("dm crypt: Fix IO priority lost when queuing write bios").

With the default write thread, io.cost can now block in dmcrypt_write(), so a throttled cgroup may delay other cgroups' writes queued behind it. This doesn't apply with no_write_workqueue, where the bio is submitted from the context that issued the original one.

Built with W=1, with and without CONFIG_BLK_CGROUP. Not runtime tested yet.

The analysis, patch and changelog were prepared with help from an AI coding assistant (Claude Opus 5.5).

author: douglowder
body:
## Why

The expo-updates integration lived in expo-observe, with native code specific to expo-updates (review on #51882). With the library integration API from the layers below, it can live in expo-updates, like the expo-image integration.

## How

**Context**

A public API for Observe integrations that live in other libraries, so the expo-updates integration can move into expo-updates (ENG-28931).

**This diff**

Add the expo-updates integration to expo-updates, on the library integration API: it registers through the `globalThis` registry, keeps its log cursor in `reporter.storage`, and reads live entries with `addLogEntryListener`. expo-observe has no code for it apart from the config types.

- The public `'expo-updates'` config and its types stay in expo-observe, as on #51882. expo-updates cannot depend on expo-observe, even as a devDependency, because `expo` → `expo-updates` → `expo-observe` → `expo-app-metrics` → `expo` is a build cycle; it copies the few integration types it uses.
- expo-observe leaves function options, such as `shouldReport`, out of the integrations config that the native module stores, for every integration.
- The integration registers when the app imports `expo-updates`. When the config sets `'expo-updates'` and the integration has not registered 5 seconds after `configure`, expo-observe prints one warning that tells the developer to import `expo-updates`.

Stack, bottom to top:
1. #53419 An error code on `reportError`.
2. #53420 A registry for integrations in other libraries.
3. #51883 A log entry listener registry in expo-updates-interface (merged).
4. #53431 Storage for library integrations.
5. #53432 `Updates.addLogEntryListener`.
6. This PR: #53433 The expo-updates integration in expo-updates.
7. #53434 Docs and an observe-tester example.

## Test Plan

author: rubas-agent[bot]
body:
Before: CI on `main` failed after #23 (run https://github.com/rubas/pippin/actions/runs/43313856639). The SIGTERM test failed, and then the whole `bun test` step died:

```
(fail) a SIGTERM that arrives while a session starts ends its child, removes the FIFO, and exits with 130 [2516.16ms]
##[error]Process completed with exit code 143.
```

Problem: The test reads the pid of the child from a file. The shell creates that file before it writes the pid, so a child that the session ends in between leaves an empty file. The test turned that empty file into pid 0. `kill(pid, 0)` then succeeds, the check fails, and the cleanup's `process.kill(0)` sends SIGTERM to the whole process group, `bun test` and the step's shell too. That is the exit code 143, and the rest of the test files never ran.

After: The test reads an empty file as "the child died before it wrote its pid". It passes, and it never signals pid 0.

Sentry: RELAY-G

<details>

The cause is in `e2e/pippin.test.ts`, in the test "a SIGTERM that arrives while a session starts...", which #22 added. `Number("")` is 0, and `process.kill(0)` signals the caller's process group. The window is the few microseconds between the shell's `open` of the pid file and its `write`, so it shows only on a slow runner.

I reproduced the exact CI end on epyc. A copy of the test lets the child create the file, sleep, and only then write, and it closes the session 100 ms late. Under `setsid -w`, the old code ended the whole session with SIGTERM. With the fix, the same copy passes. `bun run check` and `bun test` pass, 14 of 14.

</details>

author: bonomat
body:
Add an opt-in `Client::submit_offchain_tx_oneshot` API that signs locally built checkpoints before SubmitTx. Compatible arkd servers finalize in that request; older servers that drop owner signatures fall back to FinalizeTx without signing again. Existing sends and submit-without-finalizing APIs keep their current behavior.

Both gRPC and REST report `SubmitOffchainTxResponse::finalized` by comparing exact submitted signatures with the raw returned checkpoints before binding restores local signatures. Existing Ark signature verification and checkpoint binding remain in place. This follows the protocol used by https://github.com/arkade-os/ts-sdk/pull/1069.

The method documents that the server receives owner checkpoint signatures before returning its Ark signature. The new response field is additive for readers but requires downstream struct literals to be updated.

Validation:
- 249 library tests pass across ark-core, ark-client, ark-grpc and ark-rest.
- `e2e_oneshot_offchain_submit` passes against local arkd v0.9.25: Alice boards funds, submits through the new API, verifies no pending transaction and both balances, then Bob spends the received funds back. CI discovers this test automatically; its older pinned arkd exercises the fallback. This test verifies completion and spendability, not the number of RPC calls.
- Full-workspace `cargo +1.99.1 clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes. Removed an existing redundant forfeit-output clone flagged by CI's newer Clippy.
- Changed files pass nightly rustfmt.
- Unit regression coverage includes retained, missing, altered and partially retained signatures, reordered checkpoints, and local-signature restoration during binding.

author: aklkv
body:
With `bootstrap: 'localFlags'` or `'localStorage'`, the SDK reports success straight away from those values and only sends LaunchDarkly's as `change` events. `streamingFlags` filters those out by default, so the context kept the local or cached values for the whole session. With `'localStorage'` that meant every session ran on the previous session's flags, while `client.variation()` reported the real ones to LaunchDarkly.

- For those two bootstraps, `initialize()` adds a `flag-details-changed` inspector. On the first full payload (the stream's `put`, or the SDK's background fetch for `'localStorage'`) it loads the client's flags, then persisted overrides, like a successful init. If they match what the context started from it does nothing, so an up-to-date cache doesn't re-render every flag. After that, `streamingFlags` applies as before.
- The inspector is only used as a signal: it runs a tick after the payload, so it reads `client.allFlags()` then, in case a streamed patch landed in between.
- A bootstrap object passed in directly, e.g. from a server-side SDK, is still taken as LaunchDarkly's values.

LaunchDarkly's typings say inspectors are for monitoring rather than app flow. It's still the only way to tell a full payload arrived when nothing in it changed, and it costs no extra request. Fetching again with `client.identify()` would drop the secure-mode hash, clear the localStorage cache on failure, and send a second identify event. The two end-to-end tests run the real SDK against a fake `EventSource` and `XMLHttpRequest`, so the floating dependencies job will catch it if a release changes when inspectors fire.

author: razzamatazm
body:
Refs #453. Left as "refs" rather than "closes" because the cause is inferred from the traceback, not confirmed against the reporter's provider.

## Summary

Mustarrd never told a provider what it was. Every request went out under the HTTP library's own name, and some providers hang up on anything that is not a media player.

```diff
 request to provider
-  User-Agent: Python/3.12 aiohttp/3.x
+  User-Agent: VLC/3.0.21 LibVLC/3.0.21      # or CATCHUP_PROVIDER_USER_AGENT
```

One helper, passed to every session that talks to a provider:

```text
services/provider_http.py        provider_request_headers()
├── services/xtream_client.py    sign-in, channel lists, guide, VOD lists
├── services/download_manager.py recording downloads
├── api/channels.py              live and catchup previews (2 sites)
├── api/vod.py                   VOD preview relay
└── services/logo_cache.py       channel logos
```

Plex and webhook requests are not provider-facing and are unchanged. FFmpeg never opens a provider URL (previews feed it stdin or a loopback relay), so it needs nothing.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a real local HTTP server standing in for the provider records what `XtreamClient.authenticate()` sends.
  ```text
  AssertionError: Lists differ: ['Python/3.13 aiohttp/3.13.3'] != ['VLC/3.0.21 LibVLC/3.0.21']
  ```
  **After:** the same test passes, and so does the override case (`TiviMate/5.1.6 (Android 12)` arrives on the wire).
- **Before:** the five other request sites opened their sessions with no `headers` (`KeyError: 'headers'` in each new test).
  **After:** each passes `provider_request_headers()`.
- A guard test walks `services/` and `api/` and fails if any `ClientSession(...)` outside Plex and webhooks is opened without the helper, so a new request site cannot bring this back quietly.
- Backend suite: 1,737 passing (12 new).

To try it: add an account as usual. To override, set `CATCHUP_PROVIDER_USER_AGENT` and restart.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting restores the old header. No schema or stored data changes.

**Blast Radius:** provider-wide

Every provider now sees a different client name on every request. VLC is the player Xtream providers most commonly support, so this should only open doors, but a provider that blocks VLC specifically while allowing unknown clients would start refusing. The env var is the escape hatch.

body:
<!-- Thanks for submitting a pull request! We appreciate you spending the time to work on these changes. Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. The four fields below are mandatory. -->

<!-- This fork of react-native provides React Native for macOS for the community.  It also contains some changes that are required for usage internal to Microsoft.  We are working on reducing the diff between Facebook's public version of react-native and our microsoft/react-native-macos fork.  Long term, we want this fork to only contain macOS concerns and have the other iOS and Android concerns contributed upstream.

If you are making a new change then one of the following should be done:
- Consider if it is possible to achieve the desired behavior without making a change to microsoft/react-native-macos.  Often a change can be made in a layer above in facebook/react-native instead.
- Create a corresponding PR against [facebook/react-native](https://github.com/facebook/react-native)
**Note:** Ideally you would wait for Facebook feedback before submitting to Microsoft, since we want to ensure that this fork doesn't deviate from upstream.
-->

## Summary:

<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->

The macOS Fabric trait initializer currently treats `mouseDownCanMoveWindow=true` as requiring a native stacking context, although true is the default in both the C++ props and native view. Consequently every otherwise layout-only View materializes, while an explicit false can lose the native boundary that is meant to prevent window dragging.

- Require the window-dragging boundary for **false**, leaving the established true default and Pressable's false override unchanged.
- Preserve native views and responder boundaries for tooltips, registered drag types and handled key lists when ordinary layout-only Views can flatten again. Keep existing mouse-event, focus, first-mouse and vibrancy requirements.
- Add two focused tests to the existing stacking-context suite: false/true transitions with a native descendant, and native-only props that must not disappear.

[AppKit documents true as permitting mouse-down propagation through superviews](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsview/mousedowncanmovewindow). The false override was deliberately added for Pressable cancellation in #1857. This macOS-specific predicate/default mismatch was introduced in #2730; it is not an upstream React Native change. Current main and the pending #3058/#3104/#3105 release-stack trait headers were checked; none contains this correction.

## Test Plan:

<!-- Demonstrate the code is solid. Example: The exact commands you ran and their output, screenshots / videos if the pull request changes the user interface. -->

Built a temporary standalone GoogleTest runner from this branch's actual `ViewShadowNode.cpp`, existing `StackingContextTest.cpp`, mounting stubs and component builder. Existing native support libraries/generated headers were reused **read-only**; no Pods or Xcode build was run. The temporary harness is not part of this PR.

- `bash .flattening-validation/compile_stacking_tests.sh fixed` — **passed**, compiled and linked the runner.
- `.flattening-validation/stacking-tests-fixed --gtest_filter='StackingContextTest.*'` — **passed all 9 tests**, covering both tree builders and incremental mounting mutations.
- `bash .flattening-validation/compile_stacking_tests.sh baseline` — **passed** compilation against the original trait header from `0b569f1497`.
- `.flattening-validation/stacking-tests-baseline --gtest_filter='StackingContextTest.defaultPropsMakeEverythingFlattened:StackingContextTest.windowDraggingBoundarySurvivesFlattening:StackingContextTest.macOSNativeBehaviorPreventsFlattening'` — **expected failure: all 3 fail**. Default props produce 10 native stub views instead of 1.
- `bash .flattening-validation/compile_stacking_tests.sh negation-only` — **passed** compilation against a mutation that only negates the mouse-down predicate.
- `.flattening-validation/stacking-tests-negation-only --gtest_filter='StackingContextTest.defaultPropsMakeEverythingFlattened:StackingContextTest.windowDraggingBoundarySurvivesFlattening:StackingContextTest.macOSNativeBehaviorPreventsFlattening'` — **expected failure: 2 pass, native-prop regression fails**, demonstrating why tooltip/drag/key requirements must be retained.
- `bash .flattening-validation/compile_stacking_tests.sh syntax-cxx` — **passed** syntax compilation of production/test sources using cxx host props and `-UTARGET_OS_OSX -DTARGET_OS_OSX=0`; this is not an iOS runtime/build claim.
- `xcrun clang-format --dry-run --Werror packages/react-native/ReactCommon/react/renderer/components/view/platform/macos/react/renderer/components/view/HostPlatformViewTraitsInitializer.h packages/react-native/ReactCommon/react/renderer/mounting/tests/StackingContextTest.cpp` — **passed**.
- `git --no-pager diff --check` — **passed**.

Not run: a fresh RNTester-macOS/Pods/Xcode integration build; live window-background dragging and Pressable cancellation; live tooltip/drag-and-drop/keyboard interactions; iOS/visionOS or Paper builds. No screenshots or AppKit runtime verification are claimed. Jest, Flow and ESLint were not run because no JavaScript changed.

Starting the TUI ran the Claude model-list probe synchronously. Startup now lists Claude with "default" plus the saved model and marks the list pending. The first time Settings opens, one async read fetches the real list from the CLI and caches it for the process. The Model row shows a loading note until it arrives. No alias list is hard-coded. ## Tests no longer call the real `obey` CLI (577ee863)
`TestObeySettingsTerminalPersistence` ran `obey doctor --json` on the real binary five times per run. The catalog read is now stubbed in the TUI `TestMain`. ## Prompt render parses one document (8aaf8611)
Rendering a packaged, non-default system prompt parsed all ~40 embedded YAML documents each time. The documents are indexed once and only the requested one is parsed: about 640 µs to about 50 µs per render. Prompt files in the user directory are still read on every render, so live edits apply.

body:
Closes #140.

## Change

- `presa.transport.http/serve!`: when it binds a loopback address (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`, the default) and no `:allowed-hosts` is given, requests whose Host is not loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`, any port) get 403. Defense in depth against DNS rebinding beyond the Origin check. A server bound elsewhere, or given `:allowed-hosts`, behaves as before.
- `handler` is unchanged; the default lives in `serve!`, which knows the bind address.
- The transports guide says so.
- Test: a default `serve!` answers 403 to a request with `Host: evil.example.com` and serves one with `Host: localhost:<port>`.

## Checks

- `bb test`, `bb jvm-test`: 0 failures
- `bb lint`: ok

Without the change the `evil.example.com` request gets 200. The test sends raw HTTP over a socket, since java.net.http does not let a caller set Host.

Each word of lessons 1 to 16 (80 words) gains two later frames, 160 in all, each naming a later chrome or band lesson as its `fromLessonId` (never a unit lesson). author: dlyngman
body:
## Summary

Since #44 and #45, a padded mark (bars, histograms, date histograms) read from a preagg table pays a padding join on every brush frame. A preagg table now holds its padding rows, so the read's own `GROUP BY` returns every category or bin and only its `ORDER BY` is left. This matters for dashboards with many histograms or bar charts updating on every brush move.

- **Padding rows built into the table.** They come from `dense()` itself, as the padding of an empty result (`SqlTransform.padRows`, `TransformCompiler.padRows`), so what a padded row holds (bin edges from the index, a colour on the bar's own field, the -1 sentinel, crossed series and facets) is decided in one place. A padding row carries the mark's group channels, `0` for every partial and `__pad = true`; real rows get `__pad = false`, joined with `UNION ALL BY NAME` so the brush and value columns a padding row leaves out come back NULL. The read filters with `"__pad" OR (...)`; a NULL test would let through real rows whose brushed field is NULL.
- **`dense()` leaves such a read as it is** (the `padded` fact on `QueryParts` and `MarkConfig`), apart from the order it asks for.
- **Only where the rows come out the same.** Count and sum measures (for a mean, min or max, an empty bin would read `0 / 0` where padding gives 0), no `topN` (it ranks before padding, so zero rows in its table would enter the ranking), no window channels. Everything else keeps the read-time join. Tables stay named by their build SQL, so identical marks still share one.
- **Same bits on both paths**, so padding rows merge with real rows and a mark's rows do not change between a base read and a preagg read:
  - `bin()` writes numeric edges with the padding's own formula (`numericBinEdgeSQL`, DOUBLE arithmetic). Values on screen are unchanged; time buckets already matched.
  - `dense()` returns REAL ids. This also makes padded bars zero-copy: their band column came back INTEGER and was copied into a `Float32Array` on every result.
- **NULL bins** are left out of the build by filtering the source column (`source IS NOT NULL`): those bins are never drawn and padding a base read drops them too. Filtering on the bin instead made the build half again as slow.

## Measured

DuckDB-WASM 1.30 (Node), the SQL the engine generates on `main` and on this branch, 1M flights rows, distance histogram, delay brush:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| preagg read (per brush frame) | 0.91–1.30 ms | 0.46–0.57 ms |
| preagg build (on hover) | 69–71 ms | 69–75 ms |
| result rows | 23 | 23, identical |

## Test plan

- [x] `preagg-value.integration.test.ts` (native DuckDB), preagg read against base read row for row: numeric bins (and REAL types on both paths), NULL values in the binned column, monthly time buckets, bars with a series; a mean keeps the read-time join. The NULL test fails without the source filter (21 rows against 20).
- [x] `transforms.test.ts`: `padRows` gives the zero rows, gives none past a `topN` or with nothing to pad; a `padded` read is left as it is
- [x] Full suite 1125 passed; svelte-check 0 errors; `npm run lint` 0 errors
- [x] Browser: `/test/preagg-legend` still reads preagg tables; histograms on `/test/date-histogram` and `/mosaic/flights-200k` still morph while brushing, with no snap at the first preagg read

Documentation: - Document the version 2 spec template as the default for new scaffolds and clarify that version 1 remains supported for existing documents. Tests: - Update protocol and connector tests to validate version 2 template resolution and scaffolding. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds the AGT-1–10 agent-plugin spec family under `brotocol/spec@2`, unifies all in-process adapters on a shared `adapter-core`, and ships an e2e harness that drives real host CLIs (opencode, pi) against a mock LLM, a scripted `bro` responder, and a generic CLI shim. - `spec@2` adds a mandatory Changelog; `spec@1` stays frozen and BRO-1/BRO-2 migrate to `@2`. - OpenCode and Kilo now use the shared adapter core instead of their own copies of the CLI ladder; Kilo gains the full fallback ladder. - AGT-1 defines a binding scenario catalog (S1–S10); each child spec maps applicable S-IDs in Verify and declares gaps explicitly. - The harness caught two bugs: `bro_*` tools never reached the model (fixed via `codemode: false`), and the OpenCode stop gate was dead because it listened to v1 event names v2 never emits — it now uses the verified v2 taxonomy (`execution.started`, `execution.succeeded`, `session.compaction.*`). - FakeBro answers `bro hooks` per test rules and journals invocations; ScriptedCli shadows other PATH CLIs (`bd`, `gh`, `dolt`) with rule-based replies. e2e test titles carry their S-IDs. - The pi driver installs through the real `bro plugins install pi` path and asserts `bro_status` reaches the model as a function tool; S8 deps tests run real `bro hooks post-tool` against dead and healthy `bd` shims, proving fail-open holds. author: amaslakov
body:
### 📝 Description

Fixes three defects in the legacy Canton bridge. Stacked on #24714; only the last commit belongs to this PR.

- **Token sends never got the too-many-UTXOs warning.** `validateUtxoCount` looked the count up under `` `${tokenId}-${instrumentAdmin}` ``, but sync stores token counts under `getKey(id, admin)`, which joins with `____`, so every token lookup read 0. It now uses `getKey`. Native sends are unchanged.
- **Two gateway caches ignored the gateway.** The topology-change check (ten minutes) and the enabled-instruments set (fifteen minutes) were cached by node id only, so two gateways sharing a node id shared cached results. Sync filters token sub-accounts with the instruments set, so switching gateway could hide enabled token accounts or keep disabled ones. Both keys now include the gateway URL, as `getPartyByIdCached`'s does, and each clear function still clears the entry it targets. The CoinModuleApi's `validateIntent` reads the topology cache too, so it gets the fix.

The admin a token transaction carries (`token.contractAddress`, from CAL) is the one sync keys the counts by. On mainnet, every Canton token's CAL `contract_address` equals the gateway's admin for that instrument, and sync already relies on that match when it filters token sub-accounts. Sync's matching of balance rows to CAL tokens by instrument id alone, found while checking this, is [LIVE-41341](https://ledgerhq.atlassian.net/browse/LIVE-41341).

Unit tests store token counts with `getKey`, as sync does, and cover 10, 11, 24 and 25 UTXOs and a count stored under another admin. Gateway tests cover cross-gateway reuse and targeted clearing for both caches. Reverting any fix fails its new tests.

### 🔗 Context

- **JIRA / GitHub issue**: [LIVE-41106](https://ledgerhq.atlassian.net/browse/LIVE-41106)

## Why

`services/stage_runs.py` handed the same values from method to method: `page, stage, steps, source` through `_make_chain`, `_measure`, `_book_of`, `_run_steps`, and `page, recipe, …` through `_process`, `_apply`, `_basis_holds`, `_fail`. author: gmr
body:
## Summary

Stop clickhouse_connect from closing and replacing its shared aiohttp session every 10 minutes. The reset races with concurrent queries.

## Problem

- IMBI-28 (26 events) and IMBI-3J (5 events): `RuntimeError: Session is closed`. Both stack traces end in `clickhouse_connect/driver/asyncclient.py:1860 _raw_request`.
- IMBI-2E (45), IMBI-2D (28), IMBI-2J (17), IMBI-2R (12), IMBI-76 (5), IMBI-74 (4), IMBI-6Y (3): `Unclosed client session` / `Unclosed connector` from GC.

In `asyncclient._raw_request`, when `max_connection_age` (default 600 s) passes, the client calls `close_connections()`. That closes the session, awaits, and then creates a new one. A query that starts during the await uses the closed session. Two requests that reset at the same time each create a new session, and the first new session is overwritten and never closed.

The Unclosed events have no stack trace. clickhouse_connect is the only aiohttp user in imbi-api that is not closed by a context manager (aioboto3 clients use `async with`), so I attribute them to this race. IMBI-2E and IMBI-74 occur at the same second with the same trace, which agrees with one leaked session plus its connector.

## Solution

Set the clickhouse_connect common setting `max_connection_age` to `0` in `Clickhouse.__init__`. The driver checks `if reset_seconds:`, so `0` disables the reset. aiohttp `keepalive_timeout` still closes idle connections. The driver has no per-client option for this, so the global setting is used.

An upstream issue against clickhouse-connect could be filed for the race in `close_connections()`.

## Testing

- New test `test_disables_connection_pool_reset` (failed before the change, passes after).
- `pytest libraries/common/tests/clickhouse`: 114 passed.
- ruff check / format, basedpyright `libraries/common/src`: 0 errors.

author: ju571nk
body:
## Summary

Claude Code runs an HTTP hook only when its URL matches `allowedHttpHookUrls`, so a hook the list blocks does not forward anything. The user and project rows now read that list and stop reporting `HookForwardsToolCalls` for a blocked hook. For a person who reviews the posture score, this removes a false finding. For the next maintainer, the matching is one small function (`url_may_match` in `claude_code.rs`) with the unclear cases named below.

Part of #539

## What changed

- The lists of the managed, user and project files merge (the existing union that `merge_overlay` applies to arrays). Unset allows every URL. An empty array blocks every HTTP hook.
- The user row sees the managed and user files, the project row sees the managed, user and project files.
- A project row also reports a user `http` hook that the merged lists admit and the user list alone blocks, because Claude Code merges the lists and runs that hook in the project. The user row keeps its own behavior.
- Managed hooks stay reported, and so do hooks of skills and plugins. Only the user and project rows drop a blocked hook.
- The user scope adds one control, `claude_code.configured.allowedHttpHookUrls`, from the first of `settings.json` and `settings.local.json` that sets the key. Its value is the number of merged patterns. No URL or host is ever put in a control, and no reason kind or event field is added. A list that only a managed file sets gives no control.
- A list that is not an array of strings is read as unset, so a bad list never hides a hook.

## Matching rules

The docs say patterns use `*` as a wildcard and compare hostnames without case and without a trailing dot. They do not say whether `*` crosses `/` and `:`, how scheme and port match, or whether a pattern may omit the scheme. Where the docs are silent, a hook stays reported. So a hook counts as blocked only when no reading admits it:

- `*` matches any run of characters, including `/` and `:`.
- URL and pattern are compared without case, path and query included. The docs state this for the host only, and the loose side keeps more hooks reported. A trailing dot on the host is ignored on both sides.
- A pattern without a scheme is tried against the URL without its scheme.
- An explicit default port (`:443`, `:80`) and a missing port are treated as the same, and a URL with no path is also tried with `/`.
- Everything else is literal, so `http://` does not match an `https://` hook, another port does not match, and a path with no `*` must match exactly.

## Verification

- Unit: the new cases in `claude_code.rs` fail on trunk and pass here (unlisted host, `[]`, listed host, host case and trailing dot, user and project lists merging, `command` hooks unaffected, open pattern readings). A control test expects the count and no URL text in the serialized control.

body:
Keeps `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` current after an audit of the analysis layer.
Documentation only.

## Added

**Issue 13 — the tool layer billed for experiments it never ran.** This is the
one most likely to change a reader's conclusions, so it has its own section.
`run_experiment` reads `interventions` or `gene_interventions` and nothing
else. A flat request such as `{"G001": "BLOCK"}` reaches the engine as an empty
experiment: charged one unit of budget, unperturbed organism returned, no
error. A model therefore cannot learn that its format is wrong.

| Model | Budget spent on empty experiments | Sessions entirely empty |
|---|---:|---:|
| gpt-4.1 | 46.9% | 44 of 117 |
| gpt-4o | 28.2% | 36 of 121 |
| gpt-5.1 | 8.7% | 8 of 124 |
| claude-opus-4-6 | 0.3% | 0 |
| claude-sonnet-4-6 | 0.0% | 0 |

Our published hard-tier ordering does not survive this, and the page says so
without claiming the corrected ordering is established.

**Issue 12** — `run_experiment` never validates an intervention's type.

## Corrected — both make the defect smaller

**Issue 10.** The tenfold signal override is at six places in five scripts,
and one of the six is *correct*: the generator really does use a tenfold
severity for a persistent-signal malfunction. No organism's discriminating set
depends on the incorrect uses — 92.5% of alternatives stay resolvable with
every signal-activation entry removed.

**Issue 11.** The page said items involving signal faults "may mark correct
reasoning as wrong". They do not. All 16 affected items are *filler* items,
whose key is fixed by category and not by their numbers, and none of the 69
discriminating items is affected. The remaining flaw is reproducibility: 13 of
the 16 pair a logged observation with predictions the engine cannot produce.

## Also

A cross-model-comparison warning in the README banner and in the usage
guidance. No issue count is given anywhere, since the list is not final.
