author: hakalb
body:
Part C of the agent-drafted devlog: the agent gets one way to write devlog drafts, and a skill that decides which merged work deserves one. The cms side (the `agents` collection that can draft and read back, never publish) landed in #826.

## What's here

- **`cdwr devlog draft --file <md> --covers <pr,pr>`** posts one draft post to the cms as the agent (`agents API-Key`, signed when `CMS_SIGNATURE_SECRET` is set for host mode). The first `# ` line is the title, the rest the body; a code fence is refused, since posts take code as a cms block. It always sends `_status: draft` and the hook from B keeps it that way. After a 201 it appends `{ postId, prs, title, at }` to `devlog-covered.jsonl` in the queue home. `--dry-run` validates and converts without sending.
- **Markdown to Lexical in the CLI, with no database.** `@payloadcms/richtext-lexical`'s headless editor with `defaultEditorFeatures` on a sanitized config that has no collections and no db adapter. Payload's modules are loaded untyped on purpose: typed, they pull Next's globals into cdwr and make `NODE_ENV` required on every `ProcessEnv`.
- **`cdwr devlog covered`** reads every drafted post back (`?draft=true&trash=true`) and writes its outcome to the file: `published`, `deleted` (trashed or 404) or `draft`. It checks `/api/agents/me` first: Payload reads an unknown key as anonymous, and without the check every draft would 404 and be marked deleted. Any refused read fails the command and leaves the file as it was. The rewrite goes through a temp file and a rename. `--json` prints the rows, `--no-check` skips the read-back.
- **`/devlog-draft`** (`.claude/skills/devlog-draft`), modelled on `suggest-improvement`: reads the covered file, the PRs merged since the newest covered one (14 days on the first run) and the `Closes COD-n` tickets, applies the bar from the parent ticket (what a visitor or tenant can see or do, a decision with a trade-off, an incident and its fix), learns from `published` and `deleted` rows, writes at most two drafts under `devlog-drafts/` in the queue home and posts each with the command. It ends with `DRAFTED <post id> <title>` per draft, `nothing this week`, or `failed: <reason>` when the read-back broke. It takes `home=<dir>`, `since=<date>` and `dry-run`.
- `.env.example` and the README name `CMS_URL`, `CMS_AGENT_API_KEY` and `CMS_SIGNATURE_SECRET`.

## Decisions worth a look

- The body carries no date: the site prints `createdAt` beside each post.
- Two or more drafts still undecided in the admin means the skill writes nothing that week.
- No scheduler change here; the weekly slot and its `--allowedTools` are part D (COD-781).

Closes COD-780

author: kwagyeman
body:
Once cameras are deployed, the formats that cross between the build tool, the server and a camera cannot change shape: a release the server holds has to stay installable, and a camera in the field has to keep being understood. Nothing in the suite would have caught a change to one.

### What changed

- **Sample bytes for each format.** `tests/ota/format_pins.json` holds one sample each of the image trailer and its certificate, the update manifest, an encrypted artifact, a lockbox, a delta patch, a registration record, the slot status sector and a boot journal entry.
- **Tests in both directions.** `tests/ota/test_format_pins.py` checks that today's code produces each sample from fixed inputs and reads it back. A lockbox is random per use, so its sample is only read.
- **The ways a format may grow are tested too.** A trailer that uses the header's reserved field, a manifest with a key nobody knows yet, and a check-in with unknown fields are all still accepted.
- **One gap closed.** The server took a boot journal entry from a check-in only when it was exactly six numbers long. A stub that later added a seventh would have had every entry dropped silently. The first six numbers are the entry; anything after them is ignored.

### Not covered

Formats that live only on the camera and are replaced over USB (the stub, its install record, the journal's on-flash layout, the stub footer, encryption at rest) are not pinned; they are expected to keep changing.

Full suite: 3827 passed, 100 % coverage.

body:
## Root cause
Nov 12/13 protected KB NAV runs #43270426555 / #43278516889 fetched current public sources and passed GAS status+preview, but stopped at `NAV_DERIVED_NAV_STATE_UNVERIFIED`. The server labels a not-yet-published prior-day NAV `NAV_MISSING` (only today's NAV is `UNPUBLISHED`). The collector rejected this expected official-publication lag as though derived financial data were corrupted.

## Changes
- Exact close-day, public-source-lag **read-only deferral** for `NAV_MISSING`/`UNPUBLISHED` only if: same close run date, official publication absent, `publicationExpected=true`, verified units and reconciliation, date within next-day grace (Friday weekend allowance), otherwise strict fail closed.
- No NAV import/derived refresh, phantom NAV or Snapshot write while publication is missing. Return `mode=DEFERRED, complete=false, reason=OFFICIAL_NAV_AWAITING_PUBLICATION` instead of failing the whole KB collector when only fresh NAV publication is pending.
- Historical missing/older stale NAV, missing or mismatched source, units, reconciliation or unrelated positions **still hard fail**. Existing import lost-ACK safety and fund writer lease stay untouched.
- Regression coverage for 11/12-to-11/13 real window, blocked writes and fail-closed negatives. Trigger the existing protected 32-day `issue-507-fund-status-readonly` via workflow-self push after merge; no new workflow, no financial writes.

## Operational scope
GAS production remains v9.293; Snapshot 11/12 39 rows already saved. This PR fixes GitHub NAV collection only. Close finality, published NAV values, PC E2E and NH postdeploy diag remain separately unverified.

author: shawn-sandy
body:
## What changed

- **The prompt count counts sent prompts only.** The status row ("Session estimate") read `$.session.turns()`, the transcript's user turns. Those also hold each slash command's record, so `/compact` added a prompt, finishing a compaction added more, and `/clear` left "1 prompt" with nothing sent. The mod now keeps its own count, incremented in `prompt.submit` when a prompt that is not a slash command or meta prompt enters the session (a dropped prompt is not counted). A compaction keeps the count, `/clear` sets it to zero, and startup, reload, `/resume` and `/branch` seed it once from the transcript.
- **The decision log's `turns` figure** is now the prompts sent since the decision, from the same count.
- **The row shows the context percent** after the token count, e.g. `52.6K tokens · 26% context`. That is the figure the Manage context button appears from.
- **The row redraws as soon as a prompt is counted**, not only when the turn ends, so it no longer shows one prompt fewer for the whole turn.
- README: the status row section, the hooks table and the decision log section describe the new count. The row examples use 26%, since the button appears from 25%.
- Adds a `.prettierrc` matching the file's existing style; `hooks/register.ts` and `hooks/register.test.ts` were reformatted with it, so part of the diff is formatting only.

## Why

The count was inflated in practice. In a live terminal session with two prompts then `/compact` then `/clear`, the row read 2, then 3, then 5 prompts, then "$0.0000 · 1 prompt". With this branch it reads 2, 2, 2, then the row is hidden until the next prompt.

## What a reviewer should know

- An earlier idea, redrawing on `classic.SessionStart` and hiding stale tokens after `/clear` or compaction, was tried and dropped: a live run showed `main` already redraws after both and the engine already drops the token figure after a compaction.
- A resumed conversation's count is seeded from the transcript, so slash commands typed before the resume still count there. Prompts from other origins that are not flagged meta (task notifications, scheduled triggers, peers) count too, as they did before.
- Not checked in the desktop app; the live runs were in the terminal.

## Checks

- `claude plugin test .`: 226 pass. The new tests were watched failing before each fix.
- `claude plugin validate .`: passes, with the existing CLAUDE.md-at-root warning.
- `tsc --noEmit -p .`: exit 0.
- A fresh-context review of the branch diff found no counting bug in normal use. Its two confirmed findings, the missing redraw after a send and a seed that could overwrite a newer count, are fixed in the last commit.

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Status information now includes context token usage and its percentage.
  * Decision logs track prompts sent since the previous decision. Counts exclude commands, metadata prompts, dropped prompts, and externally delivered messages, and include compaction summaries.
  * Prompt counts reset when a session is cleared.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated session and status guidance to explain prompt counting, compaction, and how counts are maintained.

ci-status's "Fail a review-lane hold an untrusted account lifted" step failed on every run of #15568 with `::error::could not read the comments of #15568; re-run this run.`, preceded by `jq: parse error: Expected string key before ':' at line 1, column 1` (job 131507198632). A re-run could not fix it.

Cause: `lane_holds` captures the base commit's `clear-escalations.mjs` `filterLaneHolds` stdout as the comment array. When a PR has a github-actions[bot] hold comment, that module checks the comment's lane run through `createGitHub`, whose fetch goes through the rate guard's process-wide latch (`rate-guard.mjs` `rateLimitLatch = createRateLimitLatch()`), whose default `log` is `console.log` (rate-guard.mjs:626, singleton at :830). #15568 has 12 comments on one page, 7 of them footed github-actions[bot] hold comments, and they parse on their own, so the module ran and checked each hold's lane run. A workflow command it logged landed on stdout ahead of the JSON, and jq failed on the leading `::`. The line was the read-floor warning (rate-guard.mjs:785) or the wait notice (:685); which one it was is UNVERIFIED, because the capture swallowed it.

## Fix

- The `lane_holds` node child sends `console.log`, `info`, `debug` and `warn` to stderr before it imports the module, so the rate guard's annotations reach the job log and stdout carries only the array.
- `lane_holds` returns 1, with an error naming the base module, unless the module printed exactly one JSON array. A module that printed nothing and exited 0 used to read as "no hold"; it now fails closed. That error names the first 120 characters of what the module printed, escaped as workflow-command data (`%25`, `%0D`, `%0A`).
- `lane_holds` also returns 1 when the module prints a different number of comments than it was given, since `laneHoldComments` returns one for each (clear-escalations.mjs:899-909).
- Both callers of `lane_holds` (the human-gated reason and the hold-lift check) get the fix. The step makes the same GITHUB_TOKEN calls as before: the comments read and the events read in the step body, plus the module's lane-run reads (its count does not change).

## Verification

- `scripts/ci-hold-lifted-by.test.sh`: eight new cases. A stub base module that logs a workflow command through `console.log` before printing the array failed before the fix with the same jq error as the job log, and passes after. The same stub still fails on an untrusted lift. A stub that prints nothing fails closed (it passed as "no hold" before). Two comment pages, with a body holding `::`, quotes, backslashes, `%`, a tab, CRLF and JSON text, read as one list. A module that prints fewer comments than it was given fails closed, the redirected warning still reaches the step output, and the error excerpt is cut and escaped. PASS=79 FAIL=0.
- `scripts/ci-hold-human-gated.test.sh` PASS=81, `scripts/ci-gh-read.test.sh` PASS=65; actionlint, shellcheck and typos clean.
- After merge: only a new pull_request event on #15568 (a push or a label change) runs the fixed step. A re-run of the four failed runs proves nothing, because "The workflow will also use the same `GITHUB_SHA` (commit SHA) and `GITHUB_REF` (git ref) of the original event that triggered the workflow run." ([Re-running workflows and jobs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/re-run-workflows-and-jobs)). In that job, "Fail a review-lane hold an untrusted account lifted" shows no `jq: parse error` and no `could not read the comments` error. Any rate-guard warning shows as its own annotation, and the step ends with the trusted-lift line or a named untrusted-lift error.

## Related

- #15568

body:
Closes #1277

The style bar showed six colours, and More style (…) repeated them with only white and the custom colour added. For arrows, lines and pens, those two colours and Reset were all More style held, so opening a popover for them was a wasted step.

## What changed

- **The bar shows every colour.** All seven presets, white included, then the rainbow custom colour. The rainbow is `CustomColorButton` in a new compact look that matches the bar's 20 pt swatches and ring. It opens the same colour editor, eyedropper included.
- **More style drops its Colour row**, and shows only when the tool has an option the bar doesn't (`StyleBarContent.offersMoreStyle`, tested): a shape's outline and fill, text and note alignment, a blur's amount, or a spotlight's strength and soft edge. Arrows, lines, pens, highlights and counters now end at the widths.
- **Reset Style** is in the Edit menu after Copy Style and Paste Style, and in the bar's right-click menu, so a bar without More style can still reset. The image and video editors both handle it. Reset in More style stays.
- Docs: guide pages 05a and 06b, the redesign spec's Style bar and video editor sections, `docs/architecture/image-editor.md`. The More style tooltip is retranslated, and "Reset Style" was already in the catalog.

## Checks

- `make lint` and `make test` pass (1498 tests, 1 new).
- In ShotDev: the note tool shows 7 colours, the rainbow and …. The arrow tool shows no …. The rainbow opens the colour editor, and a picked colour shows inside it with the chosen ring. Right-click › Reset Style puts the arrow back to red.
- Not tried: the Edit menu item itself (it calls the same model method as the context menu), the video editor's bar, and Tab through the new swatch.

## Not done

author: gabriel-kahen
body:
Resources can now retain an explicit caller loop, request sticky cancellation and accept deferred close while a separately reserved ticket owns the cleanup result. The legacy net/TLS adoption and cancellation behavior stays compatible. This is the common foundation split out of #922; it contains no socket implementation, subprocess stream adapter or integration repair commits.

The public loop uses the common exact registry, with stable platform kind values and kind/tag/generation checks. Owner-thread maintenance drives native teardown. Genuine watch-removal errors retain bookkeeping for repair/retry; already-gone registrations normalize to success. Linux wake pipes use atomic close-on-exec/nonblocking creation. The private legacy wait context safely retires its backend on a removal error before the caller releases its descriptor.

Routine legacy I/O reads immutable registry metadata and acquires no managed lock. Managed owners use a full-ID hash index and pending-only owner queues; release pumps only when the owner has pending cleanup. Tests retain 128 failed results on one loop and recover all original results after slot reuse. This is why I propose keeping one reserved ticket per resource: serial callbacks can leave many independent failures unresolved.

Validation: fresh scoped build and 9/9 CTests; five standalone shared/handle/net/TLS suites in normal and ASan/UBSan/leak modes. [Portable source-bound evidence](https://github.com/Gabriel-Kahen/eshkol/blob/gabe/shared-loop-leases/docs/development/evidence/shared-loop-leases-2026-11-12.md). The same common production bytes also passed the [combined hosted native socket/common/PROCESS run](https://github.com/Gabriel-Kahen/eshkol/actions/runs/43312363510) on Linux and macOS arm64; that run's wider source/scope is recorded separately in #922.

Builds on #845 and canonical `e2c83bd48`. Land [the independent integration repairs (#925)](https://github.com/tsotchke/eshkol/pull/925) first, then this foundation; #914's adapter depends on it, followed by the amended #916 scaffold and socket core. The cleanup-ticket API remains a proposal for review. TCP/UDP/TLS public API migrations and PROCESS aggregate cleanup ownership are separate coordination items. This stays draft pending that review.

author: phrolovia
body:
## Summary

Gives the docs a real API reference: a page for every export, entry point pages, and card-based API sections on the guide pages, all built from one data set.

### Reference pages
- **Every export has its own page** at `/api/<entry point>/<name>`. Each page shows:
  - Its kind, entry point and guide.
  - Its selectors, pipe name or `exportAs` name, and its import statement, each copied with a click.
  - Its members as cards, grouped and tinted by section (inputs, outputs, methods, inherited members…), each with its type, flags and default beside its name.
  - What uses it.
  - Filters that narrow the cards to one section, or to the members whose names, types, signatures and descriptions contain some text.
  - Type names that link to their own pages.
- **Every entry point has a page** at `/api/<entry point>`: its import path, its guides, and its exports as a grid of cards grouped and tinted by kind, with the same filters. `/api` lists the entry points.
- `npm run build:api-data` writes the pages' data to `dist/docs-api`. The tester's serve and build scripts run it first, and so does `test:lib`, so the data isn't committed.

### Guide pages
- **API sections are cards:** each of the 85 component pages shows its API section as cards tinted by kind. Each card links to the export's page and shows its first sentence and its selectors as copy pills.
- **`api.md` is now a table of links.** It stays for search and the AI docs, and no longer lists every member.
- **Guides link to the reference pages** for details that used to be in the API section.

### Hidden plumbing
- **41 exports are marked `@hidden`:** the tokens, services and helpers that only Mona UI's own entry points use, such as `DROPDOWN_POPUP_INPUT_TOKEN` and `CalendarService`. The reference, search and the AI docs leave them out, and the reference goes from 1121 exports to 1079. They stay exported. They aren't marked `@internal`, because `stripInternal` would drop them from the typings the other entry points build against.
- **The extractor honors `@hidden`** on constants and overloads too.

### Fixes along the way
- **Tags in descriptions:** an `<` in a description is escaped. A raw `<title>` had swallowed most of the chart API table.
- **Aurora Dark:** it's registered again, since choosing it in the theme picker threw an error, and it now meets the built-in themes' contrast.
- **Wrapping:** long code in a guide's table cells wraps. So do long signatures and import statements on the reference pages, where they used to scroll in a block the keyboard couldn't reach.
- **Outline order:** the page outline follows the order of the headings, including headings added after the page renders.
- **Link color:** links in the API reference use `primary-subtle-foreground` instead of `primary`. The primary color is about 1.5:1 on Anna Dark. In the light themes this makes the links a darker shade of the same color. This change is its own commit (b05fe2374), so it's easy to revert.

## Notes for reviewers
- **Library documentation tests:** they now check inputs, outputs, defaults and methods against `dist/docs-api` instead of the member tables in `api.md`.
- **Shared code:** the kind colors (`api-kind-hues.ts` and the `api-kind-*` classes in `styles.css`) and `app-api-filter-bar` are shared between the guide pages, the entry point pages and the export pages. `docs/internal/docs-page-schema.md` describes all of this.
- **Undecided exports:** 13 exports were left public because whether to hide them is a judgment call: the `*_DEFAULT_MESSAGES` constants, `canonicalizeLocaleId`, `FilterMenuComponent`, `FilterService`, `TimeSelectorComponent` and a few event types. They can be marked `@hidden` in a follow-up.

## Testing
- **All pr.yml steps pass locally.** The only failures were in test-audit, from copies of `generate-cldr-week-data.spec.ts` under a local `.claude/worktrees` folder, which CI doesn't have. Without them it passes, 11 of 11 files.
- **axe, with color contrast:** it passes on the export, entry point, index and guide pages in all six themes, with filters on and off. It also passes at phone width in Luna Light and Anna Dark.
- **Forced colors:** a selected filter shows the system Highlight color, focus outlines show, and the cards keep their borders.
